AECOM is actively seeking a talented Entry-Level Field Geologist for immediate employment in Colorado Springs, CO or Franklin / Nashville, TN office. This position would support the Environmental Business Line in the exciting and growing field of military munitions response geophysics, working primarily on Federal munitions response projects at various field locations across the United States, Hawaii, Guam, and other international locations. Working at AECOM means being part of a global team and collaborating with award-winning professionals across the world. Aspire to be a key player on some of the best projects regionally, nationally, and internationally. This position is expected to begin ASAP. Under the supervision of a Project Geophysicist or senior-level team member, the successful candidate’s responsibilities will include: Using on-the-job learning to apply data acquisition field practices and techniques using advanced near-surface geophysical classification systems to collect geophysical data to identify anomalies related to munitions in the shallow subsurface. Performing supervised field tasks, such as geophysical data acquisition utilizing standard and advanced geophysical classification electromagnetic induction systems, real-time kinematic global navigation satellite systems, and simultaneous location and mapping with LiDAR positioning systems. Gathering geophysical data and other information to be used in the preparation of scientific reports and compiling and organize environmental data collected by others. Preparing basic data and scientific documents utilizing knowledge of natural sciences (geology and geophysics) to explain observations. Assisting senior-level team members in planning and coordination efforts of field programs. Qualified candidates must be prepared for extensive travel and fieldwork in challenging environments. Out-of-state and international travel will be required. This position requires 95-100% field work at project sites. The ideal candidate must be able to work effectively both as an individual and within a collaborative team environment. They must be able to demonstrate effective and timely communication skills. The flexibility to work on a multitude of diverse projects, a positive attitude, and commitment to workplace health and safety are imperative. For the right candidate, this position holds significant potential to learn leadership and management skills that offer growth opportunities within AECOM’s munition response program. Minimum Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Geophysics, or related science. Valid U.S. Driver’s License required to visit project sites, clients, and other AECOM offices. As a condition of employment, selected candidate must pass a Motor Vehicle Records review. Candidate will submit to medical surveillance screening upon hire. Due to the nature of the work, U.S. citizenship is required. Preferred Qualifications: General knowledge of geophysical and environmental concepts. Ability and desire to travel for weeks- to months-long project assignments. Strong organizational skills and the ability to document. Safety-minded individual with the desire to implement safe working practices and be an active participant in safety kick-off calls and daily “tailgate” safety briefings. Experience with basic Microsoft Office applications (Excel, Access, Word, PowerPoint) and ability to write and to convey complex thoughts and ideas in a clear, concise manner. Database, GIS, CAD, and visualization software skills are desirable. OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER Certification or ability to obtain one within 2 months of hire. Ability to lift and carry 50 pounds and safely drive a full-size pickup truck. Tolerance for work in outdoor environments in a range of weather conditions. Relocation assistance is not available for this position. At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment. **Sourcing Expertise:** Hands-on experience with LinkedIn Recruiter, Boolean search techniques, and other tools for identifying and engaging relevant talent. - **Recruiting Technology:** Familiarity with applicant tracking systems such as Rippling or Ashby, or comparable recruiting platforms. - **Communication Skills:** Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to create personalized, compelling outreach messages that establish authentic connections with candidates. - **Analytical Approach:** Ability to track sourcing metrics, assess pipeline performance, identify bottlenecks, and adjust strategies based on data and results. - **Organizational Skills:** Strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple requisitions, candidate pipelines, and priorities simultaneously. - **Ownership and Initiative:** A proactive, results-oriented mindset, with the ability to work independently, take responsibility for outcomes, and continuously improve recruiting processes. - **Collaboration:** Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively with recruiters, hiring managers, and cross-functional stakeholders. - **Mission Alignment:** Genuine interest in contributing to an organization that supports first responders and their families. - **Work Arrangement:** Ability to work remotely within the United States and travel occasionally to Carlsbad, California, as business needs require. ## Benefits - As a Student Finance Coordinator, you will guide prospective and current students through their financial aid packages, explaining tuition costs, available funding sources, and any remaining payment obligations. You will assess eligibility for federal, state, military, and other financial assistance programs while helping students understand their borrowing options and manage their education-related debt. Through phone calls, emails, and other communication channels, you will provide personalized financial guidance and responsive customer support. Working in a remote educational services environment, you will collaborate with internal teams to ensure accurate financial aid processing, timely disbursements, and clear communication. This opportunity is ideal for a detail-oriented, service-driven professional who enjoys problem-solving and making education more financially accessible. ### Accountabilities - Provide inbound and outbound support to prospective and enrolled students by phone, email, and other communication channels regarding completed financial aid packages and changes to funding arrangements. - Conduct financial readiness calls, financial aid package review calls, and account reviews for students who are no longer enrolled, helping them understand their financial responsibilities. - Explain financial aid award letters in detail, outlining the amounts covered by federal, state, military, and external funding sources and identifying any remaining tuition or out-of-pocket payment obligations. - Review student financial aid applications and supporting documentation to determine eligibility in accordance with applicable U.S. Department of Education requirements. - Evaluate overlapping student loans, annual borrowing limits, and aggregate loan limits to support accurate eligibility decisions, timely disbursements, and resolution of exceptions. - Discuss current student loan balances, borrowing eligibility, and future funding availability with students, helping them understand the potential impact of additional borrowing on their overall debt. - Provide guidance on available payment plans, alternative private loan lenders, and internal loan programs to help students identify appropriate options for covering outstanding educational expenses. - Analytical and problem-solving abilities, including the capacity to identify discrepancies, assess financial information, and resolve account-related issues. - Familiarity with student financial aid processes, including federal Title IV requirements, loan eligibility, funding limits, and financial aid package adjustments. - Ability to manage multiple student inquiries and administrative responsibilities while maintaining accuracy and meeting deadlines. - Sound judgment and discretion when handling sensitive financial information and discussing student borrowing and payment obligations. - Ability to adapt to changing procedures, funding circumstances, and student needs while maintaining consistent service quality. - Must be in good standing with any personal student loan obligations and maintain that standing throughout employment. **Work schedule:** - Monday through Thursday: 11:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time. - Friday: 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Eastern Time. - Fully remote position available nationwide within the United States. ## Benefits - **Competitive salary:** Annual base salary ranging from $31,200 to $45,000, depending on qualifications, experience, education, skills, and market conditions. - We draw from decades of experience and a significant investment in proprietary technology, infrastructure and risk analytics to invest across four main strategies: Quant, Tactical, Fundamental Equity and Discretionary Macro & Fixed Income. **Our Culture** At Schonfeld, we’ll invest in you. Position Title: Construction Coordinator (Electrical Intern) - Summer of 2027 Position Location: Across the United States, depending on project location Position Schedule: The anticipated work schedule is Monday through Friday, generally from 7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m ., with lunch provided on-site. All approved business travel, lodging, and project-related living expenses will be covered for the duration of the assignment . To help maintain work-life balance, interns will have the opportunity to travel home every other weekend, subject to project schedules and manager approval. Job Summary The Construction Coordinator Intern (Electrical) will support the contractor and/or owner's representative throughout all phases of a mission-critical construction project. Working alongside experienced construction professionals, you'll gain hands-on exposure to project planning, field coordination, quality assurance, scheduling, safety, and project delivery while helping ensure projects are completed safely, on schedule, within budget, and to the highest quality standards. Throughout the internship, you'll assist with tracking project progress, maintaining project documentation, and coordinating with architects, engineers, contractors, and clients. From pre-construction planning through project turnover and closeout, you'll develop practical experience supporting reporting, risk management, issue resolution, and day-to-day construction operations. This is a structured learning opportunity designed for individuals beginning their careers in construction management. You'll work under the guidance of experienced professionals, receive mentorship, and build the technical and professional skills needed to succeed in the construction industry while learning DLB Associates' processes, standards, and best practices. The Construction Coordinator Intern (Electrical) is expected to communicate professionally and collaborate effectively with project teams while supporting DLB Associates' commitment to safety, quality, integrity, and exceptional client service. Essential Functions Assist project teams with contract administration and coordination meetings. Support document tracking, including submittals, RFIs, and change orders. Help monitor project schedules and budgets using company tools and templates. Assist in preparing reports and presentations summarizing project progress and key metrics. Support field teams in verifying installations meet design and quality expectations. Help document construction activities through photos, logs, and progress summaries. Assist in collecting and organizing closeout documentation. Learn about risk management, safety, and quality assurance practices on active job sites. Prepare visual materials and reports for internal and client-facing updates. Participate in team meetings and contribute to discussions on project improvements. Maintain professional communication and collaboration with team members and contractors. Leverage AI-enabled and digital tools to enhance efficiency, reduce manual effort, and support consistent, high-quality work output. Identify opportunities to improve processes and demonstrate a continuous learning mindset, seeking out new technologies, skills, and methods that elevate individual and team performance. Adapt to emerging technologies and evolving digital workflows, actively supporting the integration and adoption of innovative tools across the organization. Completion of Assigned Tasks and Deliverables on Time and on Budget Performs Other Related Duties as Assigned Position Requirements (BEGINNER level for all the following) Knowledge of fundamental construction and project management principles, including scheduling, budgeting, coordination practices, and the materials, methods, and tools used in commercial or mission-critical facilities. Ability to learn commissioning processes for electrical, mechanical, and controls systems in mission-critical environments. Ability to communicate clearly and concisely with both technical and non-technical audiences. Ability to learn construction management software such as Procore. Skilled in completing assignments accurately and with attention to detail. Skilled at using MS Office Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams), along with exceptional organizational skills for file management. Ability to leverage AI and emerging technologies to streamline workflows, optimize operational processes, and contribute to company-wide innovation Ability to follow company and site safety requirements. Ability to analyze and prepare documents, reports and correspondence. Ability to work successfully as a member of a team and independently with moderate supervision. Ability to work under pressure and meet close deadlines. Ability to work independently and collaboratively with onsite and remote team members. Ability to analyze complex information and develop plans to address identified issues. Physical Demands The following physical demands must be met by the employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is: Frequently manipulating small parts/tools Frequently required to remain in a stationary position Frequently moving through data center and outdoor environments (heat, cold, precipitation), including navigating tight spaces, accessing areas via stairs or ladders, and occasionally working in overhead or under-equipment positions. On occasion the employee may move equipment weighing up to 50 pounds. Travel Requirements Must have a valid driver’s license Assigned to a Data Center project near Buffalo, New York and required to be on-site there Monday through Friday, generally from 7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Interns will be permitted to travel home every other weekend, subject to project schedules and management approval. You will be issued a corporate American Express card to cover project-related travel expenses, including airfare, lodging, meals, and other approved costs. Effective May 7, 2025, and in accordance with U.S. federal regulations for domestic air travel, a valid REAL ID (or an acceptable alternative, such as a passport) is required for travel associated with this position. Travel is defined as physically leaving home on behalf of business activities including but not limited to client sites, meetings with other employees, meetings for business development purposes, running errands on behalf of the business, attending industry conferences, etc. Travel may involve transportation by car or plane depending on the destination and nature of the business needs. Reporting to the Senior Director of Global Marketing, this role serves as the strategic marketing lead for the business, translating commercial priorities, customer needs and industry trends into integrated marketing strategies that drive brand relevance, demand, customer engagement and revenue. This is a highly cross-functional and hands-on role. Manage major event programs from planning through execution, including project plans, timelines, deliverables, budgets, vendors, speakers and cross-functional stakeholders. Develop distinct marketing strategies for key and emerging segments, including destination marketing organizations, airports and attractions, informed by customer needs, industry trends, geographic considerations, seasonality and audience insights. Develop and execute integrated, full-funnel marketing programs across events, content, email, paid media, social, web, webinars, retargeting and other channels to support acquisition, engagement, retention and expansion. Develop account-based marketing strategies for priority accounts and market segments. Develop and manage marketing budgets and recommend investment across programs and channels based on business priorities and performance. Serve as the primary strategic marketing partner to the Destinations commercial organization, maintaining a strong understanding of sales priorities, customer needs, market challenges and pipeline opportunities. Translate commercial needs into scalable marketing programs rather than one-off deliverables wherever possible. Partner with Digital Marketing and Marketing Operations on campaign activation, lead routing, tracking, reporting and optimization, using campaign, pipeline, engagement and ROI data to refine marketing strategy. Ensure marketing programs and content are relevant across global markets, including localization, regional market fit and geographic nuances. Partner with Product Marketing to activate approved product positioning, messaging, sales enablement and customer stories across campaigns, content, events and customer communications. Project Management & Cross-Functional Leadership Lead complex global marketing initiatives involving stakeholders across Sales, Product Marketing, Content, Digital, Communications, Insights, Design, Marketing Operations, executives, customers and external partners. Serve as the central point of coordination for major Destinations marketing initiatives, keeping stakeholders aligned and projects moving from strategy through execution. Manage multiple concurrent initiatives while maintaining strategic alignment, execution quality, deadlines and attention to detail. Identify risks, dependencies and roadblocks early and drive them toward resolution. Manage and coordinate agencies, vendors, research partners, industry organizations and other external stakeholders as needed. Establish repeatable processes and workflows that improve execution and reduce unnecessary one-off work. Position Summary Acuren is seeking Entry Level NDT Assistants to support operations in South Roxana, IL. (THIS WILL BE A LOCAL CALLOUT/TRAVEL POSITION) NDT Assistants will assist in performing calibrations, Nondestructive Tests, and evaluations for acceptance or rejection determinations according to written instructions and record results. Responsibilities Set up and utilize Nondestructive Test equipment Assist Radiographers in the calibration of NDT equipment Assist Radiographers to conduct tests to ensure quality or detect discontinuities (defects) using NDT methods of inspection Record results of inspections Assist performing NDT procedures, carrying equipment and other operations Perform other job related tasks as assigned by management Requirements High School Diploma or equivalent Some college preferred Technical background desired Must be able to have experience, credentials and history to be certified as Trustworthy & Reliable to comply with federal and state regulations, as determined by a thorough background check Motor Vehicle Driving record must meet company standards to drive company vehicles MUST BE ABLE TO PASS DRUG/ALCOHOL AND BACKGROUND SCREENS PER CLIENT REQUIREMENTS. Benefits Competitive Salary Medical, dental, vision, and supplemental insurance 401K Plan Paid Holidays Paid Time Off Pay Transparency: As per applicable state law the job posting pay range is $21.63-$34.13/hr depending on experience and applicable certifications. Company Overview Acuren’s strength begins with its people. Guided by our values— People First, Integrity Always, One Team, Higher Standards, and Innovative —we work to create safe, respectful, and high-performing environments for our employees, clients, and communities. We are honored that our people have recognized Acuren as worthy of inclusion in the Forbes 2024 and 2025 list of Canada’s Best Employers. This recognition reflects the importance we place on investing in our people, protecting everyone we work with, and acting with integrity in every engagement. Acuren delivers comprehensive inspection, testing, certification, and asset integrity solutions that help organizations ensure critical assets are safe, compliant, and optimized for reliable performance. Our specialized expertise and advanced capabilities support clients across energy, industrial, and public infrastructure sectors. Our services include inspection; traditional and advanced NDE/NDT; failure analysis; rope access; materials, field, and reliability engineering; drones; robotics; V-Deck; and condition-based monitoring. Through these capabilities, we help clients evaluate asset condition, manage operational risk, and make informed decisions throughout the asset lifecycle. Our work supports the integrity and safety of assets across petroleum refining, pipelines, power generation, pulp and paper, mining, pharmaceutical, aerospace, and automotive industries. Acuren employs more than 5,000 professionals who support mechanical integrity and inspection programs across industrial sectors. Our approach is practical and focused: provide capable local teams with certified, well-equipped personnel supported by trained and experienced leaders. Building on a strong heritage of safety, quality, and professionalism, we continue to advance technical capabilities and support reliability programs that create value for clients and employees. Accessibility accommodations are available to applicants upon request. role: Visiting Graduate Student (Academic Credit) - Simpkins Lab - Department of Neurology - Per Diem (On-site)
description: About Us: We are a leading research institution committed to advancing scientific knowledge and innovation. Our team is dedicated to conducting ground breaking research and providing meaningful learning opportunities for aspiring scientists. Join us and contribute to our mission while gaining invaluable experience in a dynamic and collaborative environment. Dr. Alexis Simpkins invites you to consider this great opportunity to join her dynamic team! We can only consider applicants who will be able to commute to our Los Angeles location a few times per week. You must reside in the commutable area. Overview of Department & Mentor: The Neurology Department provides clinical care, education, quality improvement, and research focused on stroke and cerebrovascular disease. Under the mentorship of Dr. Alexis Simpkins, the visiting scholar will support medical and scientific writing projects that advance research communication and translate clinical and research knowledge into clear, useful communication tools for patients and families. Research writing activities may include literature synthesis, manuscript development for original research and case reports, preparation of abstracts and presentations, reference management, and revision for journal submission. Patient-facing projects may include education handouts, after-visit materials, care-navigation resources, frequently asked questions, website or portal content, and other materials that explain stroke prevention, diagnosis, treatment, recovery, and follow-up. The appointment is educational and collaborative, with research manuscripts and patient-facing content reviewed by appropriate clinical, scientific, and institutional stakeholders before submission or use. Role Activities & Timeline: Role Activities and curriculum (skills to be learned) over the course of 1 year: Months 1–2: Orientation; HIPAA, privacy, compliance, IRB or quality-improvement training; introduction to stroke care, publication ethics, scientific writing, health literacy, and content governance. Months 3–4: Literature review, evidence synthesis, identification of manuscript or case-report opportunities, patient-communication needs assessment, and development of project scopes and writing plans. Months 5–8: Drafting and revising original research manuscripts and case reports; preparing abstracts, references, tables, figures, and presentations; drafting patient education and care-navigation materials with mentor and stakeholder review. Months 9–10: Journal-guideline and readability review, citation and copyright checks, feedback incorporation, usability review of patient tools, and preparation of materials for submission or pilot implementation. Months 11–12: Final manuscript and patient-tool revisions, submission or dissemination support as approved, evaluation summary, presentation of completed work, and recommendations for ongoing maintenance. Career Development mentorship throughout: Medical and scientific writing feedback. Manuscript development and publication-process mentorship. Patient communication and stakeholder-engagement skills. Presentation development, critical thinking, and evidence translation. Systems Access: N/A Role Summary & Objectives: This visiting scholar appointment is designed for a student enrolled in a master's-level program in communication, writing, medical writing, health communication, public health, health administration, or a related field, or for a medical student interested in medical and scientific communication. The scholar will learn to synthesize clinical and scientific evidence, communicate accurately with research and clinical audiences, and translate complex health information into patient-centered language. Working with the mentor and multidisciplinary collaborators, the scholar will support original research manuscripts and case reports from literature review and outline development through drafting, reference management, revision, figure and table preparation, journal-format compliance, and presentation development. The scholar will also help create and refine patient communication tools using plain-language, health-literacy, accessibility, and usability principles, incorporating feedback from clinicians and patient-facing teams. Objectives are to: (1) strengthen medical and scientific writing skills; (2) develop practical experience with original research and case-report manuscript preparation; (3) translate evidence into clear patient-facing materials; (4) learn publication ethics, authorship, citation, copyright, and research-compliance requirements; (5) evaluate clarity, readability, usability, and stakeholder feedback; and (6) present completed writing products and recommendations to the department. All work will follow institutional privacy, compliance, copyright, and research or quality-improvement review requirements, and final manuscripts and patient-facing content will require appropriate review and approval. Required Education & Experience: • Must be 18 years of age or older. • Must have a HS Diploma or GED. • Must reside in the greater Los Angeles area or surrounding cities while conducting all activities related to the intern or visitor appointment. • VISITORS: Must be receiving funding from an eligible sponsoring institution (employer, educator, funder, etc.). Preferred Education & Experience: Master's student currently enrolled in Communication, Writing, Medical Writing, Health Communication, Public Health, Health Administration, or a related program; or current medical student. Strong written communication skills and demonstrated interest in medical or scientific writing. Interest in research manuscripts, case reports, patient education, health literacy, or healthcare communication. Basic knowledge of literature review, evidence synthesis, or research methods desirable. Experience with Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Adobe, reference-management software, or content-management systems considered an asset. Experience with readability assessment, qualitative feedback, survey tools, or data visualization considered an asset.

role: Administrative Assistant - Office of the Dean of Students
description: Duties and Responsibilities Executive and Administrative Support Manages the Associate Vice Chancellor for Student Advocacy and Dean of Students’ calendar, priorities, and time commitments, anticipating needs and coordinating administrative details to support institutional responsibilities, fiduciary requirements, and the effective execution of the dean’s priorities. role: Research Engineer Intern - Environments, Data and Post-Training
description: # **About Mercor** Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents. Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices. ## **About the Role** As a Research Engineer at Mercor, you’ll work at the intersection of engineering and applied AI research. You’ll contribute directly to post-training and RLVR, synthetic data generation, and large-scale evaluation workflows that meaningfully impact frontier language models. Your work will be used to train large language models to master tool use, agentic behavior, and real-world reasoning in real-world production environments. You’ll shape rewards, run post-training experiments, and build scalable systems that improve model performance. You’ll help design and evaluate datasets, create scalable data augmentation pipelines, and build rubrics and evaluators that push the boundaries of what LLMs can learn. ## **What You’ll Do** - Work on post-training and RLVR pipelines to understand how datasets, rewards, and training strategies impact model performance. - Design and run reward-shaping experiments and algorithmic improvements (e.g., GRPO, DAPO) to improve LLM tool-use, agentic behavior, and real-world reasoning. - Quantify data usability, quality, and performance uplift on key benchmarks. - Build and maintain data generation and augmentation pipelines that scale with training needs. - Create and refine rubrics, evaluators, and scoring frameworks that guide training and evaluation decisions. - Build and operate LLM evaluation systems, benchmarks, and metrics at scale. - Collaborate closely with AI researchers, applied AI teams, and experts producing training data. - Operate in a fast-paced, experimental research environment with rapid iteration cycles and high ownership. ## **What We’re Looking For** - Strong applied research background, with a focus on post-training and/or model evaluation. - Strong coding proficiency and hands-on experience working with machine learning models. - Strong understanding of data structures, algorithms, backend systems, and core engineering fundamentals. - Familiarity with APIs, SQL/NoSQL databases, and cloud platforms. - Ability to reason deeply about model behavior, experimental results, and data quality. - Excitement to work in person in San Francisco, five days a week (with optional remote Saturdays), and thrive in a high-intensity, high-ownership environment. ## **Nice To Have** - Real-world post-training team experience in industry (highest priority). - Publications at top-tier conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ACL). - Experience training models or evaluating model performance. - Experience in synthetic data generation, LLM evaluations, or RL-style workflows. - Work samples, artifacts, or code repositories demonstrating relevant skills. ## **Benefits** - Health Benefits eligible at 30+ hours a week - Overtime eligible at 1.5x from 40 to 55 hours; 2x over 55 hours-week. - $1.5K monthly stipend for meals - Relocation & Housing Support - Free Equinox membership - $200 monthly laundry reimbursement - $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

Responsibilities The ideal candidate has had exposure to environmental laws and regulations including California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), National Environmental Protection Act (NEPA), and/or the Clean Air Act, and a passion for applying sound scientific research and judgment to guide our clients through the environmental clearance and permitting process. This role will consist of preparing technical analyses in the fields of Air Quality, Energy, Noise, or Greenhouse Gas/Climate Change, utilizing state-of-the-art models, current scientific datasets, recognized guidelines and policies, and other relevant tools to solve some of the most pressing environmental needs of the day. Additional responsibilities are: Solve complex problems, assist project managers, and collaborate across teams to produce our clients’ visions for the future built environment. Prepare quantitative analysis with accuracy and precision to meet applicable scientific and legal standards. ## Company Overview Lydian is developing the lowest cost sustainable fuels from waste CO2, water, and renewable electricity to decarbonize the aviation industry. Our breakthrough technology replaces oil and gas refining with fully electrified, modular, and flexible reactor systems that produce fuel with 95% lower emissions than traditional jet fuel. Since our founding in 2021, Lydian has achieved key milestones in record time, including the production of our first liquid fuel from our pilot system, capable of producing 10,000 gallons of fuel per year for a fraction of the capital and time of alternative approaches. We are building a motivated, diverse, and collaborative team that is passionate about addressing the growing climate crisis and is committed to excellence in their work. In particular, we look for tenacious people who are energized by solving the hardest, highest impact problems that come their way. ## Position Overview Lydian is looking for a 6-month Mechanical Engineering Co-op for Spring 2027 to design, build, and test mechatronic equipment that helps automate catalyst loading in our proprietary fuel synthesis reactor. You will take on hands-on engineering challenges—from understanding a process and developing concepts to designing in SolidWorks, selecting components, and building and testing prototypes. Your initial projects will focus on developing tooling and machinery for catalyst loading in our pilot reactor, including automated indexing, injection, and inspection. You will work closely with Lydian’s engineers and scientists to turn practical needs into reliable equipment that supports our sustainable fuel reactor systems. This is an hourly, in-person position based in Boston, MA, with a minimum commitment of 6 months. ## Responsibilities - Understand catalyst-loading needs and translate them into equipment requirements, concepts, and practical test plans. - Develop and compare mechanical and mechatronic design concepts, then create SolidWorks models, assemblies, and drawings for selected designs. - Specify and select mechanical and electrical components, such as actuators, sensors, motors, and other system hardware. - Build, assemble, and iterate on prototypes, fixtures, and equipment; work hands-on to integrate components and resolve fit or function issues. - Test equipment, troubleshoot issues, analyze results, and use what you learn to improve designs and demonstrate reliable operation. - Contribute to the development of catalyst-loading equipment, progressing from pilot-scale tooling toward full-scale systems. - Document designs, component selections, build details, test procedures, and results so the work can be understood and improved by the team. - Collaborate with engineers and scientists across the team to incorporate project requirements and solve technical problems. ## Qualifications - Currently pursuing a B.S. or M.S. in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering field. - Some hands-on experience with mechatronics design through coursework, projects, internships, or work—for example, robotics or automated manufacturing equipment. - Experience using SolidWorks or comparable 3D CAD software to develop parts and assemblies; ability to turn a design concept into a buildable model. - Able to understand an open-ended technical problem, develop and compare ideas, and make progress through hands-on design, building, and testing. - Interest or experience in specifying and selecting mechanical and electrical components for a system. - Comfortable working hands-on in a lab, shop, or prototyping environment, with attention to safety and detail. - Clear written and verbal communication, including documenting design choices and sharing test results. - Curiosity, eagerness to learn, and a proactive, collaborative approach to solving technical problems. - Desire to work in a fast-paced environment and solve interesting technical problems. - Experience with fabrication, machining, 3D printing, electrical wiring, or controls programming is a plus, but not required. ## **Company Culture and Benefits** - Paid engineering-focused internship with a collaborative in-person technical team - Challenging, meaningful work that can directly impact company success - Opportunities for networking/exposure within the climate tech community - Mentorship from a great team of engineers and scientists

description: **Please Note:** To provide the best candidate experience amidst our high application volumes, each candidate is limited to 10 applications across all open jobs within a 6-month period. **Advancing the World’s Technology Together** Our technology solutions power the tools you use every day--including smartphones, electric vehicles, hyperscale data centers, IoT devices, and so much more. Together, we’re building a better tomorrow for our employees, customers, partners, and communities. **What You’ll Learn** - Project Overview: Every new generation of AI accelerator pushes more power through stacked memory, and temperature is now one of the limits on how fast and how dense HBM can be. Our lab builds compact thermal models that turn workload-driven power maps of a 3D-stacked HBM into transient temperature maps in minutes rather than the hours a full CFD run takes, while staying close to CFD accuracy. As an intern you will own one piece of this platform end to end: from the physics and the CFD reference to a validated model that architecture, power, and package teams use to make design decisions. - Skills You’ll Learn: - Heat conduction in 3D-stacked die: TSV arrays, micro-bumps, underfill, and anisotropic effective properties - Compact and reduced-order thermal modeling - CFD modeling and validation with Simcenter Flotherm - Scientific computing at scale: sparse solvers, preconditioning, and fast Python/MATLAB code - Power-thermal co-simulation and thermal-aware design of AI memory systems **What You’ll Do** Samsung’s Power & Thermal Lab is seeking a thermal engineering intern to help build and calibrate models of HBM stacks and package. We are a **small, fast****‑****moving team** where **direct ownership** and **minimal busywork** empower every member to tackle the same real‑world problems. Working with authentic data, real partners, and production‑grade results, our contributions flow straight into platforms used across the company. As an intern, the models you build feed design discussions for future HBM products. You will work on **real projects with tangible results**, receive mentorship, and help shape the scope of work in a collaborative environment where hardware, software, and thermal experts work side‑by‑side on next‑generation AI memory technologies. **Location:** Daily onsite presence at our San Jose headquarters in alignment with our Flexible Work policy **Reports to:** SVP, R&D (Power & Thermal Lab) - Build and calibrate CFD models (Simcenter Flotherm) of HBM stacks and packages under realistic cooling conditions, and use them as the reference for fast models. - Extend our compact thermal model to new stack heights, die configurations, and base-die power, and quantify its accuracy against CFD in both steady state and transient. - Develop homogenization methods that replace fine features (TSV arrays, micro-bump layers, underfill) with effective properties, and establish where they hold and where they break. - Speed up thermal solvers by orders of magnitude through model-order reduction, sparse linear algebra and preconditioning, GPU acceleration, or machine-learning surrogates. - Run transient simulations driven by real AI workload traces, locate spatiotemporal hotspots, and explore thermal-aware policies such as throttling, refresh control, and power-map scheduling. - Evaluate advanced cooling and thermal-interface options (cold plates, two-phase cooling, TIMs, backside cooling) and translate them into boundary conditions and design guidance for HBM. - Couple the thermal model with the lab's trace-driven power simulation engine so that power maps and temperature maps evolve together in time. - Document methods and results clearly and present them to engineers and lab leadership. - Complete other responsibilities as assigned. **What You Bring** - Pursuing a PhD (preferred) or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, or a related field. - Must have at least 1 academic quarter/semester remaining - Strong foundation in heat transfer, especially transient conduction in multi-layer solids and thermal contact resistance. - Hands-on experience with numerical methods (finite-volume, finite-element, or finite-difference) and scientific programming in Python and/or MATLAB. - Ability to judge simulation results critically (mesh convergence, boundary conditions, energy balance) and to explain discrepancies between models. - Experience with Simcenter Flotherm, Ansys Icepak/Fluent, or COMSOL, preferred - Experience with compact or reduced-order thermal models, model-order reduction, or ML surrogates for physical simulation, preferred - Background in electronics packaging, 3D-IC / chiplet thermal management, or advanced cooling, preferred - Filevine is a Legal AI company delivering Legal Operating Intelligence for the future of legal work. Grounded in a singular system of truth, Filevine brings together data, documents, workflows, and teams into one unified platform—where modern legal work happens with clarity and consistency. Powered by **LOIS**, the Legal Operating Intelligence System, Filevine connects context across every matter to transform legal operations from reactive to proactive. LOIS reads, understands, and reasons across your data to surface insight, automate complexity, and give professionals the clarity and confidence to see more, know more, and do more. Fueled by a team of exceptional collaborators and innovators, Filevine’s rapid growth has earned AI awards and recognition from Deloitte and Inc. as one of the most innovative and fastest-growing technology companies in the country. **Department Statement:** The Information Security team is responsible to ensure the SOC efforts are effective and aligned with industry standards and best practices. Interns are treated as contributing members of the team and are paired with an experienced analyst for coaching, ticket review, and career guidance. **Job Summary** Filevine is looking for a Security Specialist – Intern to join our Information Security team. This is a paid, mentored internship for early-career candidates building toward a career in cybersecurity, whether through an academic program, a certification track, or self-directed, demonstrable hands-on experience, who want real-world experience defending a modern cloud-based software platform. Working alongside our Security Specialists, you will help monitor our environment, triage security alerts, investigate suspicious activity, and improve the documentation and automation that keep the SOC running. You will finish the internship with practical experience across the alert lifecycle, a completed capstone project, and a clear picture of what a career in security operations looks like. If you are curious, detail-oriented, and enjoy solving puzzles, we want to talk to you. ### Responsibilities - Monitor security alerts and events in the SIEM, endpoint detection and response (EDR), email security, and cloud security tools under the guidance of Security Specialists. - Perform initial (Tier 1) triage of alerts: gather context, determine whether an alert is a true positive, false positive, or benign, document findings, and escalate per SOC runbooks. - Work the SOC ticket queue: keep tickets accurate and up to date, track investigations to closure, and communicate status clearly to the team. - Investigate employee-reported phishing emails: analyze headers, links, and attachments in a sandbox, help block malicious indicators, and assist with user notifications. - Assist with vulnerability management by reviewing scan results, helping validate findings, and tracking remediation with system owners. - Help tune detections and reduce alert noise by identifying recurring false-positive patterns and proposing rule adjustments. - Review threat intelligence and vendor advisories, summarize what is relevant to Filevine, and help map observed activity to the MITRE ATT&CK framework. - Support incident response activities as directed, including evidence collection, timeline building, and note-taking during active incidents. - Create and improve SOC documentation: runbooks, playbooks, knowledge base articles, and onboarding guides. - Complete a capstone project (for example, building a new detection, automating a triage step with a script, or improving a playbook) and present the results to the Security team at the end of the internship. ### What You Will Learn - How an enterprise SOC operates day to day: the alert lifecycle, escalation paths, incident handling (aligned to NIST SP 800-61), and the metrics used to measure a SOC. - Hands-on use of production security tooling, including a SIEM, EDR, email security, identity and access management, and cloud security platforms. - Practical investigation skills: log analysis, phishing analysis, basic malware triage, and writing clear, defensible investigation notes. - How security operations supports compliance obligations (for example, SOC 2 and customer security requirements) in a legal technology company that handles sensitive client data. - Professional skills: working a queue, communicating with engineers and non-technical stakeholders, and receiving structured feedback from a dedicated mentor. ### Qualifications - Pursuing a career in cybersecurity or a related technical field through a degree program, certification track, bootcamp, or self-study. Formal enrollment is not required; demonstrable experience (a documented home lab, CTF results, open-source contributions, or prior IT, help desk, compliance or system administration work) is equally welcome. - Working knowledge of networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/S, common ports and protocols), operating systems, and introductory security concepts, gained through coursework, certifications, or hands-on experience. - Foundational understanding of common attack techniques (phishing, malware, credential abuse, privilege escalation, lateral movement) and the defensive controls that counter them. - Hands-on exposure to security tools through coursework, labs, competitions, a home lab, or prior work, such as Wireshark, Nmap, a SIEM (Splunk, Elastic, Microsoft Sentinel, or similar), or Security Onion. - Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document technical findings clearly and concisely for both technical and non-technical readers. - Curiosity, attention to detail, sound judgment, and a willingness to ask questions and learn from feedback. - Demonstrated integrity and the ability to handle confidential information with discretion. - Able to commit to the stated weekly schedule for the duration of the internship. ### Preferred Qualifications - Progress toward a security or IT certification such as CompTIA Security+, Network+, CySA+, or GIAC GFACT / GSEC — started, in progress, or planned. - Any self-directed security learning: Capture the Flag (CTF) events, collegiate competitions (for example, CCDC or National Cyber League), a campus security club, a home lab, online labs such as TryHackMe or Hack The Box, or a security-focused course sequence. - Awareness of common security frameworks — MITRE ATT&CK, the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, or NIST SP 800-61 incident handling guidance. Classroom-level familiarity is enough; we will teach the rest. - Any exposure to cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP) or identity providers (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, or similar), including coursework, a free-tier account, or administering accounts in a prior job. - Comfort with ticketing, tracking, or documentation tools such as Jira, Confluence, ServiceNow, or a GRC/audit platform. - Background in compliance, audit, risk, privacy, or a similar control-oriented role — including SOC 2, ISO 27001, or HIPAA work — and an interest in moving toward the technical side of security. - Genuine enthusiasm for the field — following security news, podcasts, or write-ups, and able to talk about a breach or technique that caught your interest. ### Internship Perks - Paid internship with competitive hourly compensation - Dedicated mentor and structured learning plan for the duration of the internship - Real production experience and a capstone project to showcase in future interviews - Potential pathway to a full-time Jr. Security Specialist – Tier 1 role for high performers - Open office working atmosphere - Laptop provided for the duration of the internship

Track maintenance agreements, warranties, licenses, and support coverage, including renewal and expiration dates. - Prepare equipment disposition packages in accordance with PBO guidance for obsolete, excess, or surplus GFP, and maintain supporting approvals, transfer, shipping, and disposal records. - Maintain asset-management logs, trackers, checklists, SOPs, and templates, and support equipment refreshes, site moves, and modernization initiatives. - Protect sensitive equipment records and handle Government information in accordance with applicable security and records-management requirements. ### Education & Experience **Required:** - Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, and Outlook. - Strong attention to detail, organizational, time-management, and written communication skills. **Preferred:** - Experience supporting federal or DoD property-accountability programs, including Government-Furnished Property. - role: COOP Site Support Technician / ORT Analyst (Senior)
description: Computer World Services, Corp. (CWS) seeks a COOP Site Support Technician / Outage Response Team (ORT) Analyst to provide senior-level, on-site technical support at the USMEPCOM Continuity of Operations (COOP) site in Indianapolis, Indiana, supporting LAN administration, end-user devices, telecommunications, network equipment, backups, system recovery, outage response, and COOP readiness. The technician participates in a staggered schedule ensuring at least one qualified technician is on site from 0600 to 1800 Central Time, Monday through Friday, and in an activation roster requiring arrival at the COOP site within 60 minutes of activation. During quarterly COOP exercises and actual activations, the technician coordinates with engineering, field support, the Service Desk, the ORT, carriers, and Government stakeholders to validate systems, restore services, and document results. ### Key Tasks & Responsibilities - Provide dedicated on-site IT support at the USMEPCOM COOP facility within the staggered 0600–1800 CT weekday schedule, and remain available for 24/7/365 support during exercises, activations, or mission-critical incidents. - Participate in the activation roster; maintain call trees, contact information, escalation paths, and activation instructions; identify a qualified local backup technician; and periodically test roster readiness. - Provide LAN administration and configure, install, maintain, and troubleshoot switches, routers, circuits, firewalls, storage devices, and related network equipment. - Support laptops, desktops, thin/zero clients, peripherals, printing, connectivity, and authentication issues for COOP-site users. - Support landline, VoIP, mobile-device, and circuit services, coordinating telecommunications support with local service providers. - Monitor local systems and network services; receive, assess, and escalate outage notifications; and provide immediate response during COOP-site incidents. - Support Severity (SEV) 1 and SEV 2 response by maintaining technical timelines and status, coordinating restoration with technical teams, utilities, carriers, and vendors, implementing approved workarounds, and validating restoration. - Collect logs, test results, and other evidence for incident reporting and root-cause analysis. - Maintain and test COOP-site system and configuration backups, perform approved restorations, and document backup integrity results. - Participate in quarterly COOP exercises (one to three days), coordinate surge personnel, support power-cycle, failover, and recovery activities, and validate network, telecom, endpoint, and application-access capabilities. - Record exercise events and results, participate in planning and after-action reviews, track corrective actions to resolution, and help maintain a multi-year continuity test and exercise program. - Support COOP technology refreshes and transitions to centralized hosting, and perform Enhanced Trust Agent duties when trained, authorized, and assigned. - Maintain site inventories, configurations, network diagrams, rack layouts, circuit records, SOPs, and recovery checklists, and provide COOP readiness information for program reporting. ### Education & Experience **Required:** - Associate’s degree in Information Technology or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. - Minimum of seven (7) years of relevant experience in systems administration, network administration, infrastructure support, COOP/disaster recovery, outage response, or a related discipline. - Hands-on experience supporting and restoring enterprise networks, systems, end-user devices, and telecommunications, and supporting backups, restoration, or continuity exercises. - Ability to work on site in Indianapolis, IN, within the staggered 0600–1800 CT weekday schedule, and to report to the COOP site within 60 minutes when on the activation roster. - Ability to participate in quarterly one- to three-day COOP exercises and to support after-hours, weekend, holiday, surge, or 24/7 emergency coverage. - Strong written, verbal, customer-service, coordination, and technical problem-solving skills. **Preferred:** - Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Information Systems, Computer Science, or a related field. - Experience supporting federal or DoD COOP environments, including exercises, failover, failback, and backup restoration. - This powerful combination enables us to quantitatively analyze open-source media, deliver strategic recommendations, and craft executive-level communication strategies for clients with missions that matter. ## **Why Us?** Our team is a vibrant mix of communication specialists, data scientists, and subject matter experts with extensive experience across U.S. Government agencies, non-profit organizations, and Fortune 500 companies. By joining Protagonist, you’ll immerse yourself in a collaborative environment where innovation thrives, and your contributions truly matter. ## **What We Do** - **Innovative Solutions:** We co-develop cutting-edge solutions with our clients to address tough communication problems and capitalize on opportunities to make a tangible impact. - **Data-Driven Insights:** Our tools and methodologies provide actionable insights that help clients meet their communication objectives and stay ahead of global challenges. - **Applied Expertise:** We integrate our solutions within client organizations, leveraging our profound expertise to address critical issues and ensure sustainable success. ## **Be Part of Something Bigger** At Protagonist, you’ll work on compelling projects that make a real difference. We seek talented individuals eager to contribute to our mission and grow alongside us. If you’re passionate about communication, data analysis, and making an impact, we invite you to explore a career with Protagonist. ## **Explore Your Future with Us!** Ready to take the next step in your career? Join us at Protagonist and be part of a team that's making a difference. Washington, DC | Minimum 20 hours/week | In-Office with Remote Opportunities (Starting Immediately) ## About You Protagonist is seeking a Software Engineering Intern to join our small, collaborative engineering team and contribute directly to the development of our Narrative Analytics® platform, which analyzes millions of online conversations to uncover the beliefs and narratives shaping how people think and act. This is a hands-on opportunity to write real code for a real product, working across backend development, user-facing applications, data pipelines, and AI-powered features. You'll work alongside experienced engineers, data scientists, and analysts to solve real technical challenges, gain exposure to modern development tools and technologies, and see firsthand how your contributions make an impact. Rather than working on hypothetical projects, you'll contribute to technology that our teams and clients use in practice. **Responsibilities:** - Build API endpoints in Python (Django REST Framework) and the React/TypeScript components that use them - Write steps in our data pipelines (Metaflow) that pull in documents, enrich them with LLMs, and index them in OpenSearch - Help build and evaluate LLM features: prompt templates, structured outputs, and scorecards that tell us whether a prompt is working - Gain hands-on experience with AWS services, including S3, Bedrock, and EKS, to support development, troubleshooting, and deployment Write tests, upgrade dependencies, fix what breaks, and help track down production bugs - Collaborate with data scientists and analysts to understand how the platform is used and how engineering contributions support analytical workflows **Requirements** - Authorized to work in the US - Must meet applicable U.S. Government contract eligibility requirements, including any citizenship or security clearance requirements associated with assigned work. - Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science or Computer Engineering - Available to work a minimum of 20 hours/week throughout the semester - This is not a fully remote position; interns must be able to work in our Washington D.C. office 1-2 days per week - Comfortable in Python - You’ve used Git for real, not just for a class assignment - Some exposure to web development (any framework), SQL, or JavaScript - Curious about NLP, machine learning, or large language models **Ideal Candidate** - A class project or side project in Django, React, or TypeScript - Pandas or other data work in Python - You’ve called an LLM API and built something with it - You use AI coding tools and can tell when they’re wrong - Docker, or any cloud provider **Additional Information** If you’re passionate about technology and making an impact, apply today! Protagonist is dedicated to fostering a welcoming and innovative environment where everyone’s voice can make a difference. Protagonist is an Equal Opportunity Employer. The internship pays $20.00 / hour or the applicable local minimum wage rate, whichever is higher. Experience working with public-sector clients and multidisciplinary teams. Professional development through AECOM’s learning and networking opportunities. Minimum Requirements Candidates must be pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Transportation Planning, Urban/Regional Planning, Civil Engineering, Public Policy, Geography, or a related field and must have completed at least 1 year of study. Candidates who have graduated with a Bachelor’s degree and plan to continue with the Master’s degree are eligible to apply for these positions. Graduates must have been enrolled in their bachelor’s degree in the most previous school term with an interest in pursuing an advanced degree in the same or similar discipline at the conclusion of the internship. Preferred Qualifications Coursework or experience in transportation or transit planning. Familiarity with GIS (ArcGIS or similar). Experience with data analysis or visualization tools. Interest in public engagement and community-based planning. Knowledge of federal, state, or local transportation programs. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint). Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment. Relocation assistance is not available for this position. Sponsorship for US employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position. role: (Senior/Junior AI Inference Reliability Engineer, Compute Infra
description: ### **About this role** We're looking for a software engineer, reliability-minded but still a builder, to own what happens in production to the Kubernetes-native control plane that provisions and runs our GPU inference fleet. The platform team builds the manifest-driven API and controllers that let the inference team declare what they need, a cluster, a model deployment, a capacity change, and get it reconciled underneath. Your job is to keep that promise true in the real world: triaging InfiniBand issues when prefill and decode nodes stall exchanging KV cache over RDMA, diagnosing hero-model and LoRA-serving faults that don't show up in generic health checks, and extending the automated self-healing system so each new failure mode becomes a permanent fix instead of a recurring page. The core value we're after is keeping the decoupling real even when things break, and keeping the fleet efficient without that efficiency becoming a new source of instability. You'll own SLOs and error budgets for inference serving, lead incident response, and turn what postmortems teach you into actual changes in the controllers and automation, not just updated runbooks. You'll also work the reliability side of capacity efficiency, since a mistuned defragmentation or bin-packing pass is itself a production risk. Strong candidates have hands-on production-reliability experience on large-scale distributed or GPU-serving systems, are comfortable troubleshooting InfiniBand/RDMA and Kubernetes controller/CRD-based platforms, and think about GPU infrastructure, and the tools that keep it reliable, as software to be engineered. A product mindset applies: the on-call experience, the clarity of an alert, and the judgment built into an automated remediation are things you ship and iterate on. ### **Responsibilities** - Operate the provisioning state machine in production: own the health of the host lifecycle pipeline, discovery, inference bring-up, GPU driver/CUDA validation, health checks, decommission/RMA, triaging stuck or failed state transitions at fleet scale and feeding real failure patterns back into how the states and transitions are designed. - Triage and extend automated self-healing: when the node-scanning and remediation platform misses something, a new failure mode, an InfiniBand issue in disaggregated prefill/decode serving, a GPU Xid variant, a hero-model or LoRA-specific fault, diagnose it live, drive the fix to production, and turn it into a new detection/remediation plugin so it's automatic the next time. - Own end-to-end reliability of the pipeline: hold the SLOs and error budgets for provisioning and fleet health, lead incident response when idempotency, retry, rollback, or drift assumptions break down in practice, and drive the systemic fix, not just the hotfix. - Partner with the inference/ML platform team from the production side: be the one who knows how real cluster topologies, interconnects, and scheduling constraints actually fail in the field, and feed those failure modes back as first-class requirements into the platform's abstractions. - Work alongside machine learning researchers, engineers, and product managers to bring our latest technologies into production, enabling advanced research through awesome engineering. - Introduce new techniques, tools, and architecture that improve the performance, latency, throughput, and efficiency of our model inference stack. - Build tools to give us visibility into our bottlenecks and sources of instability, then design and implement solutions to address the highest-priority issues. - Lead reliability cross-functionally: build coalition across infra, ML platform, and product teams around shared reliability priorities, manage stakeholders through incidents and roadmap trade-offs, and represent the reliability point of view in planning so it shapes decisions before they ship, not after an outage. ### **Requirements** - Experience operating a provisioning or host-lifecycle pipeline in production, comfortable troubleshooting stuck or failed state transitions (discovery, bring-up, GPU driver/CUDA validation, health checks, decommission/RMA) at fleet scale, and translating real failure patterns back into improvements to the state machine’s design. - Deep experience owning production reliability for large-scale distributed systems; GPU/ML-serving infrastructure experience is a strong plus. - Hands-on experience troubleshooting InfiniBand/RDMA networking issues, ideally in a multi-node training or disaggregated-inference context — comfortable reading IB port counters and subnet manager logs, not just application metrics. - Familiarity with the operational realities of multi-tenant model serving (LoRA/adapter-based serving) and with running differentiated SLOs across model pools of different priority. - A demonstrated track record of eliminating operational toil through automation and tooling you built yourself, not just process or documentation. - Hands-on experience with Kubernetes controller/CRD patterns, reconciliation loops, and node-level health/remediation systems. - Comfort with event-driven architectures, backpressure/circuit-breaking design, and treating observability (metrics, logs, traces) as something built into a system, not added after an incident. - A software-engineering mindset first: you write and ship production code, and you think about GPU infrastructure as software to be engineered, not a fleet to be manually operated. ### **About Together AI** Together AI, the AI Native Cloud, is purpose-built for AI engineers. AI application developers get high-performance inference that scales reliably, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for creating frontier-level specialized models, and pre-training at massive scale for fully custom intelligence, all around a marketplace of leading open models that teams can run, adapt, and own. Trusted by Cursor, Decagon, ElevenLabs, Salesforce, and Zoom, Together serves 400+ trillion tokens a month. ### **Compensation** We offer competitive compensation, startup equity, health insurance and other competitive benefits. The US base salary range for this full-time position is: $160,000 - $280,000 + equity + benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by location, level and role. Individual compensation will be determined by experience, skills, and job-related knowledge. ### **Equal Opportunity** Together AI is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is proud to offer equal employment opportunity to everyone regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, veteran status, and more. # **Panther: Better Health Is Skin Deep** Panther is unlocking the tremendous biological power of our skin, delivering efficacious, shelf-stable treatments directly to customers. Panther's precisely engineered smart microarray patches (SmartPatches) address a wide range of needs in Skin Health (cosmetics, medical aesthetics) and are designed to treat conditions in Systemic Health (infectious diseases, allergies, cancer, autoimmune diseases, metabolic disorders). Billions of people around the world lack access to effective treatment, and we will change this. SmartPatches enable effective, tech-enabled customer experiences, and our AI platform provides valuable insights for improved patient outcomes and the development of even better treatments. SmartPatches are affordable to manufacture and distribute, and easy to apply, resulting in greater access and market expansion. Panther is developing clinically validated products, the first of which launches in 2027. ## **The Opportunity** ## This is a 6-month co-op that begins in January 2027, with the option to extend through the summer. Panther is building the delivery platform that lets any partner place its treatment precisely into the skin, and algorithmic formulation is where every product starts. AI models built on Panther’s own data take a partner’s active ingredient, target release profile, SmartPatch™ geometry and regulatory requirements, and generate candidate formulations. They then screen those candidates in silico for solubility, molecular interactions, mechanical strength and shelf stability. Only the strongest move on to physical testing (drug release, toxicity, ex vivo human skin and in vivo models). The result is a clinical formula and a scalable manufacturing process, reached faster than with legacy trial-and-error. Partners get a faster path from molecule to product. Panther is looking for an AI and machine learning researcher with a strong chemistry foundation who wants to apply computational methods to real formulation and drug delivery problems. You will work directly with the R&D team to build models that help us understand and predict how our formulations, active ingredients and patches behave. This is a hands-on role with real ownership. You will scope problems, choose tools, build models and present results to leadership. # **The Impact You’ll Make in Your Co-Op** AI formulation engineers accelerate Panther's formulation work from expert trial-and-error into a repeatable, data-driven pipeline. By the end of year one: a closed loop with measurable gains. By the end of the year at least one partner molecule will reach a clinical-ready formula with fewer lab iterations.The work produces invention disclosures that add to the IP library. # **What You Will Do** - Build machine learning models that predict formulation properties such as stability, solubility, dissolution and compatibility between actives and polymers. - Apply physical chemistry and molecular modeling, including molecular dynamics, to study the molecules we work with: small molecules, peptides, proteins and polymers. - Develop physics-based and generative models of transport, such as how formulations dissolve and diffuse through skin over time. - Work with small, high-quality experimental datasets, using synthetic data generation to augment and anchor real lab data. - Benchmark open-source foundation models and scientific AI tools, and recommend which ones Panther should adopt for R&D and formulation work. - Partner with our formulation and lab teams in Pittsburgh to turn experimental data into models, and models into experiments worth running. - Document your methods and results clearly, and present findings to the CTO and the wider team. # **Qualifications** - Advanced degree in chemical engineering, materials science, pharmaceutical sciences or computational chemistry, or a BS with 2+ years of equivalent industry experience. - Solid chemistry foundation: physical and organic chemistry, molecular structure and interactions, and how formulation chemistry affects stability and performance. This is a core requirement. - Hands-on machine learning experience, ideally with generative models and data-scarce problems, including synthetic data strategies. - Experience with molecular dynamics, cheminformatics or molecular modeling tools. - Strong foundation in physics and numerical simulation, such as fluid dynamics, transport or multi-scale modeling. - Proficiency in Python and the scientific computing stack. Familiarity with ML frameworks and open-source models. - Interest in life sciences, drug delivery or skincare. Biology background is a plus. # **Preferred Qualifications** - Experience with dissolvable microneedles, transdermal or intradermal delivery. - Using LLMs or generative models for materials or formulation discovery. - Publications, patents or invention disclosures in drug delivery or computational formulation. - Startup experience: building tools from scratch and switching between cosmetic, medical-device and partner projects. # **Who Thrives here** - Self-starters who are comfortable with ambiguity and can make progress without a large team or established infrastructure. - Pragmatic problem solvers who pick the right tool for the problem rather than the most complex one. - Clear communicators who can explain technical work to scientists, engineers and executives. # **Benefits and more** - People who want to see their work shape a real product. - Build something unique and high-impact with a world-class team of experts in technology, healthcare, and science. - Hands-on ownership of Panther’s algorithmic formulation work: you scope the problems, choose the tools and build models that shape real products. - Work directly with the CTO and close collaboration with our Formulation and lab teams in Pittsburgh, with exposure to Process Development and Device work. - Apply frontier AI, generative and molecular modeling to real drug delivery problems, with your work feeding invention disclosures and Panther’s IP library. - A small, collaborative team where your work is seen and your ideas are heard. - In-person company events - Fully stocked kitchen, plus in-office lunch twice a week **Equal Opportunity Employer** Panther Life Sciences is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, pregnancy, marital or partnership status, age, national origin, citizenship, veteran or military status, disability, medical condition, genetic information, caregiver status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

role: Student Marketeer - Loyola University New Orleans
description: BE A BRAND & PRODUCT AMBASSADOR Live and breathe the brand personality traits and company values, representing the brand in a premium way through everyday interactions with consumers or customers. Build and execute a tailored and innovative campus plan that engages students and brings the brand to life at your university. Create a strong network on and around your campus, establishing and maintaining relationships with key local individuals. Identify local collegiate content creators in relevant Red Bull scenes and work with your FMS to bring them into the World of Red Bull. Grow the user base by inviting positive trial and awareness of Red Bull through product sampling to consumers at the right place and right time - answering any questions and concerns from consumers. Work at Red Bull events, collegiate activations, and supported events to help ensure an unforgettable brand experience for consumers. Build awareness and encourage participation in the World of Red Bull, including collegiate events and activations. Increase brand engagement on your Social Media handles through authentic content. BE A SALES EXPERT Build relationships with local sales account managers and ensure Red Bull is available and visible in outlets, on your campus and in your region. Collaborate with sales to open new distribution points for Red Bull within your university campus and beyond. Leverage relevant assets from the world of Red Bull in order to keep us top of mind in sales accounts. Ensure perfect execution of defined store standards. EXECUTIONAL EXCELLENCE Deliver executional excellence and show love for the details in all areas of your role. Share ideas and collaborate with your team through regular face-to-face and online interaction. Plan & report your activities in the dedicated online platform in a timely manner and with accuracy. Contribute to business development by providing local insights, trends and overall opportunities. **Are you an upcoming 2027 PhD or PharmD graduate eager to apply your scientific expertise in a real-world setting and explore a career in medical communications?** Join **Precision University**, our immersive internship program designed to introduce advanced degree holders to the field of medical writing. This paid, 100% remote internship runs for up to 12 weeks starting February 2027, with flexible evening instruction (10–15 hours per week) to accommodate your academic and research commitments. While full-time employment is not guaranteed, successful interns may be considered for Medical Writer roles following program completion. **About the Role** As a Medical Writing Intern, you'll work closely with the Medical Communications team to gain exposure to the principles of medical writing and the innovative work of clients developing groundbreaking medicines and treatments. You’ll learn how to develop content for a range of deliverables tailored to diverse audiences, from healthcare professionals to patients.
