role: Student Marketeer - North Carolina State University
description: BE A BRAND & PRODUCT AMBASSADOR Live and breathe the brand personality traits and company values, representing the brand in a premium way through everyday interactions with consumers or customers. Build and execute a tailored and innovative campus plan that engages students and brings the brand to life at your university. Create a strong network on and around your campus, establishing and maintaining relationships with key local individuals. Identify local collegiate content creators in relevant Red Bull scenes and work with your FMS to bring them into the World of Red Bull. Grow the user base by inviting positive trial and awareness of Red Bull through product sampling to consumers at the right place and right time - answering any questions and concerns from consumers. Work at Red Bull events, collegiate activations, and supported events to help ensure an unforgettable brand experience for consumers. Build awareness and encourage participation in the World of Red Bull, including collegiate events and activations. Increase brand engagement on your Social Media handles through authentic content. BE A SALES EXPERT Build relationships with local sales account managers and ensure Red Bull is available and visible in outlets, on your campus and in your region. Collaborate with sales to open new distribution points for Red Bull within your university campus and beyond. Leverage relevant assets from the world of Red Bull in order to keep us top of mind in sales accounts. Ensure perfect execution of defined store standards. EXECUTIONAL EXCELLENCE Deliver executional excellence and show love for the details in all areas of your role. Share ideas and collaborate with your team through regular face-to-face and online interaction. Plan & report your activities in the dedicated online platform in a timely manner and with accuracy. Contribute to business development by providing local insights, trends and overall opportunities. Must be at least 18 years of age Must have a valid US driver’s license University or college enrollment required Must be fluent in English, additional languages an advantage Able to work flexible part-time hours, including some evenings and weekends for a minimum of 15 hours per week Immersed in student life with an understanding of the collegiate landscape and local city, including behind-the-scenes activities & hot-spots Connected with a diverse range of influential groups and individuals on campus Affinity for project management, working 'behind the scenes’, and winning sales A team player, willing to represent Red Bull with branded outfits and onboard the Red Bull Mini Employees may be required to lift and/or move items weighing 25 pounds or more, as needed The hourly rate for this position is $16.00/ hour. The hourly rate is subject to change and may be modified. Red Bull North America, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, veteran status, age, or any other classification protected by Federal, state, or local law. As a Red Bull Student Marketeer, you are part of the most dynamic and empowered brand and product ambassador program in the world. Reporting to the local Field Marketing Specialist (FMS), you will learn Red Bull’s target group and are responsible for driving the brand image and product understanding on your campus and in the region. You will reach new consumers, excite university students, increase sales, and drive visibility of the Red Bull brand. This includes direct contact with consumers and customers, inviting product trials, and working at Red Bull events to ensure an unforgettable brand experience for consumers. Student Marketeers value flexibility over a 9 to 5 job and love to work in a creative and inclusive working atmosphere.

role: Traffic Engineering Intern - Hiring Event with AECOM - Raleigh
description: AECOM is hosting an exclusive, invitation-only hiring event in Raleigh on October 28-29, 2026. This is a great opportunity to learn and connect with AECOM for career opportunities starting Spring/Summer 2027. The event kicks off on Wednesday evening with a networking mixer from 6-8 pm, where you can hear from AECOM staff about various projects, career paths, and the company itself. You’ll also have the chance to meet other students, recent graduates, and AECOM professionals from across our business lines. On Thursday, interviews will take place at our Raleigh office. This is a fantastic opportunity to learn about and connect with AECOM for early career opportunities. AECOM is actively seeking a creative, self-driven, motivated-to-learn Traffic/Safety Engineering Intern for employment in the Greenville, SC office. Imagine working on rewarding traffic/safety engineering projects within a diverse culture. You’ll receive exceptional training and mentoring from our dynamic team of transportation engineering professionals. Working with project managers and lead engineers, your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to: Assist Traffic Safety and Traffic Operations professionals as needed. Research and analyze vehicular and vulnerable road user (pedestrian, bicyclist, personal conveyance device user, or worker in a work zone) crash data. Provide analysis to support development of design or operational ideas and solutions. Develop an awareness of standard engineering practices, techniques, and procedures. Assist in preparation of studies, conceptual designs, calculations, sketches, diagrams, schematic drawings and working drawings. Communicate and collaborate in a team environment and adapt to dynamic project needs. Minimum Requirements: Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or related field. Must have completed one year of study. Preferred Qualifications: Strong written and verbal communication skills. Familiarity with data visualization tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau) and basic data science concepts. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Word and willingness to learn advanced techniques. Relocation assistance is not available for this position. Sponsorship assistance is not available for this position. At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment. About AECOM AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options , well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan. AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at . What makes AECOM a great place to work You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. Work with Us. Change the World. At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations. There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world. We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

What would be a big plus: - Hands-on experience with APIs, LLMs, agents, and DevTools. - A taste for turning technical depth into compelling storytelling. - Participation in active developer communities, hackathons, or open-source projects. . ## **DETAILS** You'll work shoulder to shoulder with the founders and the team, with real ownership from day one: your work ships to production and reaches thousands of developers. ## **ABOUT LINKUP** ## ### **OUR VISION** **We believe in a future of AI agents and the agentic web.** These digital entities can create more value for humanity than we ever could alone, but they depend on the internet to operate, collaborate, take action, and gather information. **AI agents need web search**. To perform well, they require information that is current, reliable, and context‑specific—not the diffuse, steadily aging knowledge frozen at their last training cut‑off. **Modern web search is built for humans, not AIs**. Instead of trusted facts, it serves links, ads, and click‑bait. People want visually engaging pages; AI systems need structured truth. An AI can absorb oceans of data, while human attention barely skims the surface. Humans think visually and intuitively; AI reasons in latent space. **Web 2.0 is sunsetting.** The deck is being reshuffled, and the Bing‑Google search oligopoly is crumbling. Indexing ever more pages is no longer the goal; semantically organizing facts for AI systems is. In the coming agentic web, Google's ad‑driven model has no natural home. **Search for AI must be rebuilt from the ground up.** We are reconstructing the web as a rigorously structured knowledge layer, mapping every concept, entity, and claim into a coherent semantic graph. This foundation delivers verified facts and rich context to AI instantly, unlocking faster reasoning, higher accuracy, and radically more useful answers for everyone. Humans search Google; AI searches Linkup. ### **OUR MISSION** Reality never stands still, and neither should intelligence. Linkup reconnects language models to a living stream of verified facts, ensuring AIs remain as current and insightful as the world they serve. Our mission is to deliver the world's freshest, most trusted knowledge to AIs. ### **OUR CULTURE** Our culture is built on the following values: - Mission. We believe we play a critical role in building the agentic web. We are 100% committed to our mission of bringing the reality of the world to AI agents. - Speed. We build fast, we build to last. We get things done, well. - Ownership. We empower every team member to take ownership of their projects, ensuring they see them through to successful completion. - Teamwork. Our strength lies in our unity. We rely on one another and embrace our diversity as a core asset. - Humility. We maintain low egos, showing respect for others and continuously learning from their insights and experiences. We expect all team members to take an active role in shaping our company culture. ### **OUR TEAM** We are a small technical team, working shoulder to shoulder to build the web of agents. A bit more about our 3 co-founders: - Philippe Mizrahi Led the development of Lyft's Autonomous Vehicles marketplace. Previously launched Amundsen , an open source search engine. - Denis Charrier Founding Engineer at Niland, an audio search company (acquired by Spotify), then Staff Engineer at Spotify. 15y of software development experience. - Boris Toledano Led robotics at Carrefour, after 3y at McKinsey & Co working on public affairs and digital transformation.

Description When you walk into a building, do you wonder how it actually works? We do too. **Summer Consultants is looking for Mechanical Engineering Interns for Summer 2027.** This is an opportunity for an engineering student who is curious about building systems and wants to see how classroom concepts become real designs in real buildings. At Summer Consultants, we design the mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and fire protection systems that make buildings safe, comfortable, functional, and reliable. Much of our work involves renovating and modernizing existing federal, institutional, higher education, and historic facilities. That means our projects are technical, hands-on, and rarely routine. **As an intern at Summer, you will support real project work alongside experienced engineers. You may assist with surveys, calculations, equipment selection, ductwork and piping layouts, drawings, and other project activities appropriate to your experience and the needs of the team.** Existing buildings do not give you a clean sheet of paper. Our engineers spend real time in the field walking buildings, surveying and documenting existing conditions, tracing systems, observing constraints, and figuring out how a new design can actually work within the building that is already there. The challenge of renovation work is solving real problems: what is already there, what can change, what must remain operational, how equipment and systems fit within existing spaces, and how a design can actually be built. Field surveys are also an important part of how our interns learn. You may help observe and document existing mechanical and plumbing systems, ask questions about what you are seeing, and learn how field conditions affect design decisions. Seeing buildings firsthand helps connect engineering concepts, drawings, and calculations to the systems that are actually installed and operating. Curious about building systems? Let's see what we can do together. **WHAT SUMMER CAN DO FOR YOU** Summer Consultants will help you: - Gain real-world experience in the MEP/FP consulting industry. - Get hands-on experience with HVAC and plumbing design, calculations, equipment selection, layouts, documentation, and existing-building surveys. - Learn how engineers survey buildings, document existing conditions, and turn field observations into practical design decisions. - Build experience with tools such as Revit, AutoCAD, and applicable mechanical design and analysis software. - Work on varied projects. We rarely have "typical" projects because buildings are unique, and so are their systems and constraints. - Learn directly from experienced engineers in the office and in the field. - Collaborate with engineers across disciplines and see how building systems work together. - Work in a small, technically engaged environment where you can ask questions, receive feedback, and build practical engineering experience. **INTERN BENEFITS & SUPPORT** - **Paid sick leave:** One hour of sick leave earned for every 30 hours worked. - **Parking and business travel:** Summer provides parking at no cost and reimburses reasonable approved expenses associated with travel to job sites and other business travel. Requirements **WHAT YOU CAN DO FOR SUMMER** In this role, you may: - Support mechanical and plumbing design work on renovation and existing-building projects. - Participate in field surveys to observe and document existing building conditions and systems. - Assist with HVAC and plumbing calculations, equipment selection, ductwork and piping layouts, and related design activities. - Help translate survey information, calculations, and existing constraints into project drawings and design documentation. - Use tools such as Revit and AutoCAD to support project work. - Coordinate with engineers and designers from other disciplines. - Ask questions, apply feedback, and take on increasing responsibility as your skills develop. - Help solve client problems with curiosity, precision, quality, and follow-through. **WHAT YOU SHOULD BRING WITH YOU** - At least two years completed toward a Bachelor's degree in Architectural Engineering (HVAC focus), Mechanical Engineering, or Mechanical Engineering Technology. - Genuine interest in HVAC, plumbing, building systems, existing-building renovation, and learning how engineering works in practice. - Curiosity about how buildings are constructed, operated, maintained, and modified over time. - Willingness to spend meaningful time in the field surveying existing conditions. - Ability to learn from experienced engineers, ask questions, receive and apply feedback, and contribute as part of a project team. - Strong written and verbal communication skills. - Strong Microsoft Word and Excel skills. - AutoCAD and Revit experience preferred. - Ability to support day-long field surveys outdoors and indoors, including conditioned and unconditioned spaces, with or without reasonable accommodation. Field work may include walking 10,000 to 20,000 steps in a day, climbing up and down a 6-foot ladder, kneeling, squatting, and bending. - Ability to obtain site access at client locations, including federal facilities, as required by project assignments.

Description When you walk into a building do you immediately start analyzing it? Do you wonder about the life safety, fire alarm and automatic suppression systems? Well, so do we. We are looking for some passionate interns to join our team of folks who are curious about building systems. The bulk of our projects are renovations, frequently of only the MEP/FP systems, so it makes for some interesting and challenging projects. The fun of renovation work is dealing with the existing constraints imposed by the structure or building operations. We find ourselves regularly solving problems like how to make the equipment fit into an existing building or figuring out how the contractor will build your design. We are such great problem solvers that 95% of our clients would refer us to others. Clients choose us when they want the job done right the first time. We serve our clients' missions as if they were our own, whether supporting the warfighter or our nation's finest government and educational institutions. With our office located in Nation’s Capital Region, our interesting client list, and a focus on renovation, you will get to go into some interesting buildings, sometimes seeing history from the inside out. Check out our projects page for some examples of our work. Curious about building systems? Let’s see what we can do together! **WHAT SUMMER CONSULTANTS CAN DO FOR YOU** - Give real world MEP/FP industry experience. - Provide hands-on experience with tools such as Revit, AutoCAD, and hydraulic calculation software. - Provide you with different projects – we have never had identical projects and we rarely have “typical” projects. Buildings are unique and so are their systems. - Help you get your boots dirty learning from experienced engineers in the field. - Provide a fun, small, and exciting work environment. **WHAT YOU CAN DO FOR SUMMER CONSULTANTS** - Dive into designing quality projects from day one. Not just drafting them, but surveying existing conditions, analyzing life safety, layout fire alarm and fire suppression systems, and lots more fun stuff. - Help us tackle our clients’ problems. Requirements **WHAT YOU SHOULD BRING WITH YOU** - 2 years completed towards a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Fire Protection Engineering. - Excellent written and verbal English communication skills. - Strong skills in Microsoft Word and Excel. - AutoCAD and Revit experience a plus. - Ability to conduct day-long field surveys outdoors and indoors in conditioned and unconditioned spaces, including walking up to 10-20k steps in a day, climbing up and down a 6-foot ladder, kneeling, squatting, and bending. - Ability to obtain site access at client locations. **COMPANY BENEFITS** - Sick Leave: You will earn one hour of sick leave each 30 hours worked. - The company reimburses costs for parking and travel to job sites.

About Trace Trace is building the data, infrastructure, and research that enable robots to learn from the real world. General-purpose robotics requires a deeper understanding of how robots learn from real-world data. Our research explores how to transform human experiences, including egocentric video, demonstrations, hand-object interactions, and multimodal sensory signals, into transferable representations, actionable knowledge, and generalizable robot behaviors. At our Brooklyn research lab, we combine fundamental research in robot learning, computer vision, and embodied AI with large-scale datasets, machine learning infrastructure, and real-world robotic experimentation. Our goal is to advance the science of robot learning while developing the datasets and learning foundations for increasingly capable, adaptable, and reliable robots. About the role We are looking for highly motivated Research Interns to join our research team and work on challenging, high-impact problems at the intersection of robot learning, embodied AI, and learning from human experience. This internship is designed for PhD students and exceptional Master's students who are passionate about advancing the state of the art in robotics and machine learning. As a Research Intern, you will take ownership of a focused research project, working closely with our scientists and engineers to formulate research questions, develop novel methods, design rigorous experiments, and evaluate results using real-world datasets, simulation, and/or robotic platforms. We encourage ambitious, scientifically grounded research with the potential to contribute to top-tier robotics, machine learning, and computer vision conferences. You will have opportunities to pursue original research, collaborate with an interdisciplinary team, and help shape Trace's long-term research directions. Research areas Research projects may span one or more of the following areas, but are not limited to: • Learning from Human Experience and Egocentric Data • Human-to-Robot and Cross-Embodiment Transfer • Foundation Models for Robot Learning • Visual-Tactile and Multimodal Robot Learning • Data-Centric Robot Learning and Scaling • Dexterous Manipulation and Generalizable Robot Skills • Robustness, Generalization, and Reliable Robot Learning We particularly welcome candidates who bring novel perspectives, strong methodological expertise, or creative research ideas that complement these directions. **About Lumafield:** Lumafield was founded in 2019 to upgrade manufacturing. We are engineers with deep experience across the product development cycle, from initial ideas to shipping hardware, across industries and specializations, who became frustrated by the cost and complexity of modern manufacturing. So we decided to upgrade it. Engineers make million-dollar decisions every day, and they need tools that give them the greatest possible insight into their products. By offering unprecedented visibility into products, as well as AI-driven tools that highlight problems and generate quantitative data, Lumafield promises to revolutionize the way complex products are created, manufactured, and used across industries. We started with industrial CT scanning, which for us was the most valuable but underutilized tool in the manufacturing toolbox, enabling us to rapidly inspect essential components non-destructively. We rebuilt the whole system, from X-ray capture, to computer vision analysis, to web-based collaboration, to the entire business model, making the most advanced manufacturing tech more accessible to every industry. Our company, like our platform, is designed for upgrades. We’re building for greater intelligence, autonomy, and speed. For deeper vision, operational excellence, and powerful insights. And then we'll upgrade it all again. Lumafield is headquartered in San Francisco, CA. and has an office in Cambridge, MA. **About the role:** Lumafield is hiring a Finance Engineer into a three-year rotational program across Finance & Accounting. A Finance Engineer is a finance professional who wires systems together, builds AI agents and workflows, then uses them to own real analysis, close work, and operations. **Program overview:** - Three one-year rotations: FP&A (reporting to the Head of Finance), Finance Operations, and Record-to-Report (both reporting to the Head of Accounting). - A readout to Finance leadership at the end of each rotation covering what you owned, what you built, and what the next Finance Engineer inherits. - Rotation managers give structured feedback at the midpoint and end of each year. - On completing the third rotation you graduate into a senior role in Finance, Accounting, or another Lumafield team that needs an AI builder with finance judgment. **The working rule on this team:** If you do something twice, write a workflow; if you write the workflow twice, write an agent. The stack you will build on includes NetSuite, Maxio, Ramp, Numeric, HubSpot, Abacum, Databricks, and Claude. Each rotation adds domain context, so after three years you have analytical, modeling, AI building, and AI orchestration skills and broad context across Finance, Accounting, and Lumafield's business and operations. ### What you'll do: - Own the analysis, modeling, and deliverables for your area, and be accountable for their accuracy and timing. - Write skills and apps building on our data lake and source systems rather than waiting on engineering or exporting to spreadsheets. - Connect systems and remove workflow bottlenecks: integrations, GL mappings, data flows, and the controls around them. - Build and orchestrate AI agents and workflows for the team, with documented review points so the output is audit-ready. - Turn recurring work into documented, reusable workflows that the next Finance Engineer can run and improve. ### Rotation 1: FP&A - Own the operating model and forecast in Abacum, including headcount, revenue, cash, and runway, and the monthly variance analysis against plan. - Build the board and executive reporting package: ARR, backlog, bookings, deployments, liquidity, and OpEx trends. - Support capital markets and M&A work: data rooms, diligence requests, scenario modeling, and lender compliance reporting. - Build the forecasting and reporting agents that keep these packages current without manual rebuilds. ### Rotation 2: Finance Operations - Own collections and accounts receivable performance: aging, DSO, cash application, and customer AP portal resolution. - Own accounts payable and purchasing in Ramp, including approval workflows, vendor management, and the NetSuite integration. - Own monthly revenue recognition under ASC 606 and sales tax compliance in Maxio and Avalara. - Automate collections, billing, coding, and reconciliation workflows with AI tooling and measure the cash impact. - Own inflows and outflow forecasting of 13 week cash forecast ### Rotation 3: Record-to-Report - Run the month-end close for your areas, including balance sheet reconciliations, flux analysis, and audit-ready workpapers. - Own inventory, COGS, fixed assets, and manufacturing cost accounting for our scanner production. - Serve as a primary contact for external auditors on the areas you own and maintain the related process and control documentation. - Build close agents that draft entries, reconciliations, and flux explanations for human review. ### About you: - Agile: comfortable rotating into a new area every year and adapting as the team, systems, and priorities change. - Demonstrated Judgment: makes sound calls with incomplete information and knows when to escalate. - Builder mindset: wires systems together, writes skills and workflow automation, and prototypes rather than waiting for someone else to do it. - AI fluency: proficient in tools such as Claude and has shipped working workflows or agents with them. - Clear communicator and writer; documentation and workpapers can be picked up by someone else. - Attention to detail: numbers tie, workpapers stand up to audit, and errors are caught before they leave the team. - Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. **ABOUT THE TEAM** The Air Dominance and Strike Low Observables Team are advancing into the next generation of LO Technology to enhance the survivability and effectiveness of unmanned air systems. Our Low Observables engineering team is responsible for designing, analyzing, testing, and sustaining stealth features that reduce radar (RCS) and infrared (IR) signatures, ensuring our systems remain undetectable in contested environments. **ABOUT THE ROLE** This is an early career role open to engineers with a degree in aerospace, electrical, or mechanical engineering. Low Observables work sits at the intersection of all three: the shape of the air vehicle, the electromagnetic behavior of its surfaces, and the materials and processes used to build it. You do not need prior stealth experience. Almost nobody arrives with it, because most of it cannot be taught outside a cleared program. We will teach you the LO-specific methods. What we are looking for is strong engineering fundamentals, comfort picking up unfamiliar analysis tools, and the judgment to tell a real result from a bad one. You will be paired with an LO engineer and start on a scoped piece of a live program, not a training exercise. **WHAT YOU'LL DO:** - Run broadband Radar Cross Section (RCS) analysis on components and full air vehicles, and learn to judge when a prediction can be trusted - Support the design and development of Low Observable unmanned air systems, from early configuration trades through detailed design - Build and improve the analysis tools, scripts, and validation workflows the team runs on - Model LO materials and treatments, and help select and optimize them for specific components - Support manufacturing and validation planning, including tolerances, inspection methods, and what is actually producible at rate - Help plan and execute RCS measurement campaigns in indoor chambers and on outdoor ranges, then reduce and interpret the data - Compare measured results against predictions, chase down the disagreements, and feed what you learn back into the models **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS** - Must be pursuing or have recently completed a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field. - Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program. - Able to start in 2027. **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:** - Coursework in at least one of: electromagnetics or RF, aircraft or vehicle design, or materials and manufacturing processes - Working knowledge of a scripting or analysis language such as MATLAB, Python, or C++ - Familiarity with a 3D CAD package such as NX, CATIA, SolidWorks, or Creo - Demonstrated hands-on engineering work: a capstone or senior design project, internship, undergraduate research, or a student competition team - Ability to explain a technical result clearly, in writing and in a design review - Exposure to any electromagnetic simulation tool, such as HFSS, CST, FEKO, or COMSOL. CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 40,000 students from 1,000+ universities, and our partners include Amazon, Google, and other leading technology companies. We've spent nearly a decade training the next generation of technical talent, and we just launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic, building one of the most ambitious AI workforce programs in the world. We're now expanding into new markets and scaling our team so we can move at the speed AI is transforming the workforce. People joining CodePath now will have the opportunity to help architect the next frontier of our work. We believe technical skill is the fastest way to turn raw talent into real opportunity. We train the engineers the AI era runs on, building toward millions of learners, hundreds of millions in revenue, and billions in economic impact. If you want to own something and be part of a 0-to-1 journey at an organization moving at the speed of AI, this is the place to build it. **About the Role** **Location:** Remote (US), with travel about once a month **Role Type:** Full-Time **Reporting to:** Head of Higher Ed **Compensation:** $110,000 to $150,000 per year More than 50 colleges and universities offer CodePath courses for credit, taught by their own faculty or by CodePath. For a student, a seat in one of those courses means industry-vetted learning and career support built into the degree they're already earning. The courses only change outcomes if students know they exist and sign up. That's your job. Students find us through a professor who mentions the course before registration opens, an advisor who forwards a note, a club event, or a friend who took the course last term. Most of that reach happens through people on campus, so your work is making it easy for faculty, advisors, career services, club leaders, alumni, and Tech Fellows to carry the message for us. You'll build all of it: the toolkits and campaigns they share, the campus presence, and the student community that recruits the next cohort. You'll be measured on how many students enroll and stay through add/drop, because each filled seat is one more student getting the training we exist to provide. You'll be a dedicated partner to our Higher Education partnerships team, who own the relationships with faculty and campus leadership, and you'll own the student side of every partner campus. Some weeks that means building a one-pager a department chair can forward on Monday, tuning an email sequence on a Wednesday, and representing CodePath at a hackathon on Friday. You'll be building this function from the ground up and you need to decide in advance how we show up and what we expect back. **What you'll own** **Partner activation and campaign development** - Build and run a term playbook for each for-credit partner, from awareness through add/drop - Equip faculty, advisors, career services, and club leaders to market CodePath courses with toolkits, talking points, and assets they can forward - Turn national for-credit applicants into enrolled students: find where they drop off and test what moves conversion - Run virtual info sessions and campus landing pages that end with a clear path to register - Own email and SMS to opted-in students: build the list, run the campaigns, and work with our lifecycle contractor so campus and direct touches land as one sequence **Student community building** - Design how alumni, Tech Fellows, and instructors show up on campus and engage students, and build the online side of that community (Discord and similar) - Own relationships with student clubs, CS and AI organizations, hackathon organizers, and campus chapters of national organizations like ColorStack, NSBE, and SHPE - Plan the event calendar a term ahead, with a clear standard for which events we do and what each should return **Measurement** - Tie every sign-up to a channel and a partner, test timing, message, and channel, and move time and budget to what works - Use AI to run the playbook at 50+ campuses without adding headcount: toolkits per campus, calendars and send dates, results in one view **What success looks like in your first year** - Every partner runs a term playbook, and fill rate and melt improve at for-credit partners - National for-credit conversion is measurably higher - Every new partner launches with a full first section - A student advocate network is live at our largest partners - The opted-in student list grows, and every sign-up traces to a channel **This role may be right for you if** - You've owned an enrollment, sign-up, or acquisition number and moved it. You set up the tracking and can show which efforts drove the result - You've gotten partners to market on your behalf: individuals who carried your message because you made it easy for them, and you can show what it produced - You've built a campus, ambassador, or community program from the ground up and can show what it produced - You’ve built campaigns from concept to launch, including copy and creative, and run email or SMS to a list you built, changing them based on the numbers - You've decided where to spend time and money (events, channels, sponsorships) based on expected return, and cut what didn't deliver - You've run a program across many sites at once (campuses, chapters, regions) on a fixed calendar, and kept it on schedule without a team under you - You’ve built AI into how you work to automate the repetitive parts, and you can show what it changed - You want your growth work to widen who gets into tech careers **Bonus** - Experience in enrollment or admissions marketing in higher education - You’ve built or scaled a technical community (a student developer org, hackathon community, Discord, or dev rel program) and can show how it grew - Hands-on HubSpot experience - You're comfortable speaking at events and on panels on behalf of CodePath **Compensation** CodePath has standardized salaries based on the position's level, no matter where you live. For this role, we're hiring for a Senior Manager level position at an annual salary of $110,000 to $150,000. Salary is determined based on your relevant experience and skills as evaluated through our interview process. **Full-Time Employee Benefits** This is a remote position—work from anywhere in the US! CodePath prioritizes employee well-being with a competitive benefits package to support your health, financial security, and work-life balance. - Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision insurance (90% employer-covered for employees and dependents), employer-funded healthcare reimbursement, FSAs, and Employee Assistance Program - Financial Security: 401(k), employer-paid life & disability insurance, and identity theft protection - Work-Life Balance: Generous PTO, paid holidays, 10 weeks of fully paid parental leave, and an annual year-end company closure (Dec 24 – Jan 2) - Professional Growth: $1,000 annual professional development stipend and home office setup support - ​​Student Loan Forgiveness: CodePath is a qualifying employer for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), helping employees manage student loan debt - Additional Perks: Pet wellness plans, legal services, home/auto insurance discounts, and exclusive marketplace savings Pay range $110,000—$150,000 USD

The Graduate Administrative Intern reflects the mission, vision, and values of Northwestern Memorial, adheres to the organization's Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards. The Administrative Internship presents a valuable opportunity for graduate students (e.g. M.B.A., M.P.H., M.H.A., M.H.I., M.P.P., etc) to gain experiential education and for Northwestern Medicine to benefit from the service, skills and knowledge that graduate students can offer. The internship is a 12-week paid summer program designed to provide experiential learning and exposure to healthcare administration and leadership. Graduate Administrative Interns are paired with a director or department leader to complete a project aligned with organizational goals and strategic initiatives. Throughout the program, interns engage with management teams, medical leadership, and cross-functional partners while gaining exposure to various aspects of healthcare operations. Interns may be placed in a variety of departments across Northwestern Medicine based on departmental internship requests, organizational needs, and project availability. Performance Improvement Other administrative and operational departments Because interns are placed in a variety of departments, project work, responsibilities, and day-to-day experiences will vary depending on the assigned department's objectives and needs. Interns may contribute to projects involving strategic planning, operational improvement, process optimization, project management, quality initiatives, data analysis, performance metrics, stakeholder engagement, research, and other healthcare administration functions. Regardless of placement, all interns gain meaningful exposure to healthcare leadership and play an active role in supporting initiatives that advance organizational performance and patient care. The internship program includes orientation sessions, mid-point and final feedback meetings, networking opportunities with senior executives, management meetings, community service activities, shadowing experiences, and executive presentations. These experiences are designed to enhance professional development, build leadership skills, and provide insight into the complexities of healthcare management. ## WHAT MAKES US EPIC? At the core of Epic’s success are talented, passionate people. Epic prides itself on creating a collaborative, welcoming, and creative environment. Whether it’s building award-winning games or crafting engine technology that enables others to make visually stunning interactive experiences, we’re always innovating. Being Epic means being a part of a team that continually strives to do right by our community and users. We’re constantly innovating to raise the bar of engine and game development. ## ENGINEERING - UNREAL ENGINE ### **What We Do** Unreal-powered projects have been on the bleeding edge of real-time entertainment for over 20 years. Our team of engineering experts are always innovating to improve the tools and technology that empower content developers worldwide. ## TOOLS PROGRAMMER INTERN (GRAPHICS) ### **What You'll Do** We're looking for a Tools Programmer Intern to evolve artist tools within the Unreal Editor. An important aspect of this role is supporting both user-driven and agentic workflows, including exploring and implementing new interaction paradigms to accelerate content creation. You'll directly impact artist productivity by developing user-facing tools for one of the leading game engines used by developers worldwide. ### **In this role, you will** - Resolve bugs and workflow issues for our internal teams and licensees - Explore new artist workflows on the intersection of agentic and interactive tools - Work closely with team members to modify existing and add new features - Have independence in making and owning implementation decisions - Be part of an experienced distributed team ### **What we're looking for** - Strong C++ skills - Experience in collaborating with other developers - Demonstrated ability in working on graphics tools, e.g. geometry, texture processing, terrain authoring, procedural generation - Experience with using agentic coding tools - Someone who is pragmatic, professional, and has a positive attitude - Prior experience with Unreal Engine is a plus, but not required - Fluent written and verbal communication skills in English *This internship has a flexible start date in 2027. Recruitment will be ongoing until teams find an ideal match. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the posting location for the duration of the internship. For more information about Epic’s Early Career Program, visit [](https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/earlycareers). This is going to be Epic!* ## ABOUT US Epic Games​ ​is a leading interactive entertainment company. For over 30 years we've been making award-winning games and engine technology that empowers others to make visually stunning games and 3D content that bring environments to life like never before. Epic's award-winning Unreal Engine technology not only provides game developers the ability to build high-fidelity, interactive experiences for PC, console, mobile, and VR, it is also a tool being embraced by content creators across a variety of industries such as media and entertainment, automotive, and architectural design. As we continue to build our Engine technology and develop remarkable games, we strive to build teams of world-class talent. ### **Like what you hear? Come be a part of something Epic!** Epic Games deeply values diverse teams and an inclusive work culture, and we are proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. Learn more about our Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Policy [here](https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/eeo-policy). **Note to Recruitment Agencies:** Epic does not accept any unsolicited resumes or approaches from any unauthorized third party (including recruitment or placement agencies) (i.e., a third party with whom we do not have a negotiated and validly executed agreement). We will not pay any fees to any unauthorized third party. Further details on these matters can be found [here](https://www.epicgames.com/note-to-recruitment-agencies).

You will work on cutting-edge Agentic AI research while tackling real-world challenges in domains such as Industrial AI, Manufacturing, Mobility, and Smart Home. Unlike purely academic environments, you will have the opportunity to develop and validate novel AI technologies on large-scale real-world applications with measurable impact. You will work closely with experienced Bosch researchers in Silicon Valley and across our global research network, receive mentorship from leading AI experts, and help transform cutting-edge research into real-world AI systems deployed in industrial domains. Responsibilities Depending on your expertise and interests, you will contribute to one or more cutting-edge research topics, including: Agent systems for industrial applications Autonomous AI agents and multi-agent systems Agent reasoning, planning, and decision making Agent memory and long-horizon task execution Agent self-improvement, continual learning, and adaptation Tool use, function calling, and agent-environment interaction Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Agentic RAG Knowledge integration and grounding for agents LLM post-training, reinforcement learning, and test-time scaling Multi-modal agents leveraging language, vision, and structured data Human-agent collaboration and interactive AI systems Agent evaluation, benchmarking, reliability, and safety Key responsibilities include: Conduct novel research in Agentic AI, LLMs, and related fields. Design, implement, and evaluate research prototypes demonstrating innovative AI agent capabilities. Collaborate closely with Bosch researchers and domain experts to address challenging industrial problems. Analyze experimental results and identify opportunities for scientific innovation. Publish research outcomes in top-tier AI conferences and journals, such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, AAAI, and COLM. Basic Qualifications Currently enrolled in a Ph.D. or Master's program in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, or a related field. Strong research background in Agentic AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), machine learning, natural language processing, or related areas. Experience developing AI agents using modern frameworks and ecosystems Strong programming skills in Python and experience with modern AI/ML framework Familiarity with agent workflows involves tool use, function calling, retrieval, memory, and multi-step reasoning. Experience conducting independent research, designing experiments, and analyzing results. Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to work effectively in a collaborative research environment. Minimum GPA of 3.0 Preferred Qualifications Publication record in top-tier AI, NLP, or machine learning venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, AAAI, COLM). Research experience in LLM-based agents, agent architecture, task planning, reasoning, and autonomous decision making. Research experience in agent optimization, including post-training, reinforcement learning, preference optimization, and self-improvement. Experience with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic retrieval systems, and knowledge-grounded agents. Experience with multi-agent systems, agent collaboration, and distributed agent workflows. Experience with multi-modal foundation models involving language, vision, and structured data. Experience in reinforcement learning, online learning, or adaptive decision-making systems. Experience with agent benchmarking, evaluation methodologies, reliability, safety, or alignment. Experience in applying Agentic AI technologies to real-world domains such as engineering design, or industrial automation. Open-source contributions or demonstrated leadership in AI research communities. Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability / veterans *Bosch adheres to Federal, State, and Local laws regarding drug-testing. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a drug screen and background check. Candidates who have been offered the position must pass both screenings before their start date. BOSCH is a proud supporter of STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering & Mathematics) FIRST Robotics (For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology) AWIM (A World In Motion) The U.S. base salary range for this intern position is $53.00-70.00 hourly. Within the range, individual pay is determined based on several factors, including, but not limited to, type of degree, work experience and job knowledge, complexity of the role, type of position, job location, etc. Your Hiring Manager can share more details about the specific salary range for this position during the interview process. For more information on our culture and benefits, please visit: Culture and Benefits | Bosch in the USA All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. The Bosch Research and Technology Center North America with offices in Sunnyvale, California, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and Cambridge, Massachusetts is a part of the global Bosch Group (), a company with over 70 billion euro revenue, 400,000 employees worldwide, a very diverse product portfolio, and a history spanning over 125 years. The Research and Technology Center North America (RTC-NA) is dedicated to providing technologies and system solutions for various Bosch business fields, primarily in the field of artificial intelligence, energy technologies, internet technologies, circuit design, semiconductors and wireless, as well as advanced MEMS design. As part of the global research organization, our AI research in Silicon Valley focuses on Foundation Models and Gen AI, Human-AI Collaboration and Trustworthy AI, AI for Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS) and Autonomous Systems, AI Systems Engineering, and Industry AI. We develop scalable, intelligent, and trustworthy AI solutions to enable inspiring user experiences for Bosch products and services in application areas such as ADAS, smart manufacturing, enterprise AI, healthcare, smart home, and building solutions. Originating from Bosch AI research in Silicon Valley, our Agentic AI Research Group advances cutting-edge research in large language models (LLMs), AI agents, and intelligent autonomous systems. Our research spans autonomous and multi-agent systems, agent reasoning and planning, agent memory, self-improvement, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), reinforcement learning, and multimodal foundation models. We aim to develop novel algorithms and systems that enable AI agents to reason, learn, collaborate, and act effectively in complex real-world environments. We actively collaborate with leading researchers and organizations across academia and industry to advance the state of the art in Agentic AI. Our work regularly contributes to internationally renowned conferences and journals, including NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, AAAI, COLM, and TMLR.

VSC Fire & Security delivers integrated, cutting-edge fire protection, life safety and security solutions, including fire suppression and detection systems, fire sprinklers, alarms and security systems. The company was founded in 1958 on quality craftsmanship and exceptional customer service, with integrity and reliability at the center of everything we do. As the premier provider of fire protection and life-safety solutions across the Southeast, VSC Fire & Security provides every customer with comprehensive solutions through outstanding design, efficient installation, reliable service and repair, and thorough inspections. VSC Fire & Security in Austin, Texas is seeking candidates for the position of **Fire Sprinkler Fitter Trainee.** **What we offer:** - Excellent pay $20.00 - $40.00 and up based on experience - Overtime eligible - Paid vacation and company holidays - Medical, dental and vision insurance options for you and your family - Health Savings Account (HSA) or Flexible Spending Account (FSA) - Company paid life insurance for full time employees - Employee apparel program - Company paid long term disability insurance - Bonus for referring new employees - Parental leave for full-time employees - Employee Assistance Program (EAP) - Boot Allowance - NICET certification test reimbursement - Opportunities for training and advancement - All needed Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) provided **What you need:** - Ability to follow written and verbal instructions. - Exceptional attention to detail and communication skills. - Eagerness for professional development and growth. - Ability to pass various background checks. - Reliable transportation, valid State Driver's License with acceptable driving record for use of company vehicle. - Desirable (but not required): - Experience in the construction, plumbing, or fire protection industry. - General working knowledge of industrial and/or commercial installation methods. - Ability to read and comprehend drawings. **What you will do:** - Under the direction of a supervisor, the Sprinkler Helper will participate in site clean-up, unloading materials, staging materials, and distributing materials. - Will learn to cut and thread pipe and will perform tasks of installation and testing of the system under supervision. - This role is designated as safety-sensitive due to responsibilities that could entail the use of motor vehicles, mobile equipment, working at heights, climbing ladders, and utilizing lift equipment. VSC Fire and Security is a drug free workplace. Equal Opportunity Employer We look forward to hearing from you! [](http://www.vscfire.com)

Count it.) **Fun Fact:** We do not allow email to be sent internally. Carrier pigeons only. JK, we use Slack. **SUSTAINABILITY:** We think Earth’s pretty rad. That’s why we take action wherever possible to limit our impact on the planet. - 1% FOR THE PLANET MEMBER: 1% of goodr’s annual sales go directly to environmental organizations. - CARBON NEUTRAL: In 2019, goodr became a [100% carbon neutral company](https://goodr.com/blogs/goodrtimes/100-carbon-neutral#:~:text=In%202019%2C%20through%20the%20purchase,a%20100%25%20carbon%20neutral%20company!). **Fun Fact:** goodr celebrates every Earth Day by releasing limited-edition sunglasses with frames made from 100% recycled materials—and the packaging is 100% sustainable, too! **ABOUT THE ROLE** Ever wonder how a pair of sunglasses gets made… or how a wild idea like pink furry frames becomes actual reality? Maybe you’re curious how in the world a company lets a flamingo named Carl run the place. Well, look no further! goodr is calling all flaminglets — yes, that’s a baby flamingo — for our **2027 Summer Internship Program**! At goodr, we show up unabashedly ourselves, own our sh\*\*t, and get things done. And we want our interns to do the same. Join us for a 9-week adventure from **January 19th, 2027 – March 19th, 2027**. Did someone say bragging rights? OH YES WE DID. Love seeing ideas come to life behind the camera or in the editing room? This internship is your ultimate backstage pass! As our **Production Intern**, you won't just be watching from the sidelines—you’ll be waddling your way through the chaotic, fast-paced world of creative content. From Line Producing and Creative Pitching to Cinematography, Post-Production, and Art Department, you’ll get to dive deep into whichever avenue excites you most. If you're ready to get your hands dirty, shadow the pros, and own a Capstone project from scratch, apply below! **RESPONSIBILITIES** - Gain hands-on experience in Creative Content Production while learning how a fast-paced sports eyewear company operates day-to-day - Support our massive content engine (averaging a shoot a week!) by assisting on Marketing Campaigns, Sunglasses Launches, and Athlete Partnerships - Collaborate across production tools and systems like Asana, , Figma, Wrapbook, and Adobe Premiere to keep our projects organized and tracking smoothly - Own a final Capstone Project from start to finish—whether that's line producing a live shoot, updating asset management processes, or kicking off a new YouTube takeover workflow - This role is in the Production team and will report directly to the Sr. Content Director - Perform other related duties as assigned **INTERNSHIP REQUIREMENTS** - Committed to the full 9-week internship: January 19th, 2027 - March 19th, 2027 - Available to work full-time: 40 hours per week, Monday-Friday, 9am-5pm - Able to work onsite at our Inglewood, CA office during regular business hours (9am - 5pm) - Must reside in Los Angeles or the surrounding area for the duration of the internship - No college degree or prior experience needed—just a passion for learning and jumping into the flamingo-filled chaos of goodr **ABOUT THE IDEAL INTERN** - Stoked to try new things, even (and especially) when you aren't an expert yet, and you view mistakes as part of the learning curve. - A passion for the world of production, whether you lean toward the creative visual side (camera, editing, pitching) or the logistical mastermind side (budgets, timelines, project management). - Excited to learn (or already know your way around) tools like Adobe Premiere, Figma, Asana, or general content organization. - Must thrive in a fast-paced and dynamic company environment - Ability to work autonomously and/or in teams - Strong communicator who lives into collaboration - Driven by personal growth and thrives in an environment of constant feedback - Is proactive and an independent problem solver! (Can you google a question?) **WHAT YOU GET** - A role at a company that is going to the moon - The opportunity to show up every day and have fun - The ability to learn and grow as a person - Mentorship from knowledgeable individuals in your potential field of choice - A chance to develop professional skills applicable to any career path - Hands-on work with passionate, talented team members - Trainings and discussions geared toward advancing your knowledge of company standards and systems - Relationships that transcend the duration of the internship - Real-life work experience and work samples to share with future employers - Pay Rate: $20/ hour - Sunglasses. AECOM is seeking an Entry-Level Environmental Statistician for our Novi or Grand Rapids, Michigan office to support our environmental remediation and consulting teams. This position is an excellent opportunity for an early-career professional with a strong quantitative background who is interested in applying statistical methods to environmental data and real-world environmental challenges. This position is expected to begin ASAP. The successful candidate will work with experienced scientists and technical professionals to organize, analyze, visualize, and interpret environmental datasets. The position will support project teams in evaluating environmental data and developing technical sound analyses for reports, presentations, and client deliverables. Job responsibilities may include, but are not limited to: Compile, organize, review, and analyze environmental datasets from investigation, monitoring, and remediation projects. Perform statistical analyses under the direction of senior statistical and technical staff. Assist with exploratory data analysis, data visualization, trend evaluation, and interpretation of results, including development of tables, figures, charts, and other data visualizations for technical reports and presentations Support statistical evaluations of environmental sampling and monitoring data. Develop dashboards and automate reporting. Assist with quality control and validation of datasets prior to statistical analysis. Use statistical and analytical software such as R, Python, Excel, or similar tools t o manage and analyze data. Assist project teams with interpreting analytical results and communicating findings clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences. Work collaboratively with environmental statisticians, scientists, engineers, geologists, GIS professionals, and other project team members. Document analytical methods, assumptions, results, and supporting information in a clear and reproducible manner. Support multiple environmental projects while meeting established schedules and quality requirements. Minimum Requirements: Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Data Science, Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, or closely related quantitative discipline. Due to the nature of work, US citizenship is required. Preferred Qualifications: Master's degree or graduate coursework in Statistics, Biostatistics, Applied Mathematics, Data Science, Environmental Science, or a related discipline. Coursework or experience involving environmental statistics, spatial statistics/geostatistics, sampling design, regression, multivariate analysis, or time-series analysis. Familiarity with one or more analytical tools such as R, Python, SAS, MATLAB, or similar statistical software. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office applications. Familiarity with GIS or spatial datasets. Experience working with environmental, laboratory, groundwater, soil, sediment, surface-water, or other scientific datasets. Previous internship, research, or academic project experience involving statistical analysis of real-world data. Strong quantitative, analytical, and problem-solving skills. Ability to communicate analytical results clearly in writing and verbally. Ability to work effectively as part of multidisciplinary project teams. Relocation assistance is not available for this position. At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment. The Summer Associate positions will be in Charlotte, NC and Atlanta, GA. Residential Development – Multifamily (Atlanta): This Summer Associate will assist the Multifamily Development team in all aspects of the real estate development process, reporting to the Managing Director of Development in the Atlanta office. **Applicants will be considered for both positions. The New York City Department of Design and Construction is seeking a college-level intern to support the Finance and Administration team within the Office of the Deputy Commissioner of IT, Data Analytics, and Project Controls. Reporting to the Director of Finance and Administration, the intern will provide administrative and analytical support across three focus areas: equipment and asset inventory management, policy and Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) documentation, and budget tracking. This is a hands-on opportunity for a student pursuing any field of study, with an interest in public service or local government, to gain direct exposure to how a NYC capital agency manages its internal operations, procurement pipeline, and budget process working alongside the team's administrative and financial staff on real, ongoing work. The intern will work closely with the Finance and Administration team and will have the opportunity to build practical skills in public-sector budgeting, procurement, and data tools such as Excel and Airtable, with guidance and mentorship from experienced staff throughout the assignment. This role includes exposure to internal budget, procurement, and personnel-related records, which the intern will be expected to handle professionally. Responsibilities - Help build out and maintain the division's IT Asset Tracker, a hardware and equipment database covering laptops, desktops, tablets, and monitors keeping device, staff assignment, and purchase order records current and accurate. - Support periodic reconciliation audits comparing tracked equipment against what's on hand and help resolve discrepancies. - Help track new hardware from purchase order through delivery and assignment to staff. - Assist in drafting and formatting new internal process documents covering workflows such as onboarding/offboarding or procurement intake using the team's established policy template and style. - Help keep the division's growing library of internal process documents organized and consistently formatted. - Assist with Personal Services / Other Than Personal Services (PS/OTPS) budget tracking spreadsheets, flagging variances for review. - Help organize and file internal budget and procurement backup documentation. - Assist with data entry and maintenance of administrative tracking systems, including the staff roster and HR action tracking. - Provide light research support (e.g., vendor or rate comparisons) and help prepare materials for internal team meetings. role: Product Manager - Early Career, AI Platform
description: **Who We Are** Addepar is a global data and AI platform empowering investment professionals to turn complex financial information into actionable intelligence. Addepar unifies portfolio, market and client data in a total portfolio view and delivers AI-powered insights within investment and client workflows. More than 1,500 firms in 60 countries use Addepar to manage and advise on nearly $10 trillion in assets. Its open platform integrates with 650 software, data and consulting partners to power end-to-end investment operations across firms of all sizes and levels of complexity. Addepar supports clients worldwide with offices in New York City, Salt Lake City, São Paulo, London, Edinburgh, Geneva, Warsaw, Dubai, Pune and Singapore. #### **The Role** We are seeking an Early Career Product Manager to join the AI product management team. Our team owns some of Addepar's flagship AI products, including Addison, agentic workflows, and the Addepar MCP. Our mission is to accelerate front- and back-office work for the investment industry. As an Early Career Product Manager, you'll get hands-on experience across the full product lifecycle, working alongside senior PMs in a high growth, fast moving environment - leveraging the latest and greatest in conversational AI, agents, and emerging standards like MCP to build transformative new products that deliver value to clients. This role will require working closely with engineering, design, product, marketing, go-to-market to drive new AI products to success. This is a fast-paced, cross-functional role for a hands-on operator who wants to get real AI products into clients' hands, making an impact at the intersection of AI, customer-centric product development, and financial technology. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States for any employer without requiring current or future visa sponsorship (for example, employment-based visas such as H-1B, F-1/OPT, or similar), and must be authorized to begin work in the U.S. on their first day of employment. #### **What You’ll Do** - Drive the end-to-end development of new AI features: help scope requirements, write specs, partner with engineering, design, and GTM to get them built and launched - Dig into how clients actually use our AI products today, surface what's working and what isn't, and turn those insights into clear, actionable product recommendations - Own well-defined pieces of the roadmap under the mentorship of senior PMs, with increasing autonomy - Get hands-on with the AI tools and techniques the team uses daily, including prompting, evaluating agent behavior, and understanding what makes an AI feature actually work in practice - Define product analytics focused on usage patterns, adoption, feature performance - Help the team stay organized and move fast: support operations, maintain product documentation, and triage incoming feedback and bugs - Work directly with cross-functional partners in engineering, design, marketing, and go-to-market to keep execution tight and stakeholders aligned #### **Who You Are** - 0–2 years of professional experience; strong internship, research, or project experience in a fast-paced, analytical environment is a plus - Genuinely excited about AI and how it's changing what products can do. You use AI tools yourself, you keep up with what's new, and you have opinions about where this is all headed - Sharp analytical instincts. You're comfortable breaking down ambiguous problems, working with data, and reasoning your way to a recommendation - A bias for ownership. You don't wait to be told exactly what to do — you ask good questions, make a plan, and move - Excellent written and verbal communication. You can explain a technical idea clearly to both an engineer and a client - Comfortable communicating with senior stakeholders, whether that's a client or an executive - Low ego, high accountability. You're as comfortable digging into the details as you are stepping back to see the bigger picture - Drawn to fast-paced, high-growth environments where the problems are still being defined and the stakes are real - Curiosity about financial services and fintech is a plus, but not required - Experience speaking or working directly with clients is a plus, but not required - Engineering/ CS background is a plus, but not required Addepar takes a market-based approach to pay. A successful candidate's starting pay will be determined based on the role, job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location, and market conditions. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the minimum and maximum target base salary for this role within the United States. Compensation for this role includes base salary + bonus + equity + benefits. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process. Additionally, these ranges reflect the base salary only, and do not include bonus, equity, or benefits. Base Salary Range $83,000—$130,000 USD **Our Values** - **Act Like an Owner -** Think and operate with intention, purpose and care. Own outcomes. - **Build Together -** Collaborate to unlock the best solutions. Deliver lasting value. - **Champion Our Clients -** Exceed client expectations. Our clients’ success is our success. - **Drive Innovation -** Be bold and unconstrained in problem solving. Transform the industry. - **Embrace Learning -** Engage our community to broaden our perspective. Bring a growth mindset. In addition to our core values, Addepar is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We seek to bring together diverse ideas, experiences, skill sets, perspectives, backgrounds and identities to drive innovative solutions. We commit to promoting a welcoming environment where inclusion and belonging are held as a shared responsibility. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation. PHISHING SCAM WARNING: Addepar is among several companies recently made aware of a phishing scam involving con artists posing as hiring managers recruiting via email, text and social media. The imposters are creating misleading email accounts, conducting remote “interviews,” and making fake job offers in order to collect personal and financial information from unsuspecting individuals. Please be aware that no job offers will be made from Addepar without a formal interview process. Additionally, Addepar will not ask you to purchase equipment or supplies as part of your onboarding process. If you have any questions, please reach out to [ta-operations@addepar.com](mailto:tainfo@addepar.com).

**This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Entry-Level Java Software Developer based in the United States.** We are looking for a motivated aspiring software developer ready to launch a career in software engineering through structured technical training and practical project experience. In this remote contract role, you will strengthen your programming fundamentals while learning to build applications using Java and essential web technologies. The opportunity combines immersive learning with hands-on development work, allowing you to apply new skills in real-world project environments. You will gain exposure to backend development, databases, APIs, and frontend technologies while collaborating with experienced professionals. Through guided training and continued project involvement, you will develop the technical confidence needed to contribute to software delivery teams. This role is ideal for an early-career candidate eager to learn, solve problems, and build a strong foundation for long-term growth in technology. ### Accountabilities - Technical Training and Development: Participate in structured, immersive training focused on Java programming, software development fundamentals, and essential web technologies. - Java Application Development: Apply Java programming skills to develop, enhance, test, and maintain software applications in accordance with project requirements. - Backend Development: Learn and contribute to backend development using Java frameworks, including Spring, to build reliable and maintainable application components. - Database Management: Work with MySQL and other relevant database technologies to retrieve, organize, and manage application data using appropriate queries and practices. - API Development and Integration: Support the development, testing, and integration of REST APIs to enable communication between software applications and services. - Frontend Development: Use HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and React, as required by project assignments, to contribute to responsive and interactive web applications. - Software Testing and Debugging: Identify and resolve basic software defects, test application functionality, and follow development best practices to maintain code quality. - Development Tools and Practices: Use tools such as IntelliJ IDEA to write, organize, debug, and maintain code while following established development workflows. - Team Collaboration: Work alongside developers and other project team members to understand requirements, share progress, resolve technical challenges, and deliver assigned tasks. - Continuous Learning: Build technical knowledge through feedback, practical assignments, collaboration, and ongoing exposure to software development methodologies and technologies. ## Requirements: - Educational Background: A bachelor's degree is required. - Foundational Programming Experience: At least 6 months of programming experience, gained through employment, academic projects, personal projects, or other relevant practical experience. - Java Fundamentals: Basic knowledge of Java programming, including core concepts such as variables, data types, control structures, methods, and object-oriented programming. - Willingness to Learn: Commitment to completing immersive technical training and developing the skills needed to contribute effectively to software development projects. - Web Development Knowledge: Familiarity with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript is beneficial, with an interest in expanding knowledge of frontend development tools such as React. - Backend and Database Fundamentals: Basic understanding of backend development, REST APIs, relational databases, and SQL is an advantage. - Development Tools: Familiarity with IntelliJ IDEA or comparable integrated development environments is helpful. - Problem-Solving Skills: Ability to approach technical challenges logically, troubleshoot issues, and apply feedback to improve solutions. - Communication and Collaboration: Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work constructively with teammates in a collaborative software development environment. - Adaptability and Initiative: A proactive attitude, attention to detail, and willingness to learn new technologies, follow technical guidance, and take responsibility for assigned tasks. - Work Authorization: Must meet the applicable work authorization requirements for the United States and the specific contract assignment. ## Benefits: - Competitive Entry-Level Contract Rate: Indicative compensation of $20–$30 per hour, depending on the assignment and agreed contract terms. - Remote Work Opportunity: Work remotely from the United States, subject to project requirements. - Structured Technical Training: Build foundational programming skills through immersive training in Java and essential web technologies. - Hands-On Project Experience: Apply newly acquired knowledge to practical software development assignments and gain exposure to real-world project workflows. - Broad Technology Exposure: Develop familiarity with Java, Spring, MySQL, REST APIs, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, and development tools. - Early-Career Development: Strengthen technical problem-solving, coding, debugging, and collaboration skills to support future career opportunities in software engineering. - Collaborative Learning Environment: Work with project teams, receive feedback, and continue developing your capabilities through practical experience.

description: We’re seeking curious minds like yours to collaborate with full-time engineers and cross functional teammates, learn development standard methodologies, and gain practical software engineering experience.
