As you work on challenging projects, you will be given increasing responsibility and rely on experiences managers and colleagues to offer support and a helping hand as you learn and develop in your role. Tasks and Responsibilities As our new Geoenvironmental Engineering intern, you will be part of our Environment and Health group supporting various types of environmental and geotechnical projects for coal combustion residual (CCR) surface impoundments, mine tailings storage facilities, and environmental remediation projects. Your key tasks and responsibilities will be: Organizing and analyzing Geotechnical and other engineering data in Excel Supporting quality assurance and control reviews of geotechnical calculations Performing project administrative activities, such as managing electronic file systems, updating schedules, tracking data, etc. Researching and performing data gathering for various topics, such as construction costs, regulatory citations, and journals. From the moment you join Ramboll, we will support your personal and professional development so that you grow with the company. For this role, we believe your starting point is Candidates should be working toward a B.S or M.S degree in in Civil, Geological, or Environmental Engineering. Candidates with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above are strongly preferred. Candidates with the completion of 4 college semesters (rising Junior status) are strongly preferred. Interest in working towards Engineer-in-Training (EIT) licensure Required Minimum Skills and Abilities: Microsoft Office, including strong Excel and Word skills Coursework or work experience with at least two of the following areas: geotechnical engineering, groundwater hydrogeology, construction management, drafting and design (including AutoCAD software), and geology. Ability to work on tasks semi-independently when given clear direction by other Ramboll staff, and ability to communicate with Ramboll staff for help and guidance if needed. Personal qualities that will help you succeed in this role include: Good interpersonal and communication skills. Work effectively in teams Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll in the Americas Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. Upon completion of the program and certification, if no ASM or otherwise qualified role is available AND the ST is meeting performance standards, the employee may remain in the ST role up to 12-months OR until an ASM or another qualified role is available (whichever comes first). Once an ASM or another qualified role is available, the certified ST must interview for that available role. If promotion to the role of ACCOUNT SALES MANAGER (or other role) does not happen prior to the expiration of the 12-mos completion period, the SALES TRAINEE role will be vacated due to end of assignment unless an exception applies. For exception, based on continued high performance, no open roles and certification completion, a manager may extend the 12-month completion period an additional 6-months. The MSBA is a quasi-independent government authority which grants funding for school building construction and renovation projects. The MSBA is pleased to provide a Co-Op opportunity to help students learn about data analysis in the building and construction industry. We are seeking a Capital Planning Assistant to provide a great opportunity to learn and gain skills in data analysis and construction. Students can expect to be challenged by their assigned projects, connect with other MSBA departments, feel valued by the MSBA community, while gaining experience and exposure to designer selection and interviews, preliminary design evaluations, and feasibility analyses. Not only will the selected Co-op learn about their day-to-day tasks through their specific work assignments, but they will have exposure to our organizational leaders and their teams through a series of internal Capital Planning Training. A Co-Op position at the MSBA provides exposure to a range of design and construction firms actively engaged in publicly funded school projects. Most Co-Ops move on to job opportunities within the industry and even return to MSBA when there is an open opportunity. The Capital Planning Data Assistant (Co-op) is a full-time opportunity (up to six months) that will temporarily provide support and assistance to Project Managers and Architects for Massachusetts public school construction projects. Responsibilities include data analysis, development of data tools, preparation of reports and presentations, and support of technical review. The individual will also assist in developing tools for information gathering and analysis of databases associated with cost-tracking, construction cost estimates, capital project statuses and policy making, as well as potentially attending site visits. Interested students should possess basic knowledge of data analysis and/or previous experience in data. ### Minimum Qualifications - Must be enrolled in, or recently graduated from, a degree program leading to a Bachelor’s or Master's in an analytical based subject. - Legally eligible to work in the U.S. ### Preferred Qualifications - Prior internship experience in a data or analysis based discipline - Working knowledge of Tableau, MS Word, Excel, and PowerPoint - Outstanding verbal and written communication skills with excellent attention to detail - Ability to succeed in a fast-paced environment with multiple, competing priorities - Ability to deliver results with limited direction and guidance and on tight deadlines; a self-starter - Highly motivated and energetic - Strong work ethic and tenacity - Minimum 3.2 GPA

role: Assistant Director, Student Experience and Operations
description: Who You Are You are passionate about helping students achieve their educational goals. You thrive in a collaborative environment and are comfortable working remotely while building strong partnerships across the organization. You possess exceptional leadership, technical, and operational expertise and can successfully bridge strategy, process, technology, and execution. As the Assistant Director, Student Experience & Operations, you will be responsible for the strategic leadership, development, optimization, and execution of the student lifecycle and journey at ACE. You will oversee operational functions, lead process and technology transformation initiatives, and ensure alignment between business objectives, student needs, and institutional priorities. You will define and implement scalable solutions that enhance the student experience, improve operational efficiency, and increase student satisfaction and success. You will need to collaborate with all student facing teams and the IT department in tandem. As the Assistant Director, Student Experience & Operations, you will provide strategic leadership for the student lifecycle, student operations, process improvement, and technology enablement across the institution. You will need to be expert in CRM and SIS processes and systems. Compensation ACE is committed to paying a competitive wage while staying true to our mission of maintaining high quality, affordable programs for our students. The starting salary range for this position is $90,000 plus all full-time employees are eligible for an annual bonus. Offers vary depending on education, prior experience, and expertise being applied to the role. What We Look for in the Ideal Candidate • Demonstrates self-reliance by meeting and exceeding organizational objectives. • Demonstrates positive attitude, motivation, concern for students, teamwork, and excellent time management skills. • Follows established processes while identifying opportunities for innovation and improvement. • Consistently produces a high volume of quality work. • Adapts effectively to changing priorities and tight deadlines. • Proven ability to work independently and collaboratively across departments. • Supports and embraces the College's Impact mission. • Possesses exceptional communication, organization, and stakeholder management skills. • Demonstrates creativity and efficiency in solving complex business and operational challenges. • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with high attention to detail. • Builds and maintains student satisfaction throughout the lifecycle. • Recognizes, anticipates, and responds to student needs. • Successfully leads teams through change, process improvement, and technology adoption. • Develops strong partnerships and influences decision-making at all organizational levels. Day to Day Responsibilities In this role, you will provide strategic and operational leadership across the student lifecycle. Your responsibilities include: • Serve as the institutional subject matter expert on all aspects of the student lifecycle. • Lead the strategy, design, implementation, and continuous improvement of the end-to-end student experience. • Direct student operations initiatives and establish operational standards that support student success. • Partner with executive leadership, business leaders, Product Owners, and IT teams to define and prioritize strategic enhancements. • Lead cross-functional initiatives that improve operational effectiveness, scalability, system functionality, and student satisfaction. • Ensure all system changes, business processes, and operational workflows align with defined student lifecycle objectives using agile methodologies. • Develop and implement policies, processes, procedures, and technology solutions that streamline the student experience. • Promote the effective utilization of technology to support staff productivity and student success. • Partner with technology teams to implement and support enterprise solutions and process enhancements. • Monitor performance metrics, operational effectiveness, and student experience outcomes, using data-driven insights to drive continuous improvement. • Provide leadership and oversight for operational teams while fostering employee engagement, accountability, and professional development. • Lead organizational change management efforts associated with process, technology, and operational improvements. • Act as a champion for innovation, collaboration, and student-centered decision-making across the institution. • Establish priorities, manage multiple initiatives, and ensure timely delivery of strategic and operational objectives. • Serve as a role model in managing deadlines, deliverables, and cross-departmental collaboration. Qualifications and Education Requirements • Master's degree required, preferably in Higher Education, Business Administration, Organizational Leadership, Information Systems, Operations Management, or a related field. • Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. • 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in higher education supporting the student lifecycle through operational, technology, process improvement, or student services functions. • 5+ years of experience leading teams and managing people leaders. • Significant experience with Microsoft CRM, Anthology, Canvas, or similar enterprise platforms. • Proven experience leading enterprise-wide operational and technology transformation initiatives. • Strong project and program management expertise, including agile methodologies and technology implementation frameworks. • Experience designing and optimizing business processes that support student success and organizational scalability. • Demonstrated ability to influence and collaborate with executive leaders and cross-functional stakeholders. • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and facilitation skills. • Ability to manage multiple strategic initiatives simultaneously in a remote environment. • Strong analytical skills with experience using operational and student data to drive decisions. Our Commitment to Employees Just as we strive to empower our students for success, we also aim to enrich the lives of our employees. For 6 consecutive years, ACE was recognized as one of Indiana’s Best Places to Work, winning the #1 spot for medium-sized companies in 2020. In addition, ACE has earned national recognition, being named a USA Top Workplace in 2022, 2023 and 2024. We believe in fostering a sense of belonging and wellness so that every member of our ACE family feels empowered, valued, and ready to reach their full potential. role: Assistant General Manager Apprentice - K12 Food Service - NANA Shareholder opportunity
description: Job Description The NMS Shareholder Apprentice Program is designed to provide motivated Shareholder candidates the unique opportunity to receive on-the-job training for a period of 24 months, and upon successful completion of the program be prepared to step into regular full-time employment as a fully qualified assistant general manager. The Assistant General Manager of Food Service Apprentice will assist the General Manager in overseeing the food service operations in a K-12 setting within the Northwest Arctic Borough School District (NWABSD), which serves approximately 1850 students across 11 remote village schools in northwest Alaska. This role includes managing food production and quality, ordering for various locations, overseeing training for food service staff, and following NSLP guidelines while bringing a fresh approach to all kitchens. Operations include meal production for students’ distribution throughout the district and managing the logistics of the distribution. The apprentice will learn how to perform all of the essential duties of the Assistant General Manager, listed below, and any other duties as assigned. Responsibilities Under the supervision of the General Manager, the Apprentice will attain required levels of competence in the following areas. Contract Management Be knowledgeable of the terms and conditions, deliverables, and services of the managed contract. Understand the scope of work for delivery and manage accordingly. Assist in client reporting as outlined in the contract Cultivate positive relationships with contract representatives Understand client expectations, and participate in annual expectation meetings Culinary Program Management Food Production Effectively use food preparation principles, production records, kitchen equipment and food crediting to prepare foods from standardized recipes, including those from special diets. Effectively implement all food safety program guidelines and procedures, as well as adhere to all health department regulations to ensure optimal food safety. Accurately prepare and ensure the production of daily production records. Effectively and efficiently plan and prepare standardized recipes, cycle menus, and melas, including the use of USDA Foods, to meet all Federal school nutrition program requirements, including the proper meal components. Food Programs Demonstrate functional knowledge of and compliance with the requirements of various retail, marketing and special programs in place. Understand and apply the Dietary Guidelines for Americans, USDA’s food guidance system concepts and general nutrition principles, and be able to use resources to prepare and integrate age/grade appropriate nutrition education curriculum with the school nutrition program. Food Service Correctly and efficiently serve food portions to meet all USDA school meal pattern requirements and encourage healthy food selections including those for special diets. Efficiently operate and use a POS system, ensuring correct application of reimbursable meal components, Offer vs Serve and confidential student eligibility identification in a financially responsible manner. Understand and apply basic principles of customer service, promoting a welcoming and professional atmosphere. People Management Training Plan, schedule and conduct required program training courses as directed Review and ensure the minimum hours of required training has been completed within the required window for new hires. Perform all recordkeeping in the LMS to keep training records accurate and up to date Maintain a minimum of 90% compliance in managed unit, communicating with the GM and direct reports on training status. Ensure direct reports understand the work procedures for their tasks Hiring Work closely with the GM and recruiting team, reviewing job descriptions, screening and interviewing candidates and participating in final hiring decisions, using the HR iCIMS dashboard. Communicate closely with selected candidates to facilitate a smooth onboarding process, including relaying information on scheduling, issuing uniforms and other tasks as necessary. Ensure new hires are given an orientation and site-specific EAP training for their school. Performance Management Clearly communicate all performance expectations and evaluative/measurements of success to the employees. Coach underperforming employees, to identify the source of underperformance and create a plan to equip them for success. Engage in NMS’ progressive disciplinary process as needed for previously coached and consistently underperforming employees, or as warranted by violations of company policy. Participate in annual reviews of performance, giving constructive feedback to the employee Participate in annual compensation reviews, as outlined in the contract. Facilitate career development conversations, identifying high potential employees Staffing Ensure adequate staffing levels and shift coverage, creating staffing schedules and communicating assignments. Manage call-outs and fill in as needed Manage payroll functions, reviewing and approving time cards accurately and timely Work Environment Ensure work environment adheres to all safety standards Report all safety incidents through the SMS in a timely and through manner Cultivate a positive work environment through consistent application of NMS’ core values Foster an open environment, soliciting employee feedback Financial Management Inventory & Procurement Management Ensure proper inventory management including correct delivery and storage of inventory, and that which has been placed on hold or recalled, as well as ensuring FIFO procedures and reporting are completed. Understand and oversee warehouse and logistics/transportation operations. Effectively and efficiently implement purchasing procedures and practices in order to appropriately and best utilize supplies and USDA Foods to meet menu requirements and comply with all federal, state and local regulations. Budget Management Participate in the management food costs and track cost per plate and food waste Understand impacts of staffing on budget performance and effectively manage staffing costs, including overtime management. Participate in the forecasting and building of the annual budgets for managed contracts Manage scope creep by ensuring we are billing for all delivered/contracted services and not delivering any out of scope work without a change order to the contract. Ensure all financial reporting is completed and reports are reviewed and appropriate action taken (DSO, Billing, Payroll) Participate in period reviews Qualifications Must be a shareholder of NANA Regional Corporation, Inc. High school diploma or GED equivalent. A valid Driver’s License and an acceptable driving record for the past three (3) years to be eligible under NMS’ vehicle insurance policy. One (1) year experience in a commercial kitchen preferred. Computer skills and proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite preferred. Working Conditions and Physical Requirements Weather: Mainly Indoors: environmentally controlled; requires most or all work to be done inside May occasionally need to work outdoors to move product, sometimes in inclement weather. Noise level: Quiet Description of environment: Standard office environment Physical requirements: Employee is required to lift and/or move up to 50 lbs. Frequently required to sit, stand, walk, use hands/fingers to handle or feel, climb, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, talk/hear, see, taste/smell, and carry weight/lift. Travel: Employee may travel up to 25% to various locations within the U.S. and/or remote locations and may be required to use alternative modes of transportation, including but not limited to snow machines, boats, small airplanes and ATVs. Travel is coordinated by NMS. Skills & Abilities Culinary skills, menu development and high volume food production skills. Time management, critical thinking, interpersonal skills, communication skills, planning and organizational skills including the ability to work independently, prioritize activities, meet commitments, and proactively manage time and a heavy workload. Ability to conduct training session in a one-on-one and group setting. NMS Core Values Safety guides our behavior. Honesty and integrity govern our activities. Commitments made will be fulfilled. All individuals are treated with dignity and respect. The environment will be protected and sustained.

At Rhoda AI, we’re building the next generation of generalist intelligent robots. We own the full robotics stack from high-performance hardware and robot systems to the infrastructure and state-of-the-art foundation world models that control our robots. Our robots are designed to be generalists capable of operating in complex, real-world environments and handling long-tail edge cases, made possible by our cutting edge research and end-to-end system design. We've raised over $450M and are investing aggressively in model research, infrastructure, hardware development, and manufacturing scale-up to make generalist robotics a reality. ## About the Role As a Software Engineer Intern working on Rhoda Platform, you'll work on the software foundation that keeps our robots running. You'll own real projects on the software platform stack: ranging from on-robot software, networking and communication infrastructure, data collection pipelines, telemetry, teleoperation, inference infra, developer tooling etc., and see your impact run on physical robots by the end of your internship. You'll sit with the engineers who build our robots and ship code that the team depends on every day. ## What You'll Do - Contribute to the networking and communication infrastructure connecting onboard robot systems to each other, to the cloud, and to teleoperation and monitoring systems - Help build data collection pipelines that capture sensor, telemetry, and behavioral data from the robot and upload it reliably to cloud storage for model training - Work on telemetry and observability systems that give the team real-time visibility into robot health and field performance - Build internal tooling that accelerates robot software development: deployment pipelines, logging, debugging tools, and field testing utilities - Support bring-up and field testing on live hardware, debugging issues across the onboard software stack - Collaborate with ML, perception, and control engineers to keep onboard systems reliable and training data high quality - Automate internal workflows to improve execution efficiency of the Rhoda teams ## What We're Looking For - Currently pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field — or a recent graduate - Solid computer science foundation: data structures, algorithms, operating systems, and networking - Genuine passion for working on robots — coursework, research, personal projects, competition teams, or internships all count - Strong programming skills in C++, Python, Golang, or Rust - Curiosity and comfort working with physical hardware in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment - Ability to debug across layers, from driver-level issues up to application behavior - Open to learn new things and grow from knowing nothing to an expert on arbitrary technical topics ## Nice to Have (But Not Required) - Experience with bringing up & manipulating robots - Familiarity with networking, IPC, or communication protocols (e.g. gRPC, DDS, QUIC, WebSockets) - Exposure to cloud storage and data pipelines (AWS, GCP, S3, GCS) - Experience with perception pipelines, control systems, or learned models running on real-time robot stacks - Prior work on prototype or pre-production hardware ## Why This Role - Your work is the connective tissue of the robot — the networking, data, and tooling infrastructure that determines how fast the team can develop and improve our humanoids in the field - Work across the full onboard stack alongside perception, control, and ML engineers & researchers on a platform pushing the frontier of humanoid robotics - Real ownership on a small team, with your code running on real robots — not a side project on the shelf

At Rhoda AI, we’re building the next generation of generalist intelligent robots. We own the full robotics stack from high-performance hardware and robot systems to the infrastructure and state-of-the-art foundation world models that control our robots. Our robots are designed to be generalists capable of operating in complex, real-world environments and handling long-tail edge cases, made possible by our cutting edge research and end-to-end system design. We've raised over $450M and are investing aggressively in model research, infrastructure, hardware development, and manufacturing scale-up to make generalist robotics a reality. ## **The Role** Our foundation world models have to run fast enough to control robots in the real world, and efficiently enough to support large-scale research. As an Inference Infrastructure Engineer Intern, you'll work with our infra and research engineers to make model inference faster and more efficient across the stack, from data pipelines down to GPU kernels. You'll own a scoped, high-impact project end to end, ship it into our production or research workflow, and present your results to the team. ## **What You'll Do** - Profile and benchmark inference for large video and world models to find bottlenecks in latency, throughput, and memory. - Apply and evaluate inference optimization techniques like quantization and low-precision inference, step distillation and sampling acceleration for diffusion-style models, attention and caching optimizations across frames, model compilation, and graph-level optimizations. - Make data movement and processing more efficient: video decoding and preprocessing, input pipelines, host–device transfer, caching, and storage/IO paths that feed inference and training. - Write and tune GPU kernels (CUDA, Triton, or similar) for performance-critical operators, and integrate them into our inference stack. - Build tooling and benchmarks that let the team track performance regressions and improvements reliably. - Work with researchers to turn promising ideas into production-quality infrastructure. ## **What We're Looking For** You don't need all of these. Strong depth in **any one** of the areas below is enough to apply: - **ML inference optimization:** hands-on experience making deep learning models run faster or cheaper, e.g. quantization (INT8/FP8), pruning/distillation, operator fusion, mixed precision, or compilers and runtimes such as `torch.compile`, TensorRT, ONNX Runtime, or TVM. - **Data efficiency optimization:** experience speeding up data loading and preprocessing pipelines (especially video or other high-bandwidth sensor data), cutting IO and memory overhead, or improving data/compute utilization in ML systems. - **GPU kernel optimization:** experience writing or tuning GPU kernels in CUDA, Triton, CUTLASS, or similar; familiarity with the GPU memory hierarchy, occupancy, and profiling tools (Nsight Systems/Compute, PyTorch profiler). ### **Basic Qualifications** - Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or a related field. - Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++. - Solid understanding of deep learning fundamentals and at least one framework (PyTorch preferred). - Comfortable reading performance data and reasoning about trade-offs between latency, throughput, memory, and accuracy. ### **Nice to Have** - **Experience with video model inference is a huge plus**, e.g. optimizing video generation, video diffusion, or world models, or real-time video understanding pipelines. - Research experience in systems or ML, e.g. publications or substantial research projects (MLSys, OSDI/SOSP, CVPR/ICCV, NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR, or similar). - Experience with real-time or latency-critical inference, e.g. on robots or edge/embedded accelerators. - Experience with multi-GPU inference (tensor/sequence/pipeline parallelism). - Contributions to open-source ML systems projects. ## **What You'll Get** - A real project with measurable impact on robots operating in the real world. - Mentorship from experienced infra and research engineers. - Access to modern GPU compute for experiments.

Overview/Job Summary The DSC Staff Auditor – Corporate position performs audits of processes and controls at dealerships and corporate locations in accordance with GAAP, laws, regulations, and company policies. The position assists the DSC – Manager Corporate Audit and other audit team members in conducting audits and SOX testing, and assists the External Auditors as they conduct the external audit. Duties/Responsibilities • Documents and evaluates the design and effectiveness of Key SOX Controls by conducting Interim, roll-forward, and year-end update Corporate, Dealership Support Services (DSS), and Dealership SOX testing in accordance with Internal Audit and External Auditor standards. • Performs audits in accordance with internal audit standards, corporate policies and procedures, GAAP, laws, and other regulatory requirements. • Completes Audit Workpapers in accordance with Internal Audit Department Standards, including efficiently and effectively summarizing the results of audit step procedures. • Assists with the development and publication of Internal Audit Department Reporting. • Becomes knowledgeable of Asbury Corporate functions and the automotive Industry. • Assists the DSC Manager – Corporate Audit with executing EY Corporate Walkthroughs and documentation. • Executes Corporate Audit Program audit steps across all Corporate functional areas as assigned by the DSC Manager – Corporate Audit. • Develops effective relationships with Asbury Executive Management, Department Heads and team members across all Asbury organizations and communicates effectively with them. • Performs other related duties to benefit the mission/vision of the organization Overview/Job Summary The Staff Accountant – Fixed Assets will play an important role as part of the Corporate Accounting Team and assists in various aspects of Fixed Assets Accounting. The position provides the opportunity to interact with Senior and Executive Management on a regular basis. Duties/Responsibilities • Asset Tracking and Management: ◦ Maintains the fixed asset register, ensuring all acquisitions, transfers, and disposals are accurately recorded. ◦ Monitors asset additions and disposals to ensure compliance with company policies and accounting standards. • Depreciation and Amortization: ◦ Calculates and records depreciation and amortization schedules in alignment with applicable accounting standards. ◦ Analyzes the impact of depreciation and amortization on financial statements. ◦ Updates asset valuations and useful life estimates as needed. • Financial Reporting: ◦ Prepares and reconciles fixed asset schedules for financial reporting purposes. ◦ Assists with month-end and year-end close processes, ensuring accuracy in fixed asset reporting. ◦ Collaborates with auditors during financial audits, providing required documentation and explanations. • Policy Development and Compliance: ◦ Develops and maintains fixed asset management policies and procedures. ◦ Ensures compliance with GAAP ◦ Stays informed of changes in accounting standards that impact fixed assets. • Disposal and Retirement of Assets: ◦ Manages the disposal or retirement of fixed assets, ensuring proper documentation and financial accounting. ◦ Analyzes gain or loss on asset disposals and reflect in financial statements. • Performs other related duties to benefit the mission/vision of the organization Overview/Job Summary The Staff Accountant Financial Reporting will play an important role as part of the Financial Reporting Team and assists in various aspects of SEC reporting, technical accounting, and Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX). The candidate in this role will play a key role in our quarterly external reporting cycle including, but not limited to, financial statement analysis, preparation of financial statements and footnotes, annual intangible asset impairment tests and other ad-hoc financial reporting requests. The position provides the opportunity to interact with Senior and Executive Management on a regular basis. Duties/Responsibilities • Assists in the preparation of quarterly and annual SEC filings and related earnings releases, including preparation and review of supporting work papers. • Assists in the preparation of all transaction-related SEC reporting requirements (8-K, debt offerings, equity offerings, etc.). • Assists in researching and documenting the Company’s position on technical accounting matters. • Assists with the accounting for acquisitions and divestitures. • Assists in the support of Asbury’s company-wide SOX program and the coordination with Internal Audit and our external auditors throughout the different phases of the annual reporting cycle. • Supports quarterly reviews and the annual audit by our external audit firm. • Assists the Manager of Financial Reporting with equity, stock compensation, lease accounting, and interest rate swaps and other accounting matters. • Assists with the annual impairment testing of the Company’s goodwill and franchise rights intangible assets. • Prepares work papers supporting key monthly close processes and analyses. • Performs other related duties to benefit the mission/vision of the organization Overview/Job Summary The Staff Analyst – Corporate Treasury and Financial Planning & Analysis will play an important role as part of the Corporate Treasury and Financial Planning & Analysis Team and will assist with various functions within those organizations such as, analyzing daily and forward-looking cash balances, analyzing merchant banking fee activities, and analyzing various performance trends. The position provides the opportunity to interact with Senior Management on a regular basis. Duties/Responsibilities • Leads analysis of daily and forward-looking cash balances and liquidity calculations. • Analyzes monthly changes in merchant banking fee activities highlighting key drivers in expenses versus budget. • Summarizes quarterly peer performance and compare versus prior quarter/year. • Analyzes monthly performance trends of the business, providing input into the monthly Asbury Financial Forecast process. • Participates in ad hoc analysis of store level operational performance. • Performs other related duties to benefit the mission/vision of the organization Overview/Job Summary The Dealership Support Services (DSS) Staff Accountant will be a part of the DSS General Accounting Team which represents the consolidated General Accounting Department for the Asbury dealerships. The role of the team will be to ensure all general accounting transactions are processed timely, reconciliations and daily postings remain within Sarbanes Oxley (SOX) requirements, to maintain a high level of customer service with Asbury’s dealerships and customers, and to continue to work on efficiency gains utilizing current technology advancements. The position provides the opportunity to interact with Senior Dealership Operational Management on a regular basis. Duties/Responsibilities • Parts Department: Sales, Inventories, Customer Management, Parts Pad, Returns, Special Orders, Price Codes. • Service Department: Sales, Warranty, Technician Accounting Concepts, Repair Order Costing and Taxation, and WIP. • Finance Department: Deal Submission, Deal Approval, Deal Compliance, Finance Reserves, and Electronic Contracting. • Compliance Team: Month-End Review of Policies and Procedures and SOX Compliance. • Controller Area: Month-End Checklists, Forecasting, Budgeting, Expense Control, Pay Calculations, Journal Usage, Title Process, Bonus Programs, and Asset Management. • General Manager Area: Marketing Process, Financial Statement Review, Customer Satisfaction, Market Share Reviews, Lot Management, and Inventory Management. • Performs other related duties to benefit the mission/vision of the organization Overview/Job Summary The Dealership Staff Accountant will participate in the Asbury Controller Academy, which will include participation in and exposure to a number of dealership areas, functions, operations, and departments. The position provides the opportunity to interact with Senior Operational Management on a regular basis. role: Associate Delivery Consultant Intern, AWS Professional Services
description: NOTE: Amazon internships are full-time (40 hours/week) for 12 consecutive weeks, starting May/June 2027. Applicants should have at a minimum one quarter/semester remaining after their internship concludes. This internship role is required to be onsite 5 days a week in Arlington, VA or New York, NY. Do you want to experiment with innovative technologies, including Cloud Computing, Machine Learning, and GenAI? Are you passionate about educating, training, designing, and building cloud computing solutions to help customers solve their most challenging problems? Amazon Web Services (AWS), a leader in Cloud Computing, is seeking interns to join our AWS Professional Services Internship program. This is a unique opportunity to play a key role in a fast-growing business and to deliver value to AWS customers of all sizes from startups to global brands. The skills and experiences you gain will be highly sought after throughout the industry and give you the opportunity for the career of a lifetime. The AWS Professional Services (ProServe) organization is a global team of experts that helps AWS customers realize their desired business outcomes when using the AWS Cloud. We deliver focused guidance through our global specialty practices, which cover a variety of solutions, technologies, and industries. In addition to working alongside our customers, we share our experience through technical artifacts and proof of concept demos. As an Associate Delivery Consultant Intern, you will gain hands-on experience in cloud computing, develop business acumen, and learn about Amazon’s peculiar culture. You will work on projects, have the opportunity to obtain the AWS certifications, and attend professional development events. This internship can lead to a full-time role in Arlington, VA, or New York City, NY, that has up to 75% travel associated. While many of our customers engage ProServe virtually, there is always the potential that a customer might choose to include travel in their contract. Delivery Consultants in AWS ProServe are aligned by technical specialty. For this internship, we are looking for candidates that are interested in and fit the AIML specialty. The program offers the opportunity to specialize in an area of interest including: AIML - AIML role supports our services that leverage data and produce business insights, which may include using Machine Learning/Artificial Intelligence/Generative Artificial Intelligence (ML/AI/GenAI). Helping our customers use and integrate Big Data services in what is arguably our industry’s most exciting space. The portfolio of services covers EMR (Hadoop), DynamoDB (NoSQL), MongoDB, Apache Cassandra, Amazon Q, and Bedrock. Security - supports our services that have a focus on enabling security specialists using AWS Services including Identity Access Management (IAM), GuardDuty, Shield, Key Management Service (KMS), CloudTrail, CloudHSM, Inspector etc. Within AWS, security is job zero, and we believe that solid security practices are the foundation for using the Cloud. We are looking for candidates who are passionate about working with products targeted for security professionals. Modernization - Modernization resources are specialists in designing applications that run natively in the cloud using programming languages such as Python, JavaScript, Typescript, etc. They are experts in building programs that run on any number of platforms including virtualized instances, containers, or server less architecture. They are full stack developers with backend, frontend, and UX skillsets. About the team Upon successful completion of the internship program, selected interns will receive a full-time offer to join the ProServe Associate to Consultant (A2C) Delivery. A2C Delivery develops the next generation of ProServe consultants who use generative and agentic AI to solve customer challenges and drive innovation within ProServe. A2C Delivery focuses on accelerating career development for recent graduates and early career professionals entering technical roles, advancing their skills and helping customers design and build flexible and resilient cloud-based solutions. While in A2C, you will learn key technical and professional skills from top AWS subject matter experts that you can use in your career working with AWS’s customers. Mentorship & Career Growth: Our team is dedicated to supporting new team members in an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship. Projects and tasks are assigned in a way that leverages your strengths and helps you further develop your skillset. Inclusive Team Culture: Here at AWS, we embrace our differences. We are committed to furthering our culture of inclusion. We have ten employee-led affinity groups, reaching 40,000 employees in over 190 chapters globally. We have innovative benefit offerings, and host annual and ongoing learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences. Work/Life Harmony: Our team puts a high value on work-life harmony. It isn’t about how many hours you spend at home or at work; it’s about the flow you establish that brings energy to both parts of your life. We believe striking the right balance between your personal and professional life is critical to life-long happiness and fulfillment. We offer flexibility and encourage you to find your own balance between your work and personal lives.

role: Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) - BCBA Trainee / Student Analyst
description: **Alpaca Health** Work Location: In Person **Student Analyst (BCBA Trainee)** If you’re in school to become a BCBA, this is a role that challenges you, changes lives, and builds a real career. What matters most is that you love working with kids, you’re dependable, and you’re ready to show up. Alpaca Health is a multi-state network of independent ABA therapists, working in homes, schools, and daycares. You’ll work alongside a dedicated BCBA who mentors you from day one, not a manager, not a corporate supervisor. **The job** You’ll work one-on-one with kids with autism in their homes, classrooms, and communities. Every day is different. You’ll follow a personalized plan from your BCBA, implement behavior strategies, collect data, and build the consistent relationships that help kids grow. Your BCBA is closely involved and reachable, so there’s no guessing and no flying solo. **What’s in it for you:** - $20–$30/hour, based on experience and location - Direct mentorship from a dedicated BCBA, not managers or a corporate chain of command - Full-time or part-time (some flexibility across mornings, afternoons, and evenings is needed to meet client needs; not sure if a schedule fits? Just ask, we have many) - Career growth support, including a path toward BCBA certification **You’re a good fit if you:** - Are currently in school to become a BCBA - Are currently a grad student in a psychology or social work program - Genuinely enjoy working with children, especially kids who need extra patience and creativity - Have reliable availability across mornings, afternoons, or evenings, since our clients count on consistency - Come from education, childcare, psychology, social work, or any role where you showed up for kids - Have reliable transportation to reach client homes and schools - Can keep up physically, getting on the floor, moving around, staying active (able to lift ~50 lbs) - Are at least 18, have a high school diploma or equivalent, and can pass a background check **Why Alpaca Health** We’re not a big clinic chain. We’re a network of independent therapists who chose this work because they believe in it, and we match every team member with a BCBA who mentors, not manages. We match families with providers who have availability now, and we work where families actually are. If you want a career where you see the results of your work every single day, this is it. **Ready? Apply now.** Not sure if you qualify? Apply anyway and tell us about yourself. We’d rather talk to one more curious person than miss someone great.

The [Pacific Legal Foundation](https://pacificlegal.org/) identifies and litigates important legal issues to set landmark precedents that benefit Americans nationwide. Using strategic and principled litigation, communications, and research, PLF battles for freedom in the nation’s capitols, courts, and the court of public opinion. As a national nonprofit law firm, PLF has brick-and-mortar offices in Sacramento, California; Arlington, Virginia; and Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, although approximately half of the staff work from home offices across the country. **Interns work remotely by default, but they can request to work physically in any of PLF’s offices. Interns are expected to work part time (24 hours per week).** **You:** An inquisitive, creative, and self-motivated college junior, senior, graduate student, or recent graduate who understands the principles of liberty and wants to advance them. You have strong written and oral communication skills, enjoy external engagement, and are eager to solve problems. **Them:** State and federal governments and their agencies that overstep their constitutional authority, impose burdensome regulations, and exercise powers that undermine individual liberty and economic opportunity. These actions affect Americans and industries across the country, threatening freedom, innovation, and constitutional limits on government power. **Us:** We fight back. Pacific Legal Foundation is the nation’s first and most successful public interest law firm dedicated to vindicating individual liberty. PLF has an unmatched record in the U.S. Supreme Court, with 18 victories and nearly 200 active cases across the nation. The Coalitions team extends this work by connecting PLF’s legal and policy expertise with external partners to advance our goals. There are two verticals of the Coalitions team: Non-Profit Partnerships (NPP) and Private Sector Partnerships (PSP). Non-Profit Partnerships work with other think tanks, foundations, and non-profits to advance our legal and policy priorities and well as manage a grant program. Private Sector Partnerships works primarily with corporations and businesses, trade associations, and industry leaders. This role would work with both verticals but would primarily work with the PSP team. The private sector relationships we build and maintain give us direct insight into the legal and regulatory challenges facing different industries and help us identify opportunities for PLF to make a difference. Through strategic partnerships, we expand the reach of PLF’s work, develop referral pipelines for potential clients and cases, and identify shared priorities to strategically build policy coalitions. Our goal is to become a preferred legal and policy partner to corporations, trade associations, and their members when government overreach threatens their livelihoods. role: KIP Spring 2027 - Legislative Intern - Citizens Against Government Waste
description: **[The Koch Internship Program](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/koch-internship-program/) (KIP)** is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Early-career professionals including undergraduate/graduate/law students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the [admissions process](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/application-process/) early! [Citizens Against Government Waste](https://www.cagw.org/) (CAGW) offers a wide variety of opportunities to college students across the country. Unpaid research, communications, and government affairs internships are available on a year-round basis and can vary in length from a semester to a few weeks in duration. Interns can choose to work part-time or full-time, as hours of work are extremely flexible. Our daily work with Capitol Hill and the White House, as well as government agencies and other nonprofit organizations, provides a close and invaluable look at how Washington works. Many projects involve working closely with staff members, while others require a great deal of independence. Interns are considered important members of our staff and actively participate in staff meetings and other events. While interns will also be required to perform clerical duties from time to time, much of the work will be substantive. **Legislative Internship** Assist CAGW’s policy staff with various aspects of the legislative process, including monitoring hearings; summarizing essential testimony and votes taken during committee meetings; tracking legislation, regulations, and political activities concerning government waste issues; and researching and developing legislative summaries, and attending various coalition meetings with other organizations. Interns may spend a majority of their time supporting the work above, but may also support other staff members as needed. This role is open to remote work, but priority is given to those available for in person work at our Washington, D.C office.

role: KIP Spring 2027 - Federal Policy Intern - Pacific Legal Foundation
description: **[The Koch Internship Program](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/koch-internship-program/) (KIP)** is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Early-career professionals including undergraduate/graduate/law students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the [admissions process](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/application-process/) early! We fight back. [Pacific Legal Foundation](https://pacificlegal.org/) (PLF) is the nation’s first and most successful public interest law firm dedicated to vindicating individual liberty. PLF has an unmatched record in the US Supreme Court, with 18 victories out of 21 cases heard by the Court. We focus on four core areas: Environment & Natural Resources, Equality & Opportunity, Property Rights, and Separation of Powers. Although our unofficial slogan is “Suing the government since 1973” we do a lot more than that. PLF's Federal Legal Policy team helps develop and execute strategies to secure federal legislative and executive reforms to expand individual liberty and reform the unconstitutional regulatory agencies. This is where you come in. You’re an inquisitive, creative, and self-motivated college junior, senior, grad or law student, or recent graduate who knows the principles of liberty and seeks to advance them. You have strong written and oral communication skills and enjoy problem solving. This internship provides an opportunity for a wide variety of experiences, including: - Reading and summarizing important legislation and executive and agency action. - Developing briefing materials for use in meetings with executive and legislative branch officials. - Attending coalition events, Hill meetings, and other related advocacy efforts. - Writing blog posts and opinion pieces relating to PLF core federal work. This position requires **in-person** presence in PLF’s Arlington (Clarendon) office. ### How to Apply **If you think you might be a good fit, submit in ONE PDF:** - A résumé that includes relevant experience in the liberty movement and professional skills. - A cover letter explaining why PLF is the place for you, why you want to fight for liberty, and what distinguishes you from typical applicants. Applicants selected for an interview may be asked to provide: - A writing sample. - A semester schedule (if taking classes during the internship period).

You will collaborate directly with senior engineers and architects, receiving mentorship and design reviews, and gaining exposure to modern GenAI patterns, including agent orchestration, tool-calling, retrieval, and evaluation, within an enterprise and fast-paced fintech environment. Launch your career developing real, impactful AI solutions in the lightning-fast world of fintech! **Program Details**Our summer program will be 10-12 weeks from May - August 2027 with the expectation of being in the office 3-4 days per week, as determined by the sponsor. Design, prototype, and develop agentic AI workflows that automate or augment business or engineering tasks (for example, analysis, triage, documentation, and knowledge synthesis) - Build internal tools or proof-of-concept systems that combine LLMs, APIs, and automation frameworks into end-to-end agentic solutions - Experiment with different agent architectures (single-agent vs. multi-agent, planner/executor patterns, human-in-the-loop workflows) and document tradeoffs - Apply best practices when building AI-driven automation - Evaluate agent behavior for reliability, correctness, and failure modes, and propose improvements - Clearly document designs, experiments, and lessons learned so work can be reused or extended by the team - Demo your work directly to customers and the leadership team ### **What You’ll Need** - Currently pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related technical field - Experience programming in Python (for automation, prototyping, and scripting) and SQL - Familiarity with APIs, JSON, and basic service integration - Foundational understanding of large language models and how they are used in applications (prompting, tool use, retrieval, etc.) - Strong curiosity and willingness to explore new, rapidly evolving technologies - A growth mindset: you ask questions and enjoy experimenting and iterating - Systems thinking: able to reason about workflows, edge cases, and unintended consequences - Clear written and verbal communication, especially when explaining technical ideas to non-engineers - Ownership mindset: you take responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks - Ability to accept feedback and iterate quickly Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. DriveWealth is unable to sponsor an employment Visa at this time. **Working at DriveWealth** We do our best work when we're in the same room. To maintain the speed our partners expect, our New York, Chicago, and Lithuania teams work in office on a hybrid schedule. We've found that being physically side-by-side is the only way to solve complex problems in real-time and stay truly accountable to the products we ship. When you're here, you're working directly with the people making the decisions. To support that work, we provide competitive compensation, equity, and a 401(k) match. We also offer Medical insurance, Dental insurance, Vision insurance, Disability insurance, and Paid Parental Leave, along with a wellness reimbursement, a company-provided phone, and a personal development allowance. Finally, we value the time you spend away from the office with generous Paid Time Off (PTO) and observed holidays. **Work Authorization** Applicants must possess the legal right to work in the country where the position is located at the time of application. DriveWealth requires all employees to provide original documentation verifying their work authorization on or before their first day of employment. For US-based roles: Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without the need for current or future visa sponsorship. DriveWealth does not provide visa sponsorship or support for employment authorization, including transfers, at this time. Offers of employment are strictly contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the Company. **How We Think About AI** We leverage AI to work smarter and move faster. We seek AI-curious talent who are proactive about using emerging tools to increase signal quality, reduce friction, and improve outcomes to deliver products faster, provide better service to our partners, and to streamline processes. Your ability to leverage our internal tools and technology to drive results is as important to us as your core domain expertise. **Compensation** Pay is generally based on the level, complexity, responsibility, location, and job duties/requirements of the specific position. We then source candidates with the requisite skills, expertise, education, training, and experience. If you are selected for an interview, please feel welcome to speak to a recruiter about our compensation philosophy and other available benefits. This role is eligible for base, bonus, equity, 401(k) match, and heavily subsidized benefits and perks. **Equal Employment Opportunity** To build technology and products that are used and loved by people and solve real-world problems, we need to build a team with many different perspectives and experiences. description: **Build your civil engineering career in site design.** You'll work on real land development projects, design real sites, and grow through hands-on experience, professional development, and mentorship from engineers who want to see you succeed. **About the Role** Bohler’s Orlando, FL office is seeking an Entry Level Civil Engineer (Land Development) who is eager to learn, grow, and make a positive impact. In this role, you will work closely with engineers, designers, and project managers to bring exciting land development projects to life, including site planning, grading, utilities, and stormwater management. Complete visibility and exposure to all aspects of land development projects - The chance to immerse yourself in the design process while working side-by-side with talented teammates - Open and transparent communication with senior leadership and local office management - Team-building activities, office events, and a collaborative, high-energy environment **What You’ll Bring** - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Civil Engineering or a related field - 0–1+ years of residential, commercial, or industrial site design and permitting experience - Familiarity with AutoCAD Civil 3D (preferred; training provided if not yet proficient) - Strong communication skills and a collaborative approach to teamwork - Motivation to take initiative and contribute to shared goals - EIT certification is helpful but not required **Get hands-on experience contributing to real projects, and see how your work helps shape communities and your career.** #LI-Onsite

description: **FANDUEL SUMMER LEAGUE** About our summer program - 10-week program: Early June – Mid August - Hybrid work environment - Meaningful opportunity to contribute to the work of our teams - Cohort experience with social events & professional development opportunities - Possibility to be considered for a full-time opportunity or return internship **THE POSITION** Sports Traders at FanDuel are the people behind the odds that our customers bet on. We utilize stats, in-house models, industry news and our knowledge to help formulate what we believe are the most accurate odds. Then we manage those odds throughout their lifecycle. This includes moving prices when breaking news hits or using our in-house models to move prices during live games. We don’t expect anyone to walk in the door and know everything at the start, so we take our training seriously and make sure that the successful candidate is well supported. We are looking for people who are passionate about Sport and who like numbers, to put it simply! If you have a high attention to detail, are calm under pressure, are comfortable with numbers and love sport then we can teach you the rest. Being able to work in a team, stay organized, and keep our customers front-of-mind are also valuable skills to have. This role will require an office presence each day, with the very occasional non-operational shift from home if you choose. Our office is in Jersey City (NJ) and is located across from the Newport PATH station and right across from Manhattan. The office includes quiet areas you can utilize; however, your primary workstation will be in the busy trading area, equipped with multiple screens and potentially your own TV. This area experiences constant noise and media activity, typical of a dynamic trading floor. The role will also require some weekend and out of hours work, as sport doesn’t stop on the weekend! **THE GAME PLAN**Everyone on our team has a part to play **Overview:** - Due to the nature of the sporting calendar, you will predominantly be focused on MLB and/or WNBA during this internship. - In time, you will be able to compile your own odds on a range of different markets using statistics and trends. For example, helping decide the price for certain players to hit a home run in a baseball game. - You will monitor our prices and learn to make moves where necessary, taking into consideration things like player news, customer behavior, industry prices, etc. - Tools, tech, & systems: Excel, SQL, Tableau **Primary Responsibilities:** - You will learn how to use our sports models to fluctuate our odds throughout the game depending on what is happening in that game at the time. This will be a large part of your training, essentially learning how to trade a live game of MLB. - Collaborate with various teams around the business to manage things like our liabilities, our onsite display and ensuring we remain compliant across our different jurisdictions. - Compare competitor offerings to ensure we have the best offering in the market for our customers. - Opportunity to contribute to other projects that may arise during your time. **THE STATS**What we're looking for in our next teammate **Required Qualifications:** - Must be a current sophomore or junior in a degree program with a numerate major, with at least one academic year remaining after the internship (summer 2027) - Must have U.S. Work Authorization and does not require employer sponsorship - Must be within commutable distance of or willing to relocate to Jersey City office - Must be willing to be in office 5 times per week - Passion for sports – you will likely need to be able to watch sport every day throughout the internship. Understanding of the rules of the MLB and or/WNBA will be required - Able to work outside normal business hours during weekdays, also able to work weekends as needed (you would only work 5 days per week maximum) - Able to acquire “Division of Gaming Enforcement” license in New Jersey – meaning you must be 18 years of age. **Skills/Experience Requirements:** - You are at least an intermediate user of Microsoft Excel - Ability to do basic mental math problems under pressure - In-depth knowledge of at least 1 US sport within the NBA, NFL, NHL, NCAAF, or NCAAB - Good understanding of the rules, play, and terminology associated with the sport of baseball, specifically in MLB or Basketball, specifically WNBA. - Strong written, verbal communication and research skills **Other:** - Experience working well in a team-oriented environment - Prior related work or project experience is beneficial - A passion and interest for developing skills related to this line of work Don’t check all the boxes? That’s okay! We encourage you to still apply if you feel like you possess an adjacent skillet and are interested in learning more about this position. **ABOUT FANDUEL** FanDuel Group is the premier mobile gaming company in the United States and Canada. FanDuel Group consists of a portfolio of leading brands across mobile wagering including: America’s #1 Sportsbook, FanDuel Sportsbook; its leading iGaming platform, FanDuel Casino; the industry’s unquestioned leader in horse racing and advance-deposit wagering, FanDuel Racing; and its daily fantasy sports product. In addition, FanDuel Group operates FanDuel TV, its broadly distributed linear cable television network and FanDuel TV+, its leading direct-to-consumer OTT platform. FanDuel Group has a presence across all 50 states, Canada, and Puerto Rico. The company is based in New York with US offices in Los Angeles, Atlanta, and Jersey City, as well as global offices in Canada and Scotland. The company’s affiliates have offices worldwide, including in Ireland, Portugal, Romania, and Australia. FanDuel Group is a subsidiary of Flutter Entertainment, the world's largest sports betting and gaming operator with a portfolio of globally recognized brands and traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: FLUT). **PLAYER BENEFITS** We treat our team right From our many opportunities for professional development to our generous insurance and paid leave policies, we’re committed to making sure our employees get as much out of FanDuel as we ask them to give. Competitive compensation is just the beginning. As part of our team, you can expect: - An exciting and fun environment committed to driving real growth - Opportunities to build really cool products that fans love - Career and professional development resources to help you refine your game plan for owning and driving your career and development - Be well, save well and live well - with FanDuel Total Rewards your benefits are one highlight reel after another FanDuel is an equal opportunities employer and we believe, as one of our principles states, “We are One Team!”. The Language Services Unit at the New York County District Attorney’s Office (DANY) provides interpretation and translation services for the investigation and prosecution of criminal cases. Under close supervision, qualified Spanish interpreter/translator interns will have the opportunity to translate bi-directionally between English and Spanish and to proofread translations for accuracy. Translation materials may include legal documents, statements, and audio recordings. Interns will make use of their verbal skills by interpreting during in-house interviews, for which mature and tactful behavior is required. All interns will also assist with screening Spanish audio recordings, in written or oral form, and in producing accurate transcriptions and translations, among other language related tasks. Responsibilities include but are not limited to: - Ability to interpret/translate both verbal and written communication from English to Spanish and Spanish to English. - Provide interpretations as required by phone/video conferences, community presentations, and in-person interviews. - Prepare transcriptions and translations from recordings. - Verbally screen audio recordings in Spanish. - Prepare written translations of a variety of materials in both language directions, including but not limited to legal documents, personal statements, press releases, general forms/letters, etc. - Proofread translations and provide feedback. - Process requests for Spanish language services and update Unit database. - In a team effort support Unit staff with translation and interpretation assignments as assigned by supervisor. In addition to the Minimum Qualification Requirements, candidates must possess the following: - Applicants must be currently enrolled as a junior or senior in college or in a graduate program or other language related program. Preference will be given to students enrolled in translation/interpretation programs. - Applicants must possess a strong bi-cultural awareness as well as a strong ability to speak, write, and use idiomatic expressions and colloquialisms in both English and Spanish. (Prior knowledge of legal language is not required). How to Apply: - Resume - Cover Letter - Unofficial transcript, including evidence of current enrollment. - Three professional references. - Two sample translations for which source texts are provided at the bottom of this posting. Please add your translations to the bottom of your Cover Letter. - As part of the interview process, interpretation internship candidates will be expected to interpret consecutively in a mock interrogation. Interns will work two days a week, 9:30 am – 4:30 pm. - Applicants must commit to a complete term. Sprinto is an **Autonomous Trust Platform** that centralizes trust requirements across **security frameworks, vendors, and customers.** Sprinto autonomously executes tasks needed to maintain trust across compliance, audits, risk management, vendor risk, privacy, and AI governance, enabling organizations to maintain a strong, reliable trust posture without draining operational bandwidth and resources on repetitive tasks. Backed by top-tier investors such as Accel, Elevation, and Blume Ventures, we’ve **raised** **$31.8M** in funding to fuel our mission. Trusted by over **4,000 organizations across 75 countries**, Sprinto helps organizations stay audit-ready, manage real-time risks, and scale fearlessly. With **300+ native integrations** and AI-driven automation, Sprinto supports **200+ global security standards natively**, including SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, and more. Sprinto's extensible architecture enables organizations to build and support an infinite number of custom integrations and frameworks. **Founded in 2020** by second-time founders Girish Redekar and Raghuveer Kancherla, Sprinto powers compliance for organizations like Whatfix, Encora, Anaconda, Whatnot, Ultrahuman, WeWork, Everstage, AI Foundation, HackerRank, and many more. ### **Life as a Sprinter -** Nobody succeeds at Sprinto by staying in their lane. We are organized around problems, not job titles. Sprinters take ownership beyond their role, solve hard problems, and care deeply about the impact they create. If something can be improved, fixed, or built, we don't wait for permission; we step in. Being remote means we rely less on proximity and more on trust. We write things down, communicate openly, and move quickly because great teams aren't built by sitting together, they're built by pulling in the same direction. We believe progress beats perfection, feedback is a gift, and doing the right thing matters, even when nobody is watching. And while we move with urgency, we never move alone. ### **The Mission -** We are hiring a **Field Sales/GTM Intern** to join our San Francisco-based **GTM** team. This is a hands-on, in-person role designed for someone who wants to learn how **High Velocity B2B SaaS sales** actually works, not from a textbook but from doing it live with a team that is building one of the fastest-growing compliance platforms in the world. You will work directly alongside our marketing & sales team, generating pipeline/leads through outbound prospecting & events. This is a part-time, paid W-2 position. Duration is 12 to 24 weeks. Hours are 20 per week, worked primarily on-site in San Francisco. ### Where You'll Leave Your Mark - This is not a shadow and observe role, you will own a prospecting motion from day one and be held to a real number. - You will work entirely focused on outbound pipeline generation. Your role is to book qualified meetings for the Sprinto sales team. The target is 12 to 20 demos per month, which is 3 to 5 per week. That is a number a focused, hungry person can hit when outbound is all they are doing. - You will build prospect lists, write and run multichannel sequences across phone, email, and LinkedIn, and log everything cleanly in our CRM. By the end of the program you will have a real pipeline number next to your name, not a project bullet. ### The Kind of Builder We're Looking For - We are not looking for someone who needs this role to figure out if they want to be in sales. We are looking for someone who has already decided. - The right person is scrappy, takes initiative without waiting to be told, and treats a no as information rather than a stop sign. - They are currently enrolled in university, graduating in 2026 or 2027, and see this as the first real step in a B2B sales career, not just an internship to fill a summer. - Prior sales experience is not required. Prior evidence of figuring things out on your own is. ### Why you should apply to Sprinto - Most internships pay you to watch. This one pays you to win. - Base pay is $20 to $40 per hour. On top of that, you earn variable pay tied to demos booked, hit your number and your total comp reflects it. We do not want to cap what you can earn in a role where your output is this measurable. **Beyond the money:** - You will get a dedicated sales coach and regular call recording reviews so you improve week over week, not just at the end. You will be trained on the same tools our full-time AEs/SDRs use, including our CRM, sequencing platform, and intent data stack, giving you a resume that reads like someone who has already been on the job. You will sit alongside and shadow our field AEs in live customer conversations, so you see what happens to the meetings you book. And you will have direct access to senior sales leadership, not through a program coordinator but because the team is small and the access is real. - This is a Series B company growing fast in a category that every enterprise is now spending on. The SF office puts you in the room with the people making the decisions. That context is hard to get anywhere else at this stage of your career.
