StubHub is on a mission to redefine the live event experience on a global scale. Whether someone is looking to attend their first event or their hundredth, we’re here to delight them all the way from the moment they start looking for a ticket until they step through the gate. The same goes for our sellers. From fans selling a single ticket to the promoters of a worldwide stadium tour, we want StubHub to be the safest, most convenient way to offer a ticket to the millions of fans who browse our platform around the world. As a Junior Technical Support (POS) specialist, you will serve as the technical support layer between frontline teams and Product Operations and Product, supporting broker sellers using point of sale (POS) systems and marketplace integrations. You will investigate issues across the transaction lifecycle, connecting what happens in the seller’s POS system with what appears on marketplaces such as StubHub. This role requires both technical troubleshooting and strong customer service skills. You will communicate directly with sellers, own cases through resolution, and use business judgment to help keep their operations running. **This Full-Time position may require weekend, holiday, daytime, and/or evening hours.** **Schedule options are as follows: Tues - Sat - 9-5:30pm OR Sun - Thu - 9-5:30pm** **This role will begin as in-office 5 days per week for the first 3-6 months and then will shift to in-office 3 days per week to ensure cross-functional collaboration.** **What You'll Do:** - Own a portfolio of support cases from initial investigation through resolution, including cases escalated by frontline teams. Maintain clear next steps, provide timely updates, and confirm that the seller’s issue is resolved. - Investigate POS and marketplace issues involving inventory, listings, pricing, order synchronization, and fulfillment. Trace transactions across connected systems to identify discrepancies and determine where a failure occurred. - Use SQL and Snowflake to investigate transaction data, and Kusto Query Language (KQL) and cloud monitoring tools in Azure and AWS to review logs and connect system activity to reported seller issues. - Troubleshoot APIs and integrations by reviewing requests, responses, JSON payloads, authentication errors, status codes, and synchronization behavior. Distinguish configuration or workflow issues from problems requiring deeper technical investigation. - Assess the business impact of each issue, including affected orders, inventory availability, fulfillment deadlines, and disruption to seller operations. Prioritize cases based on urgency, scope, and customer impact. - Build trusted relationships with broker sellers and internal account teams. Communicate professionally by email, phone, or chat, using clear explanations that match the seller’s technical understanding. - Write accurate, well-structured emails that explain findings, actions taken, required next steps, and follow-up expectations. Manage difficult conversations with empathy, composure, and realistic commitments. - Partner with frontline teams to investigate issues that require technical support. Resolve issues within your scope and coordinate with Product Operations and Product when further investigation or product changes are needed. Provide actionable escalations with relevant identifiers, timestamps, reproduction steps, logs, business impact, and troubleshooting already completed; retain ownership of seller communication. - Explain product features, integration requirements, and marketplace workflows to help sellers use tools effectively and prevent repeat issues. - Maintain complete case records and contribute to troubleshooting guides and knowledge articles. Identify recurring issues and share findings that support product and process improvements. - Additional duties as assigned. **Who You Are:** - An analytical problem solver who investigates systematically, validates assumptions against evidence, and knows when to escalate. - A clear writer and confident communicator who can translate technical findings into practical guidance for business customers. - Customer-focused, with the relationship management skills to build trust, understand seller needs, and follow through on commitments. - Business-minded, with an understanding of how technical failures affect sales, operational workload, fulfillment, and customer confidence. - Organized and accountable, with the ability to manage multiple cases, prioritize competing needs, and maintain accurate documentation in a high-volume environment. - Adaptable and collaborative, with sound judgment, attention to detail, and a willingness to learn evolving products, policies, and technical tools. **What You've Done:** - At least 1 year of experience in technical support, application support, or customer support involving technical troubleshooting. - Demonstrated experience supporting business customers, managing ongoing customer issues, and delivering timely, professional follow-through. - Hands-on experience using Salesforce to manage support cases, document investigations, track follow-up actions, and maintain accurate customer records. - Working knowledge of SQL and Kusto Query Language (KQL), with the ability to write and interpret queries to investigate transaction discrepancies and application errors. - Practical familiarity with Snowflake for data investigation and with Azure and AWS monitoring tools for reviewing application logs and troubleshooting issues. - Understanding of integrations and how data moves between POS systems and marketplaces. - Experience documenting investigations and explaining technical issues and resolutions clearly in written customer communications. **Preferred Experience:** - Experience with ticketing marketplaces, broker operations, POS platforms, or commerce systems that manage inventory, listings, and orders. - Experience troubleshooting APIs using tools such as Postman, including reviewing JSON payloads, authentication errors, and HTTP status codes. - A degree in information technology, computer science, data analytics, or a related field, or equivalent technical training and practical experience. - Relevant certifications, such as Microsoft Certified: Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900), AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner, or SnowPro Core Certification, are a plus. **What We Offer:** - **Accelerated Growth Environment:** Immerse yourself in an environment designed for swift skill and knowledge enhancement, where you can scale your career. - **Top Tier Compensation Package:** Enjoy a rewarding compensation package that includes premier benefits, aligning with our commitment to recognizing and valuing your contributions. - **Paid Time Off:** Generous Paid Time Off, allowing you to manage your schedule and recharge as needed. - **Comprehensive Benefits Package:** Prioritize your well-being with a comprehensive benefits package featuring 401k and premium Health, Vision, and Dental Insurance options. The anticipated gross base pay range is below for this role. Actual compensation will vary depending on factors such as a candidate’s qualifications, skills, experience, and competencies. Base pay is one component of StubHub’s total compensation and competitive benefits package, which includes 401(k), paid time off, paid parental leave, and comprehensive health benefits. Base Range $55,000—$55,000 USD **About Us** StubHub is the world’s leading marketplace to buy and sell tickets to any live event, anywhere. Through StubHub in North America and viagogo, our international platform, we service customers in 195 countries in 33 languages and 49 available currencies. With more than 300 million tickets available annually on our platform to events around the world -- from sports to music, comedy to dance, festivals to theater -- StubHub offers the safest, most convenient way to buy or sell tickets to the most memorable live experiences. Come join our team for a front-row seat to the action. **PhD Internship 2027: Engineering - Boston** Boston, US | Full-time | Fixed-term| Hybrid Salary: $55.70 per hour, DOE **About us** Riverlane’s mission is to master quantum error correction (QEC) and unlock a new age of human progress. From advances in materials and climate science to complex chemistry simulation for new drug design, quantum computers will help humanity solve some of its most important challenges. But without QEC, the industry’s defining technical challenge, such breakthroughs can never be achieved. Riverlane is the world leader in QEC technology. QEC is a complex problem that requires a range of skills, talent, and passion. Having raised more than $125M in funding to date to accelerate our cutting-edge R&D in quantum error correction (QEC), Riverlane partners with many of the world’s leading quantum hardware providers and government agencies to make fault-tolerant quantum computing a reality. We’re making remarkable progress and growing fast. **About the role** Delivering practical quantum error correction requires tightly integrated quantum and classical systems. Decoding algorithms must process large volumes of error data within demanding latency, bandwidth, compute and power constraints. As an engineering Intern, you will investigate the classical computing architectures needed to support scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computers. Your project will sit at the intersection of quantum error correction, computer architecture and hardware-software co-design. Depending on the project, you could explore efficient QEC decoding or predecoding methods, model the classical resources required by fault-tolerant quantum programs, or investigate how decoding workloads can be distributed across different levels of a computing system. You will work alongside Riverlane’s researchers and engineers in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with support from a dedicated supervisor. Your work will contribute to our understanding of how QEC systems can meet the performance requirements of increasingly large quantum computers. **What you will do** - Contribute to a research project focused on the classical systems and architectures required for scalable quantum error correction - Investigate methods for reducing the compute, communication, memory, latency or power requirements associated with QEC - Develop algorithms, simulations or architectural models to evaluate potential approaches - Explore trade-offs between decoding performance, logical error suppression and classical resource requirements - Consider how QEC workloads could be implemented across software, FPGA, ASIC or other computing architectures - Collaborate with researchers and engineers working across QEC theory, decoding, software and hardware - Analyse results and communicate your findings through technical discussions, presentations and written reports - Produce clear, reproducible research code and supporting documentation **What we need** - You must be currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Mathematics or another related technical field - Research experience in at least one of the following areas: - Quantum error correction or fault-tolerant quantum computing - Computer architecture or quantum-classical systems - Decoding algorithms or error-correcting codes - FPGA, ASIC or digital hardware design - Experience developing computational models, simulations or research software - Proficiency in Python, C, C++ or another relevant programming language - A strong understanding of computer systems and architecture - Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills - The ability to communicate complex technical ideas clearly - The ability to take initiative and work effectively with researchers and engineers from different disciplines - Authorisation to work in the United States for the duration of the internship **Even better if…** - You have experience researching quantum LDPC or surface codes - You are familiar with QEC decoding or predecoding techniques - You have explored the classical resource requirements of fault-tolerant quantum computing - You have experience with hardware-software or compiler-hardware co-design - You have worked with RTL, SystemVerilog, FPGA or ASIC development workflows - You understand the latency, bandwidth or power constraints affecting quantum control and decoding systems - You have experience with scientific computing, quantum circuit simulation or QEC simulation tools - You have contributed to academic publications, open-source software or collaborative research projects **Important notes** - You must be legally authorized to work in the United States for the duration of the internship - If you intend to work under Curricular Practical Training (CPT), Optional Practical Training (OPT) or another form of student employment authorization, you are responsible for obtaining the necessary approval before your start date - Any offer of employment will be contingent upon verification of your identity and authorization to work in the United States, as required by law - You must be available to work full-time for 10 to 12 weeks - You will be required to sign an agreement assigning ownership of intellectual property produced during your internship to Riverlane - This internship is based at our US office in Cambridge, Massachusetts **How to apply** Please upload your CV and a cover letter. Your CV should include details of your education, research experience and relevant technical skills. Your cover letter should explain why you are applying for the internship and the skills and experience you would bring to the role. **Deadline** Please submit your application by **November 6th, 2026** **Pay and Expenses** We will reimburse reasonable expenses incurred as part of your role, such as approved travel to meetings or conferences. We are unable to cover the cost of travelling to Cambridge, Massachusetts at the beginning or end of the internship or accommodation during the internship. **What you can expect from us** You can expect a diverse and collaborative working environment that brings together experts in software and hardware development, quantum information theory, physics, mathematics and other technical fields. Our global team represents more than 20 nationalities. We also provide free snacks and refreshments and organize regular social and cultural events. If you have any questions, please contact [jobs@riverlane.com](mailto:jobs@riverlane.com). *Riverlane is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome qualified applicants and consider them for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local law.* *We know that strong candidates may not meet every requirement listed. If you are interested in the opportunity and believe your experience could be relevant, we encourage you to apply.* *Riverlane provides reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities. We work to protect our natural environment and water resources, while powering our world for future generations. Around the world, we’re feeling the effects climate change, rapid urbanization, loss of biodiversity. The rate at which we’re seeing large-scale, unforeseen events such as floods and wildfires, is becoming more frequent. You role will also include assessing, developing, and supporting the management of sustainability and resilience projects. This position will offer valuable hands on experience in the field of water engineering, allowing you to develop your skills and contribute to meaningful projects. The ideal candidate should have unrestricted availability to travel as needed and enthusiasm for on-site field work at construction sites. We’re a team of friends bound together by a mission to preserve our planet for future generations through innovative energy solutions and modern infrastructure. Intersect develops, constructs, and operates the most ambitious power and data center infrastructure in the country by co-locating industrial demand with dedicated gas and renewable power generation. Intersect was acquired by Google in March 2026 and operates as an independent subsidiary. We are developing and constructing multiple gigawatts of energy and data center projects in the U.S., enabling more data center and generation capacity to come online faster. We’re on an aggressive growth trajectory and looking for people hungry to tackle the largest energy challenges on the planet. **Location & Team Gatherings** We are currently looking for candidates located within 60 miles of the listed location above. We connect as a team at our Team Week experiences four times a year and at our recently established Hub locations - SF Bay Area, NYC Metro Area, NY; Denver, CO; Austin, TX; Calgary, AB; and Toronto, ON. **About this role** As Campus Operations Manager — Meitner Energy Center on Intersect's Operations team, you'll hold the premier asset leadership role on-site in Pampa, Texas, serving as the single point of accountability for the safety, performance, and long-term reliability of our flagship multi-technology generation campus powering co-located Google data center infrastructure. You'll orchestrate a behind-the-meter energy ecosystem combining approximately 500 MW of solar PV, 650 MW of wind generation, 1 GW / 2 GWh of battery energy storage, 300 MW of fast-start reciprocating gas generation, and a 345kV/34.5kV breaker-and-a-half switching station—including a 300 MW BESS and 300 MW gas microgrid configured for islanded operation to sustain critical data center load independent of the ERCOT grid. You'll direct an integrated leadership tier of Solar, Wind, BESS, Gas, and High Voltage / Substation Site Managers alongside internalized maintenance teams to maximize campus Equivalent Availability Factor (EAF), enforce stringent NERC CIP and ERCOT compliance, and ensure seamless power delivery from commissioning through long-term operations. Partnering closely with Engineering, Technical Services, Asset Management, Origination and Trading, executive leadership, the Transmission Service Provider, and local authorities, you will set the operational standard for one of the most technically ambitious power campuses in the country. **Team overview** This team plays a critical role in advancing Intersect's mission to accelerate the clean energy transition. The Operations team ensures that our utility-scale generation, storage, and high-voltage assets perform safely, efficiently, and reliably at scale—combining deep technical judgment, data-driven decision-making, and disciplined field execution to maximize uptime across the fleet. Joining this team means leading the most complex multi-technology campus in our portfolio from construction handoff into long-term operation, shaping how dedicated clean energy and flexible thermal infrastructure power modern computing while growing alongside collaborative industry leaders. **What you'll do** Lead Campus Strategy and Multi-Technology Orchestration - Provide overarching operational leadership across co-located solar PV, wind, BESS, and fast-start reciprocating gas assets, aligning technology-specific targets into a unified campus strategy. - Manage, mentor, and evaluate the Wind, Solar, BESS, Gas, and High Voltage / Substation Site Managers, establishing standardized governance, work practices, and reporting cadences across all disciplines. - Optimize campus-wide Capex and Opex through shared logistics, collective spare parts management, cross-utilization of labor and tooling, and disciplined financial workflows in Stampli and SideTracker. Command High-Voltage Infrastructure, Interconnection, and Microgrid Readiness - Oversee safe, continuous operation of the 345kV/34.5kV breaker-and-a-half switching station and 35kV collector pathways, owning switching, clearance, and outage coordination across generation and behind-the-meter load. - Maintain continuous readiness of the 300 MW BESS and 300 MW reciprocating gas microgrid for islanded operation, overseeing grid-forming inverter controls, black start capability, transition/resynchronization procedures, and periodic verification testing. - Serve as the primary on-site interface with the Transmission Service Provider, balancing authority, and ERCOT scheduling coordinators while enforcing flawless NERC CIP and ERCOT reliability standard compliance. Drive Cross-Technology Performance, Dispatch, and Commissioning Handoff - Partner with Origination and Trading and the Operations Control Center to optimize real-time dispatch across variable clean energy, BESS state of charge, and fast-start gas to meet rigid power factor, market, and behind-the-meter data center commitments. - Direct preventative maintenance programs engineered for Texas Panhandle environmental extremes—including ~40°F diurnal temperature swings, dust mitigation, and high-lightning/surge exposure—while leading root cause analysis with Technical Services. - Lead construction-to-operations handoff across all technologies, including commissioning validation, punch list closure, staffing execution, and executive briefings synthesized via SCADA/EMS, G Suite, Lucidchart, Claude, and Gemini. Champion Safety, Regulatory Compliance, and Community Stewardship - Enforce a zero-harm safety culture under OSHA Title 29 protocols, standardizing LOTO, high-voltage switching, arc flash procedures, and incident command across battery thermal, gas, wind rescue, and severe weather hazard profiles. - Manage local regulatory and community obligations in Gray County, including Chapter 312 tax abatement compliance, wildlife mitigation plans, and county road agreements. **What you'll bring** - Bachelor's degree in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, Clean Energy Management, or an equivalent technical military or field leadership background. - 10–12+ years of experience in utility-scale power generation operations, including at least 5+ years managing complex, multi-technology clean energy sites, hybrid power plants, or heavy industrial campuses. - Proven track record of managing other managers and leading multi-disciplinary, internalized maintenance teams in high-consequence, 24/7 operational environments. - Deep operational familiarity with medium voltage (35kV) collector systems and high voltage (345kV) substation architecture (breaker-and-a-half configuration strongly preferred), paired with hands-on expertise in at least two core site technologies: solar PV, wind generation, BESS, or reciprocating gas generation. - Hands-on knowledge of microgrid and islanded operations, including grid-forming inverter controls, black start, and seamless load transfer serving critical behind-the-meter data center or industrial load. - Robust working knowledge of ERCOT market protocols, ERCOT reliability standards, NERC CIP compliance, OSHA Title 29 protocols, and local frameworks such as Chapter 312 tax abatement compliance. - Proficiency with SCADA/EMS platforms, SideTracker, Stampli, G Suite, Lucidchart, and generative AI tools (Claude, Gemini) to synthesize complex operational and financial data into executive-ready briefings. - Commitment to working full-time on-site in Pampa / Gray County, TX (with up to 20% travel), leading with composure through active construction/commissioning boundaries and Texas Panhandle weather extremes. - A strategic, people-first leadership style grounded in safety, accountability, and operational rigor, aligned with Intersect's core values of Equity, Humility, Authenticity, Long-run Value, and People Come First. **Application questions** - Do you have 5+ years of experience managing multi-technology utility-scale generation sites (two or more of wind, solar PV, BESS, or gas thermal) and leading other managers? (Yes/No) - Do you have direct operational and switching oversight experience with high-voltage (345kV or 230kV+) substations and NERC CIP / ERCOT compliance? (Yes/No) - Describe your experience operating or maintaining readiness for an islanded microgrid or hybrid plant serving critical behind-the-meter load—how did you balance real-time dispatch against islanding reserve requirements?

You will be responsible for selling available inventory inside our premium seating areas including luxury suites, Audi Sport Club, Sideline Social, Concourse Boxes West Club, and group hospitality areas. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES • Responsible for maximizing revenue through over the phone & face to face sales of Orlando City and Orlando Pride premium products including multi-year luxury suite rentals, single match luxury suite rentals, multi-year Audi Sport Club agreements & West Club Season Tickets. • Make 50+ outbound touch points daily with the goal of setting an appointment with new and returning clients. • Set and conduct 10+ stadium and out-of-office appointments per week to assist in closing new business. • Conduct VIP tours with potential prospect sales at Inter&Co Stadium. • Actively self-prospect and research new sales leads and potential clients through various platforms including LinkedIn & local Chambers. • Build and enhance current relationships to grow account base through repeat business and referrals. • Maintain a beneficial membership with a local networking group and Chamber of Commerce. • Exceed weekly, monthly & yearly ticket sales goals. • Handle incoming calls from sales prospects and existing clients. • Utilize Salesforce CRM software to manage customer accounts. • Work all Orlando City & Orlando Pride home matches and other events to support luxury suite sales initiatives. • Provide excellent service through phone calls, emails, written communication and in-person visits in/out of the office and special Inter&Co Stadium events. • Participate in all ticket sales events, game duties, sales trainings, and meetings. • Other duties as assigned. QUALIFICATIONS It’s never just a job at Orlando City SC. It’s a way of life. We live and breathe soccer. We believe each role is as unique as the person who does it. To join our team, you will also possess these qualifications: • Bachelor’s Degree from accredited college/university in a related field preferred. • Minimum of 2-3 years sales experience, preferably in sports and entertainment. • Track record of consistent top sales performance. • Passion for a growth-oriented career in sales. • Excellent customer service skills and ability to communicate effectively. • Highly motivated, competitive, and committed to the sports industry. • Possesses strong computer skills and ability to comprehend basic mathematics. • Exceptional time management and presentation skills. • Detail-oriented and organized; ability to handle several projects at once. • Familiarity with Archtics and CRM Platform • Ability to work flexible hours including nights, weekends, and holidays. • The ability to attain and maintain Safesport certification. • The ability to pass a background screening. About Orlando City SC & Orlando Pride: In November 2013, Orlando City Soccer Club was awarded a Major League Soccer (MLS) franchise, becoming the league’s 21st franchise. The team began play in March 2015, with 62,510 fans packing the then-Orlando Citrus Bowl for the Club’s MLS debut. The Lions have reached the postseason in five-consecutive seasons (2020-24), qualified for the Concacaf Champions Cup (formerly Concacaf Champions League) in both 2023 and 2024, and reached their first final in 2020 during the MLS is Back Tournament. In 2022, Orlando City won its first championship of its MLS era, lifting the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup trophy, which also marked the first championship by any professional team in the City Beautiful. Prior to its time in MLS, Orlando City boasted a decorated history in the United Soccer League, winning the league’s championship in both the 2011 and 2013 seasons. In October 2015, the Orlando Pride was announced as the 10th team in the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL), bringing professional women’s soccer to the state of Florida for the first time. The team began play in April 2016, setting a then-league single-game attendance record in its first-ever home game, with 23,403 fans witnessing the Club’s first win. The Pride feature a star-studded roster of domestic and international talent and, in 2024, brought the first professional major league title to the city of Orlando, with the Club winning the NWSL Championship. The season saw the Pride complete the double, winning both the Championship and the NWSL Shield as the best team in the regular season, capping off a historic campaign that set numerous league records. Former Orlando City defender Seb Hines serves as the team’s head coach, not only the first Black head coach in the league, but also the first to win both the Championship and the NWSL Shield, and the 2024 NWSL Coach of the Year. In 2017, both teams moved into its privately-owned, soccer-specific venue – Inter&Co Stadium – located in the heart of downtown Orlando. In July 2021, the Club – which includes Orlando City SC, the Orlando Pride, Orlando City B (MLS NEXT Pro) and Inter&Co Stadium – was purchased by the Wilf Family, who also own the Minnesota Vikings of the National Football League. Early Career Rotational Program (ECRP) Associate Are you curious about how breakthrough products go from concept to customer? As an Early Career Rotational Program (ECRP) Associate, you'll complete three eight-month rotations across Qualitrol's Research & Development and Manufacturing organizations, contributing to projects that support product innovation, manufacturing excellence, and the technologies that keep critical infrastructure running around the world. No two rotations are the same. One day you might be supporting a new product launch, while another could be spent improving a manufacturing process or partnering with teams across the business to solve a complex challenge. Along the way, you'll work with experienced engineers and leaders who are invested in helping you learn, contribute, and grow. We're looking for emerging engineers who are energized by learning, comfortable navigating ambiguity, and motivated by meaningful work. More than a rotational program, ECRP is an opportunity to explore different possibilities, discover what excites you most, and build a career with lasting impact. Explore Different Functions. Build Your Future. During your three rotations, you’ll have opportunities to: Support the development, testing, and launch of new products and technologies. Gain real world experience in product design, industrialization, project management, and manufacturing operations. Partner with cross-functional teams to solve engineering, operational, and customer-focused challenges. Analyze products, processes, and data to identify opportunities for improvement. Apply continuous improvement principles to enhance quality, efficiency, and performance. Work with sensing technologies and monitoring solutions used by customers around the world. Present recommendations and project outcomes to technical and business stakeholders. Who We’re Looking For Recently completed or on track to complete a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, or a related technical field. Curious, adaptable, and motivated to learn through new experiences. Interested in exploring both Research & Development and Manufacturing. Comfortable asking thoughtful questions, seeking clarification, and learning from colleagues across different functions. Team-oriented, with a collaborative approach to solving technical and business challenges. Excited to build a broad foundation before moving into a more specialized role. Technical Skills Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Foundational understanding of engineering principles, product development, or manufacturing processes. Ability to evaluate technical challenges, develop recommendations, and communicate insights effectively. Effective collaborator who can manage multiple priorities and contribute within cross-functional teams. A plus: Previous internship, co-op, research, laboratory, design, manufacturing, process engineering, or continuous improvement experience.

OVERVIEW: The Geological Resources Team conducts multidisciplinary applied research and develops innovative approaches to improve the understanding of geological subsurface processes related to conventional and unconventional, as well as low carbon resources. Domains of specialization include structural geology, organic and inorganic geochemistry, rock physics and geomechanics. The Graduate Summer Intern supports a defined research project involving laboratory experimentation, data analysis, modeling, literature review, or evaluation of emerging technologies related to resources characterization, exploration and development. Working under the guidance of experienced researchers, the intern will contribute to project deliverables while gaining practical experience in an industrial R&D environment. SCOPE: Focused on completing a defined, supervised research assignment related to the team’s multidisciplinary missions. PRINCIPAL DUTIES: Research and Technical Support Contribute to a defined research project involving structural geology, organic/inorganic geochemistry, rock physics, or geomechanics for conventional, unconventional or low carbon resources. Conduct focused literature reviews and summarize relevant advances in resources characterization, exploration and development. Assist with laboratory experiments, technology evaluations, or workflow development under the guidance of experienced researchers. Explore topics that may include basic rock and fluids characterization, chemical and physical properties based exploration workflows, physical properties modeling and prediction, multiscale faulting and fracturing. Data Analysis and Problem Solving Analyze experimental results and, as applicable, geological, petrophysical, completion, or production data using appropriate methods and software. Develop, modify, or apply code and research software, as needed, to support data analysis, modeling, experimental workflows, or technology development activities. Apply scientific and engineering principles to investigate research questions, identify trends, and develop well-supported conclusions. Document methods, assumptions, results, and limitations to support reproducible research. Collaboration and Communication Collaborate with team members and other R&D groups, participate in technical discussions, and incorporate feedback into assigned work. Prepare a technical report, project updates, and a final presentation summarizing the research problem, approach, results, and conclusions. Support preparation of publications, conference materials, or other technical communications when appropriate. Safety and Professional Responsibilities Follow all laboratory safety procedures and contribute to a safe, accident-free work environment. Comply with company safety, cybersecurity, confidentiality, and professional conduct requirements. Perform other project-related duties as assigned within the scope of the internship. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS: Bachelor’s degree in engineering, geoscience, physics, mathematics, or a related field, with current enrollment in a graduate program in one of these disciplines. Relevant coursework or research experience in geology, porous media, fluid flow, geochemistry, petrophysics, geomechanics, laboratory characterization, or related subsurface systems is preferred. Experience in laboratory experimentation, data analysis, modeling, numerical methods, or scientific computing is desirable. Familiarity with technical computing or programming tools such as Python, C++, or MATLAB is desirable. Ability to review technical literature, analyze results, maintain research records, and communicate findings clearly in written and spoken English. Ability to work independently and collaboratively, follow guidance, and demonstrate professionalism, attention to detail, and a strong work ethic. Availability for the full internship term. OVERVIEW: The Production Technology team conducts applied research and develops innovative materials and geomechanics related methods and technologies to improve the mechanism understanding and practical operations of drilling, completion, production and underground storage in both conventional and unconventional reservoirs. **A World-Changing Company** Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. ### The Role We are a software engineering team applying open-source data technologies to some of the world's hardest and most important problems. We build the data processing infrastructure that underpins Palantir Foundry, supporting applications that help hospitals care for more patients, help clinical teams coordinate timely diagnoses, and keep essential supplies moving through global disruption. You will work deep inside the systems that make this possible: how computations are represented, how query plans are optimized, how operators execute, and how data is read and written efficiently. We build on and extend Apache Spark, Apache DataFusion, and Apache Iceberg, bringing advances in open-source engines and table formats into the demanding environments our customers operate in. Our work serves many products and workloads across Foundry, including no-code pipelines, interactive analysis, and the processing that keeps the Ontology up to date. Working alongside experienced engineers, you will take on real problems in our production systems. That could mean writing a new planning rule, adding a capability to a native execution engine, or making large tables faster to scan. You will see your work through design, code review, testing, and release. Correctness, compatibility, and predictable performance are central to everything we build, and you will learn how to deliver all three. Join us if you want to learn how modern data systems work from the inside and apply that knowledge to consequential problems. ### Technologies We Use - Java, Scala, Rust, and Python - Apache Spark, Apache DataFusion, Apache Comet, and Velox for data processing and query execution - Apache Iceberg for table management and catalog interoperability - Apache Arrow and Apache Parquet for in-memory data processing and columnar storage - Gradle and Cargo for builds, and GitHub for collaboration You do not need prior experience with these technologies. We expect you to learn them here. ### What We Value - Curiosity about how data systems work, from query optimizers and execution operators to file formats and distributed processing - A high bar for correctness and a willingness to dig until you understand why something behaves the way it does - Comfort following a problem across languages, services, and layers of the stack - A practical approach to performance, grounded in measurement rather than intuition - Eagerness to learn, ask questions, and incorporate feedback - Interest in applying deep systems engineering to real-world problems, with empathy for the people who depend on our software ### What We Require - Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics, or a similar field, or equivalent practical experience - Proficiency in at least one language such as Java, Rust, Scala, C++, or C - Strong foundations in algorithms, data structures, and concurrency - Strong written and verbal communication skills - Coursework or projects in databases, compilers, operating systems, or distributed systems - Contributions to open-source projects - Must be planning on graduating in 2028. This should be your final internship before graduating.

role: Research Intern - Algorithms Group: Generative Modeling
description: **Overview** Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The Algorithms group at MSR Redmond is looking for Research Interns to advance research in generative modeling. Opportunities include fundamental algorithmic innovation to enhance the efficiency and generation quality of existing models (e.g., diffusion models, image auto-regressive models, language models) and the design of next-generation generative modeling techniques (see examples below). - [Latent Zoning Network: A Unified Principle for Generative Modeling, Representation Learning, and Classification (NeurIPS 2025)](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/latent-zoning-network-a-unified-principle-for-generative-modeling-representation-learning-and-classification/) - [Distilled Decoding 1: One-step Sampling of Image Auto-regressive Models with Flow Matching (ICLR 2025)](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/distilled-decoding-1-one-step-sampling-of-image-auto-regressive-models-with-flow-matching/) - [Distilled Decoding 2: One-step Sampling of Image Auto-regressive Models with Conditional Score Distillation (NeurIPS 2025)](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/distilled-decoding-2-one-step-sampling-of-image-auto-regressive-models-with-conditional-score-distillation/) - [Weak-to-Strong On-Policy Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26246) - [Can LLMs Learn by Teaching for Better Reasoning? role: Research Intern - Extended Perception Interaction Cognition (EPIC)
description: **Overview** Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. This position is for a research internship with the EPIC (Extended Perception, Interaction & Cognition) research group in Microsoft Research’s Redmond Lab. We have multiple positions available. Research Internships will be focused on creating new interactive experiences that “blend artificial and human intelligence”. Topics range from coupling the power of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques with interaction design to reinvent how we work with content, to building the next generation of multi-modal interfaces adapting in real time to user tasks and contexts. Key skills sought for this internship include: - Generative AI: Large Language Models (LLMs), Vision Language Models (VLMs), Stable Diffusion, video/world/action models, real-time models, multi-agent development, and related technologies - Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) system building and agentic development: Experience building interactive prototypes with TypeScript, Node.js, and React, using coding agents and agentic workflows to accelerate development. Demonstrated programming and software architecture fundamentals are essential to guide agents, review generated code, and validate system behavior. Additional relevant skills (depending on projects): - Interaction design: experience with devising multimodal interactions (touch, pen, speech), context sensing, responsive & adaptive User Interfaces (UIs) - Experience design: storyboarding, envisioning video techniques - User Experience (UX) research: conducting qualitative and quantitative user studies We value your ideas and unique viewpoints on these topics, as well, and hope that our partnership and collaboration will shape initial directions into exciting, ambitious, and impactful research contributions that only you could have crafted. We are an interdisciplinary group of researchers, engineers, scientists, and designers at Microsoft Research who study Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) through prototyping, system-building, design sketching, and observational study of human behavior. Patreon is a media and community platform where over 300,000 creators give their biggest fans access to exclusive work and experiences. We offer creators a variety of ways to engage with their fans and build a lasting business including: paid memberships, free memberships, community chats, live video, and selling to fans directly with one-time purchases. Ultimately our goal is simple: fund the creative class. And we're leaders in that space, with: - $10 billion+ generated by creators since Patreon's inception - 100 million+ free memberships for fans who may not be ready to pay just yet, and - 25 million+ paid memberships on Patreon today. We're continuing to invest in building the best creator platform with the best team in the creator economy and are looking for **Software Engineering Interns** to support our mission. *This role is based in **San Francisco or New York** and open to those who are able to be in-office 3 days per week on a hybrid work model.* Our summer internship is a 12-week program running **May–August or June–September 2027**. This internship is designed for students graduating between **December 2027 and June 2028**. ## About the Role What you will do: - **Make an impact.** You’ll build and ship a feature that directly supports the creator economy and helps your favorite creators turn their passions into sustainable careers. - **Collaborate with the best.** You’ll be embedded within a world-class engineering team, working closely with engineers, product managers, designers, and data scientists to bring your project to life. - **Learn and grow.** With guidance from an experienced engineer mentor, you’ll tackle technical challenges, gain hands-on experience, and grow your skills throughout the internship. - **Have fun!** Beyond building great products, you’ll participate in team activities and events. ## About You - Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field (i.e. Mathematics, Physics). - Strong foundation in Computer Science fundamentals and data structures. - Proficiency in one or more programming languages such as Python, Swift, Kotlin, or TypeScript. - Eagerness to learn, adapt, and grow through feedback. - Genuine passion for Patreon’s mission and supporting the creator economy. ## About Patreon Patreon powers creators to do what they love and get paid by the people who love what they do. Our team is passionate about making this mission and our core values come to life every day in our work. Through this work, our Patronauts: - **Put Creators First |** *They’re the reason we’re here. When creators win, we win.* - **Build with Craft |** *We sign our name to every deliverable, just like the creators we serve.* - **Make it Happen |** *We don’t quit. We learn and deliver.* - **Win Together |** *We grow as individuals. We win as a team.* We hire talented and passionate people from different backgrounds because workplace diversity and inclusion is critical to our ability to serve creators worldwide. If you’re excited about a role but your past experience doesn’t match with every bullet point outlined above, we strongly encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re a creator at heart, are energized by our mission, and share our company values, we’d love to hear from you. *Patreon is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We provide employment opportunities without regard to age, race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, disability, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other protected class. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the interview process, please let us know via email at* [*accomodations@patreon.com*](mailto:accomodations@patreon.com)*.* *Patreon operates under a hybrid work model, where engineering interns are expected to come into the office three days per week, excluding sick time and leave. The goal of this policy is to be intentional about the in-person time we spend together to strengthen the feeling of community at Patreon.* *At Patreon, we believe in fair and transparent pay. In compliance with New York and California pay transparency laws, we are sharing the expected salary range for this role.* *The posted salary range is dependent on the location and the level. This range may encompass multiple levels within the role’s job family. The final offer will be based on candidate’s experience, skills, competencies, and geographic location, aligning with the appropriate job level within Patreon’s leveling framework.* *Patreon reserves the right to modify or update compensation and benefits at any time.*

role: Garage Door Install Apprentice, Minneapolis MN
description: We are looking for high performers to join us. The **Installer** job is physically demanding. Stamina and enthusiasm are required! You don’t need to have experience with garage doors. role: Nu AI Core Summer PhD Research Internship
description: # **About Nu** Nu serves more than 140 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services. Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Visit our [Institutional Page](https://www.nu.com/2026-en) ## **About the Program** The Nu AI Core Summer Internship Program is a research-focused internship for PhD students working at the frontier of artificial intelligence and machine learning. Over about 12 weeks, interns collaborate with engineers, applied scientists, and researchers on complex AI challenges. Each intern leads an end-to-end research or applied AI project that combines research methods with large-scale production environments. The program builds long-term relationships between industry and academia and with emerging AI research talent. # **Program Structure** - **Duration:** ~12 weeks - **Start dates:** May–June, aligned with US university calendars - **Location model**: Remote, with one in-person week at Nu's Palo Alto office in Silicon Valley, fully covered by us. **What you get** - Dedicated research mentor - Ownership of a scoped AI research project - Access to large-scale datasets and compute infrastructure - Research talks and technical seminars - Final research presentation to leadership and AI teams # **Research Areas** Interns may work on projects related to: - **Machine learning and deep learning** - **Large language models and generative AI** - **Recommender systems and ranking models** - **AI infrastructure and model optimization** - **Responsible AI and model evaluation** Projects typically combine **research experimentation with applied system development**, including model design, experimentation, and large-scale evaluation. # **Candidate Profile** This program targets **PhD students conducting research in AI and machine learning** who are interested in applying their work to real-world systems. Applicants are typically pursuing a PhD in fields such as: - Computer Science - Machine Learning - Artificial Intelligence - Statistics - Mathematics - Computational Linguistics - Electrical Engineering - or related quantitative disciplines. # **Basic Qualifications (Application/ Screening Filters)** - Currently enrolled in a PhD program - Research focus in machine learning, AI, statistics or related areas - Strong programming skills in Python or similar languages - Experience working with machine learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) - Experience designing experiments and evaluating models - Experience working with large datasets or training ML models # **Preferred Qualifications** Strong candidates may also demonstrate: - Publications at top AI/ML conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, KDD, RecSys, CVPR, CIKM or equivalent-conferences for related fields) - Experience working with large-scale ML systems or distributed training - Experience with LLMs, generative AI, or foundation models - Open-source contributions in AI or ML - Experience collaborating in interdisciplinary research environments # **What We Value** We are particularly interested in candidates who demonstrate: - Strong research rigor and experimental methodology - Ability to translate research ideas into practical systems - Track record of identifying novel research directions or reframing existing problems - Intellectual curiosity and independent problem solving - Collaboration with engineers and cross-functional teams - Interest in deploying AI systems with real-world impact # **Benefits** - Top Tier Medical Insurance - Top Tier Dental and Vision Insurance - Life Insurance and AD&D - Extended maternity and paternity leaves - Nucleo - Our learning platform of courses - NuLanguage - Our language learning program - NuCare - Our mental health and wellness assistance program - 401K - Saving Plans - Health Saving Account and Flexible Spending Account # **Location for this opportunity** Remote, but only for USA PhD students ## Our recruitment process may involve the use of artificial intelligence–enabled tools, such as automated interview transcription and analysis, to support the evaluation process. Artificial intelligence is not used to make final hiring decisions; all decisions are made by human reviewers. To maintain a consistent and fair process for every candidate, Nu does not provide individualized technical feedback. role: Student Life Coordinator at KU Hillel
description: # Student Life Coordinator ## University of Kansas Hillel ## Role Overview Make your mark on Jewish student life by joining KU Hillel as our next Engagement Associate. You will build one-on-one relationships with students, plan and execute engaging events and programs around campus, and help inspire students to make a commitment to Jewish life. KU Hillel proudly serves more than 1,000 Jewish Jayhawks with a dynamic professional team and strong community partnerships. KU Hillel is a student-centric and data-informed team that is committed to dreaming big, entrepreneurial thinking, and always creating new and exciting opportunities to build student leadership, provide pre-professional training, and build a sense of belonging on campus. This is a relationship-focused, student-facing role, perfect for folks who love meeting new faces, building authentic relationships over coffee, and connecting students with opportunities. This role is ideal for an early-career professional (even right out of college!), especially someone with experience in Jewish summer camps, youth group leadership, athletics, or experiential education, who is energized by working directly with students, building belonging through shared experiences, and reaching students who may not initially see themselves in traditional Hillel spaces. This is so much more than your average 9-to-5. And, most importantly, you’ll be excited to support and be supported by a community that sees KU as home. After all, you are in Kansas! ## What You’ll Do - Be the first face and warm welcome to KU students, and help foster a community of belonging amongst Jewish students on campus. - Take a leading role in representing KU Hillel on campus through visible and head-turning opportunities in order to ensure every student on campus has the opportunity to discover who we are. - Contribute to team planning, reflection and assessment - and embrace new responsibilities as you grow with us. - Work with our first-year student community, students in Greek life, and students from multifaith families. - Supervise, mentor, and empower student leaders and volunteers to take ownership of Jewish programming and outreach. - Meet yet-to-be-engaged students wherever they are— be that in the on-campus dining hall, their favorite downtown coffee shop, or grilling kosher hot dogs on Greek Row. - Plan and engage with students to facilitate regular Shabbat and Holiday experiences, as well as social programming. If you enjoy Challah baking or experimenting with recipes in the kitchen, we’ve got an extra apron for you, too! - Assist the KU Hillel team with other on-campus activities, including recruitment for Birthright Israel trips and cohort-based learning opportunities. ## What You’ve Accomplished - You thrive on meeting new people, understanding their interests, and forging meaningful connections. - You have experience in Jewish summer camps, youth groups, or experiential leadership strongly preferred. - You enjoy working collaboratively with a team to solve problems and explore new initiatives. - You see yourself as a creative person who takes initiative and a proactive approach to problem-solving - You’ve demonstrated interest in student engagement, leadership development, and Jewish life. - You have the ability to work collaboratively while also taking ownership of projects and relationships. - You’re comfortable with working a flexible schedule that includes evenings, weekends, and Jewish holidays. ## What You’ll Bring to the Job - Recent college graduates or graduating seniors with 0-2 years experience. People with relevant internship and leadership experience are encouraged to apply. - Bachelor's degree - This is an in-person role located in Lawrence, KS; remote work is not available for this position. Staff frequently choose to live in nearby Kansas City (about a short podcast’s drive away). - A deep passion for Jewishness, Judaism, the Jewish people, and Israel. - An entrepreneurial spirit — you’re excited to take smart risks, try new ideas, and learn when something doesn’t go as planned. - Confidence in initiating, brainstorming, and running programs — both independently and collaboratively. - Familiarity with Google Suite, Canva, and social media platforms is a plus. - A willingness to work nights and occasional weekends when students are available — and to take time off to recharge. The pace of work follows the academic calendar year. ## What You’ll Receive - The salary range for this role is **$46,000 - $49,000.** - Monthly cell phone stipend. - A comprehensive benefits package, including health insurance, retirement plan, Life, AD&D, and Long Term Disability (LTD) insurances, Flexible Spending accounts, generous vacation/sick time, and parental leave. - High-level professional development to help develop core skills and gain expertise from changemakers, engagers, and Jewish life experts. - Mentoring and career coaching to help you during and after your position - A network of terrific colleagues from across the Hillel movement. - Travel opportunities, both domestically and internationally, multiple times per year. ## About **KU & Lawrence, Kansas City, and Our Community** KU Hillel proudly serves more than 1,000 Jewish Jayhawks with a dynamic professional team and strong community partnerships. KU Hillel is a student-centric, data-informed team committed to dreaming big, entrepreneurial thinking, and creating new and exciting opportunities to build student leadership, provide pre-professional training, and build a sense of belonging on campus. Kansas City and Lawrence are incredible places to live: - Kansas City is a major metropolitan area with a population of over 2.2 million, while Lawrence offers a true college-town atmosphere with about 100,000 residents, blending cultural energy with a more relaxed pace of life. - Both Kansas City and Lawrence are highly livable communities, featuring all the cultural amenities of a big city, with the midwestern hospitality that makes you feel at home. - Kansas City is a cultural hub for the arts and museums, and home of the very best barbecue in the world. Kansas Citians are passionate about our hometown teams, the beloved Chiefs and Royals, and KC is considered the Soccer Capital of the USA. - Lawrence is home to the University of Kansas, where we “bleed crimson and blue” every day. The place where basketball was born, you can travel the world in Jayhawks gear, and be proudly greeted with “Rock Chalk Jayhawk,” a welcome sign that you’re in good company. *\*\*Interested candidates willing to relocate to Kansas are encouraged to use* [*Jewish Federation’s See KC program*](https://www.jewishkansascity.org/jewishkc/seekc) *as a resource to learn more about living in Kansas City and our incredible Jewish community. Kansas City boasts a thriving Jewish community of more than 20,000, including an* [*incredible group*](https://www.jewishkansascity.org/yad) *of young professionals living in and around the KC Metro Area.\*\** The University of Kansas (KU) is centered in Lawrence, Kansas. Today, Lawrence remains a crossroads of culture, celebrating the artists and innovators that populate its history and create an unmistakable identity. So, too is the spirit of the Jayhawks that powers KU. KU is the state’s flagship institution, home to innovative research and the constant pursuit of knowledge. KU Hillel is affiliated with Hillel International. Hillel International enriches the lives of Jewish students so they may enrich the Jewish people and the world, and envisions a world where every student is inspired to make an enduring commitment to Jewish life, learning and Israel. ## **About Hillel International** In 1923, Rabbi Benjamin Frankel started Hillel with humble means, a noble mission and a breathtaking vision: to convey Jewish civilization to a new generation. Today, Hillel International continues to enrich the lives of Jewish students and is the largest Jewish campus organization in the world at nearly 1,000 colleges and universities across North America and around the world. As Hillel evolves as an organization, the mission remains steadfast: to create lasting connections with every Jewish student that foster an enduring commitment to Jewish life, learning, and Israel and train them to become the next Jewish leaders. **Hillel is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an accepting and inclusive environment for all.**

Meter is a vertically integrated networking company. Hardware, software, services, ISP, and autonomous networks run on a single data pipeline, from the local network to the data center. Most of the networking industry treats hardware as a commodity–we don’t. Build the hardware right, and everything above it gets better. Meter designs its own Firewalls, Switches, Wireless Access Points, PDUs, and Gateways because customers subscribe to the network instead of buying individual boxes; we're accountable for how the hardware performs for years. We sweat details most people never see, like the logo stamped inside the enclosure and the sound spec on our fans. Great hardware takes more than designing circuits and shipping products: It means thinking hard about performance, reliability, manufacturability, supply chain, installation, sustainability, and the full product lifecycle. We’re hiring Hardware Engineering Interns to solve real technical problems across Meter’s hardware engineering and operations teams. Over 12 weeks, you’ll own a well-scoped project picked to fit your interests, your experience, and the problems that matter most to Meter: - Next-generation power adapters: Prototype compact, efficient power supplies that could ship in future Meter products. - Hardware lifecycle and sustainability: Figure out how Meter hardware can be refurbished, reused, or recycled, and what it takes to extend its life. - Installer tooling: Build tools, fixtures, or diagnostic devices that make Meter networks faster to install and troubleshoot. - Acoustics and thermal systems: Design quiet, efficient cooling for future high-performance networking and data center products. - Supply chain intelligence: Use component and supplier data to spot risks and bottlenecks before they hit a hardware build. ## **What success looks like** You’ll take a meaningful hardware problem from an open question to a recommendation backed by evidence, and leave behind something the hardware team can use: data, prototypes, test results, engineering requirements, supplier evaluations, or tools. Your day-to-day will depend on your project, but you may: - Design, build, and test electrical or mechanical prototypes for future Meter products - Evaluate components, technologies, architectures, materials, and suppliers - Write test plans and characterize performance, reliability, thermals, acoustics, power, and other system-level behavior - Work with our manufacturing partners in Taiwan to understand their capabilities, constraints, cost, and scalability - Present your findings and recommendations to the hardware team at the end of the internship ## **Who you are** You’re curious, hands-on, and you learn by building. You’re a good fit if: - You’re pursuing a degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related technical field - You like taking an ambiguous technical problem and breaking it into questions you can answer through engineering and experimentation - You’ve built, tested, debugged, or taken apart hardware on a design team, in a lab, or at home, or you’re eager to start - You’re comfortable working with physical systems: PCBAs, mechanical assemblies, test equipment, prototypes, manufacturing data, or supplier samples - You can explain technical findings clearly and turn your work into recommendations others can act on Experience with PCB design, CAD, embedded systems, thermal design, or data analysis is a plus, but none of it is required. Above all, we’re looking for people who want to understand how great hardware gets built. ## **Why Meter?** The internet runs the world. Every purchase you make and every video call you join is packets moving through networks. But those networks haven’t changed in decades. They’re brittle, complex, and surprisingly hard to set up for a business. We started Meter to build better networks, and that meant building everything ourselves: our own enterprise hardware, intuitive software, and streamlined operations. Today we deploy those networks at scale. Bridgewater, Lyft, Reddit, and the San Antonio Spurs rely on Meter to keep thousands of employees and locations online. Our bet is simple: Everyone will use the internet more than they do today. Meter is building the networking stack that makes connectivity as easy and reliable as water or electricity. ## **Compensation** - The estimated pay for this role is $40–$50 per hour. This role is also eligible for a relocation and housing stipend. By applying to this job you acknowledge that you've read and understood [Meter's Job Applicant Privacy Notice](https://www.meter.com/careers/job-applicant-privacy).

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. **ABOUT THE TEAM** The Air Dominance and Strike Low Observable Team are advancing into the next generation of LO Technology to enhance the survivability and effectiveness of unmanned air systems. Our Low Observables engineering team is responsible for designing, analyzing, testing, and sustaining stealth features that reduce radar (RCS) and infrared (IR) signatures, ensuring our systems remain undetectable in contested environments. **ABOUT THE ROLE** This is an intern role open to engineers finishing a degree in aerospace, electrical, or mechanical engineering. Low Observables work sits at the intersection of all three: the shape of the air vehicle, the electromagnetic behavior of its surfaces, and the materials and processes used to build it. You do not need prior stealth experience. Almost nobody arrives with it, because most of it cannot be taught outside a cleared program. We will teach you the LO-specific methods. What we are looking for is strong engineering fundamentals, comfort picking up unfamiliar analysis tools, and the judgment to tell a real result from a bad one. You will be paired with an LO engineer and start on a scoped piece of a live program, not a training exercise. **WHAT YOU'LL DO:** - Run broadband Radar Cross Section (RCS) analysis on components and full air vehicles, and learn to judge when a prediction can be trusted - Support the design and development of Low Observable unmanned air systems, from early configuration trades through detailed design - Build and improve the analysis tools, scripts, and validation workflows the team runs on - Model LO materials and treatments, and help select and optimize them for specific components - Support manufacturing and validation planning, including tolerances, inspection methods, and what is actually producible at rate - Help plan and execute RCS measurement campaigns in indoor chambers and on outdoor ranges, then reduce and interpret the data - Compare measured results against predictions, chase down the disagreements, and feed what you learn back into the models **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS** - Must be pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field. - Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester. - Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program. - Ability to complete an in-person 12-week internship in one of our offices in summer 2027. **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:** - Coursework in at least one of: electromagnetics or RF, aircraft or vehicle design, or materials and manufacturing processes - Working knowledge of a scripting or analysis language such as MATLAB, Python, or C++ - Familiarity with a 3D CAD package such as NX, CATIA, SolidWorks, or Creo - Demonstrated hands-on engineering work: a capstone or senior design project, internship, undergraduate research, or a student competition team - Ability to explain a technical result clearly, in writing and in a design review - Exposure to any electromagnetic simulation tool, such as HFSS, CST, FEKO, or COMSOL. X-Patch, SENTRi, and McMoM2D are government codes and we do not expect you to have used them - Coursework or project experience with composites, additive manufacturing, casting, or injection molding - Experience with laboratory RF measurement: network analyzers, anechoic chambers, or antenna pattern measurement - Experience reducing, visualizing, and sanity-checking measured data sets - A prior internship or co-op in aerospace, defense, or another hardware-heavy environment US Hourly Range $34—$50 USD The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Engineers and technicians work side by side, with deep collaboration and real-time feedback, to shape how we build better and faster. With a manifest and a launch date, it’s up to the team to deliver on Terran R: solving challenges in real time, optimizing for scale, and constantly improving processes. As the vehicle evolves, so will the factory, with opportunities to apply automation, machine learning, and advanced technologies. Provide Design for Manufacturing feedback to structures teams during the development phase and through the first prototype and flight builds **About You:** - Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing, mechanical engineering, or other engineering discipline - 1+ years progressive and related experience required, including internship experience - A history of improving manufacturing processes and the ability to independently identify and lead development projects needed to meet processing requirements - Strong engineering fundamentals in process improvement, forming, metallic processing, mechanics of materials - Deep knowledge of common metallic manufacturing processes, tools, inspection methods and GD&T - Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to interface with engineering and manufacturing groups to understand process constraints and provide design inputs for improved manufacturability - Strong 3D & 2D design/drafting skills per ASME Y14.5M (NX preferred) **Nice to have, but not required:** - Direct experience with roll forming and press brake forming aluminum alloys - New product introduction of an aerospace hardware system into a manufacturing, test, and production system with proven success - Experience in managing projects in a fast-paced environment At Relativity Space, we are committed to transparency and fairness in our compensation practices. role: AI Research Intern: Wireless Foundation Models
description: At Bosch Research in Pittsburgh, we are looking for an enthusiastic research intern to advance the state of the art in foundation models for wireless sensing and perception. The intern will explore how large-scale self-supervised and multimodal learning can enable generalizable representations of human activities and environments from radio-frequency (RF) signals and wireless channel measurements. The research will focus on developing foundation models that learn reusable representations from diverse wireless sensing data and transfer across sensing tasks, environments, devices, and users. Potential applications include human presence detection, activity recognition, motion understanding, and fine-grained behavioral and contextual understanding. The intern will work closely with Bosch researchers on the following responsibilities: Develop novel foundation-model architectures and representation-learning methods for RF signals and wireless channel measurements. Investigate self-supervised, contrastive, generative, and multimodal learning approaches for large-scale wireless sensing data. Study model generalization and adaptation across environments, users, devices, and downstream perception tasks. Develop and evaluate methods for fine-tuning, few-shot learning, or zero-shot transfer to downstream wireless perception applications. Conduct comprehensive experimental evaluations and comparisons with state-of-the-art approaches. Develop a proof-of-concept demonstration of the proposed technology. Summarize research findings and contribute to a high-quality research publication and/or patent application. Required Qualifications: Currently enrolled in a PhD program in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Robotics, or a related field. Strong background in machine learning, deep learning, or representation learning. Experience working with wireless sensing or RF signal data, including channel measurements or related time-series signals. Strong understanding of modern deep-learning architectures and training techniques. 2+ years of programming experience in Python and strong proficiency with PyTorch. Ability to independently design, implement, and evaluate research ideas. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Experience with self-supervised learning, foundation models, transformers, contrastive learning, or generative models. Experience with wireless sensing for applications such as presence detection, activity recognition, localization, or smart-home sensing. Experience collecting and processing wireless channel measurements, complex I/Q samples, signal-strength data, or related RF sensing data. Experience with RF data-acquisition pipelines, wireless signal preprocessing, or time-series feature extraction. Experience with multimodal learning involving wireless signals, language, vision, audio, or other sensor modalities.
