role: 2028 Point72 Academy Investment Analyst Summer Internship Program - US
description: **2028 Point72 Academy Summer Internship — U.S.** Are you a student interested in pursuing a career in investing? If you are graduating between December 2028 and July 2029, we invite you to apply for our 8-week summer internship, taking place from June to August 2028. Launch your investing career in the Point72 Academy, an investment analyst training program designed to prepare you for a potential career on our fundamental equities teams. Since 2015, the Academy has graduated more than 250 analysts onto our platform as of August 2026; some are portfolio managers today. The Point72 Academy Summer Internship combines structured training with real investing experience, including hands-on research on our investment teams. You’ll build the core skills used by public-markets investors and experience firsthand what it’s like to work as an Analyst at Point72. The internship can be your starting point into the full-time Point72 Academy Associate Program. **During the internship, you will:** - Build a foundation in company research, financial analysis, and the skills needed to contribute as an investment analyst - Receive training in accounting, modeling, presenting, and compliance. - Work directly on an investment team, gaining exposure to researching companies and industries alongside our analysts and portfolio managers - Learn how investment ideas are developed, debated, and refined in a live market environment - Receive feedback from Academy coaches as you dive deeper into data analysis and prepare a final investment pitch Explore efficient ways to harness AI in your investment processes and workflows in collaboration with Compliance, Information Security, and the Office of the Co-CIO **About Point72** Point72 is a leading global alternative investment firm led by Steven A. Cohen. Building on more than 30 years of investing experience, Point72 seeks to deliver superior returns for its investors through fundamental and systematic investing strategies across asset classes and geographies. We aim to attract and retain the industry’s brightest talent by cultivating an investor-led culture and committing to our people’s long-term growth. We’re a firm that thrives on ideas, and we’ve found that the Point72 Academy has provided us with diverse viewpoints and perspectives, and we are able to offer support in their growth and development as analysts and portfolio managers. **Who we’re looking for**: We welcome students from all academic disciplines. Your field of study or major is not a determining factor; we're looking for intellectual curiosity, integrity, strong judgment, and an interest in understanding businesses and markets. We want you to apply if you are: - A current student who will graduate from university between December 2028 and July 2029. - Fascinated by research, problem-solving, and analyzing how businesses work across different industries - A clear communicator who can develop a point of view and explain your thinking - Committed to continued success in your academic and professional career with the highest levels of professionalism, integrity, and excellence. - Committed to the highest ethical standards. - Highly self-driven and motivated to explore a career in finance. What to expect: - Your online application, essays, and resume will serve as an introduction to who you are as a candidate. Once you complete the online application, we will begin reviewing your profile. - Selected candidates will then receive an email invitation to participate in a case study, allowing you to showcase your experiences and demonstrate your business acumen. - Following submission and review of your case study, the next step would be an online assessment and virtual one on one interviews with various members of the Academy team, if selected. There is no set application deadline for this position. Candidates are considered as they apply, until the program is at capacity. We strongly encourage you to apply and fulfill all requirements as soon as you feel ready to begin the hiring process. Please note, you may only submit one application to the Academy internship program globally, so only apply to the region you are most interested in. Don't miss this opportunity to kickstart your career in the world of investing with the Point72 Academy. *The annual base salary is $120,000 - $140,000 (USD) which will be prorated based on internship start and end date. Actual compensation offered to the successful candidate may vary from posted hiring based upon geographic location, work experience, education, and/or skill level, among other things.* *Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.* *Please note that any use of GenAI is strictly prohibited when completing this application.*

Overview FIRE’s 10-week, paid Summer Internship Program gives undergraduate students a hands-on opportunity to defend civil liberties and advance free speech. FIRE interns do meaningful work alongside our staff, receive mentorship, participate in weekly seminars with leading experts on freedom of expression, and help execute some of FIRE’s most important student programs of the year. Interns work full-time at FIRE’s Philadelphia office. The 2027 program will run from Tuesday, June 1 through Friday, August 6, 2027. Interns receive a $6,400 stipend and will receive additional compensation for their work as counselors during FIRE’s Free Speech Forum. The program is highly competitive. FIRE typically selects just 8–12 interns from a pool of hundreds of applicants each year. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and students are encouraged to apply early. Applications open October 19, 2026 and close Sunday, January 3, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. ET. Qualifications and Responsibilities FIRE is seeking passionate, team-oriented, and driven undergraduate students with a strong interest in free speech and civil liberties. The internship is open to rising sophomores, juniors, or seniors attending colleges or universities in the United States. All interns are expected to demonstrate excellent research, writing, and communication skills. Strong candidates are responsible, organized, eager to take initiative, and are willing to engage with ideas and viewpoints they may agree with. The ability to work under pressure and a sense of humor are also important. Because interns spend the summer working together closely as a cohort, we also look for candidates who are collaborative, open to feedback, and excited to contribute to a team. FIRE interns: Work closely with our student development, defense, policy reform, legislation, development, and media teams to assist with research and administrative projects. Assist with the planning and execution of the FIRE Student Network Summer Conference , taking place in July 2027 in Philadelphia, and lead educational and interactive sessions for conference attendees. Serve as a residential counselor during the Free Speech Forum, providing supervision, mentorship, and facilitation of educational activities centered on free speech. Have the opportunity to contribute to FIRE’s Newsdesk . Learn the foundational arguments for protecting core rights in our free society through reading and discussion in weekly seminars with FIRE’s staff and other experts on civil liberties. Written responses are evaluated not only on answers given, but also on clarity, style, and quality. We encourage applicants to thoughtfully prepare their responses to the questions. Applications open Monday, October 19, 2026, and close Sunday, January 3, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. ET. The selection process consists of two virtual interview rounds followed by an in-person finalist interview in Florida. Finalists will interview with FIRE staff and participate in FIRE’s Student Development Conference. FIRE covers travel and lodging for candidates invited to the final interview. 2027 Selection Timeline October 19, 2026: Applications open January 3, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. ET: Applications close By January 20, 2027: Finalists invited to the in-person interview round February 25–27, 2027: Final interviews and Student Development Conference in Florida Beginning March 5, 2027: Offers extended Questions about FIRE’s Summer Internship Program can be sent to . Frequently Asked Questions 1. What does an average day in the life of a FIRE intern look like? Interns typically start the day by catching up on and discussing recent news. Throughout the day, interns collaborate with various FIRE staffers in helping to support FIRE’s response to breaking news and our ongoing defense of free speech. Interns work both individually and in teams, and are involved in a variety of functions. This includes everything from development and conference planning to education and outreach. Interns also take part in educational sessions with FIRE’s staff and free speech experts. 2. Is the FIRE internship open to high school students, graduate students, law students, or international students? No. At this time, the internship is open only to undergraduate students who will be rising sophomores, juniors, or seniors and who attend colleges or universities in the United States. For information about other opportunities at FIRE, please visit our jobs page. 3. Will FIRE provide housing? No. Housing and transportation during the internship are the responsibility of individual interns. FIRE’s office is centrally located in Philadelphia, with a variety of housing and public transportation options nearby. Past interns have found summer housing through university housing programs, sublets, and local housing groups. 4. Can I complete the internship remotely or in a hybrid format? No. The Summer Internship Program is fully in person at FIRE’s Philadelphia office. 5. What are the required hours? The internship requires a full-time commitment of 40 hours per week. FIRE’s regular office hours are Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Interns must be available for the entire 10-week program, from June 1 through August 6, 2027. 6. Are the start and end dates flexible? No. Interns must participate for the full 10-week term, and we cannot accommodate adjustments to the program’s start or end dates. The cohort experience is an important part of the internship and we want all interns to begin and complete the program together. The summer has a full calendar of speakers, seminars, conferences, and professional development opportunities.For those reasons, interns should not plan vacations or other extended time away during the program. 7. Is previous camp counselor experience required? No. Previous camp counselor experience is not required. Because FIRE interns serve as counselors during the Free Speech Forum, prior experience as a camp counselor, resident adviser, teacher, coach, mentor, or in a similar supervisory role can strengthen an application. However, we encourage qualified students to apply regardless of whether they have held a counselor position before. 8. What does the interview process look like? The interview process consists of two virtual interview rounds followed by an in-person finalist interview in Florida. Finalists will be invited to Florida to interview with FIRE staff and participate in FIRE’s Student Development Conference. FIRE covers travel and lodging associated with the trip. Additional details will be provided to applicants who advance to the final round. Students who are studying abroad during the final round will have the option to participate virtually via Google Meet. 9. What makes a strong application and FIRE intern? Strong applicants demonstrate excellent writing and communication skills, intellectual curiosity, initiative, and an interest in free speech and civil liberties. We also look for candidates who enjoy working with a team, and are receptive to feedback. Successful interns are self-starters who seek out ways to contribute and are just as willing to handle a small task as they are to lead a major project.

Shield AI may be the place for you. Your work may include a focus on gearbox development and integration, including gears, shafts, bearings, housings, lubrication systems, and related interfaces. Complete defined design tasks involving component sizing, material selection, tolerance analysis, and mechanical packaging - Perform foundational structural, kinematic, and machine-design calculations with guidance from senior engineers - Help build, inspect, test, and iterate prototype hardware for functionality, performance, and reliability - Support pre-production builds, aircraft integration, and ground and flight testing - Investigate well-defined technical issues, document findings, and contribute to root-cause and corrective-action activities - Ability to create or interpret basic engineering drawings - Familiarity with dimensional tolerancing and GD&T fundamentals - Ability to perform foundational engineering calculations and clearly document assumptions and results - Hands-on interest in designing, building, integrating, or testing mechanical hardware - Strong problem-solving, organization, documentation, and communication skills - Ability to complete well-defined engineering tasks with guidance from peers and managers - Ability to collaborate effectively, accept feedback, and work in a fast-paced environment with evolving priorities - A demonstrated record of working hard, being trustworthy, holding yourself to high standards, and being kind to others - Ability to obtain an S//SAR-level security clearance is desired ### Preferred qualifications: - Internship, student-team, research, or project experience involving aircraft, UAVs, robotics, automotive systems, or other mechanical products - Coursework or project experience related to gearboxes, gearing, bearings, shafts, splines, seals, lubrication, or rotating machinery - Familiarity with gear geometry, gear-train calculations, bearing selection, or mechanical power transmission - Experience with NX or a similar production CAD platform - Exposure to tolerance stack-ups, mechanical fits, and GD&T application - Exposure to finite element analysis, including static, modal, buckling, or fatigue analysis - Familiarity with MATLAB, Python, or other engineering analysis tools - Hands-on machine-shop, mechanic, fabrication, assembly, or inspection experience through professional, academic, or hobby activities - Exposure to FMEA, design of experiments, root-cause analysis, or reliability testing - Familiarity with additive manufacturing, machining, casting, forging, or other mechanical manufacturing processes - Exposure to RTCA DO-160, MIL-STD-810, structural testing, vibration testing, or mechanism testing - Ability to thrive in startup, R&D, or defense-innovation environments

role: Policy and Government Affairs Spring 2027 Undergraduate Intern
description: World Wildlife Fund (WWF), one of the world’s leading conservation organization, seeks an Undergraduate Policy and Government Affairs Spring 2027 Intern. Interest in conservation and international development issues with a concentration in International Relations, Public Policy, American Government, or Political Science. Interest and willingness to learn about Capitol Hill, the Administration (specifically U.S. Department of Interior, U.S. Department of Agriculture, and U.S. State Department) and non-governmental organizations. Excellent written and verbal communications skills. Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, collaboratively and independently. Strong interpersonal skills crucial for developing working relationships, internally and externally. Strong organizational skills. Attention to detail. ### **About the Role** The Speculative Decoding team at Together AI builds the draft models and algorithms that let large language models generate faster without changing their outputs. Our speculators run in production on frontier open models such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM. Our work sits at the intersection of model training, inference algorithms and serving systems, and we co-design all three to lower the cost and latency of generation. As a research intern, you will dive into open questions in speculative decoding: new drafter architectures and verification schemes, knowledge distillation and training recipes that align draft and target models, and drafters that adapt as traffic shifts. You will train and fine-tune draft models at scale on dedicated GPU clusters, and test your ideas against realistic serving workloads, including long-context and agentic traffic. Projects aim to answer important research questions in speculative decoding, enabling faster generation on frontier models, drafters that keep pace with changing workloads, and robust, reproducible evaluation under real traffic. ### Past Research Speculative decoding research by Together researchers, interns and academic collaborators includes: - [Speculative Speculative Decoding](https://openreview.net/forum?id=aL1Wnml9Ef) (ICLR 2026) - [When RL Meets Adaptive Speculative Training: A Unified Training-Serving System](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06932) (ICML 2026) - [Beat the Long Tail: Distribution-Aware Speculative Decoding for RL Training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13841) (MLSys 2026) ### **Responsibilities** - Research and prototype new efficient speculative decoding algorithms and draft model architectures - Train, fine-tune and distill draft models, and design rigorous experiments to validate hypotheses. - Implement optimized version for serving engines to show efficacy in real world workloads - Communicate the plans, progress, and results of projects to the broader team - Share findings through technical write-ups and blog posts, and help bring successful ideas into production ### **Requirements** - Currently pursuing a Master's or Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field - Strong knowledge of Machine Learning and Deep Learning fundamentals - Hands-on experience training or fine-tuning large models with distributed training frameworks (e.g., Megatron-LM, FSDP) - Familiarity with modern model architectures, such as Mixture-of-Experts and hybrid attention ### Preferred Qualifications - Prior research experience in speculative decoding, efficient inference, or efficient machine learning - Publications at leading conferences in machine learning or systems (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, MLSys) - Experience with knowledge distillation, post-training, or reinforcement learning - Familiarity with LLM serving engines (e.g., vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) - Contributions to open-source machine learning projects ### **About Together AI** Together AI, the AI Native Cloud, is purpose-built for AI engineers. AI application developers get high-performance inference that scales reliably, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for creating frontier-level specialized models, and pre-training at massive scale for fully custom intelligence, all around a marketplace of leading open models that teams can run, adapt, and own. Trusted by Cursor, Decagon, ElevenLabs, Salesforce, and Zoom, Together serves 400+ trillion tokens a month. ### **Internship Program Details** Our internship program runs 12 to 14 weeks, giving you the opportunity to work alongside industry-leading engineers and researchers across multiple teams. This cohort's internship dates span January 4th to April 9th. ### **Compensation** We offer competitive compensation, housing stipends, and other competitive benefits. The estimated US hourly rate for this role is $58 - $70 an hour. Our hourly rates are determined by location, level and role. Individual compensation will be determined by experience, skills, and job-related knowledge. ### **Equal Opportunity** Together AI is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is proud to offer equal employment opportunity to everyone regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, veteran status, and more. For more information about our privacy policy, please visit: ###

**Overview** Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The Agentic Data Memory team at Catalyst Lab is hiring Research Interns to advance Artificial Intelligence (AI) and agentic systems. Our research spans graph-based methods, agent memory and data, workflows and harnesses, loop engineering, and evaluation. You can learn more about Catalyst Lab and its projects at **Responsibilities** Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. Research Interns work on well-defined projects that encourage open exploration and collaboration, guided by dedicated mentors. The Research Internship concludes with a final presentation open to Microsoft employees and, ideally, a peer-reviewed scientific publication. **Qualifications** **Required Qualifications** - Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science or a related STEM field. **Other Requirements** - Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. - In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. **Preferred Qualifications** - 1+ year(s) of research experience in natural language processing, information retrieval, machine learning, graph machine learning, or systems for AI, demonstrated through publications or preprints. - Experience building or evaluating LLM-based agents, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), knowledge graphs, or memory systems for agents is strongly preferred. - Experience designing benchmarks, evaluation protocols, or controlled experiments, including statistical analysis of results, is a significant plus. - 1+ year(s) experience in Python and domain-relevant libraries and frameworks (e.g., PyTorch); familiarity with running experiments on GPU clusters or cloud infrastructure is a plus. - 1+ year(s) experience in Calculus, Probability and Statistics and/or Machine Learning. The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here: Microsoft accepts applications and processes offers for these roles on an ongoing basis throughout the academic calendar (September - April). This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. --- Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. ***\*Due to the nature of projected responsibilities associated with this opportunity, which may require the operation of a motorized vehicle to conduct business on behalf of TKDA, candidates must be at least 21 years of age as of May 28, 2027, to be selected for further consideration.*** If you are an undergraduate pursuing a bachelor’s degree in civil engineering with a strong interest in transportation, and more specifically within the railroad and/or mass transit sector, then we have an exciting opportunity for you to join our team this upcoming summer in Riverside, California! As a member of our Rail team, you will work alongside civil engineers and technicians and become engaged in a variety of active projects for site planning, roadway, utility, parking lot, grading and drainage, storm water management, and track design projects. Our goal will be to expose you to the various stages of a project life cycle from conception through construction so you have a better understanding of the work we do, how we do it, and more importantly, what it would be like to be an engineering consultant. Throughout your internship, you will have the opportunity to contribute to the development of preliminary and final designs using AutoCAD and Civil 3D, and frequently perform calculations for project dimensions and elevations as well as earthwork, utilities, and track quantities. You will also assist with preliminary site assessments and surveys and construction administration responsibilities by working closely with other team members to provide information and feedback on the construction status of projects and any potential construction or design-related challenges that may arise. The ideal candidate would be available to work 40 hours per week with occasional overtime throughout the summer of 2027 from mid-May through mid-August. This position would primarily work from our office in Riverside or an assigned project site; however, there may be instances in which this position would be provided with flexible / hybrid work arrangements. ### Required Qualifications - Undergraduate pursuing a bachelor’s degree in civil engineering with a transportation emphasis. - Strong working knowledge of MS Office Suite applications (Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.). - Previous experience or training with AutoCAD, Civil 3D, or Microstation. - Strong interpersonal skills and effective verbal and written communication skills; Ability to ask questions, engage in discussions with team members, and assist with technical report and specification preparation. - Ability to accurately read and interpret construction documents in accordance with construction activities and requirements. - Ability to work outdoors on active construction sites while carrying up to 40 pounds and standing for extended periods of time to perform observation and inspection responsibilities. - Possess a valid Driver’s License with a clean driving record; Ability to travel as needed for construction administration and site inspections/visits, etc. ### Advantageous Qualifications - General understanding of drafting techniques and construction plan development practices. - Previous experience or coursework related to site design and/or linear design. - Previous experience with construction administration tasks including staking, surveying, inspections, or observations.

description: Role Description The Greenager Program is a San Francisco Recreation and Park Department and Port of San Francisco Youth Stewardship and Leadership program. The program was created and designed to offer teens a chance to play an important role in the community by improving the City’s green spaces, raising awareness, creating place-based projects and/or projects based on issues or themes that participants value and are interested in. The program is for 9th to 11th graders who live in or attend a school in the Tenderloin, Northeast, or Southeast neighborhoods. Greenagers are trained and provided with multiple leadership opportunities. They lead public volunteer service projects, participate in community events, go on fun team excursions, and more. These are general duties for Greenagers (High School Interns): Learn proper tool usage and safety; Learn how to steward the parks of San Francisco; Assist with outreach during community events, including but not limited to setting up, breaking down, and tabling; Participate in appropriate training, lesson plans, and team-building activities; Participate in recreational activities that involve team bonding such as camping overnight, kayaking, rock climbing, etc.; Motivate and support each other to encourage a strong working relationship within the team; Complete forms, surveys and assignments by their due dates; Provide feedback for staff and peer leaders; Be responsible for your time in & out; and Follow proper City and County of San Francisco Respect in the Workplace Policy guidelines and procedures. 1. You must be in 9th to 11th grade for the SFUSD 2026-27 school year and preferably LIVE IN or ATTEND a school in District 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, or 11. Other students who either live in or attend a school within San Francisco may be deemed eligible . District 3: Chinatown District 5: Western Addition, Fillmore District 6: Tenderloin, Treasure Island District 9: Portola, Bernal Heights District 10: Bayview, Hunters Point, Visitacion Valley, Silver Terrace District 11: Excelsior, Crocker Amazon *These are not full lists of the neighborhoods in each district—please look up your supervisory district if you do not see your neighborhood listed on: . 2. You must have a current Social Security number - required for City and County employment. Successful candidates will be required to obtain a Work Permit. A 2.0 GPA or higher may be required for a work permit. Students should NOT request a work permit at this time until notified of a job offer. Desirable Qualification Possession of at least 3 hours of volunteer work experience with SF Rec and Park or any organization in the Bay Area. (Verification of volunteer hours may be required upon request.) What else should I know? All dates below are tentative and may be subject to change. Race and Social Equity Statement We believe that parks and open space in San Francisco provides the opportunity to model equitable access for all. With this belief, San Francisco became the first city in the United States for which 100% of its residents live within a ten-minute walk of a park. The Recreation and Park Department’s goal is to close the gaps and improve equity and access to quality parks and open space, and recreation activities for historically marginalized communities. We envision a department that proactively infuses racial and social equity in its internal operations. With a multi-disciplinary team of talented individuals - gardeners, recreation leaders, park rangers, custodians, craft shop personnel, park and recreation managers and more, the department is committed to doing its part to provide equitable access to parks and programs for all the communities we serve to enjoy, as well as foster a work environment where our differences are celebrated, and everyone has what they need to thrive regardless of their race, age, ability, gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, or country of origin. The City and County of San Francisco encourages women, minorities and persons with disabilities to apply. Applicants will be considered regardless of their sex, race, age, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition (associated with cancer, a history of cancer, or genetic characteristics), HIV/AIDS status, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, military and veteran status, or other protected category under the law. The San Francisco Recreation & Park Department is now accepting applications for 9910 Greenager Program for Spring 2027. Interested applicants are encouraged to apply immediately. In addition to submitting an online application, applicants MUST complete AND submit a Supplemental Questionnaire . Instructions can be found under the 'HOW TO APPLY' section of this job announcement. ONLY applicants who submit both an online application AND the Supplemental Questionnaire will be considered for participation in the department's selection process. We offer First-Year and Second-Year positions: First-Year Greenagers are those who have never completed the program before. Duties include habitat restoration, participating in environmental education activities, working with volunteers, presenting on a community research project, and learning how to lead volunteer days. Second-Year Greenagers are those who have graduated from the program previously. Duties include completing the daily program summary, planning a project day, providing feedback for staff, mentoring First-Year Greenagers, conducting evaluations for their mentees, leading the First-Year Greenagers in icebreakers, restoration, and environmental education activities. Previous Greenager graduates are welcome to apply for the Second-Year positions. Application Opening : October 16, 2026 Application & Supplemental Questionnaire Deadline: FILE IMMEDIATELY. Applications may close at any time but not before October 30, 2026, 5:00 pm . Compensation : $25.00 hourly Appointment Type : This position is a temporary exempt, as-needed appointment. This position is seasonal and will not result in an eligible list for a permanent civil service position. Employees serve at the will of the Appointing Officer. Amid a dynamic and ever-evolving urban landscape, the San Francisco Recreation and Park Department stewards one of the premier urban park systems in America. In 2017, San Francisco became the first city in the nation where all residents have access to a park within a 10-minute walk, a direct result of the Department’s commitment to increasing and improving parkland in the city Learn More . Considered by San Franciscans to be one of the City’s most popular and effective public agencies, our Department currently manages more than 230 parks, playgrounds and open spaces throughout San Francisco, including two outside city limits—Sharp Park in Pacifica and Camp Mather in the High Sierras. The system includes full-complex recreation centers, swimming pools, golf courses, sports fields and numerous small-to-medium-sized clubhouses that offer a variety of sports- and arts-related recreation programs for people of all ages. Included in the Department’s responsibilities are Golden Gate Park, Coit Tower, the Marina Yacht Harbor, the San Francisco Zoo and Lake Merced. More than 2,000 talented individuals are part of our team, from gardeners, foresters, and recreation leaders to park rangers, custodians, electricians, painters and more. Our core mission, as it has been throughout our history, is to provide opportunities for San Francisco residents and visitors alike to gather, play, learn, relax, and enjoy nature in the city.

The NYC Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) protects public health and the environment by supplying clean drinking water, collecting and treating wastewater, and reducing air, noise, and hazardous materials pollution. DEP is the largest combined municipal water and wastewater utility in the country, with nearly 5,500 employees. DEP delivers more than 1.1 billion gallons per day of the highest quality drinking water to 8.3 million NYC residents and more than 1 million people in Upstate New York and has a wastewater conveyance and treatment system capable of processing over 1.3 billion gallons of wastewater per day to protect the environment and the city's surrounding waterways. The Bureau of Environmental Compliance's mission is the enforcement of environmental laws and regulations, which affect the health and safety of the public and environment. Specifically, the bureau enforces the City's Asbestos regulations as well as the Air and Noise Codes. The Bureau is comprised of the Division of Air & Noise Policy, Permitting and Enforcement and the Asbestos Control Program. These divisions respond to; air and noise code complaints; inspect and track asbestos removal projects; and foster the goals of environmental protection. The Environmental Engineering Intern will perform technical duties in support of the New York City Air Pollution Control Program. The selected candidate will receive training and develop proficiency in performance of the following duties: examine application requests to register and operate combustion and industrial process equipment; performs field inspections, including use of testing instrumentation of equipment to be permitted; preparing technical reports related to field inspections and other technical and regulatory matters; may also be assigned other duties related to stationary air pollution source control; inspecting premises and construction sites in connection with issuance of pertinent permits; inspecting an installation to assure adherence to specifications, plans and work permits; conducting engineering analysis and write preliminary report of new technologies presented to the Department. Valid NYS Driver's License is mandatory. role: Rotational Security Officer (1 week on / 1 off, plus Benefits) - FedEx Anchorage
description: Job Description The Security Officer provides services for a variety of large and small business clients where health, safety, and security is our #1 priority. This is a public environment at the FedEx Shipping Center and surrounding areas with the corresponding levels of traffic (employees, visitors, customers, etc.). The schedule for this position is a rotational one (1) week on / one (1) week off schedule. The work week is Monday-Sunday, 12 hours a day working either 6:00am-6:00pm or 6:00pm-6:00am. Responsibilities Personally monitors either visually, electronically or audibly a variety of assigned areas, or grounds by working in a variety of assignments including but not limited to roving inside the facilities, roving in a vehicle, other locations deemed appropriate. Ensures own actions and those of others observe maximum level of safety and compliance. Will verbally de-escalate situations to ensure the safety of fellow employees, customers, and clients. Examines doors, windows, and other areas of the store to determine they are secure. Reports and records data such as property damage, unusual occurrences, accordance with company policies and procedures. Warns violators of rule infractions and may apprehend or expel violators. Notifies on site individuals of visitors wishing to see them. Assists in properly responding to a variety of emergencies or disasters in order to preserve life and property, including but not limited to fire safety, active shooter protocol May perform routine input or monitoring of safety and life support computer programs. May issue and record ID badges. May check heating, lighting, sprinkling, security, ventilation, fire, etc., systems to make sure they are operational. May also be combined with other position duties. Notify supervisor is safety and sanitation standards are not being met. This position has no supervisory responsibilities. Other duties that are pertinent to the department or unit’s success also may be assigned. Qualifications High school diploma or GED equivalent. At least two (2) years of security, law enforcement or military experience. A valid Driver’s License and an acceptable driving record for the past three (3) years to be eligible under NMS’ vehicle insurance policy. Must pass background check to obtain a Security Identification Display Area (SIDA) badge. Must be able to obtain and pay the Alaska Guard License fee of $98.25 prior to beginning work. Must be able to cooperate and work as part of a team with fellow employees, customers, and clients. Must be able to make decisions in the moment with little to no supervision. Must be able to be on your feet for 12 hours per shift for the scheduled rotation. Contract requires employees to speak, understand, read and write English. Must be safety oriented as this is a safety sensitive position. Must meet and adhere to all safety guidelines and regulations set forth by the company and client. Working Conditions and Physical Requirements Weather: Indoor/Outdoor. Frequently exposed to arctic conditions. Noise level: Moderate to Loud Description of environment: This is a public aviation facility. Must constantly be able to stand, walk, climb, push, pull use hands and arms, stoop, kneel and crouch. Physical requirements: Must be able to lift and move up to 50lbs. Must be able to work a rotational week on / week off schedule with 12 hour shifts.

description: AECOM is hosting an exclusive, invitation-only hiring event in Arlington on November 18-19, 2026. You’ll also have the chance to meet other students, recent graduates, and AECOM professionals from across our business lines. On Thursday, interviews will take place at our Arlington office. Conducts engineering design under the supervision of an experienced engineer. Creates designs, calculations, sketches, diagrams, schematic drawings, and final working drawings under the supervision of an experienced engineer. Collects and analyzes data under the supervision of an experienced engineer. Uses computer software as a tool for solving basic engineering problems. Performs work in accordance with agreed upon budget and schedule under supervision. Minimum Requirements: Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering or related field. Prior experience in field assessments or site visits for civil engineering projects. Relocation assistance is not available for this position. Do you excel at navigating complex processes, building strong relationships, and finding thoughtful solutions in a busy university environment? The University of Southern Maine invites you to bring your expertise to the College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences. We are seeking a student-centered Director of Academic Administration and Student Services to manage the day-to-day operations of the College Dean’s Office. Working closely with the Dean, academic departments, faculty, staff, and student support teams, you will coordinate essential academic processes, help resolve student-related matters, and strengthen the systems that support teaching and learning. This role calls for independent judgment, discretion, strong communication, and an ability to balance competing priorities. Key responsibilities include: Managing academic administrative operations, policies, procedures, course scheduling coordination, and catalog updates. Coordinating and tracking curriculum proposals, academic reviews, special projects, and new initiatives. Overseeing Polymath Pathways coordination, including curricular, scheduling, and student-support needs. Managing graduation certifications, academic actions, student appeals, and other matters requiring Dean’s Office review. Providing academic approvals for standardized forms, including program and grade changes and course withdrawals. Responding to student questions and concerns and collaborating with advising, registration, and academic departments. Working with the Dean and Associate Deans to support undeclared students in exploring and declaring majors. Compiling reports and analyzing enrollment and academic data using MaineStreet and other University systems to support planning. Coordinating Dean’s Office communications, events, meetings, records, and operational logistics. Improving administrative workflows, supporting budget and scholarship account tracking, and supervising assigned staff or student workers as needed. Pay and Benefits This is a full-time, in-person position based on our Portland Campus. This position offers an annual salary of $58,000.00. Candidates must reside within a 90-minute commutable distance from the USM campuses. This requirement is essential for the ability to participate in supporting and building upon the university culture of "student focused every day" and allows for regular participation in on-campus activities, meetings, and fulfills the responsibilities of the role effectively. The University of Southern Maine offers highly competitive benefits for full-time and eligible part-time employees that includes (but is not limited to): 13 paid holidays plus earned vacation time and sick time. Health, dental and vision insurance. Short-term and long-term disability insurance. Basic life insurance and supplemental life insurance. A tuition waiver program for employees and their spouse or dependent child(ren). A 403(b)-retirement plan. Free access to the METRO system, including the Husky Line with service between our Portland and Gorham campuses. See the Benefits Information Summary for details. About the University of Southern Maine The University of Southern Maine is a vibrant academic community located in the greater Portland, Maine area, including campuses in Portland, Gorham, Lewiston, and online. USM is part of the University of Maine System and offers a comprehensive array of undergraduate and graduate programs, emphasizing hands-on learning, community engagement, and interdisciplinary collaboration. With a highly engaged student-centered learning environment, USM is a steward of higher education, helping drive the economic, cultural, and civic life in the communities where our campuses are located and beyond. USM is committed to providing expanded access to high-quality education that elevates economic opportunity and contributes significantly to the vitality of a diverse society. To learn more about USM, visit About Our University . The University of Southern Maine fosters a welcoming and supportive campus environment that respects and appreciates varied perspectives, enhancing teaching, learning, personal growth, and overall institutional achievement. role: Program Manager II, NAST GoCarts Management , Scheduling Transfers And Reusables
description: Come build the version of GoCarts logistics that schedules itself. Every day, our network moves tens of thousands of GoCarts between fulfillment, sortation, and repair sites, and every one of those moves is a promise, that the right GoCarts show up at the right site before it runs short. When that promise is at risk, the GoCarts scheduling team is the one that catches it. We're good at catching. We need a Program Manager to help us build for the day we don't have to. GoCarts scheduling is the layer that keeps the network solvent in reusable assets. We own the proactive planning that places GoCarts before sites feel the gap, the reactive intervention that resolves shortages in real time, and — this is the part that matters — the mechanisms that make those interventions unnecessary. Our hardest problems aren't scheduling problems. They're throughput, visibility, and signal problems, and we're moving the whole program from reactive execution to proactive, data-driven decision-making. In this role you will: Own outcomes, not status decks. Build mechanisms, not workarounds. Automate what you touch. Turn bottlenecks into asks leadership can act on. Key job responsibilities - Own the end-to-end health of the GoCarts scheduling program across proactive and reactive tracks, and the metrics that define it: asset solvency, defective-asset rate, trailer dwell, and fill rate. - Drive peak-season readiness, including solvency targets, defective-asset reduction, injection plans, and contingency strategy, and manage the tradeoffs between them. - Diagnose true network constraints, separating the real bottleneck (for example, repair throughput) from the symptom (scheduling), and build the data and business case to resolve it with the right owners. - Manage cross-functional dependencies with repair and capacity partners, holding partner commitments to committed dates and escalating risk clearly and early. - Close data-visibility gaps with partner data teams, improving scan compliance and site-level inventory signals so scheduling runs on actuals rather than assumption. - Partner with science and automation teams to advance the roadmap toward continuous demand-versus-inventory detection, alerting, and model-driven resolution. - Author crisp, data-backed narratives for senior leadership that frame risk, ownership, the ask, and the plan forward. - Develop and own KPI reporting across the program portfolio, with clear visibility into milestones and performance.

ABOUT THE NEW YORK ACADEMY OF SCIENCES The New York of Academy of Sciences is an independent, not-for-profit organization that since 1817 has been committed to advancing science for the benefit of society. With more than 20,000 Members in 100 countries, the Academy advances scientific and technical knowledge, addresses global challenges with science-based solutions, and sponsors a wide variety of educational initiatives at all levels for STEM and STEM related fields. The Academy hosts programs and publishes content in life and physical sciences, the social sciences, nutrition, artificial intelligence, computer science, and sustainability. The Academy also provides professional and educational resources for researchers across all phases of their careers. The position will have primary responsibility for managing the day-to-day operations of the Leon Levy Fellowships in Neuroscience program, assist with the planning and delivery of professional learning and career-development opportunities for STEM professionals, and support the development and expansion of the Academy's fellowships and professional learning portfolios. The Program Manager will work closely with program participants, speakers, mentors, scientific advisors, partner institutions, funders, and colleagues across the Academy to coordinate high-quality programming and participant experiences. ESSENTIAL DUTIES: Fellowships & Professional Learning (Approximately 80%) Manage the day-to-day operations of the Leon Levy Fellowships in Neuroscience program, including fellow onboarding, program schedules, seminars, mentorship activities, professional development opportunities, symposia, and reporting requirements. Support the planning and execution of award ceremonies, scientific symposia, and related events in collaboration with the Awards team and other Academy stakeholders. Collaborate with Marketing, Communications, Development, Events, Finance, and other Academy departments to support program promotion, fundraising activities, reporting, and related initiatives. Experience working with scientists, researchers, fellows, trainees, or other STEM professionals at various career stages. The Fellowship provides a space in which participants can experience a variety of job functions and thereby refine their professional pathway. role: Research Intern - Efficient AI Software Systems
description: **Overview** Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. Researchers in artificial intelligence (AI) are building systems that can reason, plan and act on behalf of the people who use them, from writing software to automating complex, multistep tasks. As these systems become more capable and more widely used, making them efficient matters more and more. That means getting the most value from the compute they use, choosing the right capabilities for each task, and adapting to the needs of the people and environments they serve. Microsoft's deep investments in the field are advancing the state of the art in efficient and agentic AI. Its researchers combine machine learning, systems research and rigorous empirical evaluation to understand how intelligent systems can balance quality, speed and cost, and how they can improve with experience. The research, tools and services that result are woven into existing and new products and, at the same time, made open and accessible to the broader community in a bid to accelerate innovation, democratize AI and help developers and organizations do more with the resources they have. **Responsibilities** Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. **Qualifications** #### Required Qualifications - Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science, STEM, or a relevant field. #### **Other Requirements** - Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. - In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. #### #### Preferred Qualifications - 1+ year(s) of experience (classroom or work-related) in one or more of the following areas: machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, large language models, AI agents, or machine learning systems. - 1+ completed courses in probability and statistics, machine learning, or optimization. - Experience conducting research on the efficiency, cost, or performance of machine learning models or systems (e.g., inference optimization, model selection, model compression, or adaptive computation). - Experience building or evaluating applications or agents that use large language models. - Experience designing benchmarks or experiments to evaluate machine learning systems, and analyzing quantitative results. - Experience comparing alternative methods, prototypes, or analytical approaches to address a research or applied problem. - Experience collaborating with researchers or engineering teams on a research or applied project. - Prior research experience evidenced by publications, preprints, or open-source research projects. - Experience communicating research findings through a presentation, poster, report, or publication. The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here: Microsoft accepts applications and processes offers for these roles on an ongoing basis throughout the academic calendar (September - April). This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. --- Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, citizenship, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, immigration status, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran or military status, race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances. We’re a team of friends bound together by a mission to preserve our planet for future generations through innovative energy solutions and modern infrastructure. Intersect develops, constructs, and operates the most ambitious power and data center infrastructure in the country by co-locating industrial demand with dedicated gas and renewable power generation. Intersect was acquired by Google in March 2026 and operates as an independent subsidiary. We are developing and constructing multiple gigawatts of energy and data center projects in the U.S., enabling more data center and generation capacity to come online faster. We’re on an aggressive growth trajectory and looking for people hungry to tackle the largest energy challenges on the planet. **Location & Team Gatherings** Intersect has been a fully flexible workplace since its founding in 2016. We’ve been very intentional about the way we do things. We are not work-from-home, hybrid, or in-office - we are any and all of those options! Deepening social connections and offering shared experiences is a cornerstone of the way we work. We connect as a team at our Team Week experiences four times a year and at our recently established Hub locations - SF Bay Area, NYC Metro Area, NY; Denver, CO; Austin, TX; Calgary, AB; and Toronto, ON. We are currently looking for candidates located within 60 miles of any of the listed hubs to foster more in-person connections while maintaining our flexible remote culture. **About this role** As a Campus Project Director on Intersect's Construction team, you'll oversee the complete execution and delivery of multi-facility clean energy campuses designed to power Google data centers. You will lead complex, multi-technology buildouts encompassing utility-scale solar, wind, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and high-voltage substation and transmission infrastructure, serving as the single point of accountability for site performance, vendor integration, and executive reporting. You will collaborate closely with internal engineering, procurement, asset management, and executive leadership, as well as external EPC partners and hyperscale client stakeholders. By deploying modern construction management platforms and leveraging clear, strategic communication, you'll drive operational excellence while ensuring safety and quality standards across all sites. **Team overview** This team plays a critical role in advancing Intersect's mission to accelerate the clean energy transition. The Construction team partners across development, engineering, procurement, and operations to build resilient, gigawatt-scale power infrastructure that energizes critical digital infrastructure. Joining this team means directing high-impact energy campuses from earthworks to commercial operation, shaping how clean energy powers the future of computing while growing alongside a dedicated group of industry leaders. **What you'll do** Direct Multi-Technology Campus Execution - Lead end-to-end site delivery for multi-facility energy campuses combining solar, wind, BESS, and high-voltage transmission scope. - Manage and mentor Campus Project Managers, serving as their primary escalation point and holding overall accountability for the success of the campus as a whole. - Establish site governance, schedule baselines, and budget oversight across simultaneous project builds powering Google data center infrastructure. - Incorporate advanced field management tools, including Terabase Construct and AI Clearing, to track site progress, optimize craft sequencing, and ensure quality. Drive High-Voltage Integration and Technical Compliance - Oversee the seamless integration of high-voltage substations, interconnection facilities, and generation assets into active grid and off-grid interconnections. - Troubleshoot complex engineering, procurement, and field bottlenecks alongside technical experts to maintain strict commercial operation timelines. - Evaluate natural gas power integration options where applicable to enhance campus resilience and microgrid performance. Lead Executive Communication and Strategic Stakeholder Alignment - Synthesize high-density technical, financial, and schedule data into executive-ready slide decks for leadership and key off-taker stakeholders. - Deliver regular strategic briefings to executive leadership detailing campus health, risk contingencies, and critical path milestones. - Maintain strong working relationships with EPC firms, key equipment vendors, utilities, and local regulatory authorities. Strengthen Safety, Cost, and Operational Culture - Enforce rigorous safety programs across all campus sites, cultivating an environment that prioritizes total personnel well-being. - Manage financial workflows using Stampli and internal financial tools to control capital expenditure, change orders, and contract compliance. - Utilize generative AI platforms such as Claude and Gemini to streamline reporting workflows, executive briefing prep, and team documentation. **What you'll bring** - Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Civil/Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline. - 10+ years of project management experience in power generation, with 3+ years specifically as a Project Director leading utility-scale clean energy projects. - Proven track record delivering complex campus-scale builds featuring solar, wind, BESS, and high-voltage (HV) scope; natural gas experience is a plus. - Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex technical challenges and produce executive-level presentation decks for C-suite leadership and external client stakeholders. - Proficiency with modern construction, workflow, and AI tools including Terabase Construct, AI Clearing, Stampli, Lucidchart, G Suite, Claude, and Gemini. - Willingness to travel up to 50% to active campus sites with a minimum once-a-month onsite footprint. - Strong team builder and strategic thinker with an adaptable leadership style focused on cross-functional alignment and field enablement. - Deep commitment to long-term value, safety, and authentic leadership, fully aligned with Intersect's core values: Equity, Humility, Authenticity, Long-run Value, and People Come First.

We are seeking a Junior Scheduler / Project Controls Consultant to support our growing project advisory and construction consulting practice. This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career professional with hands-on experience developing and maintaining construction schedules who is looking to expand their capabilities in project controls, schedule analysis, and construction advisory. The successful candidate will ideally have approximately two years of experience working with a general contractor, construction manager, specialty contractor, or similar construction organization, with direct exposure to developing, updating, and managing construction schedules. The role will support projects across the building and infrastructure sectors and will work closely with senior schedulers, project controls professionals, project managers, and technical experts. Key Responsibilities Assist in the development, review, and maintenance of detailed construction project schedules. Develop and update Critical Path Method (CPM) schedules based on project scope, construction sequencing, and contractor work plans. Support preparation of baseline schedules, schedule updates, recovery schedules, and short-term look-ahead schedules. Review contractor schedule submissions for completeness, logic, sequencing, durations, and compliance with project requirements. Monitor project progress and incorporate actual progress into schedule updates. Identify critical and near-critical activities, schedule constraints, and potential impacts to project milestones. Assist with analysis of schedule variances and changes to the critical path. Work with project teams to collect schedule information, progress data, and supporting documentation. Assist in preparing schedule narratives, progress reports, schedule graphics, and management presentations. Support schedule impact assessments and preliminary delay analyses under the direction of senior scheduling and claims professionals. Assist with evaluating change orders and potential time impacts. Review project documentation, including drawings, specifications, contracts, progress reports, RFIs, submittals, and change documentation, to understand project sequencing and schedule impacts. Participate in project meetings and schedule review meetings with clients, contractors, designers, and other project stakeholders. Support broader project controls activities, including progress measurement, reporting, cost and schedule integration, and project performance analysis. Maintain clear and organized documentation supporting schedule updates and analyses. Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Construction Engineering, Architecture, or a related field. Approximately 2 or more years of relevant construction industry experience, preferably working for a general contractor, construction manager, or specialty contractor. Practical experience developing or maintaining construction schedules. Understanding of construction sequencing, project milestones, and the relationship between design, procurement, and construction activities. Basic understanding of Critical Path Method (CPM) scheduling principles. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to organize and analyze project information and communicate findings clearly. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. Ability to work collaboratively as part of a multidisciplinary project team. Preferred Experience using Oracle Primavera P6. Experience with Microsoft Project or other scheduling/project controls software. Experience working on commercial buildings, healthcare, higher education, transportation, infrastructure, or other complex construction projects. Exposure to schedule review, delay analysis, change-order evaluation, or construction claims. Familiarity with construction drawings, specifications, contracts, and project documentation. Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification or interest in pursuing professional certification is a plus. Ideal Candidate The ideal candidate has started their career working directly within the construction industry and understands how projects are actually planned and built. They have had hands-on exposure to construction scheduling and are interested in developing deeper expertise in project controls, schedule analysis, and construction advisory . This position is particularly well suited to someone who has spent the first few years of their career with a contractor or construction manager and is interested in transitioning into a consulting environment where they can work across multiple projects, clients, and construction sectors. What You Will Develop In this role, you will have the opportunity to develop expertise in: Advanced CPM scheduling Primavera P6 Construction schedule review and analysis Project controls and performance reporting Schedule risk and critical path analysis Change and delay analysis Construction claims and dispute support Project advisory and owner representation You will work alongside experienced construction, engineering, scheduling, and project controls professionals and gain exposure to complex projects from both the contractor and owner perspectives. For more information, please visit Job Type: Full Time (4 days a week in office with one hybrid/ remote day) The position may be based in our Atlanta, New York, or Boston office. Some travel to project sites and client offices may be required depending on project assignments. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. role: Associate Consultant - Entry-Level Clinical Data Technology Consulting
description: Veeva’s Consultant Development Program (CDP) is an accelerated pathway that transforms early-career professionals into high-impact consultants who deliver cloud and AI solutions, helping global Life Sciences companies bring life-changing therapies to patients. ### The Role You’ll work hands-on with innovative Clinical Data Management technology, collaborating directly with internal teams and external customers to design, configure, and implement our clinical data software. In this role, you’ll learn our industry-leading clinical trial cloud platforms and work with cutting-edge AI solutions to transform how life sciences companies manage clinical trial data. Empowered from day one by a team-first culture, you will accelerate your career growth as a technical consultant who thrives in an environment where we work hard for our customers and each other. ### The Program As part of the Consultant Development Program, you will: - **Ramp up quickly:** Your journey begins with an intensive, team-based onboarding program that combines hands-on learning, transparent feedback, and active collaboration to develop the consulting skills and industry knowledge to make an impact right away. - **Learn by doing:** You won't be watching from the sidelines. You will take on real responsibility and work directly with customers to solve clinical data management problems within your first three months. - **Thrive together:** Grow alongside a supportive team of seasoned leaders and peers who actively champion your development through open communication and actionable feedback. - **Build your future:** Advance from Associate to Consultant in less than 2 years. More importantly, you’ll develop the foundation for a successful, long-term career where you can continually expand your technical expertise, lead complex projects, and evolve with our global and diverse team. ### What You'll Do As part of our Professional Services team, you are a strategic partner guiding clinical operations and data management teams through implementation. We will teach you how our CDMS software works, and you will use that knowledge to design, configure, and deliver solutions that drive real business value]. Your day-to-day will involve: - **Designing & tailoring the software:** You will lead the configuration of our Vault CDMS platform to fit each customer's unique clinical trial requirements—setting up study workflows, structuring clinical data models, and aligning system capabilities to study protocols. - **Conducting discovery workshops:** You will lead interactive discovery workshops with customer stakeholders (e.g., Clinical Data Managers, CRCs, CRAs) to gather business requirements, map out existing data management workflows, and translate their vision into actionable technical specifications. - .**Managing project scope & execution:** You will take ownership of core implementation deliverables by scoping study requirements, building timeline estimates, and keeping project milestones on track from study design through go-live. - **Guiding the customer as an expert:** You will lead the customer with best practices to ensure their clinical data collection and study management processes are optimized for maximum long-term value. ### What We Are Looking For | We are open to graduates of a variety of backgrounds and look for a specific mindset: **Education & Preferred Background** A Bachelor's or Master's degree in a quantitative or life science field is preferred, such as: - Biomedical Engineering, Health Informatics, Bioinformatics, Biostatistics, Data Science, Computer Science, Engineering - Clinical Research, Public Health, Biology, Pharmacology **Desired Experience** Prior experience (internships, co-ops, academic projects, or entry-level roles) in one or more of the following areas is highly valued: - Data entry or management in a healthcare/research setting, or experience at a CRO, as a Clinical Research Associate (CRA), or Clinical Research Coordinator (CRC) - Clinical trial operations, monitoring, or clinical data management - Data analysis using statistical software (SAS, SPSS, Python, R) - Design training, UX Design, or Human Factors Studies - Business or technical consulting - Speech and Debate or Manufacturing **Technical Skills & Mindset** - **Technical Familiarity:** Basic familiarity with database concepts. For example, SQL for querying relational databases and Python or R for data manipulation and analysis - **Drive:** You thrive in a challenging, intense environment that rewards initiative and rapid learning - **Curiosity:** You have a genuine desire to be hands-on with software and master new technologies - **Communication:** You are fluent in English with excellent verbal and written communication skills - **Analytical Mindset:** You are a strong critical thinker with a proven track record of analytical performance - **Integrity:** Veeva is a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) and a “do the right thing” company, and we expect that from all employees - **Work Ethic:** A commitment to excellence and passion for working hard to achieve results - **Travel:** Willingness to travel as needed (up to 20-30% of the time) - **Experience:** Open to recent graduates of Bachelor's or Master's programs (up to 2 years postgraduate experience maximum) ### How We Hire | Our process is different from most. It is designed to be fast, efficient and respectful. Here are the steps: - **Apply:** Submit your resume, a short cover letter, and take a quick personality test. - **Fast Response:** We will notify you of your next step typically within one week. - **Interview & Case:** Interview with a Veeva leader. If successful, we will give you a real-world scenario (with 3 days to prepare) to present to our team. - **Offer:** We make decisions quickly—usually within a week of your final presentation. ### Perks & Benefits - Medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance - Flexible PTO and company paid holidays - Retirement programs - 1% charitable giving program ### Compensation - Starting Salary: $80,000 USD - Perform well, and in one year you’ll receive a compensation increase and participate in our bonus program
