# **About Us** At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale. With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world. Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, , Nvidia, and Bridgewater. # **About the Team** This team works directly with companies building and running AI agents in production, helping turn ideas and prototypes into systems teams can rely on. This is a hands-on, highly technical team that partners closely with customer engineers across the full lifecycle, from pre-sales evaluations to post-deployment advisory work. The focus is on achieving the technical win, co-designing agent architectures, and helping customers operate agents reliably at scale using the LangChain suite. Deployed Engineers sit at the intersection of **engineering, product, and go-to-market**, shaping how LangChain is adopted in the field and feeding real-world insights back into the platform. # **About the Role** You'll work on some of the hardest problems in applied AI alongside customers. You will help customers adopt innovative new practices in agentic engineering, and ensure they ship reliable agents into production, quickly. The feedback loop is fast, the impact is visible, and your work directly shapes how AI agents are built in the real world. # **What You’ll Do** - Co-architect and co-build production AI agents with customer engineering teams and customers - Own the technical win in pre-sales by designing POCs, answering deep technical questions, and guiding evaluations - Help customers deploy and operate agent-based applications such as conversational agents, research agents, and multi-step workflows - Advise customers post-sale on architecture, best practices, and roadmap-level decisions - Build and run tailored demos, trainings, and workshops for developer audiences - Surface field feedback and contribute reusable patterns, cookbooks, and example code that scale across customers - Interface with LangChain's engineering, product and design (EPD) team to share field perspectives and guide product direction based on customer priorities - Occasionally contribute code upstream when it meaningfully improves customer outcomes - This role requires 40% travel to customer sites to support deployment, onboarding, and ongoing technical engagement # **What You’ll Bring** - **1-3 years of experience** in software engineering, customer engineering, solutions engineering, founding engineering, or a similarly technical role, ideally at a startup or high-growth company - Strong **Python, JavaScript** and systems fundamentals - Hands-on experience building and deploying **agent-based or LLM-powered applications** beyond simple API calls, including multi-step workflows, orchestration, and failure handling - Strong technical communication skills and builder credibility; Can explain technical tradeoffs clearly, translate complex AI concepts into actionable insights, and build trust with technical customers and engineering teams - Excited to work directly with customers during POCs, architecture reviews, and technical evaluations - Take responsibility for **outcomes**, not just recommendations - Have a **bias toward action** and enjoy figuring things out as you go - Are excited about **shipping AI agents in production** ## **Nice to Have’s:** - You’ve deployed **AI agents in production**, especially using **LangChain, LangGraph**, or similar frameworks - Worked with **LLM evaluation, observability, or guardrails** - Have experience with **cloud environments** (AWS, GCP, Azure), containers, and Kubernetes concepts - Have **shipped and operated production software** and are comfortable owning systems under real-world constraints # **Compensation** Annual OTE range: $160,000-185,000 USD **Compensation Philosophy:** We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations. # Benefits Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit [](https://shield.ai/). Follow Shield AI on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai), [X](https://x.com/shieldaitech), [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai), and [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI). ### Job Description: The Hivemind Solutions HIL Infrastructure and Test Engineering Team is seeking an Integration Engineer II to develop and test the systems that bring Hivemind mission autonomy and vision capabilities onto real aircraft. You'll build Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) infrastructure, develop automated tests, and validate mission autonomy software in HIL and Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) environments. You'll also support vision system development through HIL testing and hands on integration of imaging sensors, onboard processing, camera pods, and gimbals for crewed and uncrewed aircraft. Working across software, electrical, and mechanical disciplines, you'll own integration and test tasks from setup through validation, collaborating with experienced engineers to resolve issues and prepare systems for ground and flight testing. We're looking for someone who enjoys building and debugging complex systems, embraces learning, and takes ownership of delivering reliable results. ### What you'll do: - Develop, build, and maintain HIL test infrastructure for mission autonomy and vision systems, including electrical integration, mechanical fixtures, and sensor interfaces, working with engineers and lab technicians. - Create and execute integration, regression, and system test plans for Hivemind mission autonomy software in HIL, SIL, and Vehicle-in-the-Loop (VIL) environments, including simulated flight and mission scenarios. - Build Python tools and automated test utilities for test execution, data collection, and analysis across hardware and simulation environments. - Develop and execute HIL tests for vision systems to validate imaging, onboard processing, detection capabilities, and hardware/software interfaces throughout development and software releases. - Identify, reproduce, and diagnose failures using test data, system logs; collaborate with development teams to resolve issues and verify fixes. - Improve test fixtures, automation, and test coverage through rapid prototyping and repeatable validation methods; document test configurations, procedures, and results. - Install, integrate, and perform functional checkout of vision systems, including camera pods, gimbals, imaging sensors, onboard processing hardware, and supporting electronics on test assets and aircraft. - Load, configure, and validate software and firmware releases; maintain accurate hardware, software, and asset records so lab and field configurations remain reproducible. - Troubleshoot sensor, compute, power, network, and mechanical interfaces using wiring diagrams, pinouts, logs, and test equipment; perform connector inspections, continuity checks, and basic wiring work under established procedures. - Support ground and flight tests, customer demonstrations, and field evaluations through equipment setup, system configuration, data collection, and post-test troubleshooting; communicate findings to engineering teams and mission partners. ### Required qualifications: - Typically requires a minimum of 2 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science, or a related discipline; or a Master's degree without experience; or equivalent practical experience. - Hands-on experience integrating and testing hardware and software in robotics, small UAS, avionics, vision systems, or related engineering projects. - Proficiency in Python for test automation, system utilities, or data analysis. - Practical electrical and mechanical skills, including interpreting wiring diagrams and pinouts and safely using a digital multimeter. - Familiarity with Linux, software installation and configuration, and basic networking concepts. - Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills, with attention to configuration accuracy and clear technical documentation. - Excellent communication and collaboration skills across software, hardware, and mechanical engineering teams, with ownership of assigned work and a willingness to learn new technologies. - Ability to obtain and maintain a SECRET clearance. ### Preferred qualifications: - Experience with HIL, SIL, or VIL testing, simulation environments, or validation of autonomous systems. - Experience with electro-optical or infrared imaging systems, cameras, gimbals, sensor pods, or onboard image processing and detection systems. - Familiarity with C++, Git, automated regression testing, or development pipelines (CI/CD). - Experience with Ethernet, serial communications, CAN, or sensor and compute interfaces. - Exposure to CAD, fixture design, rapid prototyping, or hands-on robotics and aircraft projects. - Experience with oscilloscopes, bench power supplies, cable assembly, connector inspection, or harness troubleshooting. - Experience supporting aircraft integration, field demonstrations, customer deployments, or ground and flight test campaigns.

Who you are This impactful role involves guiding middle and high school students through self-discovery exercises, career exploration, and goal setting to help them realize their potential. As a Career Coach, you will guide in-person workshops and group coaching sessions, using an interactive and engaging approach to inspire students to define and pursue their career aspirations. This role is ideal for individuals passionate about guiding youth and helping students unlock their potential. We are looking for a diverse group of Career Coaches who can work with youth/teenagers, go through our training program and inspire students to find their passion/purpose. Term limit: detailed training is provided, 4-month unpaid internship position that fully meets requirements for school credits/ certifications with hands on experience provided (including projects, hours requirements, hands on experience and all paperwork that goes with it). Essential Duties and Responsibilities Career Guidance and Goal Setting: Assist students in identifying personal interests, strengths, and career goals, helping them to create personalized career development plans and set SMART goals. Facilitating School-based Programming: Lead high-energy, interactive group sessions based on a structured workshop script to engage students in self-discovery and career planning. Student Progress Monitoring: Track and evaluate students’ progress by documenting individual needs, goals, and action steps after each session to ensure continuous development. Advising on Career Pathways: Use assessments to help students evaluate their aptitudes and interests and advise them on relevant educational and career pathways. Building Resilience and Personal Development: Support students in developing resilience and a growth mindset, preparing them to overcome challenges they may face in achieving their career goals. Required Skills Active Listening: Demonstrates excellent listening skills, fully attending to students’ comments and questions to foster a supportive environment. Organizational Skills: Manages multiple responsibilities with strong organizational skills, ensuring each session is well-structured and impactful. Rapport Building: Naturally builds trust and rapport, helping students feel valued, supported, and confident in their potential. Positive Outlook and Motivation: Brings an optimistic attitude and encourages students to reach their full potential, inspiring confidence and resilience. Assertiveness and Decision-Making: Shows confidence in guiding sessions and making timely decisions, following established procedures to support student progress. Diversity-Oriented: Embraces and respects diversity, working inclusively with students of all ages, genders, ethnicities, and backgrounds. Energetic and Enthusiastic: Maintains high energy and enthusiasm in every session, making the career exploration process engaging and exciting for students. Integrity and Trustworthiness: Upholds honesty and integrity, establishing credibility and trust in all interactions. Team Building: Encourages collaborative efforts among students, helping them work together toward shared goals. Self-motivation and Independence: Manages tasks effectively and works autonomously without direct supervision. Additional Information Participation and Availability Weekly at school coaching : Must be able to present 1-2 times a week at a designated school location for several hours. Weekly commitment of 10 hours total. Training: Weekly in-person training is provided to guide through the program. All hours are eligible for ceritification and school credits. Friendly and approachable demeanor with a solid commitment to creating an inclusive and supportive environment. Must be able to pass a background check. Location and Work Authorization Candidates must be based in Atlanta, Georgia and have legal authorization to work or study in U.S. Ideal for students/volunteers with Coaching, Counselling, Teaching, Behaviour Therapy, Training, Summer Camps and similar experiences. What we do Passion for Life is a non for profit organization that operates with the power of dedicated volunteers like you. We help under-resourced youth transform their passions into rewarding careers. Our mission is to provide forward-thinking career coaching and immersion opportunities driven by the student’s passions and talents in a fun, structured, and high-energy environment. Passion for Life was created to be a high-energy and engaging process that helps students identify their passions and gain clarity on how to utilize their core strengths and talents to select a career.

role: *Entry Level Clinical Research Candidates-Talent Community (Detroit, MI)
description: ### **About Profound Research** Profound Research partners with community physicians to offer clinical trials as a therapeutic option for their patients. We handle all infrastructure, regulatory compliance, and administrative operations so physicians can focus on patient care. Our model gives patients access to the newest therapies while maintaining the trusted patient-physician relationship. **Our Mission:**Improving Lives by Providing Advanced Therapeutic Options **Our Vision:**Creating the Absolute Best Patient-Physician Experience in Clinical Research **Our Values:** - **Compassion:**We prioritize the patient-physician relationship, ensuring every interaction is service-oriented and patient-centered. - **Urgency:** We work hard and practice selflessness, acting swiftly and decisively to meet the needs of our patients, partners, and colleagues. - **Solution Orientation:** We embrace challenges with a positive mindset, communicate directly, and identify and implement effective solutions with efficiency. - **Excellence:** We insist on excellence, holding ourselves accountable and empowering each other to deliver best-in-class service while maintaining the highest ethical and scientific standards. # Join Our Talent Community: Build Your Future in Clinical Research Profound Research is building a community of **recent graduates and entry-level professionals who have a foundation in clinical research and are ready to begin or continue building their careers in the field.** This includes individuals who have gained clinical research experience through internships, academic programs, hands-on research experience, or completion of a clinical research fast-track program. ***This is a talent community and expression of interest — not a current job opening.*** By joining the Profound Research **Entry-Level Clinical Research Talent Community**, you'll have the opportunity to introduce yourself to our team and be part of our network of emerging clinical research professionals. As future entry-level opportunities become available, we may connect with individuals in the community whose background, training, interests, location, and experience align with our needs. ## Where Our Talent Community Is Located We are currently building our Entry-Level Clinical Research Talent Community in and around: - Detroit, Michigan - Munster, Indiana - Las Vegas, Nevada - Southern California, including the San Diego area Candidates must currently reside in or around one of these markets to join the community. ## Why Join Our Talent Community? Clinical research brings together science, medicine, patient care, and innovation. At Profound Research, our teams support clinical trials across a variety of therapeutic areas, providing emerging clinical research professionals with the opportunity to apply their existing knowledge while continuing to develop their skills in a real-world research environment. Our research portfolio includes studies in areas such as: - Oncology - Cardiology - Neurology - Dermatology - Vaccines & Infectious Disease - Other evolving therapeutic areas By joining our talent community, you can put yourself on our radar for future opportunities and continue building upon the clinical research knowledge, training, and experience you have already developed. ## What Future Entry-Level Opportunities May Include While specific responsibilities will vary by site, study, and future opportunity, entry-level clinical research professionals may have the opportunity to: Support clinical research studies and participant visits under appropriate supervision. Assist with participant flow, including greeting participants, rooming, and preparing for study visits. Support data collection and clinical research documentation. Assist with organizing study materials, supplies, and visit documentation. Apply existing knowledge of clinical procedures such as vital signs, EKGs, phlebotomy, specimen collection, and specimen processing, as appropriate to the role. Support laboratory and specimen-related workflows. Build upon an existing understanding of how clinical research protocols are implemented in a real-world research environment. Apply and further develop knowledge of Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Good Documentation Practices, SOPs, and regulatory requirements. Interact with study participants and contribute to a positive, patient-centered experience. Work alongside Clinical Research Coordinators, investigators, and other research professionals. Gain additional experience with clinical research systems, documentation platforms, and study workflows. Continue developing the skills and experience needed to grow within clinical research. ## Who Should Join? We're looking to connect with **recent graduates and entry-level clinical research professionals who already have foundational clinical research knowledge, training, or experience** and are interested in continuing to build a career in the field. This talent community may be a good fit for individuals who have recently completed a degree program and gained clinical research experience through an internship, academic research, or another hands-on setting, as well as individuals who have successfully completed a **clinical research fast-track or similar structured training program** designed to prepare them for entry-level clinical research work. ## What Happens After You Join? Joining the talent community is not an application for a specific position and does not guarantee an interview or employment. Once you join, your information may be reviewed as future opportunities develop. When a potential entry-level clinical research opportunity becomes available, our team may reach out to members of the community whose background, training, experience, and interests align with the opportunity. Join our **Entry-Level Clinical Research Talent Community** and let us know you're interested in continuing to build your future in clinical research. We're committed to developing the next generation of clinical research professionals — and we'd like to get to know you. **Join the Profound Research Entry-Level Clinical Research Talent Community today.** *This is a talent community and expression-of-interest opportunity, not a current job vacancy. Joining the community does not guarantee future employment or placement.*

Our model gives patients access to the newest therapies while maintaining the trusted patient-physician relationship. **Our Mission:**Improving Lives by Providing Advanced Therapeutic Options **Our Vision:**Creating the Absolute Best Patient-Physician Experience in Clinical Research **Our Values:** - **Compassion:**We prioritize the patient-physician relationship, ensuring every interaction is service-oriented and patient-centered. - **Urgency:** We work hard and practice selflessness, acting swiftly and decisively to meet the needs of our patients, partners, and colleagues. - **Solution Orientation:** We embrace challenges with a positive mindset, communicate directly, and identify and implement effective solutions with efficiency. - **Excellence:** We insist on excellence, holding ourselves accountable and empowering each other to deliver best-in-class service while maintaining the highest ethical and scientific standards. **Join Our Talent Community: Build Your Future in Clinical Research** Profound Research is building a community of students who are in the final stages of completing their degree programs who are interested in learning, connecting, and exploring future opportunities in clinical research. ***This is a talent community and expression of interest — not a current job or internship opening.*** By joining the Profound Research Clinical Research Internship Talent Community, you'll have the opportunity to introduce yourself to our team and be part of our network of emerging clinical research talent. As future internship opportunities become available, we may connect with individuals in the community whose background, interests, location, and experience align with our needs. Where Our Talent Community Is Located We are currently building our Clinical Research Internship Talent Community in and around: - Detroit, Michigan - Munster, Indiana - Las Vegas, Nevada - Southern California, including the San Diego area Candidates must currently reside in or around one of these markets to join the community. Why Join Our Talent Community? Clinical research brings together science, medicine, patient care, and innovation. At Profound Research, our teams support clinical trials across a variety of therapeutic areas, giving emerging professionals the opportunity to learn about the development and evaluation of new therapies. Our research portfolio includes studies in areas such as: - Oncology - Cardiology - Neurology - Dermatology - Vaccines & Infectious Disease - Other evolving therapeutic areas By joining our talent community, you can put yourself on our radar for future opportunities and begin learning more about what it means to build a career in clinical research. What Future Internship Opportunities May Include While specific responsibilities will vary by site, study, and future opportunity, clinical research interns may have the opportunity to: Future internship opportunities with Profound Research are paid. We are also willing to collaborate with your college or university to meet applicable internship or academic program requirements, including required hours, documentation, learning objectives, evaluations, and other school-specific requirements. Support clinical research studies and participant visits under appropriate supervision. Assist with participant flow, including greeting participants, rooming, and preparing for study visits. Support data collection and clinical research documentation. Assist with organizing study materials, supplies, and visit documentation. Gain hands-on exposure to clinical procedures such as vital signs, EKGs, phlebotomy, specimen collection, and specimen processing, as appropriate. Support laboratory and specimen-related workflows. Learn how clinical research protocols are implemented in a real-world research environment. Gain exposure to Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Good Documentation Practices, SOPs, and regulatory requirements. Interact with study participants and contribute to a positive, patient-centered experience. Work alongside Clinical Research Coordinators, investigators, and other research professionals. Become familiar with clinical research systems, documentation platforms, and study workflows. Learn how clinical trials contribute to the development of new therapies. Who Should Join? We're looking to connect with individuals who are curious about clinical research and interested in building a career in healthcare, science, or research. What Happens After You Join? Joining the talent community is not an application for a specific internship and does not guarantee an internship, interview, or employment. Once you join, your information may be reviewed as future opportunities develop. When a potential internship opportunity becomes available, our team may reach out to members of the community whose background and interests align with the opportunity. Join our Clinical Research Internship Talent Community and let us know you're interested in being part of the future of clinical research. We're committed to developing the next generation of clinical research professionals — and we'd like to get to know you. Join the Profound Research Clinical Research Internship Talent Community today. *This is a talent community and expression-of-interest opportunity, not a current internship vacancy. Joining the community does not guarantee future employment or internship placement.*

## FPGA ENGINEER (NEW GRAD SUMMER 2027) Freeform builds AI-native manufacturing systems that unify software, hardware, and physics to produce industrial-scale parts at the speed of human ideation. By treating manufacturing as a single integrated system, we unlock a new era of innovation where complex hardware is designed, built, and scaled without limits. As an FPGA Engineer at Freeform, you will play a key role in developing and deploying the software systems that power our autonomous metal 3D printing factories. You’ll work with a talented engineering team from some of the world’s most innovative companies across a range of projects including controls, high-speed data acquisition, high-performance computing (GPU’s and FPGA’s), and geometry processing pipelines that enable precise and fully automated manufacturing at scale. Your work will directly impact the performance, reliability, and scalability of our factory systems. The ideal candidate thrives in ambiguity, takes initiative on complex technical problems, and works collaboratively across disciplines to deliver robust, high-performance software solutions. This is an opportunity to build foundational systems for a new category of manufacturing technology - where your code doesn’t just run, it drives physical innovation. 3D printing experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, collaborative engineers who love solving hard problems and creating amazing technology! **Responsibilities:** - Developing new logic components for use on FPGAs - Implementing custom algorithms on FPGAs for signal processing - Implementing custom controllers on FPGAs - Working with other software engineers to develop embedded Linux applications to interface with FPGA logic components - Packaging and using IP components in FPGA block diagram design - Working both on development boards and in a production environment **Basic Qualifications:** - Bachelor's degree in computer engineering, electrical engineering, or computer science - Hands on electrical experience from internships or engineering clubs such as FSAE, Baja SAE, solar car, rocket club, robotics club, or similar - Experience developing in VHDL or Verilog **Nice to Have:** - Experience with Xilinx Zynq Ultrascale+ MPSoC - Familiarity with Xilinx Vivado/Vitis toolchain development environment - Experience with embedded software development including embedded Linux and System on Chip (SoC)-based architectures - Experience with heterogeneous computing platforms and high-speed data acquisition systems - Familiarity with C/C++ or other high-level programming languages - Excellent verbal and written communication skills - Creative thinker able to apply first-principles reasoning to solve complex problems **Location:** - Based in Hawthorne, our vertically integrated facility brings technology development, R&D, and production together under one roof. We operate at the center of LA’s deep tech ecosystem, surrounded by some of the most ambitious hardware innovation happening anywhere in the country. - Our fast-paced, cross-functional environment is built on close collaboration, and as such, this role requires full-time onsite presence (five days a week), with very limited exceptions. **What We Offer:** - We have an inclusive and diverse culture that values collaboration, learning, and making deliberate data-driven decisions. - We offer a unique opportunity to be an early and integral member of a rapidly growing company that is scaling world-changing technology. - Benefits - Significant stock option packages - 100% employer-paid Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance (premium PPO and HMO options) - Life insurance - Traditional and Roth 401(k) - Relocation assistance provided - Paid vacation, sick leave, and company holidays - Generous Paid Parental Leave and extended transition back to work for the birthing parent - Free daily catered lunch and dinner, and fully stocked kitchenette - Casual dress, flexible work hours, and regular catered team building events - Compensation - Our intent is to offer a salary that is commensurate for the company’s current stage of development and allows the employee to grow and develop within a role. - In addition to the significant stock option package, the estimated salary range for this role is $125,000-$150,000, *dependent on the candidate's academic level (Bachelors, Masters, or PhD) and demonstrated out of classroom experience*. - Freeform is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values diversity; employment with Freeform is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

description: JOB DETAILS Rotational Day Shift: 3am-3:30pm Pay: $30-$40 per hour DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Maintenance Technician III is an Electro-Mechanical position and responsibilities will include but not be limited to supporting manufacturing operations, adjusting and repairing equipment as needed, tracking usage of and ordering replacement parts. Diagnose and repair complex electro-mechanical problems with manufacturing equipment Perform detailed setup on equipment including recipe changes and control adjustments Repair and keep mechanical machine components in top operating condition Advanced understanding of electrical principles such as voltage, current and resistance Diagnose and repair electrical control circuits, field devices, sensors, photo eyes, etc. Advanced understanding of electrical safety and motor control circuits and programmable drives Troubleshoot the inputs and outputs on PLC and repair issues Complete projects to add electrical circuits and controls, new equipment and relocate machines Maintain and repair pneumatic systems including repairs of cylinders and other components Perform simple to complex mechanical Preventative Maintenance Tasks following instructions Enter all work completed in computer-based maintenance program Monitor and report spare parts usage including completing parts order forms Adjust equipment based on Statistical Process Control data and team with QA Train Level I and II technicians in more complex tasks and skills Performs other duties as assigned Associates degree in related field is desired 3-7 years’ maintenance experience in a manufacturing environment Knowledge of and experience with Lock-Out, Tag-Out procedures Able to strictly adhere to safety policies/procedures and be committed to customer quality. Proficient in Word and Excel Must be willing to attend training sessions as needed, including out of state locations Ability to assist in Training Level I and II Technicians Intermediate knowledge of fabrication (ex. welding, basic machining) Possess strong work ethic and knowledge of intermediate troubleshooting Able to read printed materials, blueprints, schematics, and computer graphics Excellent verbal and written communication skills Ability to work independently and within a team, including the ability to establish and maintain cooperative working relationships employees, vendors, contractors, and suppliers Ability to show attention to detail in a very fast paced environment Flexible and willing to work overtime as required Physical Demands: The physical demands are representative of those that must be met by employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made upon request to enable individuals with qualified disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job. Must possess strength, stamina and mobility to perform heavy physical work with exposure to potentially hazardous conditions, use varied hand and power tools, drive a motor vehicle and/or light construction equipment, fork trucks, platform lifts etc. Lift and move materials and equipment weighing up to 90 pounds and heavier weights with the use of proper equipment While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to walk; use fingers and hands to handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; stoop and kneel; talk and hear. The employee is frequently required to stand and sit for long periods, as well as occasionally be required to climb or balance. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust and focus. Exposure to variable temperatures as impacted by the weather Work Environment: Mainly a manufacturing facility, where exposed to moving mechanical parts, forklifts, heavy pallets, moderate to loud noise level, and air-borne dust, powders, and fumes. description: **Summary:** Our team leads the integration of business strategy, innovation, and project management into the practice of law. As one of the largest law firms globally, Barnes & Thornburg’s Legal Operations team plays a crucial role in delivering top-tier service to major global companies. Under the supervision of the Department Chief and a dedicated mentor, you will work on project-based assignments aligned with your field of study and the firm’s strategic priorities. This role provides invaluable real-world experience in the evolving field of legal operations. **Internship Eligibility:** The BT R.I.S.E. To be eligible candidates must be: - Enrolled in either a 2 or 4 year degree program - Entering their junior or senior year in Fall of 2027 - Available to participate for 10 consecutive weeks **Key Responsibilities:** - **Project Coordination**: Support the planning, execution, and tracking of legal and business projects, ensuring timelines and deliverables are met. - **Process Improvement**: Identify opportunities for process optimization and propose solutions to enhance efficiency within the Legal Operations team. - **Data Analysis**: Analyze project data and key performance indicators (KPIs) to provide insights and recommendations for ongoing projects. - **AI Solutions**: Work with the firm’s approved AI tools to create and collaborate on AI solutions both for the business and legal sides of the firm. - **Attorney Collaboration**: Work with attorneys to understand possible process and technology opportunities to assist with their clients and practices. - **Cross-Departmental Collaboration**: Work internally within Legal Operations teams and externally with departments such as Finance, Marketing, and IT to collect insights, streamline workflows, and drive key initiatives forward. - **Project Documentation**: Assist in maintaining comprehensive project documentation, including timelines, reports, and status updates to ensure stakeholders are informed. - **Presentation Skills**: Prepare and present project status reports, highlighting key milestones, challenges, and results. role: Sample Receiving Technician (Entry-level/Non-degree) - Eurofins Environment Testing Northeast - North Kingstown, RI
description: Performs sample handling in accordance with state and local EPA regulations. Participates in performing tasks related to sample receipt, storage and disposal as well as shipping samples to outside laboratories. Responsibilities: Follow laboratory standard operating procedures (SOPs) in the handling and disposal of samples. Light laboratory duties Perform sample receiving duties including, but not limited to: sample documentation upon receipt, sample storage and sample disposal. Effectively communicate with Sample Receiving Manager on sample receipt related discrepancies including but not limited to: incorrect bottle type / preservation, additional containers not listed on the chain of custody and reporting when sample receipt temperature is out of spec Packing and shipping samples Preparing client bottle orders Assists laboratory with glassware cleaning for all departments. Assists chemists and other technicians as needed. Perform all responsibilities in a safe and responsible manner in accordance with Eurofins Laboratory safety policy. Maintains a safe and healthy work environment that is in compliance with the requirements of Eurofins Laboratory’s Health & Safety program (and local laws and regulations). Utilizing computer based laboratory information system to electronically track and store sample containers and for shipping purposes Performs all responsibilities in an organized and timely manner in strict accordance with courier arrival times, sample hold times and with the nightly Fedex pickup Basic Minimum Qualifications (BMQ): High school diploma or GED Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) experience helpful The ideal candidate would possess: Computer skills Organizational skills and attention to detail Strong communication (oral and written) Ability to work in a fast-paced production setting Learn quickly Ability to work independently and as part of a team, self-motivation, adaptability, and a positive attitude Ability to learn new techniques, perform multiple tasks simultaneously, keep accurate records, follow instructions, and comply with company policies Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds Requirements: Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English Position is full-time 2nd shift Monday – Friday 1:30 pm - 10:00 pm. Will train on 1st shift Monday - Friday 9:00 am - 5:30 pm for 1-2 weeks. Candidates currently living within a commutable distance of North Kingstown, RI are encouraged to apply. Pay range: $18-20/hr. Please note - Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) provides a compensation range for informational purposes, the actual base salary may vary based upon, but not limited to, relevant experience and skill set, base salary of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location. As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work. we offer excellent benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options. *The benefits package offered will vary based on the employee's full-time or part-time regular status. To learn more about Eurofins, please explore our website . We support your development! Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development. We embrace diversity! Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique. Sustainability matters to us! At Eurofins, we believe sustainability is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our vision to be the Global Leader in “Testing for Life,” our mission to contribute to a healthier and safer world, and our core values, we are building a strong foundation for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives. Eurofins’ commitment to sustainability begins within our own companies through a shared responsibility to people and the planet. With climate change posing an imminent threat, Eurofins and its many companies recognize their duty to proactively reduce or offset the environmental impact of essential operations while also helping our clients do the same—serving as a true ESG Enabler. Find out more in our career page: Company description: Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate. The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and Eurofins Scientific 2/2 March 2023 agroscience contract research services. It is one of the market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and in the support of clinical studies, as well as having an emerging global presence in Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisations. It also has a rapidly developing presence in highly specialised and molecular clinical diagnostic testing and in-vitro diagnostic products. In over 35 years, Eurofins has grown from one laboratory in Nantes, France to 61,000 staff across a decentralised and entrepreneurial network of ca. 900 laboratories in 61 countries. Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products. In 2025, Eurofins generated total revenues of EUR 7.296 billion, and has been among the best performing stocks in Europe over the past 20 years. [State Affairs](http://www.stateaffairs.com/) is the nation’s leading news and policy intelligence platform focused on state governments. We combine nonpartisan coverage of Statehouses across the country alongside state government data and AI-native tools into a singular platform. We inform and empower decision makers, policy professionals and citizens through our award-winning journalism and data – delivering profound insights to help our customers decode and act on state politics and policy. We’re building a category-defining business that will reshape America as we strengthen visibility into what’s happening and why at the state level. As a Software Engineering Intern, you’ll join our engineering team in Washington, DC and ship real features to real users, not side projects. You’ll work across the full stack: React/Next.js interfaces, Node APIs, and Postgres data models that keep up with petabyte-scale content. Help generate applications through community events, recruitment activities, and direct outreach. Welcome to the DNC Accounting Internship Application! The DNC Accounting department is accepting applications for our Spring 2027 Internship Program! This is a separate application from the DNC General Internship Application because it requires specific experience. Interning with the DNC’s Accounting team is a unique opportunity for future leaders to gain real life, hands-on experience in Democratic political accounting, learn and experience industry processes, strengthen their understanding of the political process, and prepare them for future opportunities in the political realm. The program will run from January 11, 2027 - March 19, 2027 and will be conducted in an in-person, hybrid, or remote format. Interns who are based in the Washington D.C. area will have an opportunity to perform in-person work for the DNC at the Democratic National Committee Headquarters and DNC events. You must be located in the United States to apply for this internship. The DNC Internship Program provides a stipend of $3,700. Housing is not provided. During the upcoming term, interns are expected to work 20 hours per week. The deadline for applications is November 27, 2026. Department Summary: The Accounting Department is a core part of the DNC. Our goal is to ensure the financial integrity and transparency of our operations through rigorous reporting, compliance, and budget tracking; managing the critical resources required to power national campaign initiatives and help support and elect Democrats across the country. Position Summary: During your time as a DNC Accounting intern, you’ll gain hands-on experience supporting the day-to-day financial operations of a major political organization. Working directly with our Accounting Team, you will assist with key financial processes, budget tracking, and compliance efforts. In this role, you’ll interact and communicate regularly with the DNC's external partners and vendors, as well as collaborate with colleagues across various departments. An Accounting intern will manage assigned, time-sensitive projects and develop a foundational understanding of non-profit and political accounting practices in a fast-paced environment. You’ll be part of the intern class and will regularly participate in broader programming, professional development, and support activities alongside interns from other DNC teams. Internship Responsibilities/Duties: Track, analyze, and reconcile cumulative vendor payments against statutory IRS thresholds to determine 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC eligibility Perform monthly bank reconciliations, post general ledger journal entries, and assist with account analysis Support day-to-day accounts payable (AP) and accounts receivable (AR) processing, vendor invoice management, and expense report verification Skills: Eager to learn, reliable, and able to work well independently and on a collaborative team High attention to detail, strong organizational skills, and clear written and verbal communication abilities Eligibility Requirements: Applicants must be 18 years of age on or before the first day of the internship and meet at least one of the following criteria: Currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at a college, community college, or university (two-to-four year institution). It is highly recommended that applicants complete at least one full term prior to submitting an application. Graduated from an undergraduate or graduate program at a college, community college, or university (two-to-four year institution) no more than two years before the first day of the internship. A veteran of the United States Armed Forces who possesses a high school diploma or its equivalent and has served on active duty, for any length of time, in the two years preceding the first day of the internship. Applicants must meet all of the following criteria: Commitment of 20 hours per week during the program Physically present in the United States to participate in this internship program Required Application Materials: Resume References SECTION: CLOSING Due to the volume of applications, we cannot review additional materials sent outside of the application form. GFT is seeking an Entry Level Geotechnical Engineer to join our Geotechnical Team in our New York, NY office. Assist in the planning of subsurface explorations and laboratory testing investigations. ### **About Campus** [Campus](https://campus.edu/) is on a mission to accelerate the talent of tomorrow and reimagine what college can (and should) be. The problem is clear: college costs have skyrocketed, but outcomes haven’t. Traditional college hasn’t kept up with the aspirations of today’s students—and they can’t afford to wait. At Campus, we’ve built a two-year, accredited college where students learn from top professors at universities like Princeton, Stanford, and Howard, in live, online classes. Our students graduate with in-demand business and AI skills—ready to launch their careers or transfer to top four-year universities. Our unique approach is grounded in a pioneering technology platform and a heavily-researched student success model that offers students dedicated advisors and on-demand tutoring and coaching. We were also named one of Fast Company's [Most Innovative Companies of 2024](https://c212.net/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4289374-1&h=905796532&u=https%3A%2F%2Fc212.net%2Fc%2Flink%2F%3Ft%3D0%26l%3Den%26o%3D4174213-1%26h%3D410953500%26u%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.fastcompany.com%252F91036638%252Fcampus-most-innovative-companies-2024%26a%3DMost%2BInnovative%2BCompanies%2Bof%2B2024&a=Most+Innovative+Companies+of+2024). We’re backed by an exceptional investor team that believes deeply in our vision for the future of education, including General Catalyst, Founders Fund, Bloomberg Beta, 8VC, Rethink Education, Sam Altman, Jason Citron, Shaquille O’Neal, and others. The world has changed. Higher ed needs to catch up, and we’re leading the way - come join us! ### **About the Team** At Campus, our Student Success team is here to help students navigate college - and life - with confidence. From Day 1 through graduation, we’re a student’s go-to partner for encouragement, accountability, and steady support. Our Success Coaches build lasting relationships with students, help them work through academic and personal challenges, and make sure no one feels like they’re doing this alone. We believe every conversation is an opportunity to move a student closer to their goals - and that the best coaches combine warmth, clarity, and relentless follow-through. ### **About the Role** As a Success Coach, you’ll manage a caseload of students throughout their journey at Campus. You’ll guide them through course planning, accountability, time management, and tough conversations, helping them connect their day-to-day work to their long-term goals. You’ll be responsible for proactive outreach, relationship building, and backend documentation, balancing care and clarity while navigating a high-paced, emotionally complex role. This is not a reactive advising job. You’ll need to reach out persistently, pivot in real time, and coach students through moments of self-doubt, struggle, and celebration. ### **You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…** - Build long-term relationships with students through coaching sessions, check-ins, and ongoing outreach - Conduct proactive outreach via phone, text, and chat to keep students engaged and accountable - Coach students through personal, academic, and motivational challenges, demonstrating empathy while helping students stay accountable for their own progress - Help students break down big goals into actionable next steps - Track progress using various dashboards - Complete forms (e.g., deferrals, withdrawals) and document notes clearly and consistently - Balance a caseload of 50-75 students, triaging by risk and term - Collaborate with Admissions and Onboarding teams to clarify handoffs and student context - Adjust quickly to changing tools, processes, or term-based priorities ### **We’re Excited About You Because You…** - Are a strong empathic communicator who creates safe, goal-oriented relationships with students through consistent outreach and regular 1:1 video and phone check-ins - Support academic progress by helping students manage time, stay on track with coursework, and work through academic or personal obstacles with empathy, clarity, and actionable next steps - description: **[The Koch Internship Program](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/koch-internship-program/) (KIP)** is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the [admissions process](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/application-process/) early! **About FEE** [The Foundation for Economic Education (FEE)](https://fee.org/) is a leading nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing the economic, ethical, and legal principles of a free society. For 80 years, FEE has been committed to inspiring and educating individuals on the values of personal freedom, entrepreneurship, and sound economic thinking. Through various programs, publications, and events, FEE empowers individuals to understand the economic principles that drive prosperity and fosters a society rooted in individual rights and limited government. **About FEE’s Student Engagement Team** FEE’s Student Engagement team inspires and awakens students by delivering the world-class learning experiences at the heart of FEE’s mission, introducing high school and college students to the ideas of a free society through in-person programs, webinars, and campus-based programs. The Student Engagement team runs single- and multi-day programs across North America and Latin America. Its summer campus programs bring students together for several days of learning about economics, entrepreneurship, and personal freedom. Behind every program is a detailed operational effort: venues and vendors, speakers and faculty, travel, materials, participant recruitment, and day-of execution. The team takes pride in getting those details correct so that every participant leaves with a world-class experience that inspires & awakens. **About This Internship** The North America Programs Intern will support FEE’s Senior Associate, North America Programs and the broader Programs team, with a primary focus on the logistics and operations behind FEE’s programming in the Washington, DC office. This is an opportunity for a highly organized, detail-oriented student or recent graduate to gain hands-on experience in event logistics, participant communication, and program operations within a mission-driven organization. In addition to supporting DC programming, the intern will contribute to key work evolving FEE’s summer campus programming, helping research, plan, and document improvements to how these programs are recruited for, organized, and delivered. The ideal candidate has a genuine interest in economic freedom and FEE’s mission, enjoys getting the details right, and is comfortable using AI-powered tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, or similar) to work more efficiently. The internship will be based out of FEE’s Dupont Circle office in Washington, DC, and in-person attendance is expected. The intern will report to the Student Engagement Director. ### Responsibilities: - Assist with end-to-end logistics for FEE’s single and multi-day seminars in Washington, DC, including venue and catering coordination, materials preparation, attendee travel, and room setup. - Provide on-site support during DC programs, helping with registration, check-in, speaker and participant needs, and day-of troubleshooting. - Support the Programs team’s work evolving FEE’s summer campus programming, including researching campus partners and venues, benchmarking comparable programs, and helping draft updated plans, timelines, and processes. - Help build and maintain logistics resources such as run-of-show documents, logistics packets, checklists, and participant communications. - Communicate promptly and professionally with speakers, attendees, and partners before, during, and after programs. - Support participant outreach and recruitment, including tracking applications and referrals and following up with prospective attendees. - Maintain accurate records in Salesforce and project trackers in for program participants, partners, and tasks. - Help track program budgets, invoices, and vendor documentation for assigned programs. - Collect and organize participant feedback and program metrics, and help prepare post-program reports. - Use AI tools to speed up correspondence, logistics coordination, research, and reporting, and flag opportunities to improve or automate program processes. ### Skills: - Current undergraduate or graduate student, or recent graduate; prior experience in event planning, student organizations, customer service, or administrative support is a plus. - Strong organizational skills and close attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines at once. - Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and a professional, service-oriented approach with speakers, partners, and participants. - Comfort with, or eagerness to learn, AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) for drafting, organizing, and research tasks. - Proficiency with Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, etc.); familiarity with Salesforce and is a plus. - Self-directed, reliable, and collaborative; follows through on assigned tasks, is open to feedback, and brings curiosity to suggest improvements. - Flexibility to support occasional early morning, evening, or weekend program events. - Interest in the ideas of a free society and a commitment to FEE’s mission and principles. - **Strong candidates will have a basic understanding of economic principles and an interest in applying that knowledge to help develop engaging educational programs and prepare educational materials and activities for high school and college students.**

## **About us** At Roadrunner, we’re replacing the broken CPQ software that Sales teams have complained about, worked around, and given up on for years. Not improving it - replacing it. We’re building a new agentic stack called PQA - Prompt, Quote, Approve, designed for the enterprise, on a data model built for how pricing actually works today. We’re Kleiner Perkins’ first incubation since Glean, led by second-time founders with successful exits, and a team of engineers from Snowflake, Databricks, Citadel, Meta, Robinhood, Brex, and so on. We’re in-person in San Francisco, and we’re just getting started. ## **What you'll do** - **Embed with our customers.** You'll sit with the RevOps and Sales leaders who live inside Roadrunner every day, turn their hardest pricing and approval problems into shipped features, and stay on the hook until they're actually solved - not just handed off to support. - **Own delivery end-to-end, in production.** From technical discovery through go-live, you're the engineer who scopes it, builds it, and keeps it running. - **Turn one-off solutions into product.** Every customer-specific integration or workflow you build feeds back into Roadrunner's core platform. The pattern you build for customer #1 is the feature customer #10 gets out of the box. - **Ship AI agents in the field.** Deploy and tune proactive agents - quoting recommendations, deal modeling, multi-step approval workflows - against real customer data and real deal pressure, then iterate on what actually breaks. - **Be the fastest feedback loop in the company.** You're often the first to see where the product breaks under real enterprise complexity. You carry that back to the core team the same day, not next sprint. ## **What you'll bring** - **Strong engineering fundamentals** - from coursework, internships, or projects. You don't need a track record of shipping to production yet; you need to be able to build fast without cutting the corners that matter. - **Real curiosity.** You want to know why something broke, not just that it broke - and you'll dig through an unfamiliar codebase or a customer's system until you find the actual answer. - **Ambition.** You want real ownership fast, not a backlog of tickets, and you're ready to earn it. - **Comfort with ambiguity** - from a hackathon, a research project, or an internship where nobody handed you a spec. - **Clear, direct communication** - with engineers and with the non-technical people you'll be sitting across from. - **Willingness to travel occasionally** to be onsite with customers when it matters. - **Based in SF or excited to relocate** - we're an in-person team. ## **Bonus points if…** - You've interned somewhere and shipped code that real users touched. - You've built something on your own - an app, a tool, a research project - because you wanted it to exist, not because a class required it. - You've spent time close to customers or end users, even outside of engineering (support, tutoring, ops), and know what it's like to translate someone's problem into something you build. - You've picked up a new language, framework, or domain fast because a project needed it. - You have a side project. Tell us what it is and why you built it. ## **What we offer** - Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family. - Lunch and dinner, as well as snacks and coffee to keep you energized. - Take what you need vacation policy. ## **Equal opportunity** We value our differences, and we encourage all to apply — especially those whose identities are traditionally underrepresented in tech organizations. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected by law. Roadrunner is an equal opportunity employer.

[Relay](https://relaypro.com/) is the Intelligent System of Action for the physical economy. While the digital revolution has often left the deskless workforce behind, we are closing that gap by transforming analog frontline operations into a data-rich, AI-powered ecosystem. We aren't just selling radios, we're building the digital foundation for the 80% of the global workforce that doesn't work at a desk. **Why Join Relay?** - **A Proven Winner:** Join a hyper-growth company trusted by over 10% of the Fortune 500, continuing to move upmarket with massive impact. - **High Value, High Impact:** With 47% of our revenue from $100K+ ARR customers and 135% Net Revenue Retention (NRR), you'll be joining a company rooted in value creation. - **Market-Leading Innovation:** The Relay platform captures 1 billion new data points weekly and features award-winning AI tools like TeamTranslate™, with 500% YoY growth. - **World-Class Leadership:** Our stellar leadership team is built to help us scale toward our next major milestones. - **The Relay Culture:** We're dedicated to helping you do the best work of your life (BWIML), investing in your growth, living out our CHASE values, and learning from talented teammates who make the work and the wins better every day. **Now, here's what we're building, and where you come in.** ## **About the Role** Value Engineering at Relay is the bridge between frontline operational reality and enterprise investment decisions. Our Value Engineers parachute into a prospect's world, learn how they operate, and build the financial case that proves Relay's ROI at the C-suite level. This is analytical, customer-facing, high-stakes work. This internship puts you in the middle of it. The Value Engineering Internship is a two-phase opportunity: a Spring semester engagement (January start, part-time) that potentially feeds into a full-time 40-hour/week Summer internship for top performers. Both phases are on-site at Relay's world-class Raleigh HQ, located near the Lenovo Center. Strong performance creates a pathway to a return offer for a Summer or Fall 2027 internship and full-time consideration upon graduation, based on business needs. You'll work directly with our Manager, Value Engineering, and the broader GTM org. This includes Account Executives, Customer Success Managers, and senior leadership — on live enterprise deals. ## **About the Team** The Value Engineering team exists to close two critical gaps: leadership isn't always in touch with the factory floor, and new technology doesn't always translate into operational impact. We bridge both by quantifying Relay's value proposition, building investment-grade business cases, and acting as a forcing function for customer ROI. Our work shapes the enterprise sales motion, customer relationships, product roadmap, and company strategy. ## **Responsibilities** - Support the development of executive-level business cases that translate frontline operational data into P&L-level ROI. - Map prospect workflows and analyze operational metrics to identify Relay's highest-impact use cases. - Build financial models that quantify the value Relay delivers across manufacturing, logistics, hospitality, and healthcare. - Partner with AEs and CSMs on pilot strategies and account planning for key enterprise opportunities. - Conduct research on industry operations and competitive benchmarks to strengthen Relay's value narratives. - Assist in developing internal tools, ROI frameworks, and proofs-of-concept that scale across the sales org. - Synthesize customer and field insights to support product roadmap and pricing strategy conversations. - Contribute to the company's wildly well-attended intern showcase — presenting your work to Relay's full team at summer's end. ## **Required Qualifications** - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Statistics, Data Science, or a related field. - Expected graduation between December 2027 and May 2029. - Minimum GPA of 3.7 - No employer work authorization sponsorship available — candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship, now or in the future. - Strong quantitative and analytical skills; comfortable building models and working with data. - Excellent written and verbal communication — ability to synthesize complexity into a clear, executive-ready narrative. - Available to work onsite at Relay's Raleigh HQ (near the Lenovo Center) for both the Spring engagement and the full-time Summer program. ## **Preferred Qualifications** - Coursework or project experience in operations research, systems engineering, supply chain, or financial analysis. - Exposure to manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, or hospitality environments through coursework, co-op, or personal experience. - Familiarity with data analysis tools (Excel, Python, SQL) and/or data visualization. - A genuine curiosity about how physical-world businesses operate and where technology creates real impact. ## **What success and impact look like in this role** By the end of the Spring engagement, you've shipped at least one analysis or framework that's been used in a live enterprise deal. role: KIP Spring 2027 - Economics Olympiad Intern - Foundation for Economic Education
description: **[The Koch Internship Program](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/koch-internship-program/) (KIP)** is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Early-career professionals including undergraduate/graduate/law students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the [admissions process](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/application-process/) early! **About FEE** [The Foundation for Economic Education (FEE)](https://fee.org/) is a leading nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing the economic, ethical, and legal principles of a free society. For 80 years, FEE has been committed to inspiring and educating individuals on the values of personal freedom, entrepreneurship, and sound economic thinking. Through various programs, publications, and events, FEE empowers individuals to understand the economic principles that drive prosperity and fosters a society rooted in individual rights and limited government. **About FEE’s Student Engagement Team** The Student Engagement department leads FEE's student-facing events. Through a mix of in-person and virtual programs, FEE partners with schools, educators, and organizations to introduce students to the principles of a free society, fostering deeper understanding and thoughtful discussions. From outreach and relationship-building to event logistics and execution, the Student Engagement team works to create engaging, high-impact experiences that challenge and inspire the next generation. Domestically, FEE's programs have reached students in nearly all 50 states. Internationally, FEE has a growing footprint in Latin America. **About This Internship** This role will assist with FEE’s new initiative, the Economics Olympiad (EO). EO is FEE's international student competition, running students through a School Round and a National Round on their way to an International Final Round. In Canada and the USA, the program is scaling to reach students at schools across both countries during the School Round, before bringing top performers together for an in-person National Round in Washington, DC. Behind the scenes, a small team of staff and partners keeps teachers, students, and parents informed and supported at every stage, helping turn the National Round into a well-run, memorable event. The Economics Olympiad Intern will be the front line of that experience — helping students, teachers, and parents get clear, timely answers as they move through the School and National Rounds, while also supporting the planning of the National Round event in DC. This is an opportunity for the ideal candidate to combine a love for the ideas of a free society with a passion for clear communication and flawless event execution. ### Responsibilities: - Draft, send, and track communications to registered teachers and students throughout registration, testing, and the National Round — reminders, deadlines, logistics updates, and FAQs. - Monitor inboxes and shared communication channels to ensure inquiries are answered promptly and accurately. - Support planning and execution of the National Round in Washington, DC, including venue coordination, vendor and catering logistics, AV needs, schedules, and day-of logistics packets. - Help maintain registration and communication records (e.g., in Salesforce) so participant status and outreach history stay accurate and up to date. - Assist with creating participant-facing materials such as logistics packets, FAQs, itineraries, and confirmation emails. - Work closely with your intern supervisor on new projects, ideas, and initiatives related to the Economic Olympiad. - Track and report relevant KPIs (e.g., response times, registration follow-through, inquiry volume). ### Skills: - Business, Economics, Project Management or other related majors desired, but not required. - Excellent written and verbal communication skills and strong customer service skills. - Ability juggling multiple priorities while keeping everything on track and maintaining careful attention to detail. - The ability to work independently and take initiative with minimal supervision. - A proactive, entrepreneurial spirit to improve existing programs. - A collaborative personality; unafraid of challenge. - An unwavering commitment to the mission and principles of FEE.

role: Member of Technical Staff Intern - US
description: ## **DRYFT** Ideas only change the world when you build them at scale. That’s what Dryft is here for. Dryft builds models that automate complex human decisions in manufacturing operations. We capture the knowledge of experienced operators across supply chain, production planning, engineering and more, simulate the consequences of their decisions, and use this understanding to help run their business. Our customers include some of the largest robotics, machine and component manufacturers in the world. We’re a small, talent-dense team with modest roots and a love for the physical world: cars, machines, planes. Our team includes graduates from Stanford, Berkeley, CDTM and TUM, winners of Stanford TreeHacks, recipients of Fulbright & Haniel scholarships, and people who have built everything from robots and race cars to software with millions of downloads. What matters more to us than credentials is how people work: humility, hard work, speed, kindness, deep customer care, and a willingness to take on problems others avoid. Working at Dryft is hard. You get unusual ownership early on, with real responsibility. But that’s also what makes it one of the biggest learning experiences of your life. We’re backed by founders and operators behind some of the most legendary tech companies of our time, Tier-1 U.S. venture firms, and board members of global industrial companies. ERPs ran the physical world for half a century. Dryft is building the intelligence layer that will power the next. ​ ## **THE ROLE** As a **Member of Technical Staff Intern**, you'll build the system that decides how some of the largest manufacturers in the world operate. That means combining agent-based reasoning with mathematical optimization and simulation on large-scale industrial data. - **Build agents people trust** – when an agent runs a factory's week, the largest industrial companies in the world have to trust it with their critical processes and understand every decision it makes; you build the routing, orchestration and guardrails behind that - **Ship features end-to-end** – you understand the user need, and you get the freedom to build it across the LLM pipeline, infrastructure, backend and frontend, in production in your first weeks - **Work close to the users** – sit with the planners who use it, see what would make their work 10x faster, and build it You'll own your own features from day one, and what you ship decides what a plant does next week. ​ ## **YOU** - **Full-stack shipper** – you've shipped production code end-to-end, you build scalable backend and infra that handles massive amounts of structured and unstructured data, and you build the interface that makes it usable - **Highly technical** – you've built something technically hard, and you can walk us through every decision behind it - **Product sense** – you spot the feature hiding in a user's complaint, and you've deleted your own favorite one because nobody used it - **You care about getting it right** – you know when it has to be 100% and when to keep it simple, and when it matters, you're still chasing the root cause at 2am - **Sense of urgency** – you'd rather ship it tonight than sleep on an open PR - **Relocation** – you're ready to work onsite in San Francisco (we support visa) ​ ## **TECH STACK** - **FE (TypeScript):** React, Chakra UI v3, TanStack Router, TanStack Query, Vite - **BE (Python):** FastAPI with Pydantic v2, Temporal, Postgres with pgvector, dagster - **AI:** Pydantic AI, Langfuse

description: **[The Koch Internship Program](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/koch-internship-program/) (KIP)** is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States.
