Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the [admissions process](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/application-process/) early! **Organization Overview** [The Foundation Against Intolerance & Racism (FAIR)](https://www.fairforall.org/) is a nonpartisan, 501(c)(3) nonprofit founded in 2021 to advance civil rights and liberties for all people. Rooted in the classical civil rights tradition and the principle that individuals should be treated without regard to race, gender, or other group identity, FAIR works to counter the spread of identity-based ideology across American institutions and to promote a common culture built on fairness, understanding, and humanity. FAIR pursues this mission through a dual strategy: identifying & supporting precedent-setting litigation that ensures diversity and inclusion efforts remain non-discriminatory, and grassroots, cultural, medical and educational programming that shifts hearts and minds at the community level. FAIR's network includes more than 50 chapters across the United States and Canada, along with professional networks of educators, clinicians, artists, and legal advocates. **Program Areas** FAIR in Medicine: A nonpartisan professional network dedicated to advancing the highest ethical standards in medical practice. FAIR in Medicine raises awareness of unethical and politicized practices in healthcare, promotes scientific debate and inquiry free from ideological pressure, and builds a common medical culture grounded in critical thinking and evidence-based care. FAIR in the Arts: A professional network championing freedom of expression and excellence in arts, entertainment, and media. FAIR in the Arts provides grants and funding for artists, curates events and mentorship opportunities, and builds a network of advisors, institutions, and enterprises that support artists facing intolerance for their work or viewpoints. FAIR in Education: FAIR in Education equips teachers, administrators, and school communities with pro-human learning resources and support to build healthy school environments. Its flagship offering is the Many Stories, One Nation (MSON) curriculum an academically rigorous alternative to "liberated" ethnic studies models that gives students a comprehensive view of the contributions of all Americans, paired with the FAIR Pro-Human Learning Standards, literature guides, and the Educators Alliance professional community. FAIR Legal Network: The FAIR Legal Network identifies and publicizes precedent-setting litigation on behalf of individuals denied equal protection, advises schools and employers on bringing policies into compliance with civil rights law, and equips FAIR members with the tools to challenge discriminatory practices in their own communities. Chapter Network & Communications: FAIR's grassroots Chapter Network spans more than 50 chapters that host discussions, outreach events, and educational campaigns locally. This work is supported by FAIR's communications, social media, and Substack newsletter operations, which extend FAIR's programs and message to a national audience. **About the Role** FAIR for All is seeking motivated, mission-aligned interns to support its programs in 2027. This general internship placement allows students to gain hands-on experience across one or more of FAIR's core program areas: Medicine, the Arts, Education, and Legal as well as organizational operations, working in close coordination with the CFO/COO. Specific project assignments will be tailored to the intern's interests, skills, and department needs. Who We’re Looking For The strongest candidates will bring technical curiosity, attention to detail, and genuine interest in how geospatial data helps renewable energy projects get built. · Currently pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in GIS, geography, environmental science, geospatial data science, computer science, or a related field. · Working proficiency in ArcGIS Pro and basic Python/ArcPy scripting, demonstrated through coursework, projects, or prior internship experience. · Familiarity with core spatial data concepts, including coordinate systems, geodatabases, and vector and raster data. · Strong attention to detail and data quality, and comfortable managing multiple workstreams. · Clear written and verbal communication skills; proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint). · Genuine interest in the energy transition, renewable energy development, or land-based project development. · Self-starter mentality with the ability to work independently and ask good questions. · Plus: experience with ArcGIS Online, Experience Builder, SQL, or Microsoft Azure. You’ll contribute to the design, development, and testing of cutting-edge automation systems. This internship offers a hands-on introduction to CAD modeling, robotic systems, and manufacturing processes, providing a dynamic platform to apply your academic knowledge, develop technical skills, and launch your engineering career under expert mentorship. **Rotational Development Path:** - Rotation 1 – Foundations: Gain familiarity with SolidWorks, mechanical drawings, Axis standards, common purchased components, project release procedures, and documentation. description: ## Hillel International ## Role Overview Hillel International is seeking a dynamic marketing and fundraising professional to serve as a project-based Campus Marketing and Development Manager. This temporary position on our growing team will let you make an immediate impact on the lives of thousands of Jewish college students over a 6-month contract. The Campus Marketing and Development Manager will support the grassroots fundraising and marketing efforts of a portfolio of campus Hillels. Top candidates will have a strong background in digital marketing and/or fundraising, with an emphasis on excellent writing, strong graphic design skills, and developing impactful campaigns using data-driven strategies to achieve positive results. We welcome applications from candidates across the U.S., with fully remote options and hybrid options available in Washington, D.C., and New York City. ## What You’ll Do - Create, write, design, and distribute digital and direct response fundraising campaigns across platforms (email, direct mail, texting, social media, and web). - Develop annual fundraising and marketing campaign calendars incorporating stewardship touchpoints, appeals, renewal messaging, and email newsletters. - Optimize campaigns at an advanced level using data-driven strategies, including A/B testing, personalization, audience targeting, and nonprofit industry trends. - Provide in-depth analysis of campaign performance to meet or exceed goals, use CRMs for audience segmentation, and provide web support related to fundraising. - Lead audience acquisition efforts (parents, alumni, donors) and lead key initiatives such as Giving Days and text campaigns. - Serve as a strategic partner to campus staff to ensure brand cohesion, powerful storytelling, and top-notch client service. - Successfully manage multiple timelines and concurrent projects across campus clients. ## What You’ll Bring to the Job - 3–5 years of experience in marketing, digital advertising, and/or fundraising within the non-profit space (deep understanding of Hillel is a plus). - Proven success planning and executing digital and multichannel campaigns. - Excellent written communication skills for crafting compelling fundraising messaging, paired with exceptional graphic design skills (Canva, Adobe Suite, etc.). - Mastery of data analysis and audience segmentation, along with experience using CRMs/databases and email marketing platforms (MailChimp, Constant Contact, etc.). - Superior organizational skills, acute attention to detail, and a client-service mindset to manage multiple stakeholders effectively. - Passion for entrepreneurship, innovation, and Jewish life ## What You’ll Receive - Competitive salary in the nonprofit marketplace. The salary range for this position is $60,000-$65,000 per year, prorated for the 6-month period of employment. - Anticipated contract period: December 2026-June 2027 - Temporary employees are eligible to enroll in our Tax Deferred 403(b) Retirement Plan and are eligible for our benefits program - Professional development, mentoring, and skill-building opportunities. #LI-REMOTE #LI-REMOTE ## **About Hillel International** In 1923, Rabbi Benjamin Frankel started Hillel with humble means, a noble mission and a breathtaking vision: to convey Jewish civilization to a new generation. Today, Hillel International continues to enrich the lives of Jewish students and is the largest Jewish campus organization in the world at nearly 1,000 colleges and universities across North America and around the world. As Hillel evolves as an organization, the mission remains steadfast: to create lasting connections with every Jewish student that foster an enduring commitment to Jewish life, learning, and Israel and train them to become the next Jewish leaders. **Hillel is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an accepting and inclusive environment for all.**

**Controls Engineer Intern** **- Position Description –** **Position Overview:** The Controls Engineering Intern learns and applies foundational automation skills while supporting internal and customer projects under close supervision. The intern works closely with other interns and the Controls team to complete tasks in PLC/HMI/robotics, documentation, and basic commissioning while building good engineering habits in safety, standards, and communication. **Rotational Development Path:** - Rotation 1 – Foundations: Gain familiarity with electrical schematics, PLC coding basics, HMI structure, standards, and documentation. Contribute to Axis internal projects and update documentation for existing customer programs. - Rotation 2 – Expansion: Tackle more advanced internal projects; begin supporting customer projects (electrical design tasks and code edits). Intro to robot programming and simulation. - Rotation 3 – Application: Provide hands-on support to customer projects: schematics updates, programming, commissioning, debug, and runoffs with supervision. **Key Responsibilities:** - Completes structured training/checklists; seeks feedback; applies lessons on subsequent tasks. - Performs small, scoped PLC ladder edits, basic structured-text tweaks, HMI tag routing and simple screens within established architecture and standards. - Reads and updates prints with redlines; maintains I/O lists, tag maps, device tagging, and device databases under review. - Assists I/O checkout, device bring-up, and online debug; follows test procedures; supports FAT/SAT with supervision. - Runs provided simulations; adjusts simple parameters; safely jogs/teaches points with guidance. - Keeps backups, change logs, and manuals current; practices disciplined version control. - Works constructively with Mechanical, Electrical, Build, and PM; communicates status/risks early. - Gathers accurate technical details and relays them to the project lead. - Follows LOTO/site rules; maintains organized benches, panels, and work areas. - Learns and practices our Operating Principles daily; asks for feedback; shows timeliness, accountability, and safe execution on small tasks. **Qualifications:** - **Education:** Currently enrolled in, or recently graduated from, a university program in Electrical/Controls/Mechatronics (or related field). - **Technical Skills:** - PLC/HMI: Basic ladder logic, simple ST edits, tag creation and implementation, simple screens/alarms. - Robotics: Safe jogging, point teaching, basic tool/frame setup. - Electrical Basics: Reads schematics/wire lists; verifies wiring against prints. - Networks & Devices: Basic device/IP setup and commissioning. - Documentation/Tools: Uses templates, checklists, and version control per team process. - **Communication:** Clear, timely communicator with project teams and other interns; asks clarifying questions early; provides crisp status and thorough hand-offs. - **Problem-Solving:** Demonstrates critical thinking and a structured troubleshoot-verify-document approach; knows when to escalate with clear context. - **Teamwork:** Collaborative, coachable, and respectful; supports peers during busy phases and shares what they learn. - **Reliability:** Punctual, meets commitments, follows procedures/standards, and keeps documentation current. - **Travel:** Occasional supervised visits to customer sites or supplier facilities as assigned

Every brief should start from a genuine customer insight, not just a creative instinct. - Pick up new tools quickly — AI creative platforms, performance analytics, scripting tools — and build light workflows that speed up concepting and briefing. - Support Trybe with creative briefs and strategic direction. ## ## Who You Are - Genuinely creative, with taste, opinions, and ideas you can defend. You communicate clearly, keep people informed, and know how to work across teams with different priorities and rhythms. - Obsessed with the customer. You think about who you're talking to before you think about what you want to say. - A "whatever it takes" operator who doesn't wait to be told what to do and finds a way to get things done. - Fast. You move quickly without sacrificing quality, and you know the difference. - Energized by AI and new tools. Not intimidated by new platforms — excited to figure them out. - Comfortable with ambiguity. You can start from a rough idea, a data pattern, or a half-formed brief and run with it. - A clear, clean communicator. Your briefs are easy to read and your handoffs don't require follow-ups. ## ## What You Bring - 1–3 years of experience in creative strategy, performance creative, brand or growth marketing, or a related discipline. - Fluency in Meta Ads Manager or similar performance platforms. You can read the data and draw clear conclusions from it. - Exposure to direct-response or performance advertising. You understand what makes an ad convert, not just look good. - Familiarity with short-form video formats and an instinct for what works on platforms like TikTok and Instagram Reels — you don't need to be a TikTok expert, but you should be a fluent consumer of the format. - Familiarity with AI creative tools (ChatGPT, Gemini, or similar). You don't need to have used all of them, but you should be the kind of person who will try them. - Basic editing literacy (CapCut, Premiere, or similar) is a plus — being able to mock up a rough cut can help unblock a concept. ## ## Why This Role You'll get a front-row seat to how performance creative strategy gets made — with direct access to senior creative and growth leadership. [FieldAI](https://www.fieldai.com/) is transforming how robots interact with the real world. Our growing R&D team is based in Boston, where we develop risk-aware, reliable, field-ready AI systems that tackle the hardest problems in robotics and unlock the potential of embodied intelligence. We take a pragmatic approach that goes beyond off-the-shelf, purely data-driven methods or transformer-only architectures, combining cutting-edge research with real-world deployment. Our solutions are already deployed globally, and we continuously improve model performance through rapid iteration driven by real field use. **Hardware Team:** The Hardware Team at Field AI develops perception and compute payloads that power autonomous robotics systems in complex real world environments. Our work spans the full hardware stack designing and integrating sensing systems (LiDAR, camera, TOF, IMU, GPS), embedded compute (CPUs, GPUs, microcontrollers, Linux, ROS), electrical systems (power distribution, communication), and mechanical components (structures, thermal regulation, ingress protection). The team focuses on both development (research, design, prototyping, testing) and operations (production, testing, QA, debugging). We’re a small, fast-moving team, and we care deeply about improving: 1) core capabilities, 2) system reliability, 3) system scalability. As a growing team we are also building operational systems and procedures from the ground up. **Mechanical Systems Intern Role:** As a Mechanical Engineer Intern on the Hardware Team at Field AI, you will contribute to the design and implementation of mechanical systems that house and support sensing and compute platforms in real-world environments. From ruggedized enclosures to thermal management to manufacturability, your work will be critical to ensuring our systems operate reliably in the field. Responsibilities may span the full lifecycle from CAD through production to field support. You will collaborate closely with electrical, compute, and systems engineers to build tightly integrated solutions ready for deployment in challenging field environments. Additionally while your focus will be on mechanical systems you will likely contribute across all hardware domains. ### What You Will Get To Do **Mechanical System Design** - **Structures:** Design and model mechanical structures including external enclosures, internal compute frames, and load-bearing chassis. - **Mounts:** Design and validate robust sensor mounts, payload attachment points, and mechanical interfaces. - **Ingress Protection:** Implement IP-rated solutions with gaskets, seals, membranes, and coatings to meet water/dust ingress standards. - **Thermal Management:** Incorporate thermal mitigation strategies such as fans, heat sinks, conductive paths, and airflow guides. - **Mass & Volume Budgets:** Ensure adherence to payload constraints, including tight volumetric envelopes and weight limitations. **Mechanical System Implementation** - **CAD & Simulation:** Build detailed SolidWorks CAD assemblies. Run FEA and thermal simulations to validate strength, durability, and heat dissipation. - **Material & Component Selection:** Choose materials and components to meet mass, strength, thermal, and manufacturability constraints. Design for Production: Apply DFM, DFA, DFS principles throughout the design lifecycle. - **System Testing:** Conduct mechanical load testing (shock, vibration), thermal validation, ingress tests, and sensor alignment assessments. - **Prototyping:** Rapidly iterate on prototypes for fit checks, thermal evaluations, and integration trials. - **Documentation & Budgets:** Generate mechanical drawings, GD&T annotations, BOMs, and assembly instructions for fabrication and QA. Manage weight, volume, and thermal budgets. **Mechanical System Production & Servicing** - **Build:** Work with vendors and contract manufacturers to procure mechanical hardware. Develop QA checks for incoming units. Support payload integration and scaling. - **Debug:** Investigate mechanical failures, deformation, and environmental weaknesses during testing and deployments. - **Monitor:** Develop protocols for monitoring the system mechanical health and loads. ### What You Have - **Education:** Current student pursuing a B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, or related field. - **CAD Expertise:** Proficient with SolidWorks or equivalent mechanical CAD platforms. - **Thermal & Structural Analysis:** Familiarity with FEA and thermal modeling tools. - **Field-Ready Design:** Experience designing hardware that survives vibration, shock, thermal cycling, and environmental exposure. - **Manufacturing Knowledge:** Experience designing for CNC, sheet metal, additive manufacturing, and assembly workflows. - **Mechanical Systems Integration:** Experience working across teams to integrate mechanical systems with compute, sensors, and power electronics. - **Lab Skills:** Comfort with mechanical debugging, thermal test setups, vibration tables, and ingress testing. - **Cross Functional Robotic Skills:** Ability to contribute electrical, sensing, and embedded computing work to deliver robust integrated systems. ### What Will Set You Apart - **Scaling:** Experience taking systems from prototype to large scale production. - **Field Environments:** Experience developing systems for harsh field environments. - **Deployed Robotics:** Experience working on robotics deployed in real world settings such as autonomous vehicles, drones, or ruggedized robots. - **Systems Level Robotics:** Fluency across mechanical, electrical, and software systems. - **Reliability Engineering:** Experience designing to meet IP ratings, MIL-STD, or equivalent ruggedness standards.

### **About the Company** We are a renewable energy and ocean technology company committed to rapidly developing and deploying technologies that will ensure a sustainable future for Earth by unlocking the vast energy potential of its oceans. Our focus is on capturing civilizational levels of ultra-low-cost renewable energy for applications including computing and affordable renewable fuels delivered to shore. The company is a public benefit corporation headquartered in Portland, Oregon, and backed by leading venture capitalists, philanthropic investors, university endowments, and private investment offices. We operate as an idea meritocracy in which the best ideas change the company’s direction on a regular basis. Our staff have worked at organizations such as SpaceX, Blue Origin, Boeing, Tesla, Apple, Virgin Orbit, Astra, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, New Relic, Bridgewater, Raytheon, Disney Imagineering, and the US Army and Air Force, as well as research universities, startups, and small companies across a range of industries. ### **About the Job** Our core technology is the node, a device that produces energy in the ocean’s harshest conditions for years at a time without human maintenance or intervention. As a Summer 2027 Engineering Intern, you will work on real technical problems that directly support the development and scaling of our Node technology. We expect to hire interns across several engineering disciplines, including mechanical engineering, manufacturing, and software. Your specific project and responsibilities will depend on your background, interests, and the highest-priority technical needs of the team. You will work alongside experienced engineers, technicians, and operators. We are looking for exceptional students who have demonstrated technical ability, intellectual curiosity, initiative, and a track record of building, solving, or shipping difficult things. You will be expected to learn quickly, ask thoughtful questions, document your work, communicate openly, and take meaningful ownership of your project. Candidates should have effective interpersonal skills and be able to thrive in a creative, scrappy, and collaborative environment. ### **Responsibilities** Responsibilities will vary by discipline and project, but may include: - Own and execute a clearly defined technical project supporting our Node technology with guidance from experienced team members. - Apply engineering fundamentals and analytical reasoning to solve technical problems. - Build, test, troubleshoot, or improve physical or software systems. - Analyze technical data and use results to inform engineering or process decisions. - Create clear technical documentation, including designs, analyses, test results, software documentation, or process records. - Participate in technical reviews and clearly communicate findings, tradeoffs, and recommendations. - Take ownership of assigned work and proactively communicate progress and blockers. - Incorporate feedback quickly and adapt as project priorities or requirements evolve. ### **Required Qualifications** - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s, master’s, or doctoral degree in an engineering, computer science, physics, or other closely related technical field. - Strong technical fundamentals relevant to your area of study. - Demonstrated experience applying technical skills through coursework, research, internships, student teams, independent projects, or other hands-on work. - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. - Comfortable working on problems where requirements or solutions may initially be ambiguous. - Able to work full-time and on-site in Portland, Oregon for the duration of the internship, approximately mid-June through early September 2027. - Authorization to work in the United States for the full duration of the internship. ### **Desired Qualifications** - Mechanical design, CAD, structural or thermal analysis, or hardware testing. - Manufacturing engineering, process development, tooling, automation, quality, production systems, or design for manufacturability. - Software development, data systems, automation, simulation, controls, infrastructure, or developer tooling. - Skills with machining, fabrication, welding, electronics assembly, and prototyping. - Designing and executing technical tests and analyzing the resulting data. - Participation in technically demanding student teams or projects such as Formula SAE, Baja SAE, robotics, rocketry, solar car, marine engineering, or similar programs. - Experience taking a project from an ambiguous initial problem through implementation and validation. - Exposure to renewable energy, marine systems, robotics, aerospace, industrial systems, manufacturing, or other complex hardware environments. - Experience working in a fast-moving technical environment where designs, processes, or software are tested and iterated quickly. The above qualifications are desired, not required. We encourage you to apply if you are a strong candidate with only some of the desired skills and experience listed. ### **Compensation** If hired for this internship, you will receive: - Cash compensation of $42.00 per hour. ### **Location and Duration** - This is an on-site position. Our offices, lab, and shop are located in **Portland, Oregon**. You must commit to being in person, in Portland, for the duration of this internship. - This internship will run from **mid-June through early September**, with exact dates to be confirmed. ***This is a short-term posting, and we will be accepting applications until end of day Tuesday, November 10th 2026 . Please ensure your application is submitted by this date as we will not be accepting late applications. We will begin reviewing submissions after the posting closes.***

Junior Electrical Engineer Overview: The Junior Electrical Engineer is a full-time, on-site role based in either Fremont, CA or Reno, NV. This role supports the design, testing, and optimization of electronics integrated into Pivotal’s flow control products, working closely with senior engineers and cross-functional teams. Day-to-day responsibilities include assisting with electrical schematics and layouts, performing basic calculations and simulations, supporting lab testing and troubleshooting, and documenting design changes and test results. The engineer collaborates with manufacturing and operations to resolve issues, ensure product reliability, and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives. The role also involves maintaining compliance with relevant safety and industry standards and participating in technical reviews and design updates. Key Responsibilities: Support the design of analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuits for flow control electronics, including sensor interfaces, valve drivers, power regulation, and communication interfaces. Create and update schematics and assist with PCB layout in Altium or KiCad under the guidance of senior engineers. Select and qualify electronic components, maintain part data and BOMs, and support replacements for obsolete parts. Build, bring up, and debug prototype boards; perform lab testing using oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies, and signal generators. Perform basic circuit calculations and simulations (e.g., SPICE), including power budgets, tolerance analysis, and thermal derating. Design and maintain electrical test fixtures, cable harnesses, and test procedures for engineering and production use. Document test results and design changes, and support the engineering change (ECO) process. Support manufacturing and field troubleshooting, including failure analysis of returned or nonconforming assemblies. Help ensure designs meet applicable safety and EMC requirements and industry standards (e.g., CE, SEMI S2). Collaborate with firmware, mechanical, and test engineers during product development and design reviews. Required Skills and Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a closely related field. 0–2 years of electrical engineering experience; relevant internships, co-ops, or project work are considered. Foundational knowledge in Electrical Engineering, with the ability to apply core concepts to product development and troubleshooting. Skills in electrical design, including reading and creating schematics, selecting components, and supporting prototype development. Understanding of low-voltage DC power conversion and distribution relevant to industrial and high-tech equipment. Ability to use common engineering tools and software (e.g., Altium, KiCad, and standard test equipment such as multimeters and oscilloscopes). Strong analytical, problem-solving, and documentation skills, with attention to detail and a commitment to quality. Effective communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work in cross-functional teams in an on-site environment. The ideal candidate will also have: Exposure to semiconductor, manufacturing, or industrial automation environments. Exposure to Copy Exactly! / Copy Exact! and related design replication methodologies. Hands-on PCB design, assembly, or soldering experience. Basic microcontroller or firmware experience (C/C++). Experience with test automation or data analysis tools such as Python or LabVIEW. Familiarity with relevant electrical safety standards and best practices.

About the Role At Selector, we operate on a "two-in-a-box" model: the Customer Engineer (CE) leads technical architecture, validation, and engineering requirements, while the Customer Success - Intern helps the business relationship, adoption, and value realization. As a CS- Intern, you are the owner of the customer business outcome . You are accountable for ensuring customers understand how Selector solves their problems, driving measurable platform usage, and proactively managing account health to ensure renewal and expansion. Core Responsibilities Outcome Ownership: Define and track customer success through the lens of business outcomes. You are responsible for knowing the status of every account you own without relying on engineering logs: Outcome → Adoption → Engagement → Health → Risk → Next Action . Business Relationship Leadership: Act as the primary business counterpart to the customer. Establish consistent operating cadences (weekly/bi-weekly synchronization) to move customer priorities forward and ensure alignment with the right stakeholders. Operational Adoption: Go beyond standard "happiness" metrics. Ensure the platform is integrated into the customer’s operational workflows. Monitor usage data—such as logins, incident/ticket generation, and outcome realization—to track whether the customer is achieving meaningful results. Account Health & Risk Mitigation: Maintain accurate account health assessments (Green/Yellow/Red). Use health signals—engagement, adoption, value realization, executive relationships, and commercial risk—to identify churn threats early. Establish and execute action plans to resolve risk before it escalates. Two-in-a-Box Collaboration: Partner closely with the assigned CE. While you own the business justification, commercial urgency, and customer governance (QBRs), you will align with your CE counterpart to ensure the technical architecture and engineering reality match the customer's business commitments. Outcome-Driven Reporting: Structure customer roadmaps around "Tracks" (major outcomes) rather than engineering tasks. Clearly communicate progress toward business targets (e.g., "Reduce MTTR by 30%") and maintain visibility into workstreams supporting those outcomes. Requirements & Qualifications Looking for 0 -2 years of experience in the relevant field. Outcome-Oriented Mindset: Proven ability to manage customer journeys based on desired business outcomes rather than just managing tasks or tickets. Strategic Communication: Exceptional ability to maintain executive alignment and act as a trusted advisor, with the seniority to lead QBRs that focus on business value and ROI. Data-Driven Account Management: Demonstrated skill in using usage telemetry and health indicators to make evidence-based decisions about account strategy and risk. Process & Governance Experience: Experience building or utilizing structured frameworks for account management (e.g., the "Track/Epic" model) to manage complex customer lifecycles. Collaborative Partnership: Deep experience working in "two-in-a-box" or similar cross-functional delivery models, where business owners and technical counterparts share accountability for success. Compensation The salary for this role is $6000 per month. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including prior experience and job location, and may vary from the amount listed.

We have multiple openings for Reserve Officers' Training Corps (ROTC) undergraduate level students for the opportunity to strengthen the relationship with the United States military and enhance the tie between the Department of Defense (DOD), Department of Energy-Defense Programs (DOE-DP), and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL). ROTC interns work on projects in LLNL programs focusing on national security issues such as: fusion ignition and laser technology research at the National Ignition Facility, advanced manufacturing and materials technologies in support of our stockpile stewardship program, high-performance computing to enable scientific discovery and Laboratory missions, non-proliferation and arms control, and intelligence assessment. Specific projects will be determined following discussions with selected students and supervising researchers. This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work. Interested individuals are to include their military branch of service, rank and clearance level (if any) when applying for this internship. You will Perform technical assignments of a basic degree of complexity and provide advanced technical support to scientist in scientific research and development projects. Will use more advanced techniques. Conduct research in assigned area under limited direction and supervision. Assist in conducting and documenting experiments. Collect and analyze data. Document and present results. Attend Reserve Officers' Training Corps (ROTC) Program lectures and assigned workshops. Present work through presentations and/or poster sessions. Perform all duties as assigned. Must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). See Additional Information section below for details. Active ROTC member to an academic institution. Must be a continuing college or university student in good standing at an accredited institution pursuing a undergraduate degree in physics, engineering, computer science, political science, biology or a related field. Ability to apply basic skills in engineering, scientific, or physics principles to solve technical problems. Effective communication skills. Ability to present and communicate concepts and ideas. Experience working with personal computers and familiarity with Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Ability to work in a team environment. Demonstrated academic achievement in physics, engineering, computer science or a related field. Qualifications We Desire GPA of 3.0 or above. Knowledge of computer science programs/software preferred. Pay Range $23.26 - $31.62 Hourly This position is under a step structure. Please note that the step placement is determined by your most recent completed academic year. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. We are seeking candidates for a co-op position within the Finished Products group. This assignment is expected to run from June through December, 2027. As a co-op at O-I, you will be offered challenging and diverse opportunities with access to a variety of networking and social activities. Your co-op experience with O-I will broaden your exposure to our organization and the industry. As you continue to grow, you will take on more independent work, acquire a skill set that contributes to your team’s success, and help shape our future! You will initially work closely with the Finished Products team members to understand the glass container manufacturing process and the role the team plays in it. More specifically, you will learn about glass container inspection and the cold end, which is the area where all containers are inspected and packaged. You will then be assigned to work on one or more projects to advance the objectives of the team in cold end operations. Once assigned, you will have the independence to explore the problem thoroughly and propose solutions to address the problem. You will then work with a team to reach a consensus on the desired solution and work independently to develop and roll out the solution to the Cold End Operations teams or other global teams. Some of the areas you may be working on as part of this assignment include: Review, preparation and creation of documents, videos, and other training materials to be used by the operations teams in O-I plants. Collaborate with other teams to deploy solutions Technical documentation Performing experiments (in lab, pilot, and production environments) Preparing technical reports to communicate experimental findings and presenting them to multidisciplinary teams Required: Pursuing Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electro-Mechanical Engineering, or similar field, with Junior or Senior status preferred Ability to balance several projects Good interpersonal skills, in particular networking with team members that may only collaborate through remote working Good written communication skills Attention to detail and organization Preferred: Ability to create video content Ability to self-start and engage Ability to handle uncertainty and changing priorities Ability to move quickly from ideation to execution Why Intern at O-I? Work with a global leader in sustainable packaging Gain exposure to real-world supply chain challenges and solutions Learn from experienced professionals and mentors Build your resume with impactful projects and tools Network with peers and leaders across the organization What we offer at O-I? Competitive compensation Opportunity for future growth and advancement Supportive teams to help you grow and learn new skills Are you an innovator, a problem-solver, and someone who thrives on challenges? Do you play to win and want to make a real impact? If this sounds like you, don’t wait—apply today and take the first step toward an exciting future! *If you are interested in multiple locations please only apply once, your preference will be discussed during the screening process.* Join our team as a Transportation Design Engineer, dedicated to solving complex transportation challenges and developing engineering Plans, Specifications, and Estimates (PS&E) for traffic and multimodal projects, including complete streets improvements, traffic signals, intelligent transportation solutions (ITS), lighting and illumination, pedestrian and bicycle infrastructure, transit access and speed/reliability improvements, temporary traffic control, and signing/striping plans. In our collaborative environment, you’ll gain experience with software such as AutoCAD and Microstation, Synchro/SimTraffic, Bluebeam, AGi32, and ProjectWise, while benefiting from the support of our companywide Engineering Discipline Group, focused on advancing capabilities and skills. You’ll develop project management skills through experience in the full life cycle of a project including citywide planning, project scoping, design, and construction support, and supporting state and local agencies implementing multimodal infrastructure improvements, policies, and plans. At Fehr & Peers you’ll maximize your personal and professional growth potential as you contribute to a variety of projects. ### Responsibilities - Provide support for planning and feasibility activities by developing concept designs and planning level cost estimates - Develop and analyze design alternatives for traffic engineering projects - Conduct field visits to review existing conditions and design constraints - Prepare design plans, specifications, and construction cost estimates - Provide design support during construction (requests for information, contractor submittals, etc.) - Effectively communicate engineering concepts in memos, reports, and project meetings - Collaborate with a diverse set of professionals including planners, engineers, technicians, analysists, and data scientists - Work under the guidance of professional engineers to gain experience that counts towards state licensing requirement for the P.E. exam - Embrace opportunities to learn and adopt new tools, technologies, and ways of working that enhance day-to-day work, while maintaining professional judgment, critical thinking, and accountability for results ### Qualifications - Bachelor's or master's degree in transportation, civil engineering, or a related field - Engineer-In-Training (EIT) Certification or the ability to obtain within 12 months - Work experience and/or completion of significant project coursework in traffic engineering design or related transportation design experience - Exceptional technical writing and public speaking skills - Work experience and/or coursework with software such as AutoCAD and/or Microstation (highly desirable) - Openness to exploring and responsibly using new technologies and tools, while maintaining critical thinking and professional judgment

# **About Mercor** Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents. Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices. ## **About the Role** As a Research Scientist Intern at Mercor, you’ll work on research at the frontier of post-training, reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), data generation, and model evaluation. You’ll investigate how datasets, rewards, and training methods affect the capabilities and behavior of large language models. This may include designing controlled experiments, developing new evaluation methodologies, conducting systematic failure analysis, and testing approaches to improve tool use, agentic behavior, and real-world reasoning. You’ll work closely with research scientists, research engineers, and domain experts to turn open-ended questions into rigorous experiments. Your work will contribute to Mercor’s research agenda and may support external publications, benchmark releases, and the development of frontier AI systems. ## **What You’ll Do** - Develop and investigate research questions related to post-training, RLVR, data quality, and model evaluation. - Design and run controlled experiments to understand how datasets, rewards, and training strategies affect model performance. - Study reward-shaping and post-training methods, including approaches such as GRPO and DAPO. - Develop methods for measuring data quality, usability, and performance uplift on key benchmarks. - Design and evaluate datasets, rubrics, evaluators, and scoring frameworks for complex model capabilities. - Conduct systematic error analysis to identify model failure modes and opportunities for improvement. - Analyze experimental results and communicate findings through clear reports, research artifacts, and presentations. - Build the research tooling and data pipelines needed to conduct experiments at scale. - Collaborate with research scientists, research engineers, applied AI teams, and domain experts producing training and evaluation data. - Contribute to research publications, benchmark releases, and other public research outputs where appropriate. ## **What We’re Looking For** - Currently pursuing a master’s or PhD in computer science, machine learning, statistics, mathematics, or another relevant field. - Are you passionate about leadership, operations, and creating exceptional experiences for guests and team members? Pilot Company is seeking ambitious and driven students to join our Field Leadership Academy Internship Program for Summer 2027. This unique leadership development experience is designed for students interested in pursuing a long-term career in retail operations and store leadership. The Field Leadership Academy is a 10-week rotational internship that provides hands-on exposure to Pilot's retail operations while connecting participants with leaders across multiple areas of the business. Through meaningful experiences, mentorship, and structured development, you'll gain firsthand insight into what it takes to lead high-performing teams, drive operational excellence, and build a career path toward Assistant Manager, General Manager, and Field Leadership roles. The program is designed to create a clear pathway from internship to future full-time leadership opportunities within Pilot Company What You’ll Do Participate in a structured 10-week rotational leadership experience across key areas of Pilot's operations. Gain hands-on experience supporting daily store operations, team leadership, guest service, and operational execution. Shadow and learn from store, regional, and divisional leaders to better understand Pilot's leadership culture and business strategy. Explore cross-functional areas including store operations, food operations, Human Resources, and field support functions. Complete a capstone project that showcases your learning and provides recommendations to support business objectives. Build relationships with leaders and mentors who will support your professional growth throughout the internship and beyond. Create an individualized career development and conversion plan focused on future leadership opportunities within Pilot Company. Why Pilot Company? At Pilot, our purpose is to show people they matter at every turn. We believe our future success depends on leaders who can create exceptional guest experiences, build strong teams, and deliver operational excellence. The Field Leadership Academy was designed to help develop the next generation of those leaders by providing meaningful experiences, executive exposure, and a structured path toward future career opportunities. Our culture is built on four core virtues: Driven, Reliable, Authentic, and Welcoming. Throughout the internship, you'll see these values in action while learning from leaders who are committed to your growth and development. This is a full-time, paid, 10-week summer internship hosted in select Pilot markets across the United States. Participants will receive ongoing mentorship, career development support, and a personalized conversion plan designed to prepare them for future store leadership opportunities following graduation Potential Career Path Field Leadership Academy Intern → Store Leadership Opportunity → Assistant Manager Development → General Manager → Field Leadership What We’re Looking For Currently pursuing a bachelor's degree with an expected graduation date within 6 to 12 months following the internship. Strong interest in retail operations, hospitality, business management, or leadership development. Desire to pursue a long-term career in store or field leadership. Demonstrated leadership experience through work, student organizations, athletics, volunteer activities, or other experiences. Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to build relationships across all levels of the organization. Adaptability, initiative, and a willingness to learn in a fast-paced operational environment. Ability to travel within assigned host markets during the internship program. Pilot Company supports a growing portfolio of brands with expertise in supply chain and retail operations, logistics and transportation, technology and digital innovation, construction, maintenance, human resources, finance, sales and marketing. **Overview:** The Investment Banking, Summer Associate will play an important role on the firm’s advisory team, supporting an appropriately staffed team in a broad range of transactions including; mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, restructurings, royalty monetizations and capital markets transactions. Summer Associates will provide deliverables that are relied upon by our senior bankers to help our clients and can expect to receive a high level of responsibility and deal execution experience. The Summer Associate may also be responsible for completing special projects as assigned by the staffer and senior bankers. The Summer Associate must enjoy working within an entrepreneurial environment that is results-driven and community oriented. The ideal individual has the ability to exercise good judgement in a variety of situations, has strong written and verbal communication as well as the ability to balance multiple priorities. The Investment Banking Summer Associate will have the ability to work independently but is also expected to thrive in a team environment. **Day-to-day Responsibilities** Investment Banking Summer Associates will get a well-rounded experience by working on multiple assignments in all stages of the deal lifecycle process, from idea generation, to formal assignment pitching, to executing a deal. Summer Associates will work with a team to help create detailed financial models used for valuation and financial analysis (DCF, LBO, M&A, accretion/dilution, comparable company and precedent transaction analysis). Prepare marketing documents, including pitch materials, confidential offering memoranda, management presentations, fairness opinions and board presentations. Conduct extensive financial and industry due diligence to evaluate the risk/return parameters of a transaction. Support senior bankers in their relationship development responsibilities, including interaction with current and prospective clients and new idea generation. Summer Associates will participate in client meetings, due diligence visits and other client interactions during which they gain exposure to key executives and senior bankers. **Qualifications** Candidates must currently be enrolled full-time in a top MBA program with a strong emphasis on finance coursework and should have a strong desire to work in investment banking. Prior healthcare industry work experience is beneficial, but not required. We are looking for candidates with strong quantitative and qualitative analytical skills, clear communication and presentation skills, and strong command of corporate finance and accounting. We seek candidates with keen attention to detail, ability to be a strategic thinker, entrepreneurial spirit, desire to excel, overall excellent judgment and character, and commitment to contributing to the MTS team culture and growing our firm. **Why Choose MTS as a Career** **MTS Health Partners, L.P.** is a fast-paced, collegial environment with a tight-knit culture focused on professional growth. Anchored by the foundation of a well-run partnership, team members have unparalleled access to Senior Bankers and are rewarded with responsibilities commensurate with demonstrated skill and professional maturity. MTS promotes an environment based on teamwork and camaraderie, with an emphasis on entrepreneurship, accountability and innovation. MTS is dedicated to promoting from within the firm and developing each team member’s career. **Why Clients Choose MTS as Their Banker** **MTS Health Partners, L.P.**, is a preeminent New York City-based healthcare investment bank, providing strategic advisory services related to mergers & acquisitions, divestitures, restructuring, and equity and structured products capital markets transactions for companies in the global healthcare industry. MTS focuses on the following subsectors of the healthcare industry: healthcare services, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, generics, medical devices and diagnostics. Founded in 2000, MTS is distinguished by its dedicated healthcare industry focus, senior level hands-on deal execution, and the unique perspective and network MTS brings given the deep experience of its senior professional team - all without the conflicts of interest that most banks face. The U.S. and global healthcare industry is currently in the midst of unprecedented growth and change in a volatile economic environment; MTS plays a crucial role in advising our clients as they face critical strategic and financial decisions during these times. Uniquely, MTS’ business model focuses on alignment with our clients, building long-term relationships and engineering and executing the “right” transaction for our client. We specialize in executing complex transactions (e.g. mergers, restructurings, privately negotiated equity, structured debt, hybrid financings) where our “skill” as bankers is more important than the “scale” of an organization, such as in widely syndicated transactions (e.g. follow-on equity offerings, senior debt offerings). However, when a situation calls for a hybrid approach of private negotiation and public syndication, we also have the ability, as a registered broker-deal, and the flexibility to call on our experience and relationships to orchestrate the appropriate deal. Whereas many banks are divided into industry coverage groups and product groups, the same deal team at MTS originates and executes the transaction, thus maintaining control of every aspect of advice, strategy, and execution and avoiding the conflicts of interest seen at other advisory firms.

# A little about us [](http://incident.io) is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Netflix, Etsy, and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime. The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously. We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join. # **Your way into tech sales** If you've been looking for an opportunity to break in, this is it. We're looking for purposeful, high-potential people who take coaching well, brush off rejection, and are always finding ways to level up. You don't need sales experience. As long as you have the raw ingredients, we can teach the rest. Sales Academy is a 3-month program where you'll learn from proven sales leaders and all-star sellers, and you'll be selling a product customers love. The world's best engineering teams rely on [](http://incident.io) when things go wrong, so you'll start your career with something worth talking about. # **What that looks like day to day** You'll start in January 2027 alongside a cohort of people who, like you, have never done this job before. You get to be bad at it in front of people who are also bad at it, and get good fast. **Part one: training.** You'll get intensive training and support from our sales leaders and tenured sellers. It covers researching prospects, cold calling, writing outreach people want to answer, and handling objections. You'll also learn how [](http://incident.io) works, who we sell to, and why they buy. There's daily practice, homework, and plenty of coaching from people who want to see you succeed. **Part two: doing the job.** For the rest of the academy, you'll work as a Business Development Rep (BDR) on live accounts. You'll make calls and send outreach, and the meetings you book will feed our pipeline. By the end, you'll be able to hold your own on a cold call with a CTO. # **What you get out of it** **It all starts here.** BDRs are the bench for the rest of our go-to-market team. People in this seat go on to become Account Executives, Account Managers, and Customer Success Managers. The goal is for everyone who finishes the academy to convert to a permanent BDR, launching a long, high-trajectory career here at [](http://incident.io). Alongside sales training, you'll get professional development and networking opportunities across the wider business. We want you to feel like part of our culture from day one, not someone passing through. **If you don't convert,** you'll still have had three months of paid, on-the-job training. You'll leave with tested, marketable hard skills and a clearer sense of your strengths and where you'd do your best work. We'll do our best to help you with your next move. # **Who you are** - **You've never been a BDR before.** You might be a new grad, someone switching careers (teaching, the military, sport, performing), or someone from traditional sales like retail, door-to-door, events, or fundraising. We care about what you're capable of, not what's on your resume. - **You really want this.** You're not drifting into tech sales. You've decided, and you can tell us why. - **You're seriously curious.** About people, about what's keeping a VP of Engineering up at night, and about why one call landed when another didn't. - **You've had to be resilient already.** You've held a room, or heard "no" over and over without taking it personally. - **You like being coached.** Someone has told you the honest version of how you're doing, and you got better for it. - **The phone doesn't scare you.** You may never have made a cold call, but talking to strangers all day sounds fun rather than horrifying. - **You want the cohort.** Learning alongside other people, being measured against them, and wanting them to do well too sounds good to you, not stressful. # **Interview process at a glance** - **Stage 1: Video application & aptitude assessment.** Send us your LinkedIn profile, your contact details, and a quick video on why you'd be great at this. From there, we'll email a link to complete a 25-minute aptitude assessment. - **Stage 2: On-site interview.** A half day in our San Francisco office with the sales team. - **Stage 3: Offer.** # **Good to know** - **This role is based in our San Francisco office.** You're welcome to apply from outside the Bay Area, but you'll need to be in the office from day one, working five days per week in office. - **We don't provide relocation assistance for this role.** - **This is a 3-month temporary role**, and the goal is to convert you to a permanent employee when the academy ends. - **Benefits start when you convert to a permanent role.** You won't be eligible for our employee benefit plans during the 3-month academy. - **Our first cohort starts in January 2027.** Applications for this cohort close on December 1st. We'll begin hiring for our April 2027 cohort January 4th.

Position Overview Novelis is one of the world leaders in aluminum recycling and rolling and a leading sustainable aluminum solutions provider. Driven by our purpose of shaping a sustainable world together, we work alongside our customers to provide innovative solutions to the aerospace, automotive, beverage packaging and specialty markets. Headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, Novelis has approximately 13,000 employees in 32 operating facilities on 4 continents. Responsibilities & Qualifications Position Overview The Specialties team in Kennesaw, GA is seeking a Surface Engineering & Corrosion Testing Co-op. This role will support evaluation of aluminum surface treatments and corrosion performance for battery applications through sample preparation, battery-relevant testing, surface characterization before and after testing, and data analysis. This role will be from May 2027 until December 2027. Responsibilities Prepare aluminum samples for surface treatment and battery-application testing. Support corrosion and battery-relevant testing activities. Characterize surfaces before and after testing using microscopy and other materials analysis techniques. Track samples, test matrices, and results. Analyze data, summarize findings, and recommend next steps. Minimum qualifications Pursuing a degree in Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, Chemistry, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field. Sophomore, junior, or senior undergraduate student enrolled in an accredited 4-year university. Strong analytical, laboratory, data analysis, and documentation skills. Must be currently authorized to work in the United States for any employer. Preferred qualifications Interest in materials science, surface engineering, corrosion science, electrochemistry, metallurgy, battery materials, or analytical chemistry. Experience with sample preparation, materials testing, chemical handling, or test coordination. Experience using characterization tools such as SEM, optical microscopy, ICP/OES, XPS, profilometry, or related techniques to evaluate surfaces before and after testing. Strong communication skills and ability to organize data, interpret results, and summarize technical findings. *Please note that we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position. Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for current or future sponsorship What We Offer: Novelis' benefits say a lot about how we care for each other. Our employees and their families have many different needs. As a result, our benefits offer choices on many levels and are high in quality, driven by the marketplace, and affordable. In addition to core benefits, we provide these unique to the industry benefits: Combined housing and relocation stipend for out of state interns or interns outside an extended radius for select positions Competitive pay Location Profile Novelis’ Global Research and Technology Center located in Kennesaw Georgia within the greater Atlanta metropolitan area is a cutting-edge full-service research and technology hub that employs approximately 200 people including world-class engineers metallurgists chemists scientists technologists and technicians. The facility includes state-of-the-art lab equipment and a diverse mix of product pilot lines that bring innovative solutions to customers in the automotive beverage can and specialty markets. Kennesaw provides a diverse and family-friendly place to live with countless museums cultural opportunities and educational institutions. Packaging Engineer Intern Job Description: The packaging engineering group of MACOM supports the design, development, and implementation of packaging solutions for RF semiconductor devices. Interns may assist in package design work and in creating / reviewing assembly drawings using CAD software. They may collect data directly or coordinate work with external labs, using metrology and failure analysis tools and techniques. They may help design experiments and analyze results using statistical techniques and process improvement methodology. Interns may also, depending on skill level, run thermal and mechanical simulations with FEA software packages to characterize new materials and device designs. Interns will periodically need to put together reports of work and present to other engineers and management.

RF Power Application Intern Role Overview: The RF Power Application Intern will design, assemble, and test RF Power application circuits in support of our RF power amplifier product line. The intern will learn to utilize RF models and measured data to drive circuit level designs. This will include learning to utilize RF test equipment and test software to perform RF measurements, such as s-parameters and circuit level characterization. This role will also utilize AWR to model and analyze RF device performance. Additional activity will include designing PCB layouts, hands-on PCB assembly and soldering, data analysis, and updating datasheets to reflect new application board designs. During the internship, the applicant will learn: RF matching design techniques RF circuit board simulation and manufacturing AutoCAD mechanical design Hands-on RF Power circuit assembly and test Documentation suitable for sharing with customers. Requirements: College student working towards a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, or the equivalent. Must have an interest in one or more of the following: magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), radar, cellular telephone, satellites, avionics or in an industry relevant to radio frequency power Mechanical aptitude, should have experience working with small tools. Soldering experience is a plus along with experience building small electronic circuits.

GaN RF Power Amplifier Intern Job Description: The engineering intern will be working at the Morgan Hill CA Design Center alongside a highly knowledgeable team of RF engineers and will initially be tasked with device characterization of MACOM’s high power GaN transistor products geared towards Base Station market. As an intern you will learn to operate the RF test bench software and Digital Predistortion testers, handling RF devices, biasing devices, capturing accurate RF data, and performing a limited amount of data processing. This device characterization activity will be in support of current product development and R D activities. A follow-on activity will task the intern to design an impedance matching network for a GaN device, using either MWO or ADS design software, in order to match the device to a 50 ohm environment. The intern will be expected to layout the impedance matching network in AutoCAD, have it fabricated and will be tasked to assemble, solder components, and tune the circuit on the RF bench. During the 12 weeks each Intern will: > Be given an individual and well-defined project with set outcome goals > Gain hands on experience > Receive excellent training and ongoing supervision > Be invited to attend an intern webinar series > Attend networking/social events > Attend and present at Poster Session about each Interns project successes and pitfalls > Receive formal, written feedback

## **Compound Management Specialist (Part-time Internship)** **Time Commitment:** 1-2 days per week **Location:** Boston, MA ### **About Proxima** Proxima is a frontier AI and data generation company discovering the next generation of proximity therapeutics by making protein interactions programmable. Our platform brings together foundation-model machine learning, a scalable data generation engine, and a partnership track record exceeding $5B in collaborations across the world’s leading biopharma and tech organizations. We’ve recently closed an oversubscribed seed round with an elite group of VCs including DCVC, NVIDIA’s NVentures, AIX, Yosemite among others. Neo-1 is our all-atom foundation model that combines state-of-the-art structure prediction and molecular generation in a single system. Neo-1 enables rapid exploration of chemical and structural space for high value, previously intractable targets, and in particular unlocks small molecule proximity therapeutics like molecular glues with AI for the first time. Together with Neo-1, it creates an integrated system capable of co-folding protein complexes while generating candidate small molecules to influence those interactions. Proximity-based therapeutics represent one of the most promising frontiers in modern drug discovery with the potential to treat previously intractable diseases and target ‘undruggable’ proteins. We’re building the tech and the team to make that happen. role: Run Perception Graduate Internship, R&D - Winter 2027
description: **Who We Are:** At Brooks, we believe movement is the key to feeling more alive. That’s why we’re driven to create gear and experiences that take people to the place that makes them feel more alive — whether it’s a headspace, a feeling, or a finish line. Everyone who works at Brooks is propelled by a company culture that sparks excitement, fuels collaboration, inspires creativity, and ignites innovation. Our brand values help bond us together and drive our success: - ***Runner First*** - *We act in the best interest of the runner* - ***Word is Bond*** - *We do what we say we’ll do* - ***Champion Heart*** - *We give our all in everything we do* - ***There is no “I” in Run*** - *We stay generous with our humanity* - ***Keep Moving*** - *We find ways to move every day, because joy is kinetic!* We welcome everyone from every walk of life looking to inspire others through the power of movement - because we’re *all* moving towards something. Let’s run there. #### Brooks Internship Program: Brooks Running hosts internships at our Seattle HQ offices to provide hands-on, meaningful work experience to further enhance your education and professional aptitude. Our interns gain exposure to real work, and projects while working side by side with Brooks employees and leadership. If chosen for this role, you will embark on 6 months of learning, professional development, and exposure to the Brooks brand and culture. #### Internship Details: Duration: 6 months Internship Target Start: January 11, 2027 Compensation: $33.00/hr Location: Seattle, HQ Schedule: 40 hours / week Please apply if you can commit to the duration, salary and location for this opportunity. #### Your Opportunity: Our Run Perception Team is seeking a master’s graduate intern to work at our Seattle HQ offices. As the Run Perception Intern, you will gain hands-on experience in product research at the leading running brand – Brooks Sports, Inc. Your primary responsibilities will be to assist Run Perception Researchers as they collect information from product testers across the nation to contribute key perceptual information regarding fit, performance, and design. This information is critical for our multi-departmental infrastructure, including Development, Design, and Merchandising, to ensure that performance integrity of our product meets the needs of our end consumers. You will also gain knowledge on how perceptual feedback influences design and development of athletic products at Brooks. With the Run Perception Team being part of our Development team, you will learn how to work closely with the Developers on building product based off insights collected not only from the Run Perception Team, but also from other collaborators across the company. #### Your Impact (Responsibilities): - Understand athletic product design features and components, and how they influence fit, feel, and ride. - Conduct internal and external perception testing data collections for inline footwear and the sourcing team. This entails targeted participant recruitment based on the product goals and consumer base, creation of perception surveys that test the hypotheses at hand, analysis of qualitative results, and synthesis of data into a clear point of view highlighting how the product is performing. - Compile and present scientific reports via PowerPoint, summarizing findings based on runner feedback that are delivered to product teams for use in product improvement. - Use your graduate-level research skills to conduct Run Perception studies that lead to innovative testing procedures and optimization of product for all who run. - Use your advanced data analytics skills to mine data in our Tableau historical dashboards containing over 3 million words of perception testing feedback for product over the last six years to recommend product improvements based on identified opportunities. - Use AI-powered tools to help analyze and summarize wear test feedback at both the individual and historical dataset level, uncovering meaningful patterns and insights that strengthen product storytelling and recommendations. - Develop loyal, engaging relationships with our product testers and the Brooks community. - Assist with the management of Brooks perception testing community social media account on Facebook with timely and accurate responses to participants and the creation of engaging content for the group. Other duties as assigned. #### Project: As a part of your experience as a graduate intern at Brooks, you will have the opportunity to complete a project under the support and supervision of your manager. Details of your project will be finalized once you arrive at Brooks based on your interests and the needs of the business. You will use your ever-growing analytical skillset as a graduate student to prepare a thoughtful and elevated project. Weave your learnings from your graduate courses into your work to challenge yourself and benefit Brooks. You will present your work and findings to senior leadership at Brooks at the end of your internship, to hone in on your research, recommendation, and presentation skills. ### Qualifications: - Master’s degree with a background in biomechanics, kinesiology, and/or exercise science or an equivalent analytical field. - Willing to commit to the intern position for six months onsite in Seattle, WA - Willingness to learn and gain hands-on experience. - Able to commit to up to 40 hours a week to be physically present at HQ. - Strong verbal and written communication skills, demonstrating effective listening through concise and clear verbal and written communication. - Experience with Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. - Well-developed quantitative skills with an aptitude for report-building, data mining, and interpretation. - Product creation or running retail experience is ideal. - Strong organizational skills. - Detail-oriented with an emphasis on quality work products. Always looking to improve our products and processes while also displaying a willingness to dive into the details and help wherever necessary. - Must be able to collaborate in a team-oriented environment. - Understanding our product line and our competitors desired. - Experience using AI for data analysis support or brainstorming desired. - Embrace Brooks values!

role: Summer 2027 Liberty and National Security Legal Internship - NYC and DC
description: The Brennan Center for Justice at NYU School of Law is a nonpartisan law and policy institute that seeks to improve the systems of democracy and justice in the United States. We work to hold our political institutions and laws accountable to the twin American ideals of democracy and equal justice for all. The Brennan Center’s work ranges from voting rights to campaign finance reform, from ending mass incarceration to preserving Constitutional protections in the fight against terrorism. Part think tank, part advocacy group, part cutting edge communications hub, we start with rigorous research. We craft innovative policies. And we fight for them – in Congress and the states, in the courts, and in the court of public opinion. We are hiring law students to intern with our Liberty and National Security Program (LNS) in our New York and Washington, DC offices for the summer of 2027. The LNS Program works to advance effective national security policies that respect the rule of law and constitutional values. Our current program priorities include ensuring that Congress and the courts serve their constitutional role as a check on executive power in the area of national security and domestic terrorism; reforming emergency powers to strengthen safeguards against abuse; ending racial, religious, and ethnic profiling in counterterrorism policies; bolstering First and Fourth Amendment protections in the digital age; and enhancing transparency, oversight, and accountability for homeland security, intelligence, and law enforcement agencies. Note: This internship is in-person at our New York City or Washington D.C. office. Legal interns work alongside staff on policy advocacy, research, and litigation initiatives. Interns may assist with a variety of activities, including legal, policy, and factual research to advance administrative and legislative advocacy at federal, state, and local levels; public education and scholarship; and litigation in trial and appellate courts. We strive to offer a fun and intellectually challenging legal intern experience that supports the vital advocacy offered by the Brennan Center. Specific responsibilities may include legal research and writing for amicus briefs, policy reports, and other advocacy documents; drafting communications to legislators; assisting with public comments to federal agencies; attending coalition meetings; drafting posts for the Brennan Center website; and more. Qualifications: Excellent legal research, analysis, and writing skills; initiative, imagination, and versatility; and a passion for our issues. We are committed to considering a wide range of candidates, including those with diverse experiences and backgrounds. If you're uncertain about meeting 100% of our qualifications, we encourage you to apply anyway. In your cover letter, please share your interest in the position and what you hope to contribute to the role. This internship is only open to law students in Summer 2027. Hours: Monday – Friday (9:00am – 5:00pm EST) Pay: The Brennan Center offers stipends to summer legal interns through the Les Fagen Legal Internship Program, thanks to the generosity of Brennan Center Board member, Les Fagen. The stipend amounts will be: 1Ls - $8,360 stipend for 10 weeks 2Ls - $9,360 stipend for 10 weeks Note: If you are working more or less than 10 weeks, a pro-rated stipend amount will be calculated if awarded. The same applies if you are working less than 40 hours a week. You will typically receive payment via physical check within your first two weeks of employment (subject to change). Duration: June – August 2027 (10 weeks) Application Deadline: January 4, 2027 Note: The Brennan Center will follow the rules of your school regarding internships. Therefore, if a school doesn’t allow you to do a paid internship for some reason (i.e., receiving credit, etc.), then your internship will not be paid. In addition, if you are participating in a formal school internship program that allows you to work more than our stated hours, we will make a determination based on our needs and further assessment of your school’s program. The following materials are required to apply for our internship: a cover letter explaining why you are interested in Liberty & National Security policy issues; a current law school transcript; a legal writing sample (5-10 pages); a current resume; and contact information for three supervisor references To Apply: Please visit >>LINK HERE with “Summer LNS Legal Internship” in the subject line, after registering in the online system.
