As a Team Lead, you may also help identify strong student referrals and serve as a helpful point of contact for your territory or campus. You will have the opportunity to earn $100 for each eligible referral you bring in who is hired and begins working on the program, in accordance with program referral guidelines. About the company you will represent: SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars. Why this is a great student opportunity • Get experience that stands out on your resume, including sales, business development, territory management, and customer engagement. • Represent a high-growth technology brand while helping expand access to reliable connectivity in nearby communities. • Be part of a program connected to SpaceX's broader mission of developing technologies that make a more connected, future-focused world possible. • Earn hourly pay plus meaningful commission, with a part-time schedule designed to work around your classes. • Build confidence talking with new people, handling objections, and learning how to turn conversations into results. • Receive paid training, coaching, and support from Mosaic leaders who want to see you succeed. What you will do Own your territory. You will be assigned neighborhoods around campus and use broadband coverage maps and territory tools to find households that may be a great fit for Starlink. You wil l help plan your routes, track your outreach, and learn what works as you build momentum. Start real conversations. Introduce Starlink through door-to-door outreach, explain the current service and hardware offerings, answer questions, and help interested customers get started using your personal referral code. Customers complete their own order on their phone, so you never handle payment or personal information. Make an impact in the community. Look for opportunities beyond the front door, including farmers’ markets, community events, local business partnerships, and civic groups where residents gather. Strong performers may have the opportunity to support Starlink events and activations. Grow your network. Turn positive conversations and satisfied customers into introductions to neighbors, family, and friends who may be looking for a better internet option. Learn from your results. Log your activity, sales, hours, and mileage in Mosaic's field app at the end of each shift. You will also have regular check-ins with your Regional Sales Manager to review wins, talk through challenges, and sharpen your approach. Who will thrive in this role? You are currently enrolled in school and can work 15 to 25 hours per week around your class schedule, including some evenings and weekends when residents are most likely to be home. You have a reliable personal vehicle, a valid driver's license, and a smartphone. Because territories are rural, reliable transportation is important. You do not need prior sales experience to be successful here. We are looking for students who are ambitious, coachable, comfortable meeting new people, and excited to learn. Experience in sales, fundraising, customer service, athletics, student organizations, or campus leadership is a plus. You are self-motivated and dependable. You will have a manager, training, territory guidance, and a clear plan, but your success will come from how you manage your time, follow through, and keep showing up with energy and curiosity. What you will walk away with • Paid training from Mosaic and Starlink/SpaceX so you feel prepared before you go into the field. • Real experience in sales, lead generation, territory planning, community outreach, and customer engagement. • Coaching and feedback from experienced field sales leaders who can help you build skills you will use beyond this role. • Resume-building experience with a well-known technology brand and a role that shows initiative, communication, persistence, and ownership. • Potential consideration for spring semester expansion opportunities or campus lead roles based on performance and program needs. Pay, perks, and support This role offers base pay of an hourly rate plus a $200 commission for each qualified activation, paid after the activation is qualified. Compensation is designed to reward both consistency and performance, making this a strong earning opportunity for students who are motivated to build their territory. Team Leads may also receive $100 for each eligible referral who is hired and begins working on the program, subject to program referral guidelines. You will also receive paid training, mileage reimbursement, a monthly cell phone stipend, Mosaic-provided Starlink apparel, territory guidance, and regular manager support. For example, a representative working 20 hours per week who reaches the program minimum target of 10 activations per month would earn a base pay plus $2,000 in commission for that month. Program timeline and details Paid training begins the week of October 5, 2026, with field selling from October 12 through the end of the year. Strong performers may be considered for spring semester expansion and campus lead opportunities. Representatives are W-2 employees of Mosaic, not of Starlink or SpaceX. Employment is contingent on a background check completed after offer. Some markets require a local solicitation permit, which Mosaic will help you obtain. Must be 18 or older and authorized to work in the United States. Mosaic Sales Solutions, part of Acosta Group, builds and operates field sales and marketing programs for leading brands. Starlink is SpaceX's internet service, helping connect people in places where traditional options may be limited. If you are an ambitious student and think you have what it takes to grow your local territory, build real-world sales skills, and make an impact in nearby communities, apply today.

Aescape is a New York-based physical AI and robotics company redefining human recovery through intelligent, precision bodywork, elevating it into a consistent, outcomes-driven practice. Powered by real-time body mapping, advanced robotics, and proprietary software, Aescape delivers deeply personalized bodywork that continuously adapts to the individual. This creates a superior way for members to move with greater ease, recover more efficiently, and optimize how they feel every single day. Aescape is building a defining brand for recovery, shifting behavior from a sporadic experience into a progressive, measurable routine, unlocking compounding benefits that build lasting resilience and laying the groundwork for an entirely new category of proactive human health and performance. Aescape powers recovery across leading fitness, hospitality, and wellness environments, including Equinox, Life Time, Marriott, Hilton, Four Seasons, Pause Studios, and Remedy Place, and is backed by Valor Equity Partners, BroadLight Capital, and Mecha Ventures. **Aescape** is looking for a **Junior Electrical & Firmware Engineer** to join our hardware team and work across the electronics and embedded software that make our robot move and sense. You will support schematic and PCB design, write and debug firmware on our embedded platforms, and spend significant time on the bench bringing boards up, instrumenting them, and fault finding across hardware and firmware. This is a hands-on early-career role on a small, senior team: you will be mentored closely by experienced engineers, given ownership of meaningful subsystems early, and you will ship hardware that real people experience with their bodies. If this sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you! **This role is based out of our NYC office in Chelsea, onsite 5 days per week.** ## **What You’ll Do** - **Electrical Design Support:** Support schematic capture, component selection, and PCB layout review for motor drive, sensing, power, and control electronics. Read datasheets closely, run the calculations behind a part choice, and help carry boards from design through fabrication and assembly. - **Firmware Development:** Write, test, and debug embedded firmware in C/C++ on our microcontroller platforms: peripheral drivers, communication interfaces (SPI, I2C, UART, CAN), sensor integration, and device control. Work within our version control, code review, and release practices. - **Board Bring-Up & Debug:** Bring up new hardware on the bench, and debug across the electrical and firmware boundary using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multimeters, power supplies, and debuggers. Solder, rework, and instrument your own test setups. - **Test & Characterization:** Build bench test setups, collect and analyze characterization data, and report what the data shows. Drive decisions from measured data and physics. - **Manufacturing & Supplier Support:** Support production test fixtures, design for testability, and electrical builds with our contract manufacturer and suppliers. Help triage and root-cause issues found in manufacturing and in the field. - **Cross-Functional Partnership:** Partner with Mechanical, Controls, Software, and Operations on motor selection, drivers, sensors, and system bring-up, and communicate what you find clearly to partners outside your discipline. - **Documentation:** Produce the documentation others need to use your work: schematics, BOMs, wiring diagrams, test plans, and test reports. ## **What You’ll Bring** - **Education & Experience:** BS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related discipline, with 0–3 years of professional experience. Internships, co-ops, research, competition teams, or substantial personal projects count. - **Circuit Fundamentals:** Solid grounding in analog and digital circuit design, power electronics basics, and schematic capture in a professional tool such as Altium. You can read a datasheet and justify a component choice with numbers. - **Embedded Firmware & Python:** Working proficiency in C or C++ on microcontrollers, bare-metal or RTOS, with familiarity across common peripherals and communication protocols, and in Python for test automation and application-level work. Comfortable with Git and code review. - **Lab Skills:** Hands-on with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multimeters, and bench power supplies, and comfortable soldering and reworking your own boards. - **Debugging Mindset:** You approach a failure with a clear question in mind: what is happening, why, and how would I prove it. You stay with a problem until you find the actual cause rather than a workaround. - **Cross-Disciplinary Curiosity:** Interest in how electronics, firmware, and mechanics come together in a working machine, and comfort working with engineers outside your discipline. - **Communication:** Clear written and verbal skills. You document what you did and explain what you found so others can act on it. - **Adaptability:** A driven self-starter who is comfortable with ambiguity and able to pivot as priorities shift in a fast-moving startup; willing to take on work outside your core role when required. - **Nice to Have:** Experience with brushless motor control or motor drivers, sensor signal conditioning, PCB layout, or robotics projects. - **Work Onsite:** Ability to work from our NYC office 5 days a week. ## **What’s In It For You** - Join a trailblazing robotics and AI company building the future of recovery - The chance to make a difference with a product that empowers healthier and happier living - Team culture driven by passion, ambition, empowerment, inclusion, curiosity, and fun! - 100% employer-paid healthcare coverage for employees with generous coverage for eligible dependents - Flexible time off - Quarterly Wellness Days - everyone fully unplugs - Generous parental leave - Complimentary OneMedical membership - 401(k) with employer matching - Home office budget - Annual stipend for professional development - Working late? Dinner is on us - Complimentary Aescape recovery sessions for yourself, friends & family **Compensation**: Base salary range of **$95,000 - $125,000** annually, plus discretionary annual bonus, plus equity grant commensurate with the role and company stage. Full-time employees are also eligible for our comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k), paid time off, and paid parental leave. ## **Equal Opportunity Employer** Aescape is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. The salary range listed above is a good-faith estimate provided in accordance with New York City's pay transparency law. ## **Begin Your Aescape Career Journey** At Aescape, we're on a mission to redefine self-care for a better world, and we're seeking trailblazers to join us on this journey. We're inspired by individuals who are passionate, driven, and eager to learn. We value diverse perspectives and resourceful, determined individuals who are committed to making a difference. At Aescape, we empower people to reach their full potential, just as our product empowers better living. If you're ready to innovate, create, and make a meaningful impact, we want you on our team. **YOUR JOURNEY. YOUR AESCAPE.**

**Overview** Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The [Data Systems group at Microsoft Research](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/group/datasystems) works on problems in data management in the era of cloud computing and artificial intelligence. We work on large-scale cloud data platforms including aspects such as resource management, storage, hardware-accelerated query processing, query optimization, and auto-tuning. Another area of interest is discovery and curation of data in the context of data lakes. We are also exploring how to enable users and AI agents to interact with data systems safely and efficiently. Our research innovations have been incorporated into Microsoft products and services including SQL Server, Azure SQL Database, Azure Cosmos DB, Microsoft Fabric, Dynamics 365, Microsoft Excel, and Power Query. Our research has also led to open-source software. Our work has also had significant impact on academia. We publish at top venues including SIGMOD, VLDB, CIDR, OSDI, and NeurIPS. Our research has received multiple best-paper, influential-paper, and test-of-time awards, including Best Paper and Best Paper Honorable Mention at VLDB 2026 and Best Industry Paper at SIGMOD 2026. As a Research Intern, you will collaborate closely with researchers and engineers to advance the state-of-the-art in data systems. Research Internship projects emphasize research innovation with the potential for real-world impact. **Responsibilities** Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. **Qualifications** Required Qualifications - Accepted or currently enrolled in a PhD program in Computer Science or related STEM field. Other Requirements - Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. - In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. Preferred Qualifications - Familiarity with data systems internals. - Proficient in application of AI/Machine Learning technologies to data management problems. The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. role: KIP Spring 2027 - Campus Freedom Intern - The American Council of Trustees and Alumni
description: **[The Koch Internship Program](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/koch-internship-program/) (KIP)** is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Early-career professionals including undergraduate/graduate/law students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the [admissions process](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/application-process/) early! [The American Council of Trustees and Alumni (ACTA)](https://www.goacta.org/) is an independent, nonprofit organization committed to academic freedom, academic excellence, and accountability at America’s colleges and universities. Launched in 1995, we are the only organization that works with trustees, alumni, donors, policymakers, and education leaders across the United States to support liberal arts education, uphold high academic standards, safeguard the free exchange of ideas on campus, and ensure that the next generation receives a high-quality college education at an affordable price. The Campus Freedom Intern advances ACTA’s mission of higher education reform by supporting efforts to help higher education leaders and the public understand the importance of free expression and view point diversity in the academy; research best-practices, surveys, and other reports on issues related to academic freedom; and effect positive change to improve the conditions for free expression and viewpoint diversity on American campuses. The CampusFreedom Intern will report to ACTA’s Paul & Karen Levy Fellow in Campus Freedom. **This is envisioned as a Washington, DC-based position but a hybrid arrangement is possible.** The CampusFreedom Intern must approach these tasks as an entrepreneurial enterprise, requiring an understanding of and proactive approach to ACTA’s program activities. He or she is expected to be personable, dynamic, well organized, highly motivated, and principled. The highest degree of personal responsibility, accountability, and honesty is expected. ### Specifically, the Campus Freedom intern will: - Assist the CFI team with analyzing academic policies regarding free speech, academic freedom, and diversity of thought on college and university campuses. - Provide research support for reports on specific topics related to the policy recommendations in the ACTA Gold Standard and other issues related to campus freedom. - Assist the CFI team in updating universities on the website using the ACTA Gold Standard for Freedom of Expression™. - Provide research and writing support for the Paul & Karen Levy Fellow in Campus Freedom. - Assist with letters and statements responding to campus freedom issues as they arise. - Monitor higher ed news and keep the CFI team informed of developments pertaining to our work.

Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly-sophisticated customers across the globe – large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military. With five satellites on orbit and many more set to launch soon, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization. Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Blackrock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA. #### **Electrical Integration Intern - Avionics (Winter 2027)** Internships at Astranis typically last for twelve weeks, and are hourly roles designed for students who are currently enrolled at a four-year university. Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. Follow Shield AI on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai), [X](https://x.com/shieldaitech), [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai), and [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI). ### Job Description: Shield AI develops intelligent autonomous systems that protect service members and civilians. The X-BAT Engineering team is building a next-generation autonomous aircraft for demanding and contested environments. We are seeking a new-graduate RF Hardware Test Engineer to help verify RF modules, assemblies, and interfaces used in airborne and ground systems. Working alongside experienced engineers, you will build practical expertise in RF measurements, instrument automation, data analysis, troubleshooting, and qualification support. This role is centered on disciplined test execution and objective evidence rather than top-level RF system architecture. This is an Engineer I (L1) position intended for candidates completing an undergraduate or graduate degree or beginning their professional career. Coursework, research, internships, student teams, and personal projects are all relevant ways to demonstrate readiness. ### What you'll do: - Execute documented RF test plans and procedures with mentorship, record test configurations, and produce clear, traceable results. - Characterize RF modules and assemblies for S-parameters, gain and loss, output power, compression, harmonics and spurious emissions, isolation, rejection, noise figure, and receiver sensitivity as applicable. - Set up and operate vector network analyzers, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, power meters, oscilloscopes, noise-figure equipment, programmable power supplies, and related laboratory instruments. - Calibrate measurement setups and characterize cables, adapters, attenuators, fixtures, and other sources of measurement error. - Develop simple test fixtures, harnesses, interface adapters, and monitoring circuits; perform basic soldering and hardware rework when appropriate. - Automate instrument control, data collection, analysis, and plotting using Python, MATLAB, or comparable tools. - Compare measured performance with requirements, identify unexpected behavior, and summarize conclusions in engineering reports and reviews. - Troubleshoot test anomalies with senior engineers and learn to distinguish device behavior from setup, calibration, software, or environmental artifacts. - Support EMI/EMC pre-compliance and MIL-STD-461 qualification testing, environmental testing, hardware integration, and ground or flight test activities as needed. - Maintain safe, organized laboratory practices and follow equipment calibration, configuration-control, and data-management processes. - Collaborate with RF, electrical, mechanical, systems, software, manufacturing, and supplier teams. - Perform other duties as assigned. ### Required qualifications: - Bachelor's or master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, or a related technical field, completed or expected within 12 months of the anticipated start date. - Coursework, research, project, or internship experience in RF or microwave engineering, communications, electromagnetics, analog circuits, or electronic hardware testing. - Fundamental understanding of S-parameters, impedance, transmission lines, gain and loss, noise, power, spectral content, and frequency response. - Hands-on laboratory experience gained through coursework, research, an internship, a student organization, or a personal project. - Basic programming and data-analysis skills in Python, MATLAB, or a similar environment. - Ability to follow test procedures, document setups and results accurately, recognize uncertainty, and ask for guidance when needed. - Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work constructively in a multidisciplinary team. - Ability to work on-site in a laboratory and hardware-development environment. ### Preferred qualifications: - Experience using a vector network analyzer, spectrum analyzer, signal generator, power meter, oscilloscope, noise-figure analyzer, or programmable test equipment. - Experience automating laboratory instruments or analyzing measurement data using Python, MATLAB, SCPI, or a comparable approach. - Familiarity with RF simulation or design tools such as ADS, AWR, HFSS, or CST. - Experience with PCB bring-up, soldering, RF connectors and cables, test fixtures, harnesses, or basic hardware rework. - Exposure to EMI/EMC testing or MIL-STD-461 through coursework, research, an internship, or laboratory work. - Exposure to environmental, qualification, reliability, or acceptance testing of electronic hardware. - Experience on a university design team, research laboratory, internship, co-op, or project involving aerospace, defense, robotics, communications, or other high-reliability hardware. - Ability to obtain an S//SAR level security clearance, if required by the program.

Gelber Group -- Passion for Trading. Powered by Technology. Headquartered in Chicago with offices across the United States and Europe, Gelber has set the bar as one of the industry’s innovative and enduring proprietary trading firms for more than 40 years. Our collaborative and entrepreneurial culture empowers each member of our team to have a meaningful impact from the start. We pride ourselves on a flat organizational structure and focus on meritocracy. If you flourish in a fast-paced environment, have a strong work ethic, and a competitive attitude, Gelber is right for you. As a Discretionary Trading Intern at Gelber Group, you will begin your 10-week internship with an education portion covering basics of liquid capital markets, the various ways in which Gelber engages these markets, and the tools and technology that link us to the markets. Once you have a grasp of these concepts, you will be assigned directly to a discretionary trading desk. This internship will begin in June 2027 and last until the first week of August 2027. We are considering recent graduates or candidates that are graduating in 2027 or 2028. *The approximate hourly rate for this position **in Chicago, IL** is $35/hr. This is a temporary role and is not eligible for employee benefits.* **Position Overview** We are seeking highly motivated individuals to participate in a summer program in which they will learn and practice the development and execution of a rates-first macro trading process. Our primary goal in the internship is to evaluate candidates for full-time employment. As a result, our interests are best served by teaching you the necessary skills to demonstrate your talent and potential. **What You’ll Do** - Experience hands-on learning and sit on a trading desk with full-time traders - Gain a thorough understanding of the financial markets through a robust program that will be intensive, challenging, and fun - The classroom portion will be tailored to the topic areas that are useful for beginning to build a discretionary macro process - Topics may include a basic understanding of each asset class, macroeconomic fundamentals, technical analysis, and risk management - Develop a deep understanding of how macro traders engage with the market - Pitch weekly trade ideas and receive in-depth feedback on quality and execution - Potential for ideas to be turned into live risk taking - Experience a multi-week simulated trading experience - Send out daily and weekly reflections as you begin to build your own trading process - Build the foundation of a macro trading process **Goals** - Gain hands on experience interacting with the market from a macro perspective - Determine if this is the career you want to pursue **Qualifications** - Rising junior or senior in an undergraduate program, or recent graduate - Interest in financial markets is a must, but prior experience or knowledge is not required - Demonstrated interest in economics or a related field, via classwork or extracurricular activities - Curiosity, self-motivation, strong communication skills, and the ability to collaborate with others in a competitive environment - Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to learn, understand, and apply new concepts - Superior analytical skills with a proven strong mathematical aptitude **Why Intern at Gelber?** - Brand new office in the heart of Chicago’s River North neighborhood, attached to the Merchandise Mart and “El” stop, and a short walk from both Ogilvie and Union Train Stations - Comprehensive 10-week program, running from June to August 2027 - Catered lunch provided Tuesday, Wednesday, & Thursdays and stocked pantry daily - Social events and work/life balance that will allow you time to enjoy the Chicago summer - Office amenities including a golf simulator, pool table, and company paid on-site gym - Casual, relaxed dress code - Comprehensive benefits package available for full-time employees *If you are based in California, we encourage you to read the Gelber Privacy Notice for California Employees and Applicants, linked [here](https://www.gelbergroup.com/gelber-privacy-notice-california-residents/).*

**About Juno** Juno leverages collective bargaining power to secure better student loan rates for graduate students. With 290,000+ members and over $2B in negotiated loan volume, we have proven that group buying works. We are the most popular way to pay for the world's top graduate programs, and we are now building the student engagement layer that will carry that across every healthcare vertical. **The Problem** Federal lending reforms have created a significant market shift. In July 2026, new caps on federal graduate loans, including the elimination of Grad PLUS for new students, came into effect, leaving millions of students with significant funding gaps. Students need transparent, competitive private options, which is exactly what Juno provides. Most of them do not know we exist yet. Our dental vertical proved what changes that: students who hear about Juno from a classmate, in their own building, months before they need to borrow. That vertical produced our highest conversion rates in the company on the back of a peer ambassador network and over 700 direct student conversations in a single cycle. We are now running that model across medicine, PA, nursing, optometry and veterinary, and we need people in the field to do it. **Your mission** Be the person students in your area actually know. You will build relationships with student organizations and chapter leadership across healthcare degrees, get Juno into the buildings, and have the conversations that turn a name in our system into a student who trusts us with the biggest financial decision of their life so far. This is not a desk job and it is not a sales job. It is a relationship job with a travel schedule. **What you'll do** - **Build school level relationships.** Chapter presidents, student government leaders and class representatives at schools across your territory. Cold outreach, follow up, and staying in touch when there is nothing to sell. - **Get into the buildings.** Book and run vendor fairs and lunch and learns on campus, including rooms, catering and materials. Run virtual sessions with schools that are too far to reach in person. - **Work the conferences.** District, regional and national student organization meetings across the US. Not just staffing a table. Talking to students, working leadership networking rooms, and coming home with ambassador candidates. - **Support and recruit ambassadors.** Be the Juno person who knows the schools in your region. Interview, onboard and back up the student ambassadors in your territory. - **Talk to students, constantly.** One to one meetings, mostly video, at real volume during peak season. You will know the top five reasons a healthcare student with a rate offer never submits an application because you heard them first-hand, not because a dashboard told you. - **Follow up faster than anyone expects.** The window between a student meeting and a decision is short and most of our competitors are slow. - **Be the expert students trust.** Become fluent in how graduate borrowing actually works: federal versus private, what drives a rate, cosigners, in-school deferral, refinancing, and what changed under the new caps. Be the person who can give a first year a straight answer. - **Bring the field back in.** School tuition deadlines, competitor activity, what students are actually asking. You are our eyes in schools we otherwise only see in a spreadsheet. **The shape of the year** Our year has a peak and this role moves with it. September to February is outreach-led. Chapter relationships, campus event booking, conference season, ambassador recruiting and onboarding. This is where next year's meetings get created. March to August is meeting-led. Students start shopping in spring and tuition deadlines run June through October. Your week becomes student conversations and follow up. Travel is roughly fifteen percent of the year and it clusters. Expect heavy stretches in the fall and in early winter. **What We Offer** **Compensation:** $70k–$100k including performance upside tied to growth milestones. **Benefits:** Comprehensive health, dental, vision, and retirement matching. **What We're Looking For** - **Background:** 2 to 5 years in a relationship-driven role, or an outlier track record. Campus programs, student organizations, field marketing, community building, admissions, events, or a zero to one motion you ran yourself. We care more about what you have built with people than what industry you built it in. Bonus, if you have experience with graduate programs. - **You are good with students.** You can walk into a room of twenty-four year olds and have a real conversation about money without it becoming a pitch. This is the single most important qualification and it will be screened for directly. - **You can do volume outreach and not get discouraged.** Half this job is emailing chapter presidents who have not heard of you and following up until someone answers. - **Relationship-building that compounds.** Student organizations, chapter leadership, ambassadors, program directors. Equally comfortable at a leadership networking reception and in a group chat with first years. - **You will get on a plane.** Regularly, in your region, including weekends when conferences fall on them. - **Comfort with seasonality.** Our year has a peak. **Job Description: Junior Generalist Engineer** **About Us** Implicit Conversions specializes in the high-level emulation of classic and retro games, enabling gamers to experience their favorite classics on modern consoles. With a dedication to preserving gaming history, we combine cutting-edge technology and a passion for gaming to revive cherished games from publisher’s back catalogs. Our portfolio includes games from the Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection, Rayman 30th Anniversary Edition, Fear Effect 1 and 2, Fighting Force Collection, Milano’s Oddjob Collection, Geppy-X and over a hundred more! **Summary** We’re looking for a creative and skilled Junior Generalist Engineer to join our team and help bring classic games to life on modern hardware. In this role, you’ll design, build, and refine emulators that make older titles run smoothly and accurately on today’s platforms. You will also write tools to help support the team workflows. You will also reverse engineer classic games (often with bespoke custom engines) to implement modern quality-of-life enhancements. You’ll collaborate closely with engineers, producers, and QA to fine-tune performance, ensure compatibility, and deliver a great player experience. Your work will play a key role in preserving and reintroducing classic games for a whole new generation of players. **Responsibilities** - Assist in developing, maintaining, and expanding upon our existing emulators and tools. - Assist in maintaining our CI/CD pipeline, installing new tools, updating machines, and writing and monitoring scripts. - Optimize games to ensure they are performant on target platforms. - Debug compatibility issues across a variety of platforms. - Reverse engineer games to patch out bugs, replace media, add achievements/trophies, and add a variety of modern enhancements. **Requirements** - 1–3 years of generalist engineering experience, with a strong interest or background in video game development. - Strong scripting language skills (Python, Lua, etc.). - Excellent C/C++ skills and understanding of algorithms. - Clear communicator who works well in a remote team and takes initiative when solving problems. - Genuine passion for retro games and emulation. **Bonus Points** - Experience building and optimizing software across multiple platforms. - Experience with game emulation or cross-platform ports (commercial or open source like libretro), including creating modifications/patches for classic games. - Familiarity with assembly languages (such as x86, ARM, or MIPS), SIMD intrinsics, and binary analysis. - Hands-on experience with reverse engineering and debugging tools such as Ghidra. - Experience with static recompilation techniques. **Target Salary:** $65k - $85k

### About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. The Avionics team builds and supports the electronics that help Zipline’s aircraft sense, compute, communicate, and fly reliably. Field Systems Engineering connects that design work with what happens across the operating fleet. We investigate failures, use flight data and hands-on testing to understand their causes, and work with engineers and operators to improve the product. Our work spans hardware, software, and day-to-day operations, so we learn directly from the people maintaining and flying the aircraft. **The Role** As a Field Systems Engineering intern, you’ll help solve real problems affecting Zipline’s aircraft in the field. You’ll work with flight data, test hardware, and collaborate with engineers and operations teams to understand how avionics systems perform outside the lab. You’ll have a mentor and a project you can own, with opportunities to present your findings and see how they inform engineering decisions. **What You'll Do** - Investigate avionics issues using telemetry, logs, physical inspection, and bench tests. - Analyze fleet data to identify patterns in system performance and reliability. - Build or improve scripts, dashboards, or diagnostic tools that make issues easier to detect and understand. - Help design and run tests to check possible failure causes and proposed fixes. - Work with design engineers, technicians, and operators to learn how systems behave in practice. - Document your methods, results, and recommendations so others can act on them. **What You'll Bring** - Currently pursuing a degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, aerospace engineering, robotics, computer science, or a related field. - Experience with hands-on technical projects involving hardware, software, or both. - Ability to analyze data or logs using Python, SQL, MATLAB, or a similar tool. - Curiosity about how complex systems fail and a methodical approach to finding answers. - Clear communication and willingness to learn from engineers, technicians, and operators. - Must be proficient and comfortable with using and building AI tools Nice to Have - Experience using CAD software to design, modify, or inspect mechanical parts and assemblies. - Hands-on experience building, testing, and debugging a physical system, such as through Formula SAE, Baja SAE, a robotics team, research, or a personal project. #### **What Else You Should Know** *This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January to April.* Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. *Candidates are limited to **three (3) applications within a 30-day period.*** Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Developing and honing technical skills in design, analysis, and testing. Learning professional communication and documentation best practices. description: Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. Form Carpenter Narrative Language: Formwork carpenters build the molds that retain wet concrete in the construction of foundations and other concrete structures. This position will manufacture forms made from steel, wood or heavy plastic. The work is physically demanding and messy, consisting of carrying the heavy forms, spraying them with oil that keeps the concrete from sticking, securing them with iron rods and inserting steel reinforcement that will give the concrete tensile strength. Once the concrete sets, form workers strip the forms, clean them and prep them for the next project. If this sounds like you, please apply! Formwork carpenters should be in top physical condition and be able to read blueprints. They must be proficient in measuring and cutting, because the premade form sizes don’t always match the exact structure dimensions, and the form worker must construct fillers to bridge the gaps. Basic knowledge of carpenter tools and the ability to figure angles, level and square the forms is essential. Form workers should have a working knowledge of the various methods used to assemble all major types of forms. And because a high percentage of commercial construction involves multilevel structures, form workers should also be comfortable working at heights. Job Description: Construct, erect, install, concrete forms; building frameworks; wood stairways, window and door frames. May also include installing cabinets, drywall and batt or roll insulation, doors and hardware, toilet partitions and accessories, trim, as well as other types of general trades tasks. Job Tasks: Measure and mark lines on materials, using ruler, pencil, chalk, and marking gauge. Verify trueness of structure, using plumb bob and level. Possess the skill required to construct and install block outs per drawings Able to install embedded angles, plates, bolts and other anchors to formwork prior to placing concrete Able as needed to position and tie reinforcing steel in footings, wall forms and flat slab placements Ability to install keyway, water stops and waterproofing materials in footings and formwork Shape or cut materials to specified measurements, using hand tools, machines, or power saw. Understand blueprints, sketches or building plans to determine dimensions and materials required for form, or framing, construction Assemble and fasten materials to make framework or props, using hand tools and wood screws, nails, dowel pins, or glue. Build or repair doors, frameworks, floors, and other wooden fixtures used in buildings, using woodworking machines, carpenter's hand tools, and power tools. Erect scaffolding and ladders for assembling structures above ground level. Select and order lumber and other required materials. Construct forms and chutes for pouring concrete. Follow established safety rules and regulations and maintain a safe and clean environment Required Knowledge: Knowledge of materials, methods, and the tools involved in the construction or repair of buildings or other structures, foundations and framing. Knowledge of arithmetic, basic geometry, and their applications to carpentry. Knowledge of raw materials, production processes, quality control, costs, and other techniques for maximizing the effective installations of concrete formwork, shoring, anchor bolts, embedded items, water stops and keyways. Knowledge of machines and tools, including uses, repair, and maintenance associated with carpentry and woodworking. Knowledge of basic building layout and leveling, grades and benchmarks. Basic knowledge of building codes. Skills Required: Using mathematics to solve problems. Ability to accurately measure lengths with ruler or tape. Basic blueprint reading Safe use of power tools such as saws, drills, planes, sanders, routers and grinders. Basic understanding and use of a builders level for setting grades. Abilities Required: The ability to apply general rules to specific problems to produce answers that make sense. The ability to listen to and understand information and ideas presented through spoken words and sentences. The ability to walk, bend, stoop, climb ladders and stairs, lift and carry materials in association with carpentry activities Job Activities: Ability to work skillfully with both hands constantly, independently safely lift and carry objects weighing up to 20 pounds routinely, 50 pounds occasionally, climb and maintain balance on ladders and scaffold, kneel, crouch, crawl, reach, push, pull, twist, finger, grasp and feel on a constant and repetitive basis, stand, walk, talk, see (20/20 vision naturally or corrected), hear within normal range and perform repetitive motion activities. Ability to work in extreme environmental conditions including excessive heat and cold, noise, vibrations, dust, fumes, oils, wear a portable respirator. Ability to work the schedule required by job demands. Ability to physically negotiate the hazards of a new construction worksite, e.g., uneven surfaces, floor openings, heights, construction debris and poor lighting.

description: **Join our dynamic Logistics Packaging Design / Engineering (LOD) team at our state-of-the-art Charleston, SC production facility and make a real-world impact. ** This role is designed for an individual eager to apply their academic knowledge to real-world production challenges, directly impacting the efficiency, quality, and sustainability of our inbound and outbound packaged products. Hands-on experience awaits you in: Production Line Optimization & Support: Actively participate in troubleshooting packaging-related issues during production Support packaging line trials for new materials, designs, or equipment, collecting data and providing feedback Material Evaluation & Application: Assist in the practical evaluation of new packaging materials and components for their suitability and performance on existing manufacturing equipment Work with suppliers and internal teams to assess material specifications against production requirements and operational capabilities Contribute to the selection of packaging materials that balance performance, cost, and environmental impact within a high-volume manufacturing setting Process Improvement & Waste Reduction: Identify and propose practical solutions to reduce packaging material waste, scrap, and rework on the production floor Participate in lean manufacturing initiatives focused on improving packaging processes Technical Documentation & Standards: Assist in developing, reviewing, and updating packaging specifications Maintain accurate records of packaging tests, line trials, and material performance data Cross-Functional Collaboration: Collaborate closely with production operators, maintenance technicians, quality control, supply chain, and R&D teams to implement packaging solutions. Actively participate in daily production meetings, sharing observations and contributing to problem-solving discussions. What we offer: World-Class Experience: Gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced, high-tech manufacturing environment. Mentorship & Growth: Benefit from direct mentorship and guidance from experienced Logistics Engineers. Meaningful Contributions: Make a tangible impact by contributing to projects with real-world applications. Exposure to Innovation: Be at the forefront of cutting-edge technology and industry best practices. The Coordinator, Advocacy and Student Programs is responsible for mobilizing young people and communities to support full access to sexual and reproductive health care services and sexual health information and protect individual reproductive freedom. Identifies key constituencies and develops and conducts mobilizing strategies. Manages student advocacy programs for high schools and colleges/universities in our region and advances the mission of PPHP through community collaboration, volunteer engagement, and outreach. Essential Functions: Public Affairs • Manages and supervises Planned Parenthood Generation Action programs and serves as PPHP’s liaison with PPFA regarding youth and young people advocacy efforts. Supports outreach events on college campuses to educate and activate college students to advocate on behalf of PPHP and sexual and reproductive health issues. • Manage High School Advocacy Program and other advocacy efforts with students at all levels. • Manage student volunteer activities including, but not limited to, canvassing and phone banks in the region. • Organizes PPHP’s annual Youth Lobby event. • Participates in community outreach and engagement events throughout our region to build our activist base. • Manage short-term advocacy and organizing projects such as Day of Action, student engagement activities and actions, voter engagement, and legislative campaigns, in the region, as assigned. • Build and retains targeted collaborative partnerships with allied organizations and coalitions in the region, consistent with affiliate educational, medical, advocacy, lobbying, and legislative goals. Represents PPHP at a broad range of meetings, coalitions, and task forces outside the affiliate, in the assigned region; leverages relationships with leaders of coalition partners and community agencies to build network of youth activists for reproductive and sexual health, rights and justice (grasstops and grassroots). • Assist in the development of the annual Advocacy & Government Relations work plan. • As needed, serve as Advocacy & Government Relations liaison to other departments, including the health centers. • Collaborate with Communications, Development, Education and Training, and other departments to organize special events to connect PPHP with our supporters and activists. • Develops and conducts presentations about legislation, policy, and advocacy for coalition partners, campus groups, and other organizations, speaks on sexual and reproductive health and rights issues to a wide variety of audiences, including youth groups, and potential and existing coalition partners – with a specific prioritization of youth-focused partners. • Supports the efforts of Planned Parenthood Hudson Peconic Action Fund as needed.

At Syngenta, our goal is to build the most collaborative and trustworthy team in agriculture, providing top-quality seeds and innovative crop protection solutions that improve farmers' success. We invite you to help shape the future of agriculture and play a role in safely feeding the world while caring for our planet. Syngenta's Sales team is seeking an R&D Intern in Woodland, CA. This hands-on role will contribute to greenhouse and field research, breeding trials, phenotyping, data management, seed handling, and seasonal operations. The intern will work directly with breeders and research staff while gaining practical exposure to vegetable breeding, seed production, and the operations of a seed company. As part of Syngenta's Emerging Talent Program, you will gain hands-on experience, exposure to day-to-day business operations, and opportunities to apply your academic knowledge to real-world challenges while developing your professional skills. Duration: June 2027 – September 2027, with the potential for an extension through October 2027 to support cucurbit breeding, harvest, and post-harvest activities. Site: Will be working on-site at the Hollar Seeds facility. Accountabilities Assist with planning and executing greenhouse and field breeding trials, including planting, transplanting, irrigation, crop maintenance, and harvesting. Conduct phenotypic evaluations of cucurbit plants and fruit according to established breeding protocols. Support controlled pollinations and crossing activities under breeder direction. Collect, record, verify, and organize research observations and plant-performance data accurately and on schedule. Enter, manage, and validate data using spreadsheets, databases, and breeding data-management systems. Harvest, label, catalogue, and maintain seed stocks, germplasm inventories, and other breeding materials. Support field-day preparation and other program activities as required. Collaborate with breeding, seed production, sales, packing, and office teams to support timely, aligned execution of breeding activities. Maintain accurate records and follow applicable research, safety, and quality standards. Build an understanding of market needs and breeding goals to support product-development awareness. Required Current undergraduate or graduate student in Plant Breeding, Plant Science, Agronomy, Horticulture, Genetics, Biology, Agricultural Sciences, or a related field. Must be continuing education after the internship and not graduate before December 2027. Ability and willingness to relocate to Woodland, California, at personal expense for the duration of the internship. Ability to work in field and greenhouse environments and to perform physical agricultural tasks. Strong attention to detail, organization, written and verbal communication skills, and commitment to accurate record keeping. Ability to work independently on assigned tasks and collaboratively within a team. Desired Strong interest in plant breeding, crop improvement, vegetable seeds, or agricultural research. Basic proficiency with Microsoft Excel and data-management practices. Prior experience in agriculture, horticulture, field trials, greenhouse crop production, phenotyping, or seed handling. Salary for this position ranges between $20 - $45 hourly. What We Offer: A culture that celebrates belonging and collaboration, promotes professional development and strives for a work-life balance that supports the team members. ⁠Competitive wages. Ongoing career development resources. The opportunity to work on meaningful, innovative projects that solve problems. Syngenta is committed to creating a culture that celebrates belonging and collaboration, promotes professional development, and strives for a work-life balance that supports the team members Syngenta has been ranked as a top employer by Science Journal. Learn more about our team and our mission here: Syngenta is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate in recruitment, hiring, training, promotion or any other employment practices for reasons of race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, marital or veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. #LI-DNI About Syngenta At Syngenta Seeds Field Crops, we're shaping the future of agriculture and empowering farmers to meet the ever-growing demand for food and fuel. We’re a global Ag Tech powerhouse, headquartered in the United States, with passionate, local experts collaborating with farmers to deliver solutions that create market opportunities. We unite precision breeding, advanced biotechnology trait choice, and digital platforms for unmatched in-field performance. Our seeds help mitigate risks such as disease, insect, weed, and extreme weather pressures, all while promoting sustainable farming practices that protect and enhance our planet. Join our mission of revolutionizing food security and transforming agriculture.

Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly-sophisticated customers across the globe – large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military. With five satellites on orbit and many more set to launch soon, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization. Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Blackrock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA. #### Thermal Intern (Winter 2027) Internships at Astranis typically last for twelve weeks, and are hourly roles designed for students who are currently enrolled at a four-year university. As an Intern, you will have an amazing opportunity to work on hard problems — we pride ourselves on giving everyone at Astranis a chance to do meaningful work on complex projects, no matter their seniority. Many past interns have designed and tested hardware/software that is heading to space on our first satellite, and many of them are now full-time employees at Astranis. If you have already graduated from a four-year university, please apply to be an Associate Engineer. #### Role - Work together with the engineering team to design, evaluate, build, and test satellite hardware and/or software. - Support design trades that successfully balance performance margins, resource use, risk, cost, and schedule. - Perform thermal analysis to varying degrees of fidelity (simplified to detailed) on a variety of different types of hardware such as propulsion components, batteries, high powered electronics, RF components, mechanisms, and printed circuit boards (PCBs). - Design, evaluate, procure and test thermal solutions such as heaters, heat pipes, thermal interface materials, and surface coatings. - Develop processes and procedures for integration and assembly which ensure thermal design intent is met. Collaborate with the integration and test team in the installation of thermal hardware as needed. - Plan and run thermal vacuum testing and verification at the component and spacecraft level. #### Requirements - Currently pursuing a B.S. or M.S. in mechanical, aerospace, or equivalent technical degree (e.g. physics or applied math) - A passion and enthusiasm for hardware development, including working in a fast-paced environment and hands-on design and development - Demonstrated ability to personally design, build, and test hardware from scratch. - US Citizenship or Green Card - Don't meet them all? Not a problem. Please apply even if you do not meet all these criteria. #### Bonus - Experience with CAD - Experience with analytical software thermal analysis such as ANSYS and Thermal Desktop - Experience with electronics systems design and packaging - Experience (projects or previous internships) related to aerospace The base pay for this position is $29.00 per hour. Base Hourly Pay $29—$29 USD **U.S. Citizenship, Lawful Permanent Residency, or Refugee/Asylee Status Required** (To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States, or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)) Our mission and products are built for everyone, regardless of gender, race, creed, or background. We believe in a diverse and inclusive workplace, and we invite all people to join our team and bring their unique perspectives to make us stronger. #### **Astranis SMS Terms of Service** 1. **Recruiting Updates:** By opting in, you agree to receive SMS updates, interview coordination, and recruiting communications from Astranis Space Technologies Corp. 2. **Opt-Out:** You can cancel this service at any time by replying **STOP**. role: Applied AI Engineer Intern - Advancing Agent Quality
description: **Role Type:** External Research Affiliate / Think Tank Contributor **Location:** South Florida preferred **Affiliation:** Local university-based Masters or PhD researcher or postdoctoral AI researcher working under faculty direction **Organization:** [](http://Brightstar.AI) **Role Summary** [](http://Brightstar.AI) is seeking a full-time or recently graduated **Masters or PhD-level Applied AI Engineer Intern** – **Advancing Agent Quality** with a strong research mindset, affiliated with a leading (South Florida) university, to contribute to its AI Think Tank and to the hands-on build-out of Brightstar’s proprietary AI systems. The intern will pair academic rigor with applied engineering: building the evaluation environments, automated raters, and diagnostic tooling that establish — with evidence rather than impression — whether an agent is reliable enough to put in front of operators, executives, and investors. The first concrete assignment is the **AI Twin Board**, Brightstar’s proprietary board-simulation product, where the intern will help build the evaluation harness end to end: realistic task suites, calibrated LLM judge, failure-mode diagnostics, and the data flywheel that feeds improvements back into the agents themselves. The AI Twin Board is the starting point, not the full scope — as Brightstar’s AI portfolio expands, the same quality discipline will be applied to other agentic systems, internal platforms, and portfolio-company deployments. Working in coordination with university professors and research leaders, the intern will also bring up-to-date knowledge of the fast-evolving AI landscape — especially **large language models, reasoning systems, emerging model capabilities, and the societal implications of advanced AI** — and help translate what current and next-generation systems may enable over the next six months to three years into Brightstar’s evaluation standards and Think Tank point of view. **Key Responsibilities** · Design, build, and scale realistic agent environments and task suites that reflect how Brightstar’s agents are actually used — board-level deliberation, research synthesis, diligence workflows, and multi-step tool use. · Develop agentic LLM judge, calibrate them against human expert evaluation, and benchmark Brightstar agents against leading frontier models. · Build trajectory-analysis frameworks and diagnostic tooling that root-cause agent failure modes — passivity, hallucination, persona drift, brittle tool execution — and feed fixes back into agent prompts, harnesses, and architecture. · Enable agents to generate and iterate on their own verifiers (automated test cases, checklists, ground-truth sets) to support effective exploration and iterative problem-solving. · Harvest multi-turn interaction trajectories into high-quality datasets and reward signals that support fine-tuning and post-training of the models Brightstar relies on. · Contribute to the **AI Twin Board** build-out as the initial focus, and extend the same evaluation approach to other Brightstar AI initiatives as the roadmap grows. · Contribute frontier AI research perspectives to the [](http://Brightstar.AI) Think Tank as part of weekly review sessions and select strategic discussions. · Review relevant research papers, conference findings, and publications from leading AI institutions and labs as inputs to the Think Tank knowledge base and to Brightstar’s evaluation methodology. · Help interpret academic and technical developments for a business and investment audience, including implications for industry transformation and applied AI opportunities. **Minimum Qualifications** · Currently enrolled in a Masters or PhD program — or serving as a postdoctoral or early-career academic researcher — in **Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computer Science, Computational Linguistics, or a related field**. · 1 years of research, project, or professional experience with LLMs or Agents. · 2 year of experience with machine learning and deep learning. · Experience in software engineering and cloud-based development. · Experience with agent builders, e.g. OpenSDK, OpenAI Agent Builder, etc. · Able to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical executive audiences. **Preferred Qualifications** · In-depth knowledge of machine learning algorithms, including supervised learning and reinforcement learning. · Hands-on experience building LLM or agent evaluation systems — autoraters, human-evaluation pipelines, benchmark design, or evaluation infrastructure. · Experience with multi-agent orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation, and tool-use / function-calling reliability. · Active research or publications in **LLMs, reasoning systems, model behavior, AI safety, or the societal impact of advanced AI systems**. · Strong research discipline, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to separate meaningful signal from AI hype. · Affiliated with a (South Florida) university and working under the supervision of a faculty member or professor, or recent graduate. **Why This Role Matters** [](http://Brightstar.AI)’s Think Tank is intended to provide **systematic forward-looking intelligence** on where AI may create value, where it may disrupt industries, and how firms can better anticipate what may work tomorrow rather than only what worked yesterday. Masters and PhD-level Applied AI Engineers are a critical part of that model, bringing academic depth, frontier perspective, and analytical rigor into the Think Tank’s quarterly insights and longer-term point of view. Moreover, this role extends beyond research to focus on the practical application of AI in terms of AI Twin Board technology, which we see as a key differentiator in our research approach and value creation methodology.
