As an Entry-Level Transportation Engineer or Planner, you’ll build a strong professional foundation by applying standard techniques and procedures under the guidance of experienced staff while developing the skills, knowledge, and confidence to grow throughout your career. We look for genuine curiosity, an openness to new experiences and tools, and a collaborative approach to problem-solving – qualities that help you learn, contribute, and take on increasing responsibility over time. These opportunities for personal and professional growth are maximized through exposure to a wide variety of transportation planning, engineering, and design projects, which may include: **Transportation planning and analysis:** transportation impact studies, bicycle and pedestrian planning, access, circulation and parking studies, multimodal operations, VMT assessments, transportation demand management (TDM), climate action plans, and freight planning. **Traffic operations, forecasting, and safety:** traffic operations analysis, transit forecasting and operations, travel behavior forecasting, systemic safety studies, and highway interchange and corridor studies. **Transportation design:** complete streets, bikeways, signing and striping, traffic signals/ITS, street lighting, roundabouts, temporary traffic control, cost estimates, project specifications, and design drawings from concept through construction-ready documents. ### Responsibilities - Conduct transportation analysis and prepare reports, memos, and other technical deliverables - Participate in meetings, including preparing presentations and public outreach materials - Support project coordination and management activities - Engage with professional organizations and industry activities - Conduct site visits and collect field data - Explore opportunities to contribute to Fehr & Peers internal Research and Development program - Embrace opportunities to learn and adopt new tools, technologies, and ways of working that enhance day-to-day work, while maintaining professional judgment, critical thinking, and accountability for results ### What Your First Year May Look Like By the end of the first month: - Participate in on-the-job training and mentoring - Contribute to several different projects - Seek additional work from project managers By the end of six months: - Work on a variety of projects with staff throughout the office - Build proficiency with several technical software programs - Prepare deliverables, including memos, reports, and presentations - Take on increasing independence and responsibility for your work By the end of the first year: - Participate in multiple client meetings - Take on increased responsibility for coordinating and managing small projects or project tasks - Start to develop deeper experience in areas that align with project opportunities, your interests, and your growing skills ### Qualifications We’re looking for candidates who bring curiosity, initiative, and a collaborative approach to their work. You do not need experience in every topic area or software program listed below—we expect you to continue learning and developing on the job. Experience can come from internships, employment, coursework, research, student organizations, volunteer activities, or other relevant experiences. - A completed bachelor’s or in-progress master’s degree in transportation, civil or electrical engineering, urban and regional planning, or a related field such as geography, math, statistics, or economics. - Relevant coursework in transportation, engineering, urban and regional planning, geography, math, statistics, economics, or related subjects. An EIT is preferred for engineering candidates. - Experience or exposure in the following transportation topic areas: Field work, traffic operations analysis, signal design, transportation planning, bicycle and pedestrian planning, transit planning, infrastructure finance, transportation and land use policy, travel demand modeling, and related areas. - Experience or exposure to relevant technical software and tools: Microsoft Excel; GIS (ArcGIS, QGIS); CAD (AutoCAD, Microstation); traffic operations analysis tools (HCS, Synchro/SimTraffic, Vistro, VISSIM, Sidra); travel demand modeling tools (Cube/Voyager, TransCAD, VISUM, Emme); and programming languages such as Python or R. - Previous experience in a professional or team environment related to transportation or another relevant field is helpful but may come from a variety of settings and experiences. - An entrepreneurial spirit and proactive approach to communication and getting work done. - Genuine curiosity about transportation and familiarity with the challenges of day-to-day travel within your community. - Interpersonal skills, a desire to collaborate, and a creative approach to problem-solving. - Organizational skills and the ability to balance priorities between multiple tasks within a defined timeline. - Experience with technical writing and public speaking through school and/or work experience. - Openness to exploring and responsibly using new technologies and tools, while maintaining critical thinking and professional judgment.

A core tenant at IMS Nanofabrication is a "People First" point of view. We agonize over getting the right people on board, in the right seats, and fostering an environment where each person can find autonomy, mastery, and purpose in their work. This entry-level role is an exceptional launchpad for recent college graduates with engineering/science degrees, as well as military veterans such as from the Navy Nuclear Propulsion Program, who thrive in high-accountability, high-consequence technical environments. Our Field Service Engineer I role emphasizes customer satisfaction, technical troubleshooting skills, and collaborative teamwork in daily operations with other Field Service Engineers. A successful Field Service Engineer I at IMS Nanofabrication displays strong problem-solving and decision-making skills, alongside a deep understanding of the impact of quickly diagnosing and addressing problems in the customer environment. They have a strong desire to master both the technical attributes of our Multi-Beam Mask Writers - some of the most advanced semiconductor lithography equipment in the world - and the people skills required to excel in front of our critical customers. This role requires an in-person presence in our Hillsboro, OR office with a daily presence at our customer site(s), strongly aligning with our US headquarters in Santa Clara, CA and our global R&D and operations team in Austria. This non-exempt role reports directly to the team lead engineer in charge at IMS America. You're Excited About This Opportunity Because You Will: Grow with a Premier Team: Be part of a growing team of professional Field Service Engineers in Hillsboro, OR. Master Cutting-Edge Tech: Internally align on and perform the activities related to the installation, annual preventive maintenance, and issue resolution of a growing fleet of multi-beam mask writers. Drive Procedural Excellence: Ensure that IMS-defined methodologies and procedures are uniformly followed, and provide critical feedback to Headquarters regarding improvements, gaps, or necessary changes. Solve High-Stakes Puzzles: Take part in special task force teams that handle customer escalations and challenging incidents, maintaining professional and regular communication with customer and headquarters functions. Keep Leadership Aligned: Ensure seamless and transparent communication of all status updates to IMS US leadership. Manage Customer Relationships: Maintain and build excellent customer relationships with local Tool Owners and other critical customer stakeholders. Represent IMS in the Fab: Attend fab-related customer meetings to update the team's ongoing and planned issue resolution, installation, and Annual Preventive Maintenance activities. We're Excited About You Because: We are actively seeking candidates who fit one of these two foundational profiles: Profile 1: Recent College Graduate You hold a Bachelor’s of Science degree in an Engineering discipline (Electrical, Mechanical, Mechatronics, Chemical), Physics, or a related STEM field. You exhibit excellent problem-solving skills and are eager to bridge theoretical engineering concepts with hands-on machinery troubleshooting. Profile 2: Navy Nuclear Propulsion Alumnus (EMN, ETN, MMN) You have successfully completed the U.S. Navy Nuclear Power School and prototype training. You possess a deep-seated respect for procedural compliance, operational safety, and quality control (QA/QC), with a proven track record of diagnosing complex mechanical, electrical, or electronic systems under operational pressure. Core Requirements & Interpersonal Skills: Exceptional interpersonal skills, with a genuine enjoyment of being part of and integrating with a global, fast-paced team. Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfortable presenting technical updates in high-visibility customer environments. 1+ years of technical field service or hands-on operational system experience (Navy nuclear plant operation/maintenance directly satisfies this). We're Elated About You Because (Preferred but not Required): You have a prior metrology or semiconductor lithography equipment support background You have hands-on troubleshooting experience with ultra-high vacuum (UHV) systems or high-voltage electronics (highly prevalent in Navy nuclear platforms and advanced engineering labs). You have experience in Linux/UNIX server system administration. We Offer: We are a leading high-tech company with headquarters in Austria and international subsidiaries (Taiwan, Korea, USA). Excellent professional and personal development opportunities in an international company. Very collegial and motivated team with short communication channels. Top-equipped workplace (modern office, laptop, height-adjustable desk). We offer a competitive salary, a convenient Santa Clara location, and a benefits package that includes paid time off, medical, dental and vision plans, life, disability coverage, and a 401K plan + company match. Individual pay is determined by several factors, including experience, location, internal pay equity, and other relevant business considerations. We review all employee pay and compensation programs annually at a minimum to ensure competitive and fair pay. IMS Nanofabrication is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, gender identity, veteran status, and disability, or other legally protected status. IMS is an equal opportunity employer. No matter where you are from, how you live, what you believe in - we look forward to receiving your application! What counts for us is the person, not the label. That's why we welcome your unique perspective. At IMS Nanofabrication, we shape the future — one nanometer at a time. Headquartered in Austria, with subsidiaries in Vienna, Taiwan, South Korea, and the USA, we are a global leader in semiconductor technology . Our cutting-edge mask writers power the world's most advanced chip manufacturing , making high-performance smartphones, PCs, and data centers possible. By pushing the boundaries of nanofabrication, we enable innovation at the smallest scale — driving progress on a global level.

# **About Ramp** Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. Explore our [Engineering Blog](https://builders.ramp.com) & [Emerging Talent](https://builders.ramp.com/emerging-talent) [Blog](#) to learn more about how we build at Ramp and what it’s like to start your career here. # About the Role Ramp is, at its core, an engineering company, and is on a mission to build the best engineering team in the US! We are looking for iOS interns (12 or 16 weeks) who are excited to be part of our story and help us build a diverse and vibrant tech community. We hire engineers with a broad set of technical skills, who are highly cross-functional, and eager to solve a wide range of engineering challenges. Our ideal candidate has a strong sense of ownership and enjoys owning projects from inception to scaling them in production. We value people who take pride in their work, and show an aptitude for learning quickly whether they’re familiar with our stack or not. You'll be working with a nimble team of committed and talented engineers and having a large, long-term impact on technical design and engineering culture. ## **What You’ll Do** - Build and ship new features for Ramp’s iOS app - Work alongside experienced engineers and contribute to our mobile codebase - Collaborate with Product and Design to bring new features and experiences to life - Learn from customer feedback and help continuously improve our product - Contribute to engineering tools and processes that help the team move quickly and scale ## **What You’ll Need** - Currently pursuing a B.S. or higher in Computer Science or a related technical field, graduating December 2027 or later - Experience with Swift and/or iOS development through internships, coursework, or personal projects - Strong programming fundamentals and understanding of mobile development concepts - Experience building a mobile app, feature, or relevant project - Ability to turn product ideas into thoughtful engineering solutions - Desire to learn quickly, take ownership, and work in a fast-paced environment ## **Nice to Haves** - Experience with SwiftUI - Familiarity with mobile design patterns and best practices - Experience shipping an iOS app or feature to real users - Exposure to technologies in our mobile stack, including Swift Concurrency, The Composable Architecture, Bazel, OpenAPI, or Buildkite - Experience with web or backend development ## **Compensation** - The monthly rate for this internship is $12,500 USD + housing stipend ## **Ramp Benefits** - Apple MacBook - Catered Lunches in NYC office Monday-Friday ## **Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)** - Flexible PTO - Centralized home-office equipment ordering - Health and wellness stipend - Budget for intra-office travel - Weekly coffee stipend ## **United States** - 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents - One Medical annual membership - 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp - Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year) - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay - Pet insurance - In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more - Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed) ## **Canada** - Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life - Life, AD&D, and disability coverage - Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime) - Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP) - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay - Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health ## **United Kingdom** - Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite - Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi - Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay ## **Referral Instructions** If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf. ## **Other notices** Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. *Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @*[**](http://Ramp.com) *email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.* [Ramp Applicant Privacy Notice](https://ramp.com/legal/applicant-privacy-notice)

CPPI OVERVIEW Charles Perry Partners, Inc. (CPPI) is a leading general contracting, design-build, and construction management firm with regional offices in Gainesville, Jacksonville, Tampa, Orlando, Fort Myers, and Palm Beach. Since 1968, CPPI has built a strong reputation for delivering exceptional service and results across a broad spectrum of projects. Our mission is to build long-lasting relationships and structures. JOB SUMMARY Our Gainesville Preconstruction Department is seeking a Preconstruction professional to join the team! The Preconstruction Engineer supports the Preconstruction Department by assisting with estimating, bid preparation, constructability reviews, and project coordination for both hard bid and negotiated work. This position plays a key role in delivering accurate estimates, managing preconstruction schedules, and ensuring client satisfaction in alignment with the company’s mission, vision, and core values. COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS Competitive compensation aligned with experience and qualifications. Generous paid vacation and holidays. Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage. 401(k) retirement plan with company match. Short-term and long-term disability plans. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS Authorized to work in the United States without the need for current or future visa sponsorship. Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Civil Engineering, Architecture, or related field (or 5 years of equivalent experience). Minimum of 2 years of experience as a Preconstruction Engineer for a Senior Level Preconstruction Engineer. Experience using on-screen takeoff software or other graphic software. Proficient in reading and interpreting construction plans and specifications. Strong understanding of commercial construction systems and cost structures. Skilled in Microsoft Office Suite (especially Excel), estimating software, and plan management tools. Strong organizational, analytical, and time-management abilities. Excellent written and verbal communication skills; detail-oriented and proactive. LEED accreditation preferred. JOB RESPONSIBILITIES Review drawings, specifications, and contract documents to identify scope, risk, and constructability issues. Perform quantity takeoffs and develop cost estimates using estimating software. Solicit and evaluate subcontractor and supplier bids; prepare bid comparison matrices. Manage prequalification of subcontractors and maintain bid lists. Assist in preparing bid proposals, pricing forms, and final deliverables for both hard bid and CM/DB projects. Support development and maintenance of preconstruction and design schedules. Conduct constructability and value engineering reviews; prepare RFIs and reports as needed. Participate in client, design, and internal coordination meetings; maintain accurate meeting records. Prepare meeting agendas and coordinate bid scope workshop meetings. Collaborate with Operations to transition awarded projects, ensuring all documents and scopes are properly handed off. Maintain accurate estimating data and support ongoing database and pricing updates. Uphold safety, quality, and company standards on all assigned tasks. Other duties as assigned. EEO STATEMENT CPPI is an Equal Opportunity Employer; we encourage individuals of all backgrounds to apply.

description: The Bowery Mission is a Christian, faith-based organization committed since the 1870s to serving people experiencing homelessness, hunger, and poverty. The Bowery Mission meets essential needs and creates transformative community with men, women, children, and families in New York so that we can together overcome homelessness and poverty and flourish. Our Bowery Campus has served as a beacon of compassionate care and life transformation in New York City. The Opportunity The Bowery Mission is seeking an experienced, mission-driven Campus Director to lead our Bowery Campus and help create a safe, welcoming, Christ-centered community where individuals can grow in relationship with God and others. As a key member of Program leadership, the Campus Director provides strategic and day-to-day leadership for campus operations, staff, safety, hospitality, and program services. This leader works across departments to ensure cohesive services, strong teamwork, excellent care, and effective stewardship of people and resources. The Campus Director will lead and develop staff, strengthen campus culture, oversee program operations and outcomes, manage community partnerships and assigned resources, and help ensure the Bowery Campus consistently reflects The Bowery Mission’s values and Principles of Care. What You Will Do Lead and develop the campus team. Create and sustain a unified, collaborative ministry culture rooted in The Bowery Mission’s values. Lead campus communication and meetings, coach and develop team members, strengthen supervision and training, support hiring and talent development, and ensure effective staffing and coverage. Oversee safe and effective campus operations. Partner with Facilities, Volunteer Services, Logistics, program teams, and other departments to maintain a safe, caring, trauma-informed environment. Oversee campus safety practices, security and fire-safety procedures, emergency response, building needs, space utilization, and Gift-in-Kind operations. Create an exceptional culture of hospitality. Ensure guests, clients, alumni, volunteers, donors, community partners, vendors, and other visitors are warmly welcomed and appropriately oriented to the campus. Continually improve customer service and help create welcoming, organized, trauma-informed spaces. Lead campus tours and help host major events, including Thanksgiving and other partner, volunteer, and organizational gatherings. Lead program management and outcomes. In partnership with senior program leadership, oversee services for guests, clients, and alumni, including chapel, community meals, clothing and shower services, social work support, residential programming, and Alumni Transitional Housing. Ensure programs reflect best practices, Christian principles, and a seamless continuum of care. Build strong community partnerships. role: ASIC Engineer I, Annapurna Labs, Early Career - 2027
description: At Amazon, our tech isn't just a tool, it's your playground. Our engineers work on scalable systems, cloud services, and customer-facing products that operate at global scale. This is an environment where you learn by building. Whether you're creating cloud-native solutions, optimizing machine learning models, or building products that drive experiences for millions of customers around the globe, your work reaches the world, fast. You'll take ownership early, collaborate across teams and disciplines, and grow your skills as you tackle new problems. There's no single path forward here, with a chance to explore different directions and shape your journey as you go. This is where ambition meets opportunity and, where the impact of what you build helps define what comes next, for customers and for you. What's in it for you? An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You'll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus. About the team Annapurna Labs designs the custom silicon at Amazon - including Graviton (our server processors), Trainium and Inferentia (our machine learning training and inference accelerators), and the Nitro system that powers modern EC2. We own the full stack, from silicon through the software that makes it work (compilers, runtimes, drivers, and the frameworks that let customers run workloads on our hardware). As an ASIC Engineer I, you'll write the programs that turns custom silicon into products used by millions. Annapurna has ASIC teams across a range of products and disciplines, and we work to place you on a technical team aligned with your interests and strengths. Example teams and focus areas include: - RTL design for machine learning accelerators (Trainium/Inferentia) - Design verification and functional validation - Physical design, timing closure, and place-and-route - SoC integration and chip architecture Throughout the interview process, we will partner with you and our hiring managers to match you to a team where your background and interests fit best, so your responsibilities are something you're genuinely excited to work on. As an ASIC Engineer I, you'll contribute to real chip development work, which may include: - Designing and implementing RTL for digital logic blocks using Verilog/SystemVerilog - Developing and running verification environments to validate design functionality and coverage - Supporting synthesis, timing analysis, and physical design flows - Debugging design issues through simulation and analysis - Collaborating with architecture, verification, and physical design teams to take features from specification to silicon - Documenting your design decisions and presenting your work to the team

role: Startup Solutions Architect, Early Stage Startups
description: Come work with the founders building what's next. Some of the most important companies of the next decade are being built right now, in San Francisco, by two or three people and an idea. We're looking for someone who wants a front-row seat to all of them, and the technical chops to help make them real. You'll work across AI/ML, FinTech, ClimateTech, healthcare, consumer, B2B SaaS, and whatever gets invented next, with many of these companies coming straight out of Y Combinator and other top accelerators or freshly backed by leading VC firms. They need a trusted technical voice in their corner from day one, and you get to be it. Picture a small team with a technical founder and maybe a couple of engineers, moving fast with Claude Code, Codex, and whatever tool shipped last week, trying to make every product, architecture, and business decision at once. There's no VP of Engineering to align with, no platform team to hand things off to, and no multi-quarter roadmap, so for the startups you work with you become the closest thing they have to a fractional CTO or chief architect. That's what makes this an adventure rather than a support role: you and the founders are figuring it out together, and a single good decision can save six months of runway while a bad one can quietly sink the whole thing. The work is bigger than architecture, and it changes week to week. One week you're helping a team understand the architecture their coding agent quietly built for them and untangling the decisions they didn't realize they'd made, the next you're figuring out how to scale after an unexpected viral launch, and the week after that you're working a compliance problem with a FinTech startup that has to move fast but can't cut corners, or talking a founder through a hard pivot and helping them separate what they've already built from where the data says they should actually go. You'll prototype alongside them, experiment with frontier AI, and carry what you learn from hundreds of founders back into AWS so the products we build reflect what the leading edge actually needs. We hire for a specific kind of person, and it starts with founder empathy over enterprise process. You get that every dollar spent on infra is a dollar not spent on talent or growth, that their timeline is measured in months of runway, and that they're emotionally all-in on this idea, so you earn trust by genuinely caring whether the team survives rather than by showing off enterprise-grade architecture. That empathy shows up as survival-first thinking: before you recommend anything, you understand their runway, their burn, their signals of product-market fit, and their next milestone, whether that's demo day, a fundraise, or a first paying customer. To advise this well you have to see the full stack of the business, letting technical choices, product, business model, runway, and the founder's own risk tolerance all inform your recommendations, because you can't advise on architecture without understanding burn rate. You stay a builder at heart, since you don't stop being an engineer when you join this team; you prototype, write code, and get your hands dirty with new models, Bedrock, agents, and RAG because that's how you stay credible with people who build for a living. And you act as a scout for the future, spotting when a single startup's tool choice becomes a cohort-wide trend twelve to twenty-four months before the rest of the market, then carrying that signal back to AWS product and service teams. You don't have to already be a Solutions Architect to do this. Great people on this team have come from founding-engineer roles, senior software engineering, AI engineering, and traditional SA backgrounds, and if you're an excellent builder who loves customers, we can teach you the AWS you need. Key job responsibilities - Act as a trusted technical advisor to a portfolio of early-stage founders, designing architectures that are right-sized for where they are today and built to grow if and when they scale - Get hands-on: prototype, build reference patterns, and demo working solutions alongside founders rather than handing them a generic playbook - Help founders understand and improve the architectures their coding agents generated, making sense of the decisions and tradeoffs baked into what they've already shipped - Help startups navigate the fast-moving GenAI landscape, from selecting the right foundation models and AI services to shipping production-ready AI-powered products - Guide founders through the real challenges of building GenAI applications, including model cost, latency, accuracy, safety, and AI best practices - Help founders make pragmatic build-and-scale decisions, including when to keep architectures disposable and adaptable while the direction is still being validated - Stay technically sharp by experimenting with new models, agent frameworks, and emerging tools, so you can advise credibly across the entire stack - Build and deepen relationships across San Francisco's startup ecosystem, including top accelerators like Y Combinator, incubators, and leading VC firms - Be a voice for your founders, connecting their feedback and needs directly to AWS product and engineering teams to shape the tools being built for them - Scout emerging technology trends across the startups you work with and translate those signals back into AWS product roadmaps - Share your expertise at startup events, demo days, and developer meetups across the San Francisco ecosystem to build trust and visibility in the community

role: Manufacturing Engineer, CNC Machining (New Grad Summer 2027)
description: ## MANUFACTURING ENGINEER, CNC MACHINING (NEW GRAD SUMMER 2027) Freeform builds AI-native manufacturing systems that unify software, hardware, and physics to produce industrial-scale parts at the speed of human ideation. By treating manufacturing as a single integrated system, we unlock a new era of innovation where complex hardware is designed, built, and scaled without limits. As a Manufacturing Engineer (CNC Machining), you will play a critical role in achieving Freeform’s goal of becoming the world leader in the manufacturing of high-value metal 3D printed parts. You will be responsible for developing, implementing, and optimizing CNC programs for precision machining operations as well as working closely with our engineers and machinist to establish machining standards for Freeform’s high-volume, vertically integrated machining workflow. You’ll use top of the line multi-axis machines—including DMG Mori and Haas—to develop complex geometries and refine machining processes for maximum efficiency, quality, and repeatability. The ideal candidate is highly technical, hands-on, and thrives in a fast-paced development environment. If you want to be at the forefront of the next era of manufacturing technology, we’d love to hear from you! 3D printing experience is not required to be successful here—we look for smart, motivated, and collaborative individuals who love tackling complex challenges and building world-class technology! **Responsibilities:** - Develop, implement, and optimize CNC programs for complex metal components, including post-processing of 3D printed parts - Program, set up, and refine operations on multi-axis CNC machines (DMG Mori and Haas) - Interpret CAD models, technical drawings, and GD&T specifications to create highly precise machining programs - Select and optimize cutting tools, speeds, feeds, and machining strategies for efficiency and repeatability - Troubleshoot and resolve CNC programming issues, collaborating with machinists and design engineers - Create, maintain, and update CNC program libraries, tool databases, best practices, and process documentation - Implement process improvements to enhance productivity, reduce cycle times, and increase machine utilization - Collaborate cross-functionally with additive designers on custom workholding, identifying whether design or process changes are the right fix for a given issue - Design and deploy automation solutions to enhance quality control and maximize production rates - Work on the production floor to provide technical support, training, and hands-on troubleshooting as needed - Ensure compliance with quality control processes, industry standards, and safety regulations **Basic Qualifications:** - Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline - Experience with CNC programming and machining (internships and/or collegiate engineering clubs are acceptable) - Experience with Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing **Nice to Have:** - Experience with MasterCAM or Hypermill - Experience with 5-axis machines - Experience with DMG Mori and Siemens controls - Experience machining hard metals such as titanium or Inconel - Experience with automation programming for probe alignment, in-situ quality checks, and adaptive process compensation based on measurement feedback - Familiarity with metal 3D printed parts and their post-processing requirements - Familiarity with machining castings or forgings - Strong problem-solving skills and a hands-on approach to debugging machining processes - Experience with quality control tools, including CMM, micrometers, and thread gauges - Ability to work with power tools, hand tools, cranes, forklifts, and other heavy equipment - Comfortable lifting/moving up to 30 lbs and standing for extended periods - Willingness to work overtime when needed **Location:** - Based in Hawthorne, our vertically integrated facility brings technology development, R&D, and production together under one roof. We operate at the center of LA’s deep tech ecosystem, surrounded by some of the most ambitious hardware innovation happening anywhere in the country. - Our fast-paced, cross-functional environment is built on close collaboration, and as such, this role requires full-time onsite presence (five days a week), with very limited exceptions. **What We Offer:** - We have an inclusive and diverse culture that values collaboration, learning, and making deliberate data-driven decisions. - We offer a unique opportunity to be an early and integral member of a rapidly growing company that is scaling a world-changing technology. - Benefits - Significant stock option packages - 100% employer-paid Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance (premium PPO and HMO options) - Life insurance - Traditional and Roth 401(k) - Relocation assistance provided - Paid vacation, sick leave, and company holidays - Generous Paid Parental Leave and extended transition back to work for the birthing parent - Free daily catered lunch and dinner, and fully stocked kitchenette - Casual dress, flexible work hours, and regular catered team building events - Compensation - Our intent is to offer a salary that is commensurate for the company’s current stage of development and allows the employee to grow and develop within a role. - In addition to the significant stock option package, the estimated salary range for this role is $95,000-$110,000, *dependent on the candidate's academic level (Bachelors, Masters, or PhD) and demonstrated out of classroom experience.* - Freeform is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values diversity; employment with Freeform is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

role: Member of Technical Staff, AI Products (Early Career - Industry)
description: ***NOTE ON ELIGIBILITY**: this role is for industry candidates already working in software engineering for the past 1+ years. **New grads and current students should NOT apply** to this role (instead, visit* [*](https://pplx.ai/newgrads)*).* ## About the role In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people now use Perplexity to transform knowledge into action, through Search, Comet, and Computer. Product Engineering owns those experiences end to end, from the interface a user touches to the search and model calls behind it, on top of roughly 200M queries a day and a 200B+ URL index. This is a full stack role in the truest sense. There are no frontend or backend lanes here, and no one waits for a ticket before starting. It suits people who love to build and want the room to do it. What you have shipped and how quickly you learn tell us far more than years on a resume or where you went to school. ## What you will do - Own a user-facing surface end to end, from the interaction, design, and frontend through the application logic, APIs, data models, and the search or model calls behind them. - Ship to production continuously. New engineers typically have code in front of users in their first week. - Build with AI as a primary tool, not a novelty. We expect you to use agents and coding models aggressively to move faster, and to have sound judgment about when their output is wrong. - Turn ambiguous product ideas into working prototypes, then use real usage data and evals to decide what survives. - Raise the quality bar on reliability, latency, and craft for the surfaces you own. - Work directly with designers, PMs, and research engineers, without unnecessary process in between. ## What we look for - 1+ years of professional software engineering experience, or a track record of strong internships where you shipped production code at scale. - Strong in at least one backend language, such as Python or Go, with real experience across services, APIs, and relational data modeling. Comfortable working in React and TypeScript on the frontend. - Real evidence of building: production work you understand in depth, shipped side projects with actual users, meaningful open-source contributions, hackathon wins, or research you turned into working software. - Comfort with ambiguity and an instinct to start building incrementally rather than wait for a spec. - Hands-on experience with AI products, with opinions about their rough edges and what that means for the product you are building. ## Nice to have - Experience with our stack: React or Next.js, Python, Go, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker, AWS. You will not be expected to know all of it on day one. - Experience building on top of LLMs: AI orchestration, RAG, evals, agents, tool use. - Product taste. You can tell a good interface from a bad one and explain how to improve it. - A public track record we can read, such as GitHub, a technical blog, or a demo we can try.

role: Quality Leadership Development Program (Co-op Project Engineer) Spring 2027
description: As part of O-I's Quality Leadership Development Program Co-op, you'll have the unique opportunity to learn from industry experts at the world's leading glass container manufacturer while working at our global headquarters in Perrysburg, Ohio. This 12 to 16-week rotational program combines hands-on quality and manufacturing experience with structured training designed to build the foundation for a successful, long-term career at O-I. As a Project Engineer Co-op, you'll take on meaningful work, solve real business challenges, and gain exposure to the people, technologies, and processes that drive our manufacturing operations. Throughout the program, you'll benefit from a comprehensive learning and development experience that includes on-the-job training, networking opportunities, and social engagement activities. You'll work alongside experienced professionals who are invested in your growth while developing technical, operational, and leadership skills that will prepare you for future opportunities within O-I. Your co-op experience will challenge you, expand your industry knowledge, and provide valuable exposure to manufacturing operations and quality systems. As you continue to grow, you'll gain greater responsibility, develop skills that contribute to team success, and play a role in shaping the future of our organization. The Quality Leadership Development Program is designed to prepare participants for technical and supervisory careers in manufacturing and quality across our North American operations. During the co-op development program, you'll: Perform a variety of tests, analyses, and studies focused on improving glass container quality. Apply problem-solving skills and statistical tools to design studies and conduct quality and complaint analyses. Participate in the evaluation and testing of new container designs. Partner with O-I manufacturing plants and customers to investigate glass container quality and manufacturing challenges. Conduct measurements and prepare reports to communicate quality findings and recommendations. Gain exposure to key plant processes, including batch and furnace operations, forming machines, equipment systems, inspection, packaging, and quality assurance programs. Develop a well-rounded understanding of plant operations, customer relations, and manufacturing management through hands-on experience, collaboration with corporate and plant teams, and potential travel to O-I facilities and customer locations. The ideal co-op participant will have: A natural curiosity and eagerness to learn. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining strong attention to detail. High motivation and the ability to work independently. Excellent communication and presentation skills with the ability to collaborate across all levels of the organization. A desire to grow into future leadership opportunities and help develop high-performing teams. Basic Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing, or a related field. Preferred degree disciplines include Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Ceramic and Glass Engineering, Maintenance and Industrial Technology, Operations Management, and Materials Science. Must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. O-I does not sponsor work visas for internships or co-op positions. What we offer at O-I: Competitive compensation Opportunity for future growth and advancement Supportive teams to help you grow and learn new skills Next Steps: If you are smart, passionate, innovative, culturally open, curious and collaborative, we’d like to hear from you. O-I is committed to fostering an inclusive environment that attracts and embraces the brightest minds and creates a culture that welcomes a diversity of ideas and perspectives while encouraging growth and rewarding performance. Apply through the “I’m interested” button today! Not ready to apply but interested in learning more about O-I's student opportunities? Sign up to receive more information from us here . All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. O-I is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and does not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class. If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application process, or in order to perform the essential functions of a position, please contact O-I at and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information. To be the leading producer of glass bottles and jars worldwide you need passion, commitment and innovation baked into the very fabric of a business and its people. For more than 120 years, our glass makers have honed their craft—channeling their creativity into more than 1,800 patents held today. When you join O-I you become part of that story. O-I has more than a century of experience crafting pure, sustainable, brand-building glass packaging for many of the world’s best-known food and beverage brands. We are proud to provide high quality glass packaging for beer, wine, spirits, food, non-alcoholic beverages, cosmetics and pharmaceuticals. We are dedicated to make what matters to shape a healthier, more sustainable and more exciting world. We transform the industry to make glass more relevant and more accessible to more people.

description: ![](https://click.appcast.io/greenhouse-te8/a31.png?ent=34&e=22630&t=1701374353806) ![](https://track.jobadx.com/v1/i.gif?utm_pixel=224e990b-8ff4-4287-8d5d-2ff09647f181&utm_ptz=EST&utm_rqt=track) ## **About the Team** DoorDash is building the world’s most reliable on-demand logistics engine for delivery! We’re looking for machine learning engineer interns to join our fast-growing engineering team to help us develop a 24x7 global infrastructure system that powers DoorDash’s three-sided marketplace of consumers, merchants, and dashers. ## **About the Role** As a Machine Learning Engineer intern at Doordash, you’ll work on tackling new challenges in machine learning and artificial intelligence. You’ll conduct research that can be applied across Doordash engineering teams and engage in external collaborations and mentoring, while also performing research in any of the following areas: Auction, Game theory, Recommender systems, Ranking, AdTech, Computer Vision, Causal Inference, and Big data analytics. We offer a 12-week summer internship program in our San Francisco, Sunnyvale, New York, or Seattle offices. ## **You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…** - Use cutting-edge research in ML/AI, NLP, RecSys, Ranking, Computer Vision, Causal Inference, Ad Tech, Graph analysis to solve real-world problems across discovery, ads,forecasting, fulfillment and search experiences at Doordash. - Contribute and execute on research ideas that can be applied and used to improve product experience at Doordash. - Collect, analyze, and synthesize findings from data and use these insights to build relevant ML models. - Write clean, efficient, and sustainable code ## We’re excited about you because you… - Are working towards a Masters degree in Computer Science, ML, NLP, Statistics, Information Sciences or related field and are graduating between Fall 2027 & Summer 2028 - Have a mastery of at least one systems languages (Java, C++, Python, Kotlin, GoLang) or one ML framework (Tensorflow, Pytorch, MLFlow) - Have experience in research and in solving analytical problems - Are a strong communicator and team player. - Have a passion for applied ML and the Doordash product - Ideally have worked on publications in machine learning, AI, data science, data analytics, statistics, or related technical fields Applications for this position are accepted on an ongoing basis **Compensation** The successful candidate's starting pay will fall within the pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including, but not limited to, skills, experience, qualifications, work location, and market conditions. Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future. In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information. DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others. To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page [here](https://careers.doordash.com/). See below for paid time off details: - **For salaried roles:** flexible paid time off/vacation, plus 80 hours of paid sick time per year. - **For hourly roles:** vacation accrued at about 1 hour for every 25.97 hours worked (e.g. about 6.7 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 3.4 hours/month if working 20 hours/week), and paid sick time accrued at 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (e.g. about 5.8 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 2.9 hours/month if working 20 hours/week). **The national base pay ranges for this position within the United States, including Illinois and Colorado.** I4 $130,600—$192,000 USD I5 $159,800—$235,000 USD I6 $193,800—$285,000 USD ## About DoorDash At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods. DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more. ## Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel. THE POSITION Hoosier Racing Tire in Plymouth, IN, is seeking a Manufacturing Engineer Intern to join our team. The Manufacturing Engineer Intern will have the opportunity to work alongside our Plant Engineering and Maintenance teams on a variety of hands-on projects supporting race tire manufacturing. The position will gain firsthand experience with the equipment, processes, and operations that support production while assisting with projects and identifying opportunities for continuous improvement. HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT Take ownership of assigned projects from development through completion and final evaluation. Support Plant Engineering and Maintenance with additional projects and day-to-day initiatives as needed. Gain firsthand experience with the operations of a large-scale manufacturing facility. Build an understanding of the roles, processes, equipment, and procedures that support efficient production. Develop practical knowledge of the racing tire manufacturing process. Contribute fresh ideas and identify opportunities to improve processes, efficiency, and overall operations. WHAT YOU BRING TO THE ROLE Be a student who is enrolled full-time and pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree from an accredited college/university and will be enrolled full-time in Fall 2027. Be majoring in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Engineering Technology, Mechatronics, or a related technical field. Have an overall cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher (unofficial academic transcripts must be provided at the time of application). Must be able to commute to Plymouth, IN. Hoosier will not pay for housing expenses for this opportunity. EEO-Statement: EEO / Disabled / Protected Veteran Employer. Continental offers equal employment opportunities to all qualified individuals, without regard to unlawful consideration to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, religion, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law. In addition, as a federal contractor, Continental complies with government regulations, including affirmative action responsibilities for qualified individuals with a disability and protected veterans, where they apply. To be considered, you must apply for a specific position for which Continental has a current posted job opening. Qualifying applications will be considered only for the specific opening(s) to which you apply. If you would like to be considered for additional or future job openings, we encourage you to reapply for other opportunities as they become available. Further, Continental provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with a disability. If you need assistance in the application process, please reply to or contact US Recruiting at 800-821-2727. This telephone line and email address are reserved solely for job seekers with disabilities requesting accessibility assistance or an accommodation in the job application process. Please do not call about the status of your job application, if you do not require accessibility assistance or an accommodation. Messages left for other purposes, such as following up on an application or non-disability related technical issues, will not receive a call back. Ready to drive with Continental? Take the first step and fill in the online application. Continental is a leading tire manufacturer. Founded in 1871, the company generated sales of €13.9 billion in 2024, currently employs around 57,000 people worldwide and has 20 production and 16 development sites. Tire solutions from Continental make mobility safer, smarter, and more sustainable. Its premium portfolio encompasses car, truck, bus, two-wheel, and specialty tires as well as smart solutions and services for fleets and tire retailers. Continental has been delivering top performance for more than 150 years and is one of the world’s largest tire manufacturers. Hoosier Racing Tire, the largest race tire manufacturer in the world, has continually promoted passion, pride, and success in the racing industry since 1957. Based in Plymouth, Ind. their state-of-the-art facility, including a fully integrated technology and R&D center, is solely dedicated to engineering, designing, supporting, and manufacturing over 1,000 different racing and high-performance tires. Instilled with the heritage of champions, Hoosier utilizes a model sales and distribution network to deliver winning results globally. Hoosier Racing Tire is a 100% subsidiary of Continental AG.

The Jr. Clinical Investigator, CRS oversees the clinical research of consumer products involving healthy paid volunteers. Develops research studies and creates standards and guidelines for clinical research services and programs. Ensures adherence to standard operating procedures, good clinical practice and FDA regulations. Oversees the clinical research of consumer products involving healthy paid volunteers. Writes protocols, collects and reviews data, prepares progress reports, analyzes results, writes summaries and conclusions and issues reports. Develops, maintains and reviews Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Ensures that study personnel have access to SOPs and that SOPs are followed. Conducts and / or supervises studies in accordance with the protocol and SOP’s. Protects the rights, safety and welfare of subjects. role: Hardware Machine Learning PhD Research Internship
description: We are deploying machine learning directly onto custom hardware – and we want you to help drive it forward. This PhD internship is an opportunity to work on research that has direct impact on IMC's work tackling open problems at the frontier of low-latency ML inference and hardware acceleration. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time. ## **About the Role** Our marketing team combines creative, customer-focused strategy with data-driven precision to reach the right customers at the right time. We’re hiring an Organic Social Content Manager to build Base into one of the most distinctive, entertaining, and trusted energy brands on social. You’ll own the day-to-day operation of Base’s organic channels, from developing the content calendar and creating original content to publishing, engaging with our audience, and learning from performance. You’ll turn Base’s products, customers, employees, and mission into platform-native stories people want to watch, share, and join. This is a hands-on creative role. You’ll develop recurring social series, respond quickly to relevant cultural moments, and personally bring ideas from concept through production. You should be as comfortable scripting and filming a video as you are writing a caption, organizing a calendar, or interpreting performance data. ## **What You’ll Do** - Own Base’s organic social strategy, content calendar, and publishing cadence across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, X, and emerging platforms. - Develop original, recurring content series that make Base, energy, and the grid interesting, useful, and fun to follow. - Concept, script, capture, edit, write, and publish platform-native content, including short-form video, photos, graphics, carousels, and written posts. - Find compelling stories across Base’s customers, products, installations, employees, markets, and mission, then turn them into content people want to watch and share. - Balance planned programming with reactive content, moving quickly on trends, customer conversations, cultural moments, and company news when Base has something meaningful to add. - Maintain the content calendar and manage the workflows behind it, including briefs, assets, approvals, deadlines, and platform-specific adaptations. - Collaborate with design, marketing, product, operations, and other teams to support launches, events, market expansions, and major company moments. - Build relationships with Base’s audience by responding to comments and messages, amplifying customer stories and user-generated content, and identifying advocates who can help grow the community. - Track organic reach, shares, saves, watch time, engagement, audience growth, and the performance of recurring series. Turn those insights into better ideas and stronger future content. - Stay close to platform changes, emerging formats, internet culture, and the brands and creators setting the standard for social content. ## **What You’ll Bring** - Experience creating and managing organic social content for a consumer brand, product-led company, creative agency, media company, or similarly fast-moving organization. - A portfolio of original social work that demonstrates strong ideas, platform-native execution, and measurable audience or engagement growth. - Hands-on content creation skills. You can take an idea from concept to published post, including scripting, filming, editing, copywriting, and packaging it for the platform. - Strong short-form video instincts, including hooks, pacing, framing, captions, sound, and storytelling. You are comfortable using mobile-first editing tools such as CapCut, Premiere, or similar software. - Excellent writing skills and the ability to make a technical or unfamiliar subject feel clear, human, and interesting. - Deep familiarity with Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, and X, including an understanding of what audiences expect from each platform. - Strong creative judgment and a high bar for what is worth publishing. You know how to participate in culture without forcing the brand into conversations where it does not belong. - Comfort working both behind and in front of the camera when the idea calls for it. You can also help coworkers, customers, and partners feel natural on camera. - A data-informed mindset. You can interpret content performance, explain what worked, and apply those lessons to the next creative cycle. - Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage a high-output calendar, multiple collaborators, and fast-moving deadlines. - A proactive, resourceful attitude and comfort creating structure in a fast-paced, high-ownership environment. ## ## **Portfolio** Please include a portfolio or links to three to five examples of social content you helped create. For each example, briefly explain the idea, your specific contribution, and what you learned from its performance. ## **About the Team** The Marketing team at Base is lean, high-ownership, and results-driven. We operate with clear accountability, tight feedback loops, and a strong bias toward action. Marketing works closely with design, sales, product, and operations to build scalable systems that support the rapid buildout of America’s next-generation power company. *Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.* ## **Our Values** - **First Principles Thinking:** Question assumptions. Principles > rules. - **Operate at Base Pace:** Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing. - **Give & Get Feedback:** Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset. - **Everyone’s an Owner:** Follow through on commitments and own results. - **Strong Opinions, Loosely Held:** Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information. - **Committed to the Mission:** Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in. - **Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit:** Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things. ## **Do the best work of your life at Base.**

Who will you be working with? Wabtec is a leading global provider of equipment, systems, digital solutions, and value-added services. Our team is focused on continually improving our best-in-class production capabilities. We combine deep domain expertise and tenured experience to deliver unparalleled products for our customers. Here you’ll interact daily with team members during the problem resolution process and will partner with other key stakeholders to support our internal customers and their responsibilities. How will you make a difference? As a member of the CNC Machinist Trainee Group, you will be responsible for performing multiple tasks to support the fabrication of locomotive/mining components. In addition to machining, you will have responsibility for assembling components and other duties as assigned. Machinists are responsible for working together as a team to improve manufacturing processes and promote a climate of cooperation. This is an estimated 9-month training program aimed at developing you into a fully qualified machinist; completion of a hands-on assessment is a requirement. This is a 2nd shift or weekend shift position. Throughout the estimated 9-month training program, you will work on 1st shift and will be transitioned to your assigned shift following the successful completion of training and your hands-on assessment. Desired Skill Sets: Working knowledge of G&M code Minimum Requirements: A minimum of 6 months of CNC Machining experience, or successful completion of a 6-month CNC certificate program. Basic knowledge of blueprints and manufacturing instructions to produce machined parts. Must be able to lift material up to 40 lbs with or without reasonable accommodation. Must have ability to properly use and care for assigned tools and equipment. Must be able to adhere to standards, do a quality job in a safe manner, within allotted time. Must have basic computer skills. Must be able to pass a pre-employment technical assessment. Every employee will be an in-process inspector. Must be 18 years of age or older. Must have high-school diploma or GED or equivalent. Must be willing to wear personal protective equipment, for example safety glasses, gloves, hats, ear plugs and safety shoes. Must be willing to work in a tobacco-free environment. Be willing to take a drug test & submit to a background check as part of the selection process. Be willing to submit to random drug tests. Legal authorization to work in the U.S. is required. We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this job. Must be willing to work as necessary to meet requirements of the position, including the ability to work occasional weekends and scheduled overtime. What will your typical day look like? CNC Machinists may include but is not limited to the following: Understand and perform all functions required to set up and operate a variety of CNC and /or manual machining equipment including but not limited to: 4 axis vertical lathes, horizontal boring machines, gear gasher, gear grinder, cylindrical grinder, mills and coordinate measuring machines. Use standard machine tools including, but not limited to drill press, band saw, lathe, press breaks, welding equipment etc., and a variety of hand, electric, and pneumatic tools Change and adjust tools as required to maintain quality Set up both fixtures and parts for machining De-burr parts Use manual and electronic inspection devices to check multiple quality parameters Strong attention to detail, problem-solving skills, and mathematical abilities required Promote climate of cooperation; leading by example mentoring others in safety, quality, environmental, lean and high performance work team philosophies Work with all facility employees on improving manufacturing processes through prototyping, fabrication and experimental machining to develop and prove concepts and design and implement necessary fixtures and tooling for manufacturing improvements Assembly of components and full assembly of finished parts Read and interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, and specifications Knowledge of materials, manufacturing processes, and quality control techniques Material transport including the use of but not limited to, radio controlled cranes, forklifts and tuggers Prying and setting heavy equipment may also be required All machinists will perform multiple tasks in any combination and concentration of the above-mentioned areas and will rotate through all or most of the processes rather than being assigned to a specific task. Machinists must be able to work as part of a team having responsibility for assembling numerous components and other duties as assigned. The starting hourly rate of this position is $29/hour (with additional night shift differential of $1/hr when working 2nd shift hours.) Available shifts: Shift availability is dependent on business needs. 4-day, 10-hour work week: 4-day (Monday through Thursday), 2nd shift hours are 3:15PM – 1:45AM. 3-day, 12-hour work week: 3-day (Friday through Sunday), weekend shift hours are 5:00AM – 5:30 PM. Must be able to work scheduled shift hours. Position Overview We are seeking a motivated Junior Infrastructure Engineer to support infrastructure operations, cloud environments, system administration, automation, monitoring, and technical troubleshooting for a USCIS federal program. The ideal candidate will have foundational knowledge of Linux/Windows systems, cloud infrastructure, networking, scripting, security, and DevOps concepts. This individual will work closely with senior infrastructure engineers, developers, cybersecurity teams, and other technical stakeholders to maintain reliable, secure, and scalable infrastructure. This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career infrastructure engineer who is interested in developing hands-on experience supporting mission-critical federal technology environments. Key Responsibilities Assist in the implementation, configuration, administration, and maintenance of cloud and on-premises infrastructure. Support Linux and/or Windows servers, virtual machines, storage, network components, and related infrastructure services. Assist senior engineers with provisioning, configuration, upgrades, patching, and ongoing maintenance of infrastructure environments. Monitor infrastructure availability, system performance, capacity, and health using enterprise monitoring and logging tools. Troubleshoot common server, operating system, network, application connectivity, and infrastructure-related issues. Support cloud infrastructure services in AWS and/or Azure environments. Assist with infrastructure automation and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) using tools such as Terraform, CloudFormation, Ansible, or similar technologies. Support CI/CD pipelines and DevSecOps processes in collaboration with application development and engineering teams. Assist with containerized environments using Docker and Kubernetes/OpenShift, where applicable. Support identity and access management activities, including user access, permissions, service accounts, and role-based access controls. Assist with vulnerability remediation, system hardening, security patches, and configuration updates in accordance with established federal and organizational security requirements. Participate in incident troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, and resolution of infrastructure-related issues. Create and maintain technical documentation, including configuration documents, SOPs, runbooks, architecture information, troubleshooting guides, and knowledge-base articles. Support infrastructure changes across development, testing, staging, and production environments. Work with senior engineers to improve infrastructure reliability, availability, scalability, security, and operational efficiency. Participate in Agile ceremonies, technical meetings, sprint activities, and team discussions as needed. Assist with production deployments and operational support activities when required. Escalate complex infrastructure and security issues to senior engineers and appropriate technical teams. Required Skills 1-3 years of relevant experience in Infrastructure Engineering, Systems Administration, Cloud Engineering, DevOps, IT Operations, or a related technical field. Foundational knowledge of AWS and/or Microsoft Azure cloud services. Basic administration knowledge of Linux and/or Windows Server environments. Understanding of networking concepts, including: TCP/IP DNS DHCP HTTP/HTTPS VPN Firewalls Load balancers Subnets and routing Basic understanding of cloud networking and security concepts. Familiarity with scripting using Python, PowerShell, Bash, or Shell scripting. Basic knowledge of Git/version control. Familiarity with CI/CD concepts and tools such as Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps, or similar. Basic knowledge of Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform, CloudFormation, or Ansible. Understanding monitoring, logging, alerting, and troubleshooting concepts. Basic understanding of Identity and Access Management (IAM) and role-based access control. Understanding of general cybersecurity principles, secure configurations, patching, and vulnerability management. Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills. Ability to work effectively with developers, infrastructure engineers, security teams, and other technical stakeholders. Good written and verbal communication skills. Ability to create and maintain clear technical documentation. Preferred Skills Hands-on experience with AWS services such as EC2, S3, VPC, IAM, CloudWatch, RDS, Route 53, or related services. Experience with Microsoft Azure infrastructure services. Exposure to Docker, Kubernetes, or OpenShift. Experience with Terraform, Ansible, AWS CloudFormation, or other infrastructure automation technologies. Familiarity with observability and monitoring tools such as Splunk, CloudWatch, Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, or similar. Understanding of DevOps/DevSecOps methodologies. Experience working in Agile/Scrum environments. Understanding of SSL/TLS certificates, encryption, secrets management, and secure credential handling. Exposure to federal cybersecurity and compliance environments, including NIST, FISMA, FedRAMP, or DHS security standards. Previous experience supporting a federal government client, particularly DHS or USCIS, is a plus. Education Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Engineering, Cybersecurity, or a related technical discipline. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly-sophisticated customers across the globe – large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military. With five satellites on orbit and many more set to launch soon, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization. Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Blackrock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA. #### **Propulsion Engineer Intern (Winter 2027)** Internships at Astranis typically last for twelve weeks, and are hourly roles designed for students who are currently enrolled at a four-year university. As an Intern, you will have an amazing opportunity to work on hard problems — we pride ourselves on giving everyone at Astranis a chance to do meaningful work on complex projects, no matter their seniority. Many past interns have designed and tested hardware/software that is heading to space on our first satellite, and many of them are now full-time employees at Astranis. If you have already graduated from a four-year university, please apply to be an Associate Engineer. #### **Role** - Make an impact on the Propulsion team by designing, analyzing, building, and testing propulsion system hardware - Take on interdisciplinary projects with other teams to support Propulsion and company initiatives - Learn how to apply your academic experience to real world situations and develop team skills to fuel you academic and professional careers #### **Requirements** - Currently pursuing a B.S. in a technical discipline (e.g. Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering, Physics) - Understanding of spacecraft systems and operation demonstrated through course work or student organizations - Demonstrated ability to personally design, build, and test hardware from scratch - Don't meet them all? Not a problem. Please apply even if you do not meet all these criteria. #### **Bonus** - Familiarity with spacecraft design with a focus on chemical and/or electrical propulsion for spacecraft - Experience with Python - Test experience with spacecraft propulsion systems The base pay for this position is $29.00 per hour.
