role: The Pauli Murray Fellowship, Communications Team
location: New York, New York, United States
description: The ACLU seeks a **Pauli Murray Fellow** in the **Communications Department** of the ACLU’s National office in **New York.** This is a hybrid role that has in-office requirements of two (2) days per week or eight (8) days per month. **This is an eighteen-month term limited position.** ## OVERVIEW ACLU’s **Pauli Murray Fellowship** was founded 2022 in honor of the Reverend Dr. Pauli Murray – activist, legal theorist, author, Episcopal priest, and former ACLU board member. The fellowship invests in and cultivates leadership pathways for individuals who have overcome systemic barriers to achievement to support development of future leaders. Target participants are those aspiring to make full-time entry into nonprofit organizations with a passion to advance civil rights and civil liberties. Those selected will embedded within an ACLU cross-functional department and charged with overseeing critical internal initiatives, projects, and priorities. They receive meaningful exposure, access, and training to enhance and broaden their professional skills. This fellowship will begin in mid-January 2027 for 18-months. **THE TEAM:** The ACLU Communications & Marketing department creates, maintains, and expands message narratives to engage our supporters and other target audiences, to help protect and expand civil liberties and civil rights, and illustrate the value and impact of the ACLU’s transformational work. Through our messaging, engagement with newsmakers, our written content, creative branding, and visual identity, we encourage support for the ACLU and help to build a more perfect union. **YOUR DAY TO DAY:** The Pauli Murray Fellow will play a critical role in developing and executing communications strategies that advance the ACLU’s work on civil liberties and civil rights across all fifty states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico. The Fellow will work towards a cohesive audience experience across national and affiliate channels on priority issues and major moments and strengthen the ability for nearly 200 communications, marketing and digital staff nationwide to work together. You will use your knowledge of advocacy communications combined with organizational skills to create resources for affiliate staff and enhance our nationwide communications staff community through: - Development and distribution of weekly rapid response communications resource digest and occasional ad hoc digests around critical moments such as Supreme Court decisions and elections. - Partner with other nationwide comms staff and affiliate advisors to facilitate and set agendas for monthly nationwide communications staff calls. - Partner with other nationwide comms staff to maintain resources related to the ACLU’s issue areas and functional resources to support excellence on a range of communications channels such as earned media, social media, graphic design and multimedia, and websites. - Support community building across the ACLU communications network though virtual meetings, staff introductions via email and intranet tools, and other forums. **Capstone Project** With the knowledge and skills the Fellow gains over the course of the program, they will complete a capstone project that explores how to best leverage the national scale and affiliate infrastructure to grow the ACLU’s list of supporters, deepen relationships with existing supporters and ultimately increase the ACLU’s capacity for influencing laws and policy. The capstone project will involve: - Discussing and defining needs with national and affiliate teams - Defining roles between national and affiliate teams to maximize impact - Mapping ACLU communications tools and tactics in ways that support our goals - Adapting general documentation and resources to make campaign-specific guides. **WHAT YOU'LL BRING:** While you may not possess all the qualifications outlined, successful candidates will bring many of the following attributes: - Proactive and self-reliant with proven experience successfully managing multiple and competing priorities - Familiarity with communications tactics — such as working with press and media outlets, social media, or creative campaigns that use graphics and videos — in the context of advocacy and educational campaigns. - Ability to take complex instructions or information and make it easy for people to use in their everyday work. - Intermediate knowledge of Microsoft Office (specifically Word, Excel and Outlook) - Familiarity with a WYSIWYG web publishing platform is a plus. **FUTURE ACLU-ERS WILL** - Be committed to advancing the mission of the ACLU - Center and embed the principles of equity, inclusion and belonging in their work by demonstrating commitment to diversity with an approach that respects and values multiple perspectives - Be committed to work collaboratively and respectfully toward resolving obstacles and conflict **KEY COMPONENTS OF THE PAULI MURRAY FELLOWSHIP** - Full-time employment, $78,000 annual salary, and benefits for 18 months at the ACLU National Headquarters in New York. - Skill development in key functions such as professional communications, organizational strategy, project management, and more. These transferrable skills will support participants in their pursuit of future leadership roles. - Stipends to expand career and professional development through conferences, coursework, graduate school coaching, etc. - Access to leaders and mentors at the ACLU including career networking opportunities. - A trip to a historical site where the fellows can deepen their understanding and learn more on the ongoing challenges related to systemic barriers. - A capstone project developed with support from a mentor that allows participants to practically apply their academic skills. - Community with fellows and colleagues. **Acquired Skills Include** Your experience as a Pauli Murray Fellow with the Communications department will strengthen your skills in the following areas: - Developing strategic communications campaigns to further advocacy goals. - Understanding communications channels and tactics and connecting them with common advocacy audiences and goals. - Developing internal communications campaigns as well as resource and training development - Project management with a wide range of stakeholders and information management across several projects simultaneously. - Facilitating both large-group information sharing meetings and small group project-specific meetings. **WHY THE ACLU** For over 100 years, the ACLU has worked to defend and preserve the individual rights and liberties guaranteed by the Constitution and laws of the United States. Whether it’s ending mass incarceration, achieving full equality for the LGBTQ+ community, establishing new privacy protections for our digital age, or preserving the right to vote or the right to have an abortion, the ACLU takes up the toughest civil liberties cases and issues to defend all people. **OUR COMMITMENT TO EQUITY, DIVERSITY, INCLUSION AND BELONGING** Equity, diversity, and inclusion are core values of the ACLU and central to our work to advance liberty, equality, and justice for all. For us diversity, equity and inclusion are not just check-the-box activities, but a chance for us to make long-term meaningful change. We are a community committed to learning and growth, humility and grace, transparency and accountability. We believe in a collective responsibility to create a culture of belonging for all people within our organization – one that respects and embraces difference; treats everyone equitably; and empowers our colleagues to do the best work possible. We are as committed to anti-oppression and anti-racism internally as we are externally. Because whether we’re in the courts or in the office, we believe ‘We the People’ means all of us. With this commitment in mind, we strongly encourage applications from all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, marital status, citizenship, disability, veteran status and record of arrest or conviction, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. If you have a need and require assistance during the application process, please let us know by completing the [applicant accommodations form](https://forms.office.com/r/64aQQbxjuD) *The Department of Education has determined that employment in this position at the ACLU does not qualify for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program.* ## SELECTION TIMELINE: #### All applications are due by Monday, November 9th, 2026 by 11:59pm EST - **Interviews: First week of December 2026** - (*Applicants can expect to hear whether or not they have received an interview by mid November)* - **Final Selection: End of December 2026** **WHO SHOULD APPLY?** Individuals making their entry into the nonprofit sector full-time, overcoming systemic barriers to achievement, are encouraged to apply—especially those with a fresh perspective and a commitment to our mission. **Minimum qualifications:** - College graduate by September 2026 seeking entry-level role - A demonstrated commitment or interest to leadership, service, civil rights and civil liberties. - Eligibility to work in the United States for the duration of the program (January 2027 - July 2028). - An 18-month, Mon-Fri full-time commitment to working at the ACLU from January 2027 - July 2028 There is no single “right” major or course of study. We are looking for strong problem solvers with an eagerness to learn, a passion to lead, and commitment to civil rights and civil liberties. This fellowship primarily focuses on organizational leadership, emphasizing the operational aspects of an organization. If you are interested in our legal fellowships or direct advocacy work please click [here](https://www.aclu.org/careers/). SELECTION CRITERIA The selection committee will engage in a consistent and holistic review process, with attention to applicants with: - A demonstrated commitment to sustained leadership and service. - A demonstrated resilience in the face of systemic barriers or adversity. - A commitment to civil liberties, civil rights, and social justice. - Commitment to the [**mission**](https://www.aclu.org/) **[of the ACLU](https://www.aclu.org/)**. - No prior connection to the ACLU (via past internships, fellowships, other connections) a plus. ## HOW TO APPLY Please submit the following no later than Monday, November 9th, 2026 by 11:59pm EST - **A resume** (no longer than two pages) - **Two Essays** - Essay 1: Consider a significant life experience or perspective that has influenced your future goals. How does it it connect with your commitment to civil rights and liberties and how do you foresee using the Pauli Murray Fellowship to help you achieve your aspirations? (400 words, Microsoft Document or PDF) - Essay 2: Personal Statement or Video Essay selected from the prompt below\* (written essays no longer than 600 words in a Microsoft Document or PDF **OR** video essay no longer than 5 minutes). - In a 1967 letter to Dr. Kathryn F. Clarenbach, Chair of the National Board of NOW, Pauli Murray wrote, “And since, as a human being, I cannot allow myself to be fragmented into Negro at one time, woman at another, or worker at another. I must find a unifying principle in all these movements to which I can adhere . . . description: The ACLU seeks a **Pauli Murray Fellow** in the **Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, and Belonging Department** of the ACLU’s National office in **New York.** This is a hybrid role that has in-office requirements of two (2) days per week or eight (8) days per month. **This is an eighteen-month term limited position.** ## OVERVIEW ACLU’s **Pauli Murray Fellowship** was founded 2022 in honor of the Reverend Dr. Pauli Murray – activist, legal theorist, author, Episcopal priest, and former ACLU board member. The fellowship invests in and cultivates leadership pathways for individuals who have overcome systemic barriers to achievement to support development of future leaders. We know that our success in doing so is tied to our success in advancing our mission. The EDIB team plays a key role in this work, continuing to move the ACLU to a culture of belonging. **YOUR DAY TO DAY:** ThePauli Murray Fellowwill be responsible for providing event support, advancing programmatic efforts, and working on designated special projects. The team is seeking a Joining Engineer Co-Op that can join the team for approximately 6 months. This role is responsible for joining qualification and development by planning and conducting experiments, evaluating results, and documenting research findings. Responsibilities Conduct literature reviews of current joining methods and practices for proposed aluminum material combinations. Plan, develop, and optimize aluminum alloy joining processes. Conduct laboratory experiments and support operation of joining and materials-characterization equipment. Prepare test specimens and perform metallography, mechanical testing, and other relevant characterization. Analyze experimental data and interpret results using sound engineering and statistical methods. Maintain organized test records and follow applicable laboratory safety and operating procedures. Document research findings and communicate results through written reports and technical presentations. Collaborate with engineers, scientists, technologists, and technicians supporting product qualification and development. Minimum qualifications Currently enrolled in an accredited four-year university in Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Welding Engineering, or a related field. Hands-on laboratory or project experience with metal joining, materials processing, or materials characterization. Experience with metallography and mechanical testing. Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills. Ability to work safely and effectively in a laboratory and team environment. Must be available for approximately 6 months during summer-fall 2027. Must be currently authorized to work in the United States for any employer. Enrolled in an accredited 4-year University. Must be currently authorized to work in the United States for any employer Going forward, employees based in Kennesaw will be expected to work in the office Monday through Thursday, with Friday available to work remotely or from the office. Preferred qualifications Graduate student pursuing a master’s degree or PhD in relevant engineering discipline. Hands-on experience with laser welding, resistance spot welding, self-pierce riveting, or related joining processes. Experience with electron microscopy or other advanced materials-characterization techniques. Experience with design of experiments, statistical data analysis, or process optimization. Experience with engineering modeling, simulation, or data-driven methods. Knowledge of aluminum alloys, automotive sheet products, or joining metallurgy. Ability to work independently, manage multiple tasks, and communicate progress with limited supervision. Demonstrated technical communication through conference presentations, publications, project reports, or comparable work. *Please note that we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position. The facility includes state-of-the-art lab equipment and a diverse mix of product pilot lines that bring innovative solutions to customers in the automotive beverage can and specialty markets. Kennesaw provides a diverse and family-friendly place to live with countless museums cultural opportunities and educational institutions. Who We Are Lambda Legal is a national organization committed to achieving full recognition of the civil rights of lesbians, gay men, bisexuals, transgender people and everyone living with HIV through impact litigation, education and public policy work. Since 1973, Lambda Legal has used impact litigation and other advocacy tools to decriminalize same-sex relationships; challenge discrimination against LGBTQ+ people and people living with HIV in the workplace, in the home, in schools, in health care, and in the military; and protect LGBTQ+ families, including by winning and defending marriage equality. Clients are not charged for legal representation or advocacy and Lambda Legal receives no government funding. Headquartered in New York City, Lambda Legal has regional offices in Los Angeles, Chicago, Atlanta, Dallas, and Washington, DC. We believe that serving the full breadth of the LGBTQ+ and HIV communities requires cultural competency and enthusiasm for diversity of all kinds. To be successful, we must approach our work with an understanding that discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity is not the only obstacle to achieving full formal and lived equality for LGBTQ+ people and everyone living with HIV; rather, we recognize the intersectional nature of discrimination, specifically including biases based on race, religion, national origin, gender, disability, education, and class. In light of this reality, we prioritize awareness and proactive commitment to counteracting these biases and their compounding effects. Internship Locations New York, NY Washington, D.C. Chicago, IL Los Angeles, CA Atlanta, GA Responsibilities Summer interns primarily assist attorneys with litigation and policy tasks. This may include legislative research and tracking, investigation, research and drafting in ongoing cases, prospective cases, and amicus curiae briefs, in all areas of sexual orientation, gender identity, and HIV discrimination. Interns may also research, draft, and/or edit publications on these issues for public education and may assist in maintenance and expansion of resources for our national legal Help Desk. Qualifications Successful candidates will welcome the opportunity to work in a racially- and gender-diverse environment and to contribute to a positive and inclusive atmosphere. Interning at Lambda Legal requires a demonstrated awareness of and commitment to the concerns of the breadth of the communities that Lambda Legal serves. Due to the focused and challenging nature of the work Lambda Legal does, we prefer to hire law students who have some experience with issues relating to our mission. Thus, a background in or familiarity with issues important to lesbians, gay men, bisexuals, transgender people, and those living with HIV will greatly strengthen an application. Commitment to public interest law also greatly strengthens an application. Considering the amount of independent work required, second- and third-year students are preferred. Lambda Legal encourages applications from people of color and people with disabilities, including HIV. Compensation Because we have limited resources, Lambda Legal requires applicants to make diligent efforts to secure summer funding from their law schools. However, to ensure that economic barriers do not dissuade talented applicants, Lambda Legal is prepared to provide compensation for students for whom funding is not available. If you are not able to get funding from your school, or your school provides funding at a lesser amount, we will provide you with summer funding or will supplement your school’s funding. Selected students will receive more information about this process after receiving notice of their acceptance. Application Students interested in summer internships should apply beginning in the Fall. We begin hiring as the applicant pool allows and continue until all spaces are filled. Our Values & DEIB Philosophy Successful candidates will embrace and champion our Organizational Values and DEIB Philosophy Statement, bringing a commitment to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and supportive workplace. They will thrive in a diverse environment, actively contributing to a culture that respects and uplifts the full spectrum of communities Lambda Legal serves. Candidates can review our Organizational Values and DEIB Philosophy Statement on our Careers Page . ________ Read more about Lambda Legal's work on our blog and Instagram . Lambda Legal believes in creating a more equitable playing field for applicants and values the depth of relevant skills built through successful education, work, and life experiences. If your background and skills are a close match for this position, you are strongly encouraged to apply. Lambda Legal is committed to further building and maintaining a staff that reflects the full range of LGBTQ+, HIV-affected and allied communities, and is an equal opportunity employer. We value a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture. Lambda Legal encourages applications from all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, marital status, citizenship or immigration status, disability, veteran status, record of arrest or conviction, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Black people, Indigenous people, people of color, lesbian, gay, bisexual, queer, transgender and gender-diverse people, women, people with abilities in multiple languages, immigrants, people living with disabilities, protected veterans, and formerly incarcerated individuals and individuals living with HIV are all encouraged to apply.

**About Cowboy Space Corp.** **Mission** Cowboy Space Corporation is solving the global energy crisis by building the infrastructure for abundant, resilient space-based solar energy. We are tackling one of humanity's most complex engineering challenges with a world-class team dedicated to delivering a revolutionary power platform. Cowboy Space Corporation is transforming how civilization powers, computes and connects - from orbit to Earth. **Background** Cowboy Space Corporation is building the infrastructure to power and connect the orbital economy. Our modular, scalable satellites collect sunlight in Low Earth Orbit to enable multiple integrated applications: transmitting energy via infrared lasers (space-to-earth and space-to-space), powering on-orbit high-performance computing clusters (GPU/TPU), and providing secure, high bandwidth optical data transport. Current energy and data systems rely on complex logistics and outdated infrastructure. Cowboy Space Corporation overcomes these challenges by enabling direct, on-demand, secure, and scalable energy distribution and data processing from space. This will revolutionize how we operate in orbit and on Earth, supporting the rapidly expanding space industrial base, ISAM (In-Space Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing) operations, remote regions, and military bases. Baiju Bhatt founded Cowboy Space Corporation in 2024. **Social Media & Community Associate (Part-Time / Internship)** Location: [Dallas preferred / Remote US] Compensation: $15-$20/hr, roughly 20 hrs/week with room to grow Department: Growth Reports to: Director of Growth **About Rare Candy** We’re a leading marketplace dedicated to trading card games—Pokémon, MTG, Lorcana, and more—used by millions of collectors to buy, sell, and showcase their collections. Our operations team powers the logistics that ensure trading cards and collectibles move quickly and safely between sellers and collectors. We grew almost 30x last year, and we aren't slowing down. **The Role** You'll work with our world-class in-house creators, including Leonhart and Powdr TCG, to get compelling content in front of more people. They make it. You get it out the door, in the right places, at the right times, with the right words around it. You don't need to be a creator yourself. You need to be the person who knows what to post, when to post it, and what to say back when a hundred people reply. That means running the calendar, writing the captions, and working the comments, DMs, and Discord. This is an early-career role, and we expect it to be someone's first or second job. What matters is that you're genuinely native to the internet and already know the TCG corner of it. You know why a video took off before anyone explains it, you follow the accounts worth following, and you have opinions about which ones are good. If you're still finishing school and can commit to the hours, that works too. The other half of the job is the unglamorous half. Posts go out on time, threads get answered, promises get kept. We need both. **What Success Looks Like** First 90 days: - Posting five days a week on TikTok and Instagram, with a live calendar written ahead of time - Creator content is out the door within a day of us getting it - Comments and DMs answered daily in a voice that sounds like a collector, not a brand - You know our accounts' numbers and can say what moved and why By end of year one: - Every drop and product launch has a post plan you built and ran - We're a presence in the places collectors hang out, not just on our own feeds - Our reply game is part of why people follow us **What You'll Do** - Post consistently across TikTok and Instagram, with X and YouTube Shorts as we scale - Write captions, hooks, and replies that sound like one of us - Work the comments, DMs, Discord, and Reddit - Watch what's happening in TCG internet and flag anything we should jump on the same day - Coordinate with our creators on timing and what goes out when - Pitch post ideas. The good ones get made - Send a short weekly recap of what performed and why **You Might Be a Fit If …** - You're extremely online in a way that's useful, not just a habit - You know the TCG space: the products, the drama, the accounts, the language - You can write. Captions, hooks, replies, all of it - You have taste. You can look at a piece of content and know what to do with it - You hit deadlines and answer messages. Talent without follow-through won't work here - Formal experience is optional. Current students welcome Bonus points if you've run an account of your own, for a brand, a hobby, or yourself. **Why This Job** - You'll work directly with Leonhart and Powdr TCG, not three layers away from them - Hours flex around your class schedule, and we can work with your school if you need credit - Small team, so your ideas get made instead of sitting in a deck - This can grow into more hours or a full-time seat if it goes well **Our Hiring Process** 1. 30-min intro chat with Taylor (Director of Growth) 2. Working session: walk us through the accounts you follow, the three TCG accounts you think are doing it right, and why, with our Growth Team (45 minutes) **Ready to Build With Us?** Send your résumé and links to any accounts you've run to with the subject line "Gotta Post 'Em All." No cover letter. Instead, tell us in three sentences what Rare Candy should be posting that we currently aren't. Rare Candy is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate individuality, from Pikachu collectors to Magic pros, and are committed to building an inclusive team.

## WHAT MAKES US EPIC? At the core of Epic’s success are talented, passionate people. Epic prides itself on creating a collaborative, welcoming, and creative environment. Whether it’s building award-winning games or crafting engine technology that enables others to make visually stunning interactive experiences, we’re always innovating. Being Epic means being a part of a team that continually strives to do right by our community and users. We’re constantly innovating to raise the bar of engine and game development. ## ECOSEC ### **What We Do** Our ECOSEC team provides a safer experience for Epic's users. We work across multiple products and services to improve technology and craft transparent policies so our players and users can have positive experiences on our platforms. ## DATA SCIENCE INTERN ### **What You'll Do** We are looking for a Data Science Intern to join the Ecosystem Security team supporting initiatives related to fraud and abuse detection. description: **Fellow, East Harlem Inclusive Learning (Special Education) Teaching Fellowship (2027-2029)** **Position Reports to:** Director, Inclusive Learning Teaching Fellowship **Start/End Date:** Late May 2027 - Late June 2029 **Application Deadline:** The next application deadline is November 30th, 2026. Please note that applications are accepted on a rolling basis. The application deadline only informs which interview finalist day you may be scheduled for. Applicants who apply early have a higher chance of getting an offer as each cohort is relatively small. **FLSA Status:** Exempt **Snapshot** This is a 2-year program that prepares aspiring teachers through rigorous coursework in Special Education at Hunter College school of Education and a 2-year paid fellowship as an inclusive learning (special education) teacher at East Harlem Scholars Academies with extensive support and training in culturally responsive pedagogy. Fellows will complete the program with a Master’s degree in Special Education and initial New York State teaching certification. **Who We Are** East Harlem Scholars Academies are community-based Pre-K to 12 public charter schools operated by East Harlem Tutorial Program (EHTP). EHTP began in 1958 as a children's reading group and has since grown into a multi-site after-school program for traditional public school students and a network of public charter schools focused on significantly increasing the college graduation rate in East Harlem. At EHTP we also aim to serve as an agent of change and thoughtfully contribute to the national fight for racial equity. Through our organization-wide commitment to anti-racism work, we prepare our scholars to effect change, challenge the status quo, and thrive in the world around them. As staff members, we face our own racial identities and conscious and unconscious biases. With this in mind, all of our professional development, curriculum, organizational materials, and processes are designed with a goal of racial justice. We ground all of our work in racial equity,in our core values (**S**ervice, **C**ourage, **H**umility, **O**riginality, **L**eadership, **A**chievement, and **R**eflection), and in our five guiding principles: 1) all children can and will succeed when provided a great education; 2) the best learning occurs when children engage in higher-order, critical thinking; 3) a nurturing and supportive environment supports students' love of learning and of themselves; 4) self-awareness promotes dynamic leadership and global understanding; 5) active community engagement richly enhances educational opportunities. These principles inform and are reflected in our current four key strategic priorities: to increase high-impact, high-quality academic curriculum, programming content, staff capacity, and coaching; to embrace and advance our use of technology; to deepen our embodiment of ethical and equitable radical humanity; and to efficiently operationalize teaching, learning, community, and care. For more information about East Harlem Scholars Academies, please visit us at . ***Hunter College School of Education*** Hunter was New York City’s first teacher training program, founded in 1870, and to this day carries on a proud tradition of achievement and commitment to preparing teachers, counselors and administrators in over 40 specializations who make a difference in the lives of children, adolescents and consumers in communities throughout New York City and beyond. The Hunter College School of Education is dedicated to the preparation of deeply thoughtful, knowledgeable and highly effective teachers, administrators and counselors. Their commitment is to educate future professionals who will make a significant impact on the academic achievement, as well as the intellectual, social and emotional development of their students. The 2014 National Council on Teacher Quality (NCTQ) review of teacher preparation programs, published by U.S. News & World Report, indicates that the Hunter College School of Education offers the greatest breadth of quality across programs in the mid-Atlantic United States and the highest overall ranking in New York State. **The Work and Why it Matters** The [East Harlem Teaching Fellowship,](https://www.ehtp.org/inclusive-learning-fellowship) an EHTP program, in partnership with Hunter College School of Education, is an innovative, cohort-based teacher-training pathway for recent college graduates and career changers that develops, supports, and certifies aspiring educators to become inclusive learning teachers for East Harlem Scholars Academies and the greater East Harlem community. The program aims to improve educational outcomes for East Harlem students and increase the number of highly effective teachers serving East Harlem. **Inclusive Learning Fellowship** - 2-year teacher preparation program - $60,000/year salary + subsidized tuition + benefits - Subsidized master’s degree and certification in Special Education from Hunter College - Teach alongside a co-teacher in a 4th - 12th grade classroom at East Harlem Scholars Academies and take graduate coursework on the evenings and some weekends As a Teaching Fellow you will: ***Enroll in Graduate Coursework*** - Engage in coursework at Hunter College, both on- and off-site (classes are held during the workday and in the evenings; there may be occasional Saturdays) - Complete all requirements for initial teaching certification ***Receive Coaching and Cohort-based Learning Opportunities*** - Conduct structured observations of and co-teach with highly effective teachers in Scholars Academies - Receive weekly coaching tailored to your needs as a classroom teacher - Receive cohort-based professional development - Engage in ongoing reflection exercises linking theory learned in graduate coursework to actions practiced in the classroom ***Contribute to Community Engagement*** - Build positive relationships with families of EHTP students through frequent communication about students’ progress and ways that families can support their children’s learning - Plan at least one Family Engagement Event for families **Who You Are** - You believe in EHTP’s [mission, core values, and racial equity statement](https://www.ehtp.org/our-story) - You are open to exploring your own identity and privilege - You enjoy working with students, have an interest in teaching elementary students, and want to gain valuable classroom experience - You are committed to teaching in the East Harlem community - You are open to giving and receiving constructive feedback and are looking for professional growth opportunities consistently - You value teamwork and are able to work collaboratively with other instructional and support staff members in an effort to best serve your students - You have the perseverance to overcome any challenge - You are highly organized and hold yourself to high professional standards - You possess strong interpersonal communication skills (written and oral) **Eligibility Requirements:** - Bachelor's degree conferred by June 2027 - Preferred minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale - If you have an undergraduate GPA that falls under a 3.0, you will be required to write a statement explaining 1) any factors that impacted your undergraduate GPA, and 2) the steps you plan to take in order to ensure that you succeed in the Fellowship program - A liberal arts or sciences major (or interdisciplinary concentration) of at least 30 credits - A liberal arts core including the following: - *a General Education core in the liberal arts and sciences to include artistic expression, communication, information retrieval* - *concepts in history and social sciences, humanities* - *a language other than English* - *scientific and mathematical processes* - *written analysis and expression* - U.S. Citizen or National/Permanent Resident status - Applicants must not have taken more than 18 college credits in special education - Experience working with students a plus, but not required - Due to the nature of our diverse student population, Arabic, Mandarin or Spanish speaking candidates are highly encouraged to apply **Compensation and Benefits:** - $60,000/year salary - Health insurance - $10,000 towards Masters’ Degree in Special Education ($5,000 per year) - NYS teaching certification upon completion of program - Paid vacation (aligned with school closings calendar) - Laptop - Academic and financial guidance - Job placement support - This two-year program counts toward your years of teaching for student loan forgiveness **or** enroll in Public Service Loan Forgiveness **Thank you in advance for taking the time to apply to East Harlem Scholars Academies.**

Arcadis is the world's leading company delivering sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy solutions for natural and built assets. We are more than 34,000 people, in over 30 countries, dedicated to improving quality of life. Everyone has an important role to play. With the power of many curious minds, together we can solve the world’s most complex challenges and deliver more impact together. **Role description:** We are currently searching for a Water Engineer to support our team in Middletown, CT. We are looking for dedicated, creative, and energetic candidates interested in tackling challenges and developing sustainable solutions to address water issues. Collaborating with our experienced water professionals, you will support and drive the development of projects, interact, and work with clients, and develop your technical capabilities. **Role accountabilities:** The Water Engineer will possess a strong foundation in engineering concepts and theories related to water, wastewater, and stormwater management. You will need to have excellent technical aptitude and be familiar with various software tools such as CAD, AutoCAD, Revit, HEC-RAS, HEC-HMS, SWMM, EPANET, and Modflow, which are beneficial for project work. You will need to be skilled in evaluating, planning, designing, and supporting the management of projects involving water treatment, wastewater treatment, and stormwater conveyance including pipelines and pumping facilities. Additionally, you will need to provide valuable support in project management efforts including managing project scopes, budgets, and client deliverables. As part of our team, you will engage in the full cycle of sustainability and resilience project management, from assessment and development to ongoing support. You will exercise judgement when working on engineering tasks, including making critical decisions on project details and selecting suitable engineering solutions. Fieldwork duties are also crucial, involving activities like site visits, water quality analysis, construction inspection, sampling, water quality analyses, flow monitoring set-up, and monitoring technology evaluations, plant operations information, process troubleshooting, and optimization. Additionally, you will support asset management projects by conducting data analytics, performance evaluations, and assessments to optimize performance of water/wastewater/stormwater facilities. Your work will also include preparing various reports and materials, participating in client meetings, and utilizing digital tools to boost collaboration and enhance project delivery such as SharePoint, BIM, PowerBI, and Augmented Reality, as well as designing and managing databases and cloud-based computing services. **Qualifications & Experience:** Required Qualifications: - A Bachelor’s degree in Civil or Environmental Engineering (or a closely related engineering discipline) Preferred Qualifications: - Prior work/internship experience at a design or consulting engineering firm or municipal work environment. - Familiarity/ experience with CAD, AutoCAD, Revit. # Solutions Engineer Intern - Summer 2027 [Relay](https://relaypro.com/) is a growth-stage tech company in Raleigh, NC, building the System of Action for Physical Operations. Frontline teams catch problems all day and say so over the radio. Almost none of it survives the shift. Relay captures it and turns it into action, through a rugged smart radio that works the way teams already do and a cloud platform that learns the operation, routes issues to the right people, and stays open until they're resolved. Fifteen years innovating in voice, 2 billion messages, 40+ Fortune 500 customers. Now we're expanding our Solutions Engineering team by hiring an SE intern with an **expected graduation date in December 2027 or Spring 2028 to support technical pre-sales and solution delivery**. ### Role Overview As a Solutions Engineer Intern, you will learn how technical expertise, customer discovery, and creative problem-solving come together during the sales process. Working alongside experienced Solutions Engineers and cross-functional partners, you will help understand customer workflows, configure and test Relay solutions, support product demonstrations and proofs of concept, and create technical resources that make our team more effective. This internship is designed for a college student pursuing engineering, computer science, information systems, data science, or another applicable technical field. You will receive mentorship, structured learning opportunities, and ownership of meaningful work—without being expected to independently lead enterprise technical sales cycles. ### What Makes Our Intern Program Different: - Executive exposure through Q&A sessions, coffee chats, and working sessions with senior leaders. - A cross-functional intern cohort with opportunities to learn alongside interns across the business. - Structured learning sessions covering product strategy, professional networking, communication, interviewing, and other career-building skills. - Real ownership of a meaningful project, supported by mentors and teammates invested in your success. - An end-of-summer intern showcase where you can present your work to the company. - An in-person Raleigh HQ experience with team lunches, volunteer opportunities, social events, and access to onsite amenities. ### What you will do: - **Learn Customer Discovery and Solution Design** - Shadow customer discovery sessions and help document operational pain points, workflows, and technical requirements. - Partner with Solutions Engineers to translate customer needs into practical Relay configurations and solution diagrams. - Learn how Relay’s platform, APIs, integrations, and device capabilities support frontline operations - **Support Demos and Proofs of Concept** - Research and organize technical information that supports customer questions, security reviews, RFIs/RFPs, and IT architecture discussions. - Practice explaining technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. - **Create Documentation and Enablement** - Document solution configurations, architecture decisions, API usage, testing results, and implementation considerations. - Create reusable assets such as diagrams, one-pagers, demo guides, checklists, and troubleshooting resources. - Help prepare clear handoff materials for Customer Success and Implementation teams. - **Complete an Intern Project** - Own a scoped summer project that improves a Solutions Engineering process, demo, prototype, integration, or enablement resource. - Present your work, findings, and recommendations to Solutions Engineering leaders and cross-functional partners at the end of the internship ### What You Will Bring: #### Required Qualifications: - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in engineering, computer science, information systems, data science, or another applicable technical field. - Expected **graduation date of December 2027 or Spring 2028**. - A strong academic record; a cumulative GPA of 3.5 or above is preferred. - Relevant technical experience gained through coursework, labs, research, internships, student organizations, hackathons, or personal projects. - Foundational understanding of software, systems, networking, cloud technology, data, or connected devices—and an eagerness to deepen that knowledge. - Some familiarity with APIs, JSON, scripting, or application integrations through coursework or projects; deep professional experience is not required. - Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to ask thoughtful questions and explain ideas clearly. - Curiosity about customer problems and enthusiasm for learning how technology can improve real-world operations. - A collaborative, dependable approach and comfort receiving feedback, iterating, and learning from others. - Ability to work full-time onsite at Relay’s Raleigh, NC headquarters for the duration of the summer internship. #### Nice to Have: - Exposure to technical presentations, demonstrations, consulting, sales engineering, customer service,or other customer-facing work. - Experience with REST APIs, Postman, Python, JavaScript, data visualization, networking, or cloud platforms. - Interest in frontline operations, manufacturing, logistics, hospitality, industrial technology, IoT, or automation. - Experience building or explaining a technical project to an audience through a class, club, competition, internship, or personal project. #### We use AI tools to transcribe and summarize interviews for internal hiring purposes. Transcripts are accessible only to authorized hiring personnel and retained consistent with our data retention policies. Candidates who prefer not to have AI notetaking used may request to opt out without impact to your candidacy. For more information, please see our Candidate and Employee Privacy Notice [linked here.](https://relaypro.com/legal/candidate-privacy-notice/)

RESPONSIBILITIES Assist in the overall leadership of the campus, ensuring all worship experiences are executed with excellence in an effort to make our guests feel seen and known. description: Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us! Figma’s Data Science team partners across product, engineering, design, marketing, sales, and operations to help Figma make better decisions with data. As a PhD Data Science Intern, you’ll bring rigorous research training to some of Figma’s most important and open-ended questions, from researching emerging product and user behaviors and Figma’s broader ecosystem to developing new measurement methodologies, applying causal inference or machine learning, and building analytical systems. You’ll own a data science project end-to-end: from framing the question and methodology to translating findings into insights that influence Figma’s products, strategy, or data science practices; with the potential to continue toward publication after the internship. ### About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. ### **About the Flight Test Engineering Team** Zipline’s **Flight Test Engineering** team is a specialized group that designs flight test courses and methods to support our overall system validation progress. This involves developing custom flight control software for complex maneuvers and collaborating with development engineers to design rigorous tests for all critical edge cases. We leverage expertise in system design, statistics, flight physics, and sound experimental methods to ensure our flight tests are effective and safe. The team partners closely with Controls and Dynamics, Embedded Software, Autonomy, Systems Engineering, Powertrain, Structure, and Flight Operations teams to build comprehensive test plans and test cards. Our work spans simulation, hardware testing, data-driven analysis, and system-level evaluations that support deployments across the globe. As an intern, you’ll collaborate with engineers across these domains, gaining hands-on exposure to how industry-leading autonomous systems are designed, tested, and validated at scale. ### **The Role** As a Flight Test Engineering Intern, you will be instrumental in analyzing flight test data logs to determine test effectiveness, identify success/failure root causes, and track performance trends. You will also directly contribute to the design of new flight test campaigns, collaborating with other engineers to define the test scope, test method, and data post-processing. This is a unique opportunity for someone excited to learn how complex robotic systems are validated, who enjoys problem-solving, and who wants to build real-world experience working with autonomy software, data analysis, and systems engineering. ### **What You'll Do** - Analyze flight test data logs using custom scripts (Python, DataBricks, SQL) to identify anomalies, assess reliability, track performance trends, and perform regression analyses. - Design, oversee the execution, and review the results of software validation and flight test campaigns to ensure new features perform as intended and prevent hardware/software regression. - Daily test and monitor the develop branch to quickly surface instability and potential future issues. - Collaborate with cross-functional partners (GNC, Aerodynamics, Structures, Systems Engineering) to ensure system-level requirements (e.g., acceleration, range, climb rate) are clear, measurable, and that vehicle changes are mature for flight testing. - Define or develop novel test infrastructure, including application-based tools to support flight testing, new instrumentation systems (e.g., load cells, vision systems). or modified flight control software, to collect auxiliary data in flight. - Establish and maintain documentation, dashboards, and SQL search queries to track test progress and operational efficiency. - Be ready to directly own any aspect of flight operations (preflight, launch, flight maneuvers, incident reporting) or supervise these activities with the flight operations team. ### **What You'll Bring** - You must have completed the second year of your undergraduate studies in physics, mathematics, mechanical, aerospace, system engineering, computer science, electrical engineering or related fields. Masters and PhD students are also eligible. - Strong mathematical and physics background. - Experience in autonomous vehicle/ robotic system integration and testing work. - Experience in data process, visualization. - Strong written and verbal communication skills. ### **What Else You Should Know** *This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January to April/May.* *The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements*Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Recognized as a Glassdoor Top 100 Best Place to Work, we offer a collaborative and caring community where you feel like you belong and are empowered to grow, learn and thrive through hands-on experience, certifications, industry training and more. **About the APX Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) Program:** APX (Advanced Partnership Accelerator) is a Center of Excellence under AFS’ Data & AI capability. The APX Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) Program represents a strategic initiative to position Accenture Federal Services at the forefront of artificial intelligence innovation in government. This program embeds top technical talent directly with federal clients to fast track the adoption and implementation of advanced technologies from Palantir, Databricks, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and cutting edge AI partners. You'll work hands-on with the most advanced AI models available, translating their transformative potential into tangible value for defense, intelligence, civilian, and public health missions. They need embedded engineers who move with urgency, autonomy, and precision while being able to reach back to broader support across AFS. As a Junior FDE, you will work at the intersection of engineering, product thinking and client delivery, helping technical teams move from ambiguous client problems, to working proof-of-concept, to production-grade deployment in a matter of weeks. In this role you will: - Embed within client environments as part of a forward deployed engineering (FDE) team to build rapid prototypes using AI tools, coding assistants, and modern frameworks - Use AI tools (LLMs, coding assistants, agentic frameworks) as part of daily development work - Support integration of solutions into complex client environments, including legacy systems and regulated data contexts - Work across the tech stack (frontend, backend, APIs, simple data pipelines) and help develop applications and workflows that use structured and unstructured enterprise data - Assist in evaluating model outputs, testing workflows, and applying responsible AI guardrails - Implement AI solutions such as RAG workflows, semantic search, prompt engineering patterns, and simple agent behaviors - Work with senior FDEs to clarify problem statements and translate them into technical plans - Participate in rapid experimentation cycles and incorporate user feedback into updates, documenting solution decisions and contributing to internal learning assets - Leverage technical expertise to help clients navigate the rapidly evolving technological landscape, serving as a trusted advisor on emerging AI capabilities, increasing user adoption and scaling mission impact - Share observations, user friction points, reusable assets and field intelligence back to APX teams to improve delivery approaches **What You Bring:** - **Mission-first Mindset & Relentless Problem Solving:** You move fast because the mission can’t wait. You make smart bets in ambiguous terrain, taking ownership early and giving every challenge your full drive before ever considering stepping back. You push through ambiguity, communicate risks and trade-offs, investigate solutions independently to forge the future, and maintain momentum even when the path forward is unclear. - **Grit & Tenacity to Engineer at the Edge**: You remain steady when projects get messy and keep pushing forward through rapid experimentation cycles. You show up confidently in client working sessions, support senior FDEs at the mission edge, adapt in real time, and help teams operate decisively even in uncertainty. - **Bias for Building:** You iterate quickly, communicate plainly across technical and non-technical teammates, ask sharp questions, and summarize decisions in a way that moves teams forward with confidence and alignment. You build work that adds value for our clients, making bold ideas happen fast. - **Limitless Curiosity & Frontier Learning:** You learn rapidly across a wide, rapidly changing technical frontier, from LLMs and agent frameworks to cloud platforms and enterprise AI ecosystems. You approach new tools with curiosity, adaptability, and velocity, and you prefer building and testing over long specification cycles. **Here’s What You Need:** - Bachelor’s Degree or demonstrated hands-on coding experience building and shipping software projects - Proficiency in at least one modern programming language (e.g., Python, R, Rust) with knowledge of building production services - Familiarity with Generative AI (LLMs, chatbots, or AI-powered apps) and eagerness to learn how model outputs influence product workflows - Exposure working with APIs and simple data flows, managing structured and unstructured data and ensure data quality. - Ability to travel, dependent on client and team - Must be a U.S. Citizen and ability to obtain a federal security clearance **Bonus Points if You Have:** - Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Economics, Statistics, or a related technical field - Experience with Palantir, Databricks, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or other emerging technology platforms - Prior client experience or collaborative technical work (consulting internships, hackathons, customer success engineering, or team-based builds) - Exposure to cloud services (AWS, Azure, GCP) from coursework, certificates, internships, or individual projects - Experience integrating or deploying code in environments with constraints (legacy systems, governance, access controls) - Demonstrated ability to take a small idea from zero-to-prototype independently

role: Dean of Students, Academy of Math and Programming (AMP)
location: New York, New York, United States
description: ### About the Position We are looking for an experienced school leader to serve as Dean of Students for our Academy of Math and Programming (AMP) in New York City. AMP is a residential program for recent high school graduates of diverse backgrounds who have experienced barriers to access and opportunity within advanced STEM education. Students spend five weeks studying mathematics, computer programming, data analysis, and game theory while building a close academic and residential community. As Dean of Students, you will support the program's academic culture and help students meet our clear expectations for attendance, participation, classroom behavior, and academic integrity. To do this successfully, you’ll have to partner closely with instructors and teaching assistants, the program director, guidance counselors, and residential director to make sure students receive consistent support. Before the on-site program begins, you will partner with Jane Street’s AMP leads on program preparation, including helping develop the code of conduct. During the program, you will be on site from 9am to 5pm, Monday through Friday, while classes are in session. Additional responsibilities will include: - Consistently applying the program's code of conduct during the academic day and helping students address concerns related to attendance, engagement, academic integrity, and classroom behavior in a constructive and developmentally appropriate way - Meeting regularly with instructors and teaching assistants to understand classroom dynamics and identify students who may need additional support - Visiting classes periodically to observe student participation and the learning environment - Meeting regularly with Jane Street’s AMP leads to align on program values and student expectations, discuss student concerns, and agree on key decisions This is a temporary, full-time summer position. The 2027 program will run from the end of June through the beginning of August. Jane Street deeply values the quality of our educational programming, and we compensate our high-caliber staff accordingly. Travel, housing (if requested), and meals will be provided. ### About You - Have leadership or school administration experience in a middle or high school, summer program, or similar educational setting - Experienced with supporting student conduct and academic expectations with sound judgment, empathy, and consistency - A clear, collaborative communicator; comfortable giving direct feedback to students and staff - Have strong observational and organizational skills, including the ability to notice patterns and follow up promptly - Able to handle sensitive student matters discreetly and escalate concerns appropriately *If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to* *agency-partnerships@janestreet.com**.*

description: About the role At Rippling, Engineering is at the heart of our business and culture. We believe in our early talent’s potential, experience and aspirations. Our mission is to open the realm of possibilities and opportunities for students by fostering growth through mentorship and training, ownership through impactful and innovative projects, and, of course, fun through our diverse culture and work hard, play harder attitude. As an Engineering Intern, you will join one of our many teams in Summer 2027 (May/June-August/September) to develop robust, well-designed products, implement new updates and features, and solve complex problems that affect our business and our clients. Rippling Interns gain the experience of full-time engineers with responsibilities, ownership, and opportunity. Interns will be assigned projects that not only have an impact on the business, but that are also scoped to fit within the time constraints of their internship so they can see the full impact of their work. We provide our interns exciting and innovative projects to work on that allow them to see the fruition of their work. During your 13 weeks at Rippling, we will provide all of the tools needed to be successful. Your dedicated mentor and manager will provide support for your learning and development throughout your time with us. You will join your fellow interns in a variety of socials, talks with Rippling leaders, and more! Our goal is to identify exceptional emerging engineers who can continue their careers at Rippling after graduation, growing into full-time contributors on our team. Note that this is a full stack software internship role! This means you will be working in the front end and the back end. The NNSS Science & Technology Directorate invites exceptional early ‑ career scientists to apply for the Bruno Rossi Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship. The Rossi Fellow will drive advances in the theory, computational modeling, and/or machine ‑ learning applications to the Scorpius linear induction accelerator (LIA) - one of the Nation’s flagship capabilities supporting NNSA missions. This is a high ‑ impact, publication ‑ friendly role embedded with a senior NNSS mentor and collaborating laboratories. Fellowship Focus Areas (Theory/Computation/ML) We are seeking exceptional early-career PhD scientists or engineers with expertise in accelerator physics and a passion for applying data science, artificial intelligence (AI), and machine learning (ML) to model, control, and optimize complex systems. We also welcome applicants with a strong background in computational science who are eager to apply their skills to challenges in accelerator science. In particular, fellows will be fully supported to lead a research program focused on one or more of the following areas. A. Accelerator & Beam Physics (Theory/Computation) · Relativistic Beam–Target Interaction Physics: Investigating beam interactions with complex bremsstrahlung converters, including X-ray source modeling, dose and fluence optimization, and converter survivability under advanced material responses. · Beam Transport in Complex Environments: Studying beam transport in solenoidal and induction systems, with emphasis on emittance preservation, halo formation and mitigation, and energy spread control under realistic operating conditions. · Collective Effects and Instabilities: Developing models and mitigation strategies for phenomena such as Beam Breakup (BBU), corkscrew motion, and transverse/longitudinal impedance-driven instabilities. Pulsed-Power and Accelerator Coupling: Exploring circuit-beam co-simulation, magnet and induction module dynamics, and timing and waveform shaping to enhance stability and brightness. Diagnostics by Design: Creating inference methods and synthetic diagnostics to extract critical machine parameters—such as emittance, current, energy, spot size, and centroid motion—from limited data, while incorporating uncertainty quantification and error budgets for machine studies. · Multiphysics Target Response: Modeling the Magneto-Hydrodynamics (MHD) and thermomechanics of converter materials under intense pulsed loading, including shock and thermal fatigue, to evaluate lifetime and performance trade-offs. Representative tools and methods: Particle-In-Cell (PIC) and Vlasov–Fokker–Planck simulations, hybrid PIC–fluid models, envelope and moment techniques, Monte Carlo radiation transport, surrogate modeling, adjoint and gradient ‑ based optimization, as well as rigorous uncertainty quantification (UQ) and sensitivity analysis. B. Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, and Digital Twin Foundations for the Scorpius Accelerator · Data-Driven Machine Tuning: Optimizing accelerator performance by leveraging cutting-edge methods to rapidly identify optimal set points and compensate for beam drifting across multiple shots and variable thermal states. Predictive Maintenance and Anomaly Detection: Applying time-series modeling to pulsed-power components and beam diagnostics for fault prediction, remaining useful life estimation, and automated alert systems. Physics-Constrained Machine Learning: Implementing novel neural network architectures and reduced-order modeling techniques, constrained by first-principles physics, to deliver fast and explainable predictions. Uncertainty-Aware Control: Developing decision-making frameworks with calibrated posteriors to ensure safe operation, while building digital twin architectures and data pipelines that integrate simulation, controls, and diagnostics in near-real time. Successful applicants will be expected to demonstrate a sophisticated understanding of these methodologies. This includes a meticulous selection of appropriate techniques, awareness of their inherent limitations. Impact This fellowship offers a distinguished opportunity to drive transformative innovation at the forefront of accelerator science. The Rossi Fellow will be instrumental in developing and demonstrating next-generation capabilities for the Scorpius accelerator and allied radiographic systems. This foundational work is critical for achieving enhanced brightness, stability, system responsiveness, and long-term reliability, directly reinforcing the strategic imperatives of NNSA’s stockpile stewardship mission. The Fellow's research will provide a definitive basis for optimizing machine studies, informing strategic hardware development, and accelerating the realization of the full Scorpius digital twin Application Materials Please combine materials into a single PDF when possible: Curriculum Vitae (with education, publications, software contributions, and up to three references to key codes or datasets). Research Statement ( ≤ 3 pages): proposed 2–3 projects aligned to Focus Areas; include methods, anticipated milestones, and potential collaborators. Selected Publications or preprints demonstrating relevant expertise. References: contact information for 3–5 referees. (Letters may be requested at the shortlist stage.) Interviews: Finalists will be invited for a two ‑ day on ‑ site interview, including a technical seminar on current work and proposed research. How to Apply & Key Dates: Deadline for full consideration: October 31 , 2026, 11:59 PM Pacific Time Interviews: November-December 2026 Decisions: January 2027 Start date: 2027 (flexible) Compensation & Support Annual salary: $130,000 Research support: Up to $250,000 across the term for R&D expenses as described above, allocated annually with NNSS mentor and program approval. D iscretionary research support across the fellowship for hardware, software, data/storage, user facility access, travel, and—subject to policy and need—the ability to fund a graduate student or research associate. Term & Support - Term : Up to 3 years (initial 2 ‑ year appointment with a 3rd ‑ year extension based on performance and program needs). - Mentorship & Visibility : Dedicated NNSS mentor; opportunities to present to NNSS/NNSA leadership and partner labs (LANL, LLNL) and to publish in peer ‑ reviewed venues consistent with program requirements. About the Fellowship & Namesake The fellowship honors Bruno Benedetto Rossi (1905–1993), a trailblazing experimental and theoretical physicist whose career helped shape modern particle physics, space plasma physics, and x-ray astronomy. Trained at the University of Bologna, and having collaborated with Niels Bohr in Denmark, Patrick Blackett at the University of Manchester, and Enrico Fermi at the University of Chicago, Rossi later became a professor at MIT. There, he pioneered the electronic coincidence method, which enabled unambiguous detection of rare, fast events and opened the door to modern high-energy instrumentation. His early work established the charged nature of cosmic rays , mapped their latitude/altitude effects, and revealed extensive air showers produced by ultra-high-energy primaries. During the Manhattan Project, Rossi led diagnostic development at Los Alamos, including fast ionization chambers and timing methods crucial to understanding implosion dynamics. After the war, he founded the renowned MIT Cosmic Ray Group, which evolved into the Center for Space Research. Rossi’s group instrumented early space missions that characterized the solar wind, and he championed the first detections that launched x-ray astronomy, demonstrating that the universe is bright in high-energy photons. The Rossi Fellow carries forward this legacy: rigorous physics, elegant instrumentation by model and algorithm, and science in service to national missions. role: International Student Advisor, International Programs Office (2926)
description: Job Description The successful candidate will serve as an immigration advisor to international students and serves as a Designated School Official (DSO). Completes immigration paperwork as well as issue, file and monitor immigration documents and applications. Responsible for updating student records in the federal government SEVIS system using ISSM for batch submissions to the SEVIS database; ensures the university’s continuing compliance with SEVIS reporting requirements and other federal reporting requirements. This position is not eligible for new visa sponsorship at this time. Candidates who already hold valid U.S. work authorization may be considered. Key Responsibilities • Serve as an advisor, advising and assisting international students regarding F-1 and J-1 immigration requirements, and prepare appropriate federal documents for work authorization and visa related requests. Advises students on the U.S. immigration, laws, and regulations that impact their enrollment and continued stay in the United States. Process I-20 and DS-2019 applications for new and continuing international students and ensure applications materials meet the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) requirements. Advise students on how to maintain enrollment status as per immigration regulations, and assist students in filing applications with DHS. Verify student enrollment, enters/updates immigration information to student database (ISSM). Maintains I-20 and DS-2019 forms and documentations used by the International Programs Office to assist students with applications and immigration issues. • Stay informed of current immigration regulations and requirements and maintains professional knowledge of international regulatory policies affecting Idaho State University students and community. Functions as a Designated School Official (DSO) and Alternate Responsible Officer (ARO) for the university’s F and J programs. • Represents the office at various meetings and serve on inter-office committees or teams in collaborative efforts as required. Advise international student organizations. Plans and delivers various workshops throughout the year. Coordinates cultural and social events and services to assist new students upon their arrival to Pocatello and Idaho State University. Assist with coordination of international student orientation for each semester. • Tracks students’ admission and the whereabouts of former international students. Tracks and report enrollment numbers and all other international student data each semester. • Other duties as assigned, maintains confidentiality as appropriate.

**About Nominal** Nominal is building the connected test and operations platform powering the world's most advanced hardware systems, from spacecraft and autonomous vehicles to next-generation defense programs. Our platform gives hardware engineering teams a single place to ingest data, analyze performance, automate test execution, and collaborate across every phase of development, so they can move faster without sacrificing safety or precision. We're a fast-moving team that owns problems end-to-end, works across disciplines, and thrives at the intersection of hardware and software. We serve top-tier commercial and defense customers, from autonomy leaders like Anduril and Shield AI to next-generation aerospace teams like Hermeus and REGENT, and performance engineering teams like Pratt Miller Motorsports, alongside mission partners within the U.S. Navy and U.S. Air Force on programs where failure isn’t an option. We’re backed by Sequoia, General Catalyst, Founders Fund, Lux Capital, and Lightspeed. Our team draws from SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril, Applied Intuition, and other leading companies, united by a common mission: giving hardware engineers the tools to build the future with speed, safety, and confidence. **The role** We’re looking for students with solid engineering fundamentals on track to graduate in Summer 2027 or sooner. As a Mission Dev (forward deployed software engineering) engineer at Nominal, you’ll work directly with engineers building and testing complex hardware systems like nuclear reactors, rockets, and supersonic aircraft. You’ll learn how our customers work, understand what’s slowing them down, and build software that helps them move faster. The role combines hands-on software engineering with product judgment: figuring out what to build, shipping it, and working with users to make sure it solves their problem. ### ### ### 🚀 What you’ll do - Work directly with customer engineers to understand their testing and analysis workflows and identify problems you can solve with software - Design and build integrations, data pipelines, and applications that connect Nominal to our customers’ systems and help them work with high-frequency, high-volume hardware data - Own projects from understanding the problem through building, deploying, and supporting the solution, with mentorship from experienced engineers and domain experts - Put working software in users’ hands early, learn from how they use it, and iterate quickly based on their feedback - Bring what you learn back to our product and engineering teams, helping turn solutions for individual customers into capabilities that benefit many ### ### ### 🎯 Reach out if… - You’re graduating in Summer 2027 or sooner and are interested in a full-time position. - You have strong core engineering skills and hands-on experience building software, whether through internships, personal projects, or academic work - You want to work directly with the people using your software and understand whether what you’ve built is making a difference - You’re excited to work through open-ended problems, learn unfamiliar systems, and figure out what’s needed to get a solution into use - You have a personal passion for solving challenging problems and contributing to the future of critical infrastructure - Your peers would describe you as ambitious, resourceful, and perseverant ### ### ### ✨ Benefits/Perks - 100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision insurance - Unlimited PTO and sick leave - Free lunch, snacks, and coffee - Professional Development Stipend - 401k Plan - In-office hardware lab with a $250 project stipend - Annual company retreat *All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin.* ITAR Requirements *To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. ## **About Base** Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time. ## **About the Role** As a growth intern, you’ll join our Go-To-Market (GTM) team, gaining practical experience in sales, marketing, and customer support. **What You'll Do** - Help execute go-to-market strategies to improve customer acquisition. - Build and maintain relationships with customers, ensuring a positive customer experience. - Analyze customer interactions using HubSpot and other tools. - Work with the sales team to meet targets and improve the process. - Research target segments and generate outbound leads. - Help launch marketing campaigns to generate inbound leads. ## **What You'll Bring** - Interest in customers, sales, and relationship building. - Understanding of technology sales and software products. - Strong communication skills in English, both verbal and written. - Ability to provide good customer service and build rapport with clients. ## **Preferred Skills** - Familiarity with HubSpot (or other CRM systems) and Zapier. - Relevant experience. ## **About the Team** The Growth team sets the pace for how fast Base can deliver affordable, reliable power to the people who need it.
