This includes owning the full research-to-production lifecycle and ensuring rapid deployment of your work in live systems. - **Model Alignment & Data Strategy**: Partner with the world's most advanced AI research teams to design, engineer, and iterate on high-impact datasets and large-scale benchmarking efforts that shape how frontier models behave, specifically focusing on critical alignment, safety, and defining optimal reward signals. - **Autonomous Problem Selection**: Autonomously identify, scope, and manage long-running research projects, choosing the most impactful problems that are critical to scaling data for AGI/ASI. - **System Infrastructure**: Collaborate closely with engineering teams on data pipelines, internal tooling, and high-performance deep learning algorithm implementations. # **WHO YOU ARE** - **Exceptional Research Depth & Strategic Vision**: Research expertise in a related field (e.g., CS, ML, NLP) ideally with that work published at a major conference (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR). You must possess the velocity to master complex fields and a proven track record in the productization of research, encompassing high-stakes evaluation, large-scale benchmarking, and product feature development. - Proven experience shipping research directly to production and live systems, specifically focusing on advanced post-training, distillation, and high-stakes evaluation methodologies. - Large-scale agent systems: orchestration frameworks, tool APIs, distributed execution, observability, and logging infrastructure. - **Strategic & Ethical Leadership**: You possess a thoughtful, strategic perspective on the societal and safety impacts of deploying general-purpose AI systems. Experience advising on or shaping governmental policy related to AI safety and governance (e.g., House of Lords or Online Safety Bill initiatives) is required. # **COMPENSATION** **Base Salary** $10,000/month **Benefits** Health, dental, vision + flexible PTO

Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. role: KIP Spring 2027 - Strategic Research Intern - Pacific Legal Foundation
description: **[The Koch Internship Program](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/koch-internship-program/) (KIP)** is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Early-career professionals including undergraduate/graduate/law students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the [admissions process](https://standtogetherfellowships.org/application-process/) early! ### **General Information** Pacific Legal Foundation identifies and litigates important legal issues to set landmark precedents that benefit Americans nationwide. Using strategic and principled litigation, communications, and research, PLF battles for freedom in the nation’s courts and the court of public opinion. As a national nonprofit organization, PLF has brick-and-mortar offices in Sacramento, California; Arlington, Virginia; and Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, although approximately half of the staff work from home offices across the country. **Interns work remotely by default, but they can request to work physically in any of PLF’s offices. This is a part-time role.** **You:** An inquisitive, creative, and self-motivated college junior, senior, grad student, or recent graduate who knows the principles of liberty and seeks to advance them. You have strong written and oral communication skills and enjoy problem solving. **Them:** Bureaucrats, city councils, mayors, governors, and federal agencies stripping Americans of their rights every day. There’s a lot of government overreach out there, and it’s backed by seemingly endless resources. **Us:** We fight back. [Pacific Legal Foundation (PLF)](https://pacificlegal.org/) is the nation’s first and most successful public interest law firm dedicated to vindicating individual liberty. PLF has an unmatched record in the US Supreme Court, with 18 victories out of 20 cases heard by the Court. PLF also has nearly 200 active cases across the nation. At PLF, we aren’t interested in doing the same thing as everyone else. We aspire to be the best player in a constantly changing game. The Strategic Research intern will be a member of the Strategic Research team. This team produces high-quality social science research to support PLF’s mission-driven goals. The team coordinates with PLF’s Litigation, Legal Policy, Constitutional Scholarship, and Communications teams. This internship is an opportunity for a wide variety of experiences, including the following: · Communicating with public officials to obtain public records. · Collecting, organizing, and analyzing data using Microsoft Excel, R, Python, GIS, or Stata. · Conducting literature reviews on such topics as regulatory reform, housing supply, property rights, coastal land rights, and more. · Developing internal data for litigation, communications, or legal policy campaigns. · Writing blog posts, op-eds, or one-pagers on topics relevant to PLF’s work. ### How to Apply **If you think you might be a good fit, submit the following application materials in ONE PDF when you upload your** **résumé that includes relevant experience in the liberty movement and professional skills:** · A cover letter explaining why PLF is the place for you, why you want to fight for liberty, and what distinguishes you from typical applicants. · A writing sample. · A semester schedule (if taking classes during the internship period).

Immuta is the Data Authorization Company, helping the world’s largest organizations control who, and what, can access their data. The way enterprises access data is fundamentally changing. Organizations are racing to put data to work across analytics and AI, while AI copilots and agents are emerging as an entirely new class of data consumer. Traditional approaches built around tickets, static permissions, and manual approvals were not designed for this speed, scale, or complexity. Immuta provides the authorization layer for modern data and AI. Our platform enables organizations to provision governed access to data by policy, by request, and dynamically for AI agents, so people and AI can access the data they need while enterprises maintain security, compliance, and control. For Chief Data Officers, that means making enterprise data dramatically easier to access and use without giving up governance. For AI leaders, it means giving AI agents secure, governed access to enterprise data so they can move from experimentation into production. Founded in 2015, Immuta is trusted by Fortune 500 companies and government agencies worldwide. - Our technology ecosystem includes Snowflake, Databricks, AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Okta, ServiceNow, Teradata, Alation, Atlan, and Starburst — connecting Immuta to the data, cloud, identity, and enterprise platforms powering modern data and AI environments. - Immuta has been recognized by Forbes as a top American startup employer, by Inc. Magazine and Built In as one of the best workplaces, and by Fast Company as one of the world’s most innovative companies. - Immuta has raised $263 million from investors including NightDragon, Snowflake, Databricks, ServiceNow, Citi Ventures, Dell Technologies Capital, DFJ Growth, IAG, Intel Capital, March Capital, Okta Ventures, StepStone, Ten Eleven Ventures, and Wipro Ventures. - We operate as a hybrid workplace with offices in Boston, MA; Columbus, OH; and College Park, MD. ## **ABOUT THE TEAM** The Product Research team sits at the intersection of theoretical computer science, applied mathematics, statistics, machine learning, and software engineering. The team turns research and algorithms into practical product capabilities that help organizations use data safely and effectively. As a Product Research Intern, you’ll work with research scientists and collaborate with software engineers and other teammates. You’ll help explore how ideas developed in a controlled research setting can be tested, adapted, and applied in the messy, real-world environments where customers use Immuta. The work is research-oriented: you’ll go deep on a problem, understand how an approach works, and help move it from an idea into something practical. ## **YOUR INTERNSHIP** At Immuta, interns are treated like members of the team. You’ll join the team’s regular workflow, contribute to real work, and take on responsibilities that reflect your skills and the team’s priorities. The exact projects will depend on what the team is working on next summer, but you can expect to: - Explore a set of potential research and product projects, then spend meaningful time developing one project related to the team’s work. - Work with research scientists to investigate approaches that could support Immuta product capabilities. - Translate mathematical, statistical, or computational ideas into prototypes, experiments, and functional software. - Apply research methods to practical problems involving data privacy, security, governance, machine learning, algorithms, or text analytics. - Evaluate approaches using data, experiments, measurements, and clear reasoning. - Collaborate with researchers, engineers, product teammates, and others to understand how research can become useful product work. - Communicate your process and findings through documentation, reports, presentations, and conversations with teammates. ## **TOOLS & TECHNOLOGIES** Depending on your role, you may work with: - Python - TypeScript - SQL and databases - Algorithms, statistics, and machine learning methods - Text analytics and classification approaches - APIs and application development workflows - Data analysis, experimentation, and measurement - AI-enabled tools and workflows used by your team You do not need to know every tool listed above. We’re looking for a strong foundation, curiosity, and the ability to learn. ## **WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR** - A strong foundation in computer science, mathematics, statistics, machine learning, or another quantitative field. - Experience with research, a substantial independent project, or working with a professor is a plus. - Programming experience and interest in applying technical skills to data and research problems. - Strong communication skills and the ability to explain your work clearly. - Curiosity, initiative, and interest in turning research into practical solutions.

description: Immuta is the Data Authorization Company, helping the world’s largest organizations control who, and what, can access their data. The way enterprises access data is fundamentally changing. Organizations are racing to put data to work across analytics and AI, while AI copilots and agents are emerging as an entirely new class of data consumer. Traditional approaches built around tickets, static permissions, and manual approvals were not designed for this speed, scale, or complexity. Immuta provides the authorization layer for modern data and AI. Our platform enables organizations to provision governed access to data by policy, by request, and dynamically for AI agents, so people and AI can access the data they need while enterprises maintain security, compliance, and control. For Chief Data Officers, that means making enterprise data dramatically easier to access and use without giving up governance. For AI leaders, it means giving AI agents secure, governed access to enterprise data so they can move from experimentation into production. Founded in 2015, Immuta is trusted by Fortune 500 companies and government agencies worldwide. - Our technology ecosystem includes Snowflake, Databricks, AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Okta, ServiceNow, Teradata, Alation, Atlan, and Starburst — connecting Immuta to the data, cloud, identity, and enterprise platforms powering modern data and AI environments. - Immuta has been recognized by Forbes as a top American startup employer, by Inc. Magazine and Built In as one of the best workplaces, and by Fast Company as one of the world’s most innovative companies. - Immuta has raised $263 million from investors including NightDragon, Snowflake, Databricks, ServiceNow, Citi Ventures, Dell Technologies Capital, DFJ Growth, IAG, Intel Capital, March Capital, Okta Ventures, StepStone, Ten Eleven Ventures, and Wipro Ventures. - We operate as a hybrid workplace with offices in Boston, MA; Columbus, OH; and College Park, MD. ## **ABOUT THE TEAM** UX Design at Immuta helps make complex data access and governance workflows easier to understand and use. The team brings together design, research, and engineering to understand user problems, explore solutions, and turn them into clear, usable product experiences. As a UX Design Intern, you’ll work with UX designers and collaborate with product and engineering teammates. You’ll help connect customer needs to what the product actually does and learn how a product team moves from understanding a problem to designing and prototyping a solution. ## **YOUR INTERNSHIP** At Immuta, interns are treated like members of the team. You’ll join the team’s regular workflow, contribute to real work, and take on responsibilities that reflect your skills and the team’s priorities. The exact projects will depend on what the team is working on next summer, but you can expect to: - Explore user and customer problems through research, conversations, workshops, and other discovery activities. - Turn research and product insights into concepts, user flows, mockups, and prototypes. - Use design tools to communicate ideas, explain design decisions, and gather feedback. - Work with engineers and product teammates to understand constraints and shape solutions that can work in the real product. - Participate in activities such as storyboarding, journey mapping, user interviews, and portfolio or design critiques. - Use front-end skills, where relevant, to prototype, test, or communicate how an experience could work across responsive and mobile interfaces. - Share your work, explain your thinking, incorporate feedback, and build confidence working across design, research, and engineering. ## **TOOLS & TECHNOLOGIES** Depending on your role, you may work with: - Figma and similar design tools - Wireframing, mockups, and interactive prototyping - Storyboarding, journey mapping, user interviews, and other research methods - HTML and CSS - Front-end frameworks such as Angular or React - Responsive and mobile design concepts - AI-enabled tools and workflows used by your team You do not need to know every tool listed above. We’re looking for a strong foundation, curiosity, and the ability to learn. ## **WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR** - A portfolio that demonstrates your design work, prototypes, research, product thinking, or other relevant projects. - Strong ability in at least one of three areas: visual design, user research, or engineering/front-end development. Experience across two or more is a plus. - You do not need to be equally strong in all three areas. We’re interested in candidates who can demonstrate clear strength in at least one and curiosity about the others. - Curiosity about users, products, and how technology can solve real problems. - Strong communication and collaboration skills. - Initiative, willingness to learn, and comfort receiving and applying feedback.

# **Chart Your Journey at Secretariat** From a collaborative culture to teammates who will always be by your side, find a career that will grow with you. Deliver your impact at Secretariat. **ABOUT THE FIRM** Secretariat is a consulting firm that helps companies, law firms, and organizations solve complex business problems—often when there is a dispute, investigation, major project challenge, or high-stakes decision involved. At Secretariat, you’ll work on some of the most important legal, risk, and regulatory challenges facing businesses around the world. From your first day, you’ll be part of a fast-growing team of smart, curious, and driven people who enjoy solving complex problems. You’ll learn by working alongside experienced professionals and contributing to projects for leading law firms, global companies, and major institutions. Our teams collaborate across offices and disciplines, bringing energy, fresh thinking, and commitment to every client challenge. We invest in your growth through hands-on experience, mentorship, professional development, recognition, and a culture that values diverse perspectives. Start your career where your work matters. Make your impact at Secretariat. **ABOUT OUR ENGINEERING SCIENCES TEAM** As part of our growing Global Engineering Sciences team, you’ll apply what you’re learning in the classroom to real-world engineering challenges across industries such as energy, chemicals, machinery, automotive, consumer products, electronics, medical devices, and the built environment. You may help investigate why products, systems, or structures fail, support testing and analysis, and contribute to projects involving buildings, bridges, industrial facilities, and other structures that shape the world around us. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers, scientists, and consultants to learn how engineering is used to solve complex questions related to performance, safety, reliability, and design. This is a great fit for students who are curious, analytical, and excited to build practical technical and consulting skills. Secretariat is a fast-growing international expert services firm with more than 500 professionals in 20+ cities worldwide. For students and early-career professionals, we offer meaningful work from day one, mentorship from leading experts, and the chance to build valuable technical, consulting, and problem-solving skills. **RESPONSIBILITIES** In this role, you’ll build practical engineering, analytical, and consulting skills by supporting real client projects from investigation through reporting. You’ll work with experienced professionals who will help you learn how to break down complex technical questions, analyze information, and communicate your findings clearly. - Support hands-on failure investigations and learn how engineers evaluate what happened, why it happened, and how it can be explained clearly. - Compare real-world conditions with original designs, drawings, specifications, and project documents. - Assist with field inspections, site visits, laboratory testing, and other investigative activities. - Perform engineering calculations, research technical issues, and analyze data to help solve complex problems. - Review, organize, and summarize project documents, technical records, photos, test results, and other relevant information. - Help draft clear, well-supported report sections that explain technical findings in a way clients can understand. - Contribute to visuals, exhibits, and demonstratives that help tell the story of a technical issue or investigation. - Analyze technical reports prepared by others and help develop supporting, concurring, or rebuttal perspectives. - Participate in team and client communications, gaining exposure to consulting work across different industries and time zones. - Build strong working relationships with colleagues, peers, and clients while contributing to a collaborative team environment. - Use curiosity, attention to detail, and strong analytical thinking to help the team meet project milestones and deliver high-quality work. **QUALIFICATIONS** - Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Building Science/Architectural Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree candidates are also encouraged to apply. - Expected graduation date between December 2027 and August 2030. - Minimum GPA of 3.0. - Interest in pursuing PE credentials is a plus. - Curious, analytical, and eager to solve complex problems in practical, real-world settings. - Strong communication skills, including listening, writing, presenting, and explaining technical ideas clearly. - Able to learn quickly, think creatively, manage competing priorities, and ask thoughtful questions when guidance is needed. - Comfortable working both independently and as part of a collaborative team in a fast-growing consulting environment. - Proficiency with Microsoft Office, especially Excel and PowerPoint. - Willingness and ability to travel as needed. - Additional language skills are a plus. - Authorized to work in the U.S. without current or future sponsorship. ## A rewarding career above all There are a lot of fine consulting firms out there. But when everything is on the line, it takes a unique combination of skill and savvy to succeed under pressure. Our culture and people are driven by passion, pride, and performance. Passion for the clients we serve, the work we deliver, and the communities we live in. Pride in our cohesive team recognized for excellence and trusted to perform in the most challenging situations. And our track record of outstanding performance across all of our disciplines speaks for itself. [Our people](https://secretariat-intl.com/people/) are motivated to be the best in everything they do – from our approach to making the complex simple to the way we mentor our up-and-coming talent to become trusted experts early in their careers. description: ISW Internship Program Overview ISW is offering in-person, remote, and hybrid internships for Spring 2027. Instructions to apply for the scholarship are below. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) is committed to training the next generation of national security leaders through its innovative educational programs. ISW seeks motivated and experienced college students or recent graduates to join our intern team. ISW offers internships across diverse research portfolios and departments, including Russia, China, and Iran's proxy networks. ISW also offers internships in Geospatial Intelligence and Technologies, National Security and lntelligence Analysis, and our Cognitive Warfare Task Force. Why Work for ISW? ISW believes that ground realities must drive the formulation of strategy and policy. In pursuit of this principle, ISW conducts detailed open-source intelligence analysis to provide timely and accurate information on current conflicts and security threats directly to policymakers and warfighters. Interns at ISW have an unparalleled opportunity to analyze conflicts in ways that directly inform policy-makers on some of the most pressing issues facing American national security. Our interns work directly with analysts. They receive classroom education, regular leadership engagement, and a chance to work with cutting-edge technologies employed in business and the intelligence community. Interns have the opportunity to stand at the front lines of military research and policy development, tackling the latest crises in the headlines. The ISW Internship Program is one of three core education programs housed within The General David H. Petraeus Center for Emerging Leaders, launched to identify, educate, and develop the future cadre of leaders committed to America’s national security. ISW views interns as an integral component of its team. ISW has worked with interns to draft, edit, and publish their own research under the mentorship of senior analysts. It has also hired many interns onto its staff. Communications Internship: ISW’s External Relations Team offers a unique opportunity to candidates interested in learning more about non-profit communications with an eye towards national security. Interns will hone their skills supporting a variety of communications functions, including media relations and monitoring, writing and copyediting, social media monitoring and management, digital content creation, and media research. Over the course of a quarter, interns will receive guidance from ISW’s professional communications and publishing staff, gradually expanding and honing their ability to develop and execute effective communications strategies. Interns will have the opportunity to create and edit videos, graphics, and written material as well as assist in special projects and company initiatives. Interns will also help develop and execute social media campaigns across platforms like X, Bluesky, Threads, LinkedIn, Facebook, and Instagram. This internship provides a great opportunity to train alongside a small and flexible external relations team in an engaging and fast-paced work environment. This is a full-time (five days per week) in-person, remote, or hybrid internship; but part-time work will be considered on a case-by-case basis. To apply, please submit a resume and cover letter. Competitive applicants are strongly encouraged to also submit one or two graphic design samples. Qualifications Candidates must be motivated and organized college students or recent graduates with demonstrated proficiency in a related field. Candidates must possess excellent writing, editing, and oral communication skills. Candidates should have experience adhering to a codified writing style guide such as the AP Stylebook, the Chicago Manual of Style, or the American Psychological Association Stylebook. Candidates should have experience reviewing the written work of others; this can include peer reviews of papers, work in a college writing center, or other copyediting experience in a professional or academic setting. Candidates should be self-motivated, creative, and capable of working in a dynamic and fast-paced environment. Competitive candidates should also have experience with visual content creation and digital communications, including social media platforms and website CMS . Spring 2027 Internship Program Dates: ISW internships start January 12, 2027. The program will run until May 14. Interns must both be authorized to work in the United States and be physically present in the United States during their internship tenure. Working remotely outside of the United States is not authorized. If you attend a US university on a student visa, you must be eligible for and obtain a CPT authorization before beginning at ISW . Applications will be considered on a rolling basis until November 13, 2026. Instructions: Please upload your resume, cover letter, and writing/editing sample. If submitting an editing sample, make sure the sample demonstrates the effect of your edits in some manner. Embedded tracked changes work for this purpose as do screenshots of your communications with the writer. You may include full-page screen captures or scans of edited content, but make sure the resolution is high enough for the image to be readable. You may also include a short synopsis explaining how your edits improved the document. Your cover letter and work sample should be no longer than five pages combined; the work sample can be excerpted from a longer paper. ISW will work with students to gain academic credit for internships where applicable. ISW Scholarship Application The Institute for the Study of War will offer intern candidates up to a $1,000 monthly living stipend as part of a scholarship program.* To be considered for the scholarship, candidates must upload a scholarship application as part of their internship application. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until November 13, 2026. Candidates will be assessed based on the following criteria: Ability to contribute as a member of one of ISW’s research, operations, business development, or external relations teams; and Financial need, such that an unpaid internship would not be possible without assistance. To be considered for the scholarship, candidates must upload a scholarship application as part of their internship application. Within the scholarship application, candidates should upload a 2- to 3-page cover letter which answers each of the following questions. (This should be a different cover letter than the one used for the internship application itself.) Which ISW internship is your top choice? Why do you believe you are qualified? What do you believe to be the most pressing national security problem the US faces today? What solution(s) would you propose? Where do you see yourself in your future career? How will an ISW internship help you get there? Why have you chosen to apply for this supplemental scholarship? Are you currently receiving federal financial aid and/or need-based aid from your university? Feel free to describe using as much detail as you are comfortable. *Please note that the up to $1,000 monthly scholarship is classified as taxable income.

Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit [](https://shield.ai/). Follow Shield AI on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai), [X](https://x.com/shieldaitech), [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai), and [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI). Our Summer Internship program is a wonderful opportunity for Fall and Spring graduates to immerse themselves in an innovative and mission driven culture. Our paid internship program will provide you with hands on mentorship, an opportunity to add real contribution to our company via your internship project, and a possible job offer at the end. You will have the chance to make lifelong friendships, expand your network, and learn all about what it's like to work in a high-growth, fast scaling tech unicorn. You'll take part in company sponsored events and enjoy exploring a new city. Read on below to learn more about this unique internship! ### About the Role Shield AI's Software Development Engineer Intern program spans engineers who design, build, and test the code that powers our autonomous systems — from user-facing applications and embedded flight software to machine learning models and the underlying systems platforms that tie it all together. Over 10–12 weeks, interns work alongside full-time engineers to analyze requirements, write and debug production-quality code, and ship a real feature or capability using our standard Agile development practices. **Example Intern Projects** - **Applications:** Build a new feature or internal tool (web, mobile, or desktop) that streamlines a mission-planning or fleet-management workflow. - **Firmware/Embedded:** Develop and debug embedded C/C++ code for a flight controller or sensor module, including bring-up and hardware-in-the-loop testing. - **Machine Learning:** Train, evaluate, and integrate a perception or decision-making model (e.g., object detection, sensor fusion) into an autonomy pipeline. - **Systems Development:** Extend a platform tool, API, or data pipeline that supports autonomy software, simulation, or cloud infrastructure. ### Required Qualifications - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field - Proficiency in at least one modern programming language (e.g., C, C++, Python, Java, or JavaScript) - Solid foundation in data structures, algorithms, and software design principles - Experience writing, testing, and debugging code, whether through coursework, personal projects, or prior internships - Familiarity with version control (e.g., Git) and collaborative development workflows - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down ambiguous requirements into working code - Effective written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively in a team environment ### Preferred Qualifications - Exposure to mobile or web application frameworks and full-stack development - Hands-on experience with embedded systems, microcontrollers, real-time operating systems, or assembly-level debugging - Coursework or projects involving machine learning, statistics, probability theory, or deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) - Experience with cloud platforms, databases, networking, or distributed systems - Familiarity with Agile/Scrum development methodologies - Prior internship, research, or club/competition experience in robotics, autonomy, or aerospace applications - Interest in or exposure to the defense, aerospace, or autonomous systems industry

role: Operations Supervisor - Early Career / Recent College Graduate
description: ShipMonk isn't just a 3PL — we're the tech-powered growth partner for ecommerce brands, running 12+ owned fulfillment centers across the US, Canada, the UK, and Europe so our merchants can stress less and grow more. ## Turn what you've learned into real leadership experience. Maybe you studied supply chain, logistics, operations, business, or engineering. Maybe you got your first exposure to the field through an internship, co-op, part-time job, or project and realized you want to build a career in operations. Now you're ready to do more than observe the operation. You're ready to **lead one**. ShipMonk is looking for early-career talent to join our Fort Worth fulfillment operation as an **Operations Supervisor**. This isn't a program where you spend your first year watching from the sidelines. You'll learn our business while taking on real frontline leadership responsibility — leading approximately 25–30 associates, managing performance, working with operational data, solving problems, and helping your department improve. ## Why start your operations career at ShipMonk? You can learn the fundamentals of supply chain in a classroom or internship. Leading an operation teaches you what happens when the forecast changes, volume spikes, labor doesn't match the plan, a process breaks, or your team needs you to make a decision. At ShipMonk, you'll build hands-on experience in: - Frontline people leadership - Fulfillment and distribution operations - Labor planning and allocation - Productivity and throughput management - Inventory and quality - Safety and compliance - Operational KPIs and data analysis - Root-cause problem solving - Continuous improvement - Cross-functional leadership And you'll do it in an environment where we believe in developing our people and **promoting from within whenever we can**. Strong performers have opportunities to take on more responsibility and continue building their careers as ShipMonk grows. ## What you'll do - Lead, coach, and develop approximately 25–30 warehouse associates - Run shift huddles and set clear daily priorities for your team - Monitor productivity, throughput, quality, accuracy, attendance, and safety - Learn how to allocate labor based on volume and operational priorities - Use data to understand performance and identify root causes - Coach associates and provide clear, timely feedback - Partner with Operations leaders and teams across HR, Safety, Quality, and Engineering - Help onboard and train new associates - Identify opportunities to eliminate waste and improve processes - Maintain a safe, organized, and compliant work area - Learn the operation from the floor up while progressively taking greater ownership ## What we're looking for We're especially interested in early-career candidates who have: - An interest in building a career in **operations, supply chain, logistics, fulfillment, or people leadership** - Exposure to a professional or operational environment through an **internship, co-op, part-time job, project, or other relevant experience** - Demonstrated leadership potential through work experience, campus organizations, athletics, volunteer leadership, military experience, or other team environments - Comfort working with data and metrics to understand performance and solve problems - Strong communication and interpersonal skills - A willingness to spend the majority of the shift on the fulfillment floor working directly with your team - Flexibility to work days, nights, weekends, holidays, and overtime based on business needs - Ability to stand for extended periods and lift up to 50 lbs. **Nice to have** - A degree, current enrollment, or coursework in **Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, Business, Engineering, or a related field** - Internship or co-op experience in supply chain, logistics, fulfillment, distribution, manufacturing, transportation, or operations - Coursework or project experience involving operations management, supply chain analytics, Lean, Six Sigma, process improvement, or data analysis - Previous experience leading a team, project, student organization, athletic team, or other group **A college degree and prior full-time warehouse supervisory experience are not required.** We're looking for leadership potential, relevant exposure, and someone who wants to build a career in operations. ## What success looks like **In your first 30 days:** You're learning the operation, getting to know your team, understanding the KPIs that drive your department, and spending significant time learning directly on the floor. **In 90 days:** You're increasingly accountable for your team's performance, using data to identify problems, coaching associates, and beginning to identify opportunities to improve your operation. **In year one:** You understand how people, labor, inventory, technology, and process come together to run a high-volume fulfillment operation. You've built real frontline leadership experience and demonstrated your ability to continue taking on more at ShipMonk. ## Work Location This is an on-site role based at ShipMonk's Fort Worth fulfillment center: **ShipMonk TX1** 2601 NE 33rd St. Fort Worth, TX 76111 **About ShipMonk** ShipMonk isn't just a 3PL; we're a **growth partner for merchants**. We provide cutting-edge technology and a network of owned and operated fulfillment centers that empower high-growth ecommerce and DTC brands to stress less and grow more. With over 2,500 employees across five countries, we're on a mission to revolutionize fulfillment by providing everything from the fastest click-to-delivery and real-time inventory to custom solutions—all with a **merchant**-**first** mindset. **Why ShipMonk?** We believe in building for the long term, and our success is powered by five key differentiators that help us become true partners to our merchants. - **Global Fulfillment Network:** Our 12+ owned and operated fulfillment centers span the US, Canada, the U.K., and Mainland Europe. We never outsource, ensuring quality and consistency. ● **Proprietary Technology:** We've eliminated the need for tribal knowledge with our AI-powered platform. It provides a real-time, unified view of inventory and orders, giving our merchants the control and visibility they need to succeed. ● **Unrivaled Support:** We provide hands-on, "mom and pop" support with a global reach. Our dedicated teams are on-site at every fulfillment center, ready to jump into action. ● **Transparent Pricing**: We believe in honest, long-term partnerships. Our all- inclusive pricing means predictable costs, with no hidden fees or surprises. ● **Committed to the Future:** We invest over $10 million annually in research and development to ensure our technology and services continually evolve, helping merchants plant roots with a partner who is here to stay. **Our Core Values** Our values are the heart of our culture. We're looking for individuals who embody these principles every day. - **Merchant-first:** We handle the logistics so our merchants can focus on what they do best—growing their business. - **People make ShipMonk:** We believe in our team and invest in our people. - **Own it:** We take ownership of our work, our mistakes, and our successes. - **Get sh\*t done:** We're a fast-paced, high-growth company that values action and results. - **Change the score:**We challenge the status quo, constantly innovating and improving. ShipMonk is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

role: Flight Operations & Airworthiness Engineering Intern - Spring/Summer/Fall 2027
description: Hermeus is a venture-backed defense aviation company reclaiming the lost art of rapid iterative prototyping to build the fastest aircraft in the world today. By prioritizing relentless hardware iteration, we deliver high-speed systems at the pace of the modern battlefield. We work with the Department of War to provide the high-speed capabilities our nation and its allies need to maintain a durable, asymmetric advantage. ### **About the Role:** As a Flight Operations & Airworthiness Engineering Intern at Hermeus, you will support the planning, development, and execution of flight operations and airworthiness activities for the Quarterhorse aircraft. This role is ideal for an engineering student with practical aviation experience who is interested in the cross functional intersection of flight operations, flight test, safety, and airworthiness. You will contribute to professional technical deliverables supporting military and civil airworthiness packages, assist with risk assessments and data analysis, and support strategic planning that will advance longer-term program objectives. The ideal candidate is a self-starter who can take ownership of complex, ambiguous problems; develop a path forward; and communicate clearly across internal and external teams. This internship offers direct exposure to the unique challenges of operating and certifying high-performance experimental aircraft in a fast-paced development environment. Spring: Around 16 weeks (January - April) Summer: Around 12 weeks (May - August) Fall: Around 16 weeks (September - December) ### Responsibilities: - Support the development of airworthiness, flight operations, and safety documentation for experimental aircraft operations. - Assist in preparing professional technical deliverables for military and civil airworthiness packages. - Support operational-risk analysis, including hazard identification, risk tracking, and management of operational constraints and mitigations. - Apply engineering fundamentals and statistical methods to assess operational data, characterize risk, and support envelope an operational expansion. - Collaborate with engineering, flight test, operations, and program teams to collect technical inputs and ensure airworthiness artifacts are accurate, complete, and traceable. - Independently identify and effectively communicate gaps, inefficiencies, and upcoming needs in flight operations and airworthiness processes. - Support longer-range planning by identifying work that advances programmatic milestones and airworthiness objectives well ahead of formal tasking. ### Requirements: - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or graduate degree in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, systems engineering, or a related STEM discipline. Undergraduate candidates should be in their junior or senior year of study; graduate students are also encouraged to apply. - Demonstrated interest in aviation, flight test, flight operations, or airworthiness. - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to develop clear, professional technical documentation. - Strong mathematical and analytical skills, including the ability to organize, interpret, and draw conclusions from engineering or test data. - Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment with shifting priorities. - Demonstrated initiative and comfort working through ambiguous technical or operational problems without a fully defined path. - Strong attention to detail, sound judgment, and commitment to safe operations. - GPA of 3.0 or above. ### Preferred Skills and Experience: - Manned or unmanned aircraft pilot experience or comparable flight experience. - Experience with experimental aircraft, flight test, aircraft maintenance, aviation safety, or airworthiness activities. - Experience designing, building, testing, or operating vehicles through internships, academic work, student teams, military service, or personal projects. - Familiarity with risk-management methods, safety assessments, reliability analysis, statistical analysis, or data-analysis tools. - Exposure to civil or military aviation regulations, certification processes, flight authorizations, or airworthiness documentation. - Experience developing technical reports, engineering analyses, test procedures, or operational documentation. - A strong desire to learn, seek feedback, and take on progressively greater responsibility.

The primary responsibilities of the Bureau of Water and Sewer Operations (BWSO) are: the operation, maintenance and protection of the City’s drinking water and wastewater collection (sewer) systems; the protection of adjacent waterways; and the development and protection of the Department’s Capital Water and Sewer Design Program. The Bureau also approves and inspects water and sewer connections performed by licensed plumbers and/or authorized contractors. In addition, the Bureau has overall responsibility for the approval and inspection of all public and private construction projects which could impact on the City’s water or sewer systems. The Bureau of Water and Sewer Operations is seeking to hire an Environmental Engineer Intern within the Division of Capital Program Management (CPM) for Distribution & Drainage section. The selected candidate will provide engineering support for stormwater management, drainage infrastructure, sewer systems, environmental compliance, and related water quality and resiliency projects. Responsibilities will include assisting with engineering analyses, data collection and evaluation, preparation of technical reports, review of design documents, and coordination with internal and external stakeholders. The employee will support the evaluation of drainage and sewer system through field investigations, hydraulic/environmental data review and modeling, GIS mapping, and engineering calculations. The position will assist senior engineers with: - Collecting, organizing, and analyzing environmental, hydraulic, and infrastructure-related data. - Supporting stormwater management and drainage improvement projects. - Reviewing drainage plans, reports, calculations, and technical documentation. - Performing basic engineering analyses and calculations. - Preparing spreadsheets, maps, figures, presentations, and technical reports. - Using engineering software, databases, GIS applications, and agency data management tools. - Participating in field visits to observe infrastructure conditions, collect information, and support project assessments. - Coordinating with DEP units, consultants, contractors, and other agencies as needed. The position provides an opportunity to gain practical experience in environmental engineering, stormwater management, drainage systems, and infrastructure planning while working under the guidance of experienced engineers. **ALL APPLICANTS MUST HAVE TAKEN CIVIL SERVICE EXAM NO. 6118 FOR ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEER INTERN, TO BE CONSIDERED FOR THIS POSITION. ** Appointments are subject to OMB approval. ### About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. ### **About the Real Estate & Development Team** The Real Estate & Development team identifies, secures, and entitles the sites that power Zipline’s network. We source markets, lead site selection and due diligence (zoning, utilities, environmental), negotiate LOIs/leases and land agreements, and drive entitlements and permitting with municipalities and partner real estate teams. We align stakeholders, manage budgets and schedules, and deliver permitted, ready-to-build locations—spanning test sites and regional hubs—before handing off to construction. By turning candidate properties into drone delivery sites at speed, we enable Zipline to scale into new regions and deliver life-changing logistics where they’re needed most. ### **The Role** As a Real Estate & Development Intern based in our San Francisco office, you will help expand the physical infrastructure that makes Zipline’s delivery system possible. You will support projects from early site identification through approvals and development, helping turn promising locations into operational sites that serve customers and communities. Along the way, you will tackle complex, real-world challenges at the intersection of aviation, real estate, technology, and the built environment. You will work alongside and learn from experienced partners across Real Estate, Engineering, Operations, Government Affairs, and Communications. Your work will contribute directly to Zipline’s mission by helping bring fast, reliable delivery to more people in more places. ### **What You'll Do** - Support market screening and site selection by evaluating zoning, land-use requirements, setbacks, utilities, easements, environmental conditions, and airspace considerations. - Assess potential sites for feasibility and risk, identifying permitting hurdles, title issues, infrastructure constraints, and other factors that could affect development. - Partner with Engineering and Operations to translate technical requirements into practical site criteria, scopes of work, site plans, and permit-ready materials. - Learn how projects move through local approval processes by working with city planners, zoning officials, building departments, and external consultants. - Coordinate with landlords, brokers, and real estate partners to evaluate site readiness and support negotiations, including letters of intent, leases, and required exhibits. - Prepare comparative site analyses, deal memos, and recommendation summaries that help cross-functional teams make informed investment and development decisions. - Build project-management skills by maintaining timelines, budget estimates, and entitlement trackers, communicating progress to stakeholders, and preparing complete handoff packages for downstream teams. ### **What You'll Bring** - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or graduate degree in real estate, urban planning, engineering, construction management, architecture, geography, environmental studies, business, public policy, or a related field. - Demonstrated interest in real estate development, site acquisition, infrastructure, permitting, or the built environment through coursework, projects, internships, or other relevant experience. - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate information from multiple sources, identify potential risks, and form a clear recommendation. - Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the judgment to work professionally with cross-functional teammates, consultants, property owners, and public-agency stakeholders. - Strong organization and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple assignments, maintain accurate project information, and follow through on deadlines. - Comfort learning new tools and working with maps, spreadsheets, plans, schedules, and project documentation; prior experience with specialized real estate, design, or construction software is not required. ### **What Else You Should Know** *Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from May/June to August/September.* *The hourly rate for this internship is $34 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.* *Candidates are limited to **three (3) applications within a 30-day period.*** Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. We value diversity at Zipline and welcome applications from those who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this position but are not sure if you are the perfect fit, please apply! Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. ### **Voluntary Self-Identification** For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

## About Vercel: Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience. Now we're scaling our products for both agents and people to ship and run software, built in the open and trusted by OpenAI, PayPal, Ramp, Supreme, and millions of developers worldwide. ## About the Role: As an Engineering Intern at Vercel, you will be an important part of our engineering team, working on real projects that will impact our products and customers. You will be mentored by experienced engineers and will be given opportunities to grow and learn. ## ## What You Will Do: Work will vary by team - but your general scope will include, but not be limited to: - Own an end-to-end project: scope it with your manager, build it, ship it, and see it in customers' hands. - Write and review production code alongside the engineers who maintain it. - Debug real systems under real conditions - trace an issue through the stack and fix the root cause. - Communicate your progress clearly, including when you're blocked. ## ## About You: - Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, graduating December 2027 or May 2028. - Strong knowledge and capability with JavaScript and/or TypeScript. Experience with Go or Rust is a bonus. - You dig into problems rather than around them - you want to know *why* something broke. - You move work forward on your own. You surface blockers early instead of waiting to be asked. - You communicate well in writing. Much of how we work is asynchronous and written down. - Fluent with AI tooling and clear-eyed about it. description: We’re looking for Software Engineering Interns to help build and scale the systems that power Datadog’s observability and security platform. Interns contribute directly to real-world engineering challenges across backend, frontend, infrastructure, data engineering, and developer tooling while working alongside experienced engineers and mentors. You’ll help design, build, and improve systems that process and analyze massive volumes of metrics, logs, and application data in real time. Whether you’re interested in distributed systems, Kubernetes, AI-powered products like Bits AI, or developer platform tooling, you’ll work on meaningful projects that deliver impact to customers at global scale. At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. **What You’ll Do:** - Contribute to production systems that process and analyze large-scale observability and application data in real time - Build and improve distributed systems across backend infrastructure, developer platforms, and cloud-native services - Help identify and solve performance, reliability, and scalability challenges in critical services supporting Datadog’s growing customer base - Own and deliver technical projects from design through deployment with support from experienced engineers and mentors - Develop technical expertise through hands-on experience with technologies such as Kubernetes, distributed systems, and cloud-native infrastructure - Collaborate with fellow interns, mentors, and engineers while building software that delivers impact at global scale **Who You Are:** - Pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or have equivalent practical experience - Targeting a **2028** full-time start date - Demonstrate strong computer science fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, and software design - Comfortable coding in one or more programming languages and excited to use AI-assisted tools to enhance software development and problem solving - Have experience using AI coding tools or a strong interest in learning how to use them effectively, while exploring how AI can improve engineering practices and products - Available to work full-time from the Datadog New York or Boston office during the internship program dates: - May 24 - Aug 20, 2027 - May 24 - Aug 27, 2027 - June 7 - Sep 3, 2027 Datadog values people from all walks of life. We know not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That’s okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your experience, we encourage you to apply. **Benefits and Growth:** - Work on meaningful technical challenges alongside engineers across the globe - Participate in mentorship and buddy programs designed to support learning and development - Join an in-person intern cohort and expand your network through engineering talks, social events, and community engagement opportunities throughout your internship - Receive relocation support and travel benefits where applicable - Enjoy office perks including snacks, drinks, and catered lunches on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday *Benefits and Growth listed above may vary based on the country of your employment and the nature of your employment with Datadog.* *This job is available in various departments within our company; to conform to US export control regulations, some of these roles may require candidates to be eligible for any required authorizations from the US government.* **If possible, please apply using your personal email address instead of your university email address.** Students can sign up for a [free Datadog Pro account](https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/datadog-github-student-developer-pack/) to learn more about our platform and products. #LI-Hybrid Datadog offers a competitive salary for this role and may include additional compensation elements. In addition, Datadog offers a wide range of best in class, comprehensive and inclusive employee benefits for this role including healthcare, paid time off, and benefits related to traveling and relocation, if eligible. The reasonably estimated yearly salary for this role at Datadog is: $100,000—$110,000 USD --- **About Datadog:** Datadog is the leading observability and security platform for the AI era, providing businesses with unified visibility across the technology stack to manage complexity at scale. It brings applications, infrastructure, data, models, and security into one place, using AI to detect and resolve issues before they impact customers. description: # **Chart Your Journey at Secretariat** From a collaborative culture to teammates who will always be by your side, find a career that will grow with you. Deliver your impact at Secretariat. **ABOUT THE FIRM** Secretariat is a consulting firm that helps companies, law firms, and organizations solve complex business problems—often when there is a dispute, investigation, major project challenge, or high-stakes decision involved. At Secretariat, you’ll work on some of the most important legal, risk, and regulatory challenges facing businesses around the world. From your first day, you’ll be part of a fast-growing team of smart, curious, and driven people who enjoy solving complex problems. You’ll learn by working alongside experienced professionals and contributing to projects for leading law firms, global companies, and major institutions. Our teams collaborate across offices and disciplines, bringing energy, fresh thinking, and commitment to every client challenge. We invest in your growth through hands-on experience, mentorship, professional development, recognition, and a culture that values diverse perspectives. Start your career where your work matters. Make your impact at Secretariat. **ABOUT OUR CONSTRUCTION DELAY TEAM** Ever wonder what happens when a major construction project does not go according to plan? When deadlines slip, costs increase, and questions arise, our Construction Delay team steps in to help uncover the story behind the schedule. We dig into project timelines, records, data, drawings, and documents to understand what caused delays and how they affected the project. As part of the team, you will work alongside experts in engineering, construction management, architecture, scheduling, and accounting on high-profile buildings, infrastructure, power and utilities, and oil and gas projects around the world. It is a hands-on opportunity to sharpen your problem-solving skills, work with real project data, learn how consulting works, and see how your analysis can help clients make sense of complex, high-stakes situations. **RESPONSIBILITIES** - Get hands-on experience learning how major construction project schedules are built, updated, and analyzed to uncover what caused delays. - Work with scheduling tools such as Primavera P6 and Microsoft Project to explore project timelines and understand how work actually progressed. - Dig into construction schedules, drawings, progress reports, emails, and project records to piece together key facts and identify what really happened. - Analyze large sets of project data to spot trends, patterns, and details that help explain why a project finished early, late, or differently than planned. - Help turn research and analysis into clear expert reports, presentations, and client deliverables that support real-world decisions. - Build the core skills that set strong consultants apart - Sharpen your analytical thinking by tackling complex questions with data, documents, and real project information. - Strengthen your attention to detail by finding the small pieces of information that can make a big difference in an analysis. - Practice explaining your findings clearly and confidently to teammates, experts, and clients. - Learn how to manage your time across multiple priorities while contributing to fast-moving client deadlines. - Grow as a communicator in a professional, team-oriented environment where your work helps make complex issues easier to understand. **QUALIFICATIONS** - Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction management, building construction, architecture, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred. - Expected graduation date between December 2027 and August 2028. - Minimum GPA of 3.0. - Prior experience with construction project management, scheduling, cost controls, internships, research, student projects, or similar hands-on work is helpful, but not required. - Comfort using Microsoft Office tools such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint; curiosity and willingness to learn new analytical and scheduling tools are equally important. - Ability to travel as needed, generally under 15%, though travel may vary by project. - A collaborative mindset, strong communication skills, and an interest in working with supportive teams to solve complex problems. - An organized, detail-oriented, and creative approach to problem-solving, with the confidence to ask questions, share ideas, and keep learning. - Must be authorized to work in the S. without the need for sponsorship in the future. At Secretariat, we believe in pay transparency and equity. Compensation for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including experience, skills, and location. About PTS: Trusted, Responsive, and Nationwide ​ Phillips Tank & Structure (PTS) is a growing, team-oriented, nationwide tank construction company with headquarters in Braddock, Pennsylvania, just outside of the City of Pittsburgh. We have over 190 employees and branch offices in Texas, California, Kentucky, and Hawaii. We specialize in designing, engineering, repairing, and constructing above-ground metal storage tanks and related structures, including welded tanks, bolted tanks, and geodesic domes. We have active projects in various industries, such as petroleum, power, chemical, and renewable fuels. At PTS, our commitment to our customers shapes everything we do. We have served companies across an array of industries, handling new tanks, repairs, and modifications. Our collective methodology, industry knowledge, and exhaustive range of abilities permit us to meet one-of-a-kind needs of our customers as they react to industry expectations. We believe in good quality and on-time delivery. We provide an excellent working relationship based on integrity and professionalism. Why Choose PTS? Positive Work Culture: PTS employees experience a healthy blend of creativity, accountability, motivation, and improvement through team-based interactions with peers and other group members. Professional Development: PTS is a growing company with many opportunities for advancement. PTS' systems-based approach to training and development helps employees quickly find the path to success in our company. Intellectual Satisfaction: Being part of a team that executes unique and challenging projects throughout the country and actually builds something is ​an exciting endeavor. Our Core Principles ​ Service: The primary expectation for all employees at PTS is to focus on service. We are called to serve our customers as well as our co-workers and suppliers. We endeavor to build a cohesive team of employees who care about the well-being of the group.​ Planning and Problem Solving: Planning and problem solving should be utilized to achieve productivity. We will strive every day to be organized and efficient in our approach. We will always look for better ways to achieve results rather than propagating inefficient or inaccurate methods. Personal Development: Every employee should assist in the development of co-workers just as each employee should pursue their own personal development. Mentor and teammate relationships lay the groundwork for future growth and rewards. We are currently looking to hire a full-time Entry Level Mechanic. Job Duties and Responsibilities • Perform regular job tasks regarding above-ground storage tank seal and dome installation, inspection, and repair. Non-welded tank apparatus installation, inspection, and repair • Become Confined Space Rescue trained through PTS's in-house training • Install, inspect, and repair above-ground storage tanks • Operate safety equipment including, fall protection, atmospheric monitors, and respiratory protection • Operate all tools on the job site including power tools, air tools, and testing equipment • Setup and operate generators and air compressors • Knowledge of heavy equipment operations including forklifts, skid steers, and aerial lifts • Understand and follow drawing packages, technical documents, and safe work plans • Understand and assist in the care and maintenance of all tooling, equipment • Assist in receiving, inspecting, and inventorying all material. • Assist in maintaining a clean and orderly job site • Completing job safety analysis, safety audits, site-specific training, and other safety training. • Other duties as assigned Requirements Have great communication and organization skills. The ability to solve problems and suggest improvements to our systems. Have excellent attendance and show up to work on time every day. The willingness to learn. Be at least 18 years old. Be able to lift 50 lbs. Have a high school diploma or equivalent. Be eligible to work in the United States. Be willing to authorize background checks. Have no criminal convictions for dishonesty, sexual misconduct, violence, or acts of terrorism. Have a valid driver’s license. Be willing to authorize motor vehicle driving record checks. Be willing to submit to pre-hire, random, and post-incident drug and alcohol testing. Ability to weld is a plus. Benefits: Competitive Pay with annual reviews Health, Dental and Vision insurance 401k with company match Great culture of teamwork, learning and development. You’ll be part of a team where YOU matter If interested, complete the job application from our website at . We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer.

The NYC Financial Information Services Agency - Office of Payroll Administration (FISA-OPA) seeks to hire an IT Intern in the Technical Services group, who will help and learn how to support maintenance and security of our corporate Windows 11 environment. This role provides a learning experience in enterprise Windows administration, focusing on patch management (Ivanti, SCCM/MECM), endpoint reporting, and technical troubleshooting. The successful candidate will assist with system audits, utilize PowerShell and Excel for data analysis, and help resolve workstation issues to ensure seamless business operations. This is an ideal entry-point for a candidate looking to gain practical experience in endpoint security, auditing, and IT support within a professional enterprise setting. Responsibilities: Under the guidance of senior IT staff, the IT Intern will participate and learn to manage Windows environment. Endpoint Management & Patching Gain hands-on experience deploying and maintaining Windows 11 updates using tools like Ivanti Security Controls and SCCM/MECM, with occasional after-hours work (weeknights/weekends) to minimize user impact. Help monitor patch deployments to ensure devices are secure. Assist in the deployment of new software, application updates, and workstation hardware refreshes. Data Analysis & Reporting Learn to run and distribute reports on software inventory, hardware health, and patch compliance. Use Microsoft Excel to organize and validate IT data, gaining experience with pivot tables, formulas, and conditional formatting. Compare data across different systems (Active Directory, SCCM, Ivanti) to ensure records are accurate. Technical Troubleshooting Develop your troubleshooting skills by resolving common Windows 11 issues, including performance lags, printer connectivity, and application errors. Learn to use professional diagnostic tools such as Event Viewer, Task Manager, and Command Prompt. Gain exposure to PowerShell by using basic scripts to automate data collection and administrative tasks. Documentation & Process Help create and update how to documentation for common technical fixes and patching procedures. Practice professional escalation by documenting your troubleshooting steps before handing off complex issues to senior engineers. Additional Information CA-06 To Apply Applicants may visit the Jobs NYC website: and apply to Job ID: 797780. role: 2027 Graduate Hardware, Validation, and Product Engineering Internships - US
description: Solidigm is seeking talented and motivated graduate students for our Hardware, Electrical Validation & Product Engineering Internships in the United States. This evergreen posting supports multiple internship opportunities across electrical validation, hardware bring-up, signal integrity, SSD product engineering, and performance characterization. As an intern, you will work on real engineering challenges supporting Solidigm's data center SSD products, including testing and validating hardware and system behavior, analyzing electrical and reliability data, and supporting product characterization. This internship is ideal for graduate students who enjoy hands-on problem solving, using lab equipment, and analyzing complex data to help bring data center storage products from development through validation. Key Responsibilities Interns may be assigned one or more of the following responsibilities based on project needs, team priorities, and individual strengths: Support validation and characterization of SSD hardware, components, interfaces, and platforms; execute test plans and verify electrical and functional requirements. Assist with validation and debug of high-speed signals and interfaces such as PCIe, including signal-integrity, power-integrity, and interoperability investigations. Use lab equipment—oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, protocol analyzers, and automated test systems—to collect data and troubleshoot issues. Validate SSD behavior in system environments; reproduce issues and analyze logs to support root-cause investigations. Support product characterization of performance, power, thermals, and reliability; analyze trends and communicate findings. Develop or improve test scripts, dashboards, and automation frameworks to improve validation efficiency and reporting. Analyze benchmark, telemetry, and test-log data to identify trends, anomalies, or product risks. Support technical analysis of SSD products, customer requirements, and competitive benchmarking. Collaborate with cross-functional hardware, firmware, validation, and product teams; document test methods and findings. Minimum Qualifications Currently pursuing a Master's or Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline. Foundational knowledge of analog and digital circuits, computer architecture, or electronic systems. Experience with a programming or scripting language such as Python, C, C++, or MATLAB. Familiarity with Linux-based development or test environments. Strong analytical, debugging, and problem-solving skills. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a technical team environment. Preferred Qualifications Experience using lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, or protocol analyzers. Familiarity with PCIe, NVMe, NAND flash, SSDs, or data center server platforms. Coursework or project experience in signal integrity, power integrity, or electronic validation. Experience with hardware bring-up, board-level debug, or system integration. Exposure to test automation, data collection, or test-framework development. Familiarity with performance benchmarking, telemetry, or log analysis. Interest in technical marketing, applications engineering, or customer-facing technical communication. What You'll Gain As a Solidigm intern, you will have the opportunity to: Work on meaningful projects tied to real data center SSD products and engineering priorities. Gain hands-on experience with hardware validation, electrical characterization, and lab automation. Collaborate with experienced engineers, architects, and cross-functional teams. Develop practical skills in lab measurement, debugging, and technical communication. Present your work and contribute to solutions that may influence future products. Grow your professional network through mentorship and intern program activities. Additional Information Work locations may include Rancho Cordova, CA; San Jose, CA; or other U.S. Solidigm locations based on business need and internship assignment. Internship availabilit and project scope may vary by team, degree level, and business requirements. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. Headquartered in Rancho Cordova, California, Solidigm combines elements of an established, successful technology company with the spirit, agility, and entrepreneurial mindset of a start-up. In addition to the U.S. headquarters and other facilities in the U.S., the company has international presence in Asia, Europe, and the Americas. Solidigm will continue to lead the world in innovating new Memory technologies with aspirations to be the #1 NAND memory company in the world. At Solidigm, we view problems as opportunities to define innovative solutions that hold the power to change the world and unleash the potential technological needs that the future holds. At Solidigm, we are One Team that fosters a diverse, equitable, and inclusive culture that embraces individual uniqueness and empowers us to bring our best selves to deliver excellence in support of Solidigm's vision and mission to be the go-to partner for optimized data storage solutions. You can be part of the takeoff of an innovative business that develops cutting-edge products, delivers strong business value for customers, provides an engaging workplace for its employees, and serves a greater impact on the world. This is a golden opportunity for the right applicant to join us and help design, build, and lead Solidigm. We want a diverse team of dedicated professionals who will not just be Solidigm team members but contribute to how we shape the future of the organization. We are seeking applicants who will grow and thrive in our culture; be customer inspired, trusting, innovative, team-oriented, inclusive, results driven, collaborative, passionate, and flexible.

Apply machine learning, data analysis, or AI techniques to improve engineering productivity or validation efficiency. Support validation of software or firmware functionality; analyze failures and assist with root-cause analysis. Analyze test results, logs, and performance metrics to identify trends and improvement opportunities.
